children.title: Classical S-Lemma
children.top_down_role: The inequality-form quadratic alternative underlying single-constraint exactness.

assumptions_latex: There exists \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(g(\bar x)<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quadratic implication holds if and only if it has a nonnegative scalar-multiplier certificate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inequality-form real S-lemma under strict feasibility.

source_refs.locator: 6. Duality in Global Optimization p. 167

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the strict-feasibility assumption, the following statements are equivalent: \[g(x)\leq0\ \Longrightarrow\ f(x)\geq0\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n,\] and \[\text{there exists }\lambda\geq0\text{ such that }f(x)+\lambda g(x)\geq0\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n.\] No definiteness assumption on the Hessians of \(f\) or \(g\) is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under strict feasibility, a quadratic implication is equivalent to global nonnegativity of one scalar-multiplier combination.
knowledge_statements.title: Classical S-Lemma

source_witnesses.locator: 6. Duality in Global Optimization p. 167

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semidefinite Matrix Form of the S-Lemma Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent augmented-matrix representation of global quadratic nonnegativity in the classical S-lemma.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write \(f(x)=[x^{\mathsf T},1]F[x^{\mathsf T},1]^{\mathsf T}\) and \(g(x)=[x^{\mathsf T},1]G[x^{\mathsf T},1]^{\mathsf T}\) with symmetric augmented matrices \(F,G\). Then \(f(x)+\lambda g(x)\ge0\) for every \(x\) if and only if \(F+\lambda G\succeq0\). Consequently, under strict feasibility, \[g(x)\le0\Rightarrow f(x)\ge0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists\lambda\ge0:\ F+\lambda G\succeq0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The classical scalar S-lemma certificate is equivalently a one-parameter positive-semidefinite matrix test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((g\le0\Rightarrow f\ge0)\iff\exists\lambda\ge0\text{ such that }F+\lambda G\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: Symmetric augmented matrices of the quadratic polynomials.

knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Matrix Form of the S-Lemma Certificate

children.title: S-Lemma Constraint-Set Variants
children.top_down_role: Quadratic alternatives for equality and two-sided constraint sets.

children.title: S-Lemma Equality Variant
children.top_down_role: Quadratic-alternative structure for a quadratic equality constraint.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete scalar-multiplier set for the homogeneous equality S-lemma.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A,B\in\mathbb S^n\), suppose \(B\) is indefinite, and assume \(x^\top Bx=0\Rightarrow x^\top Ax\ge0\). Define \[L=\sup_{x^\top Bx>0}\frac{-x^\top Ax}{x^\top Bx},\qquad U=\inf_{x^\top Bx<0}\frac{-x^\top Ax}{x^\top Bx}.\] Then \[\{\mu\in\mathbb R:A+\mu B\succeq0\}=[L,U],\] and the homogeneous equality S-lemma implies \(L\le U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The valid equality multipliers form the closed interval determined by generalized Rayleigh bounds over the positive and negative cones of the constraint form.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) takes both positive and negative values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{\mu:A+\mu B\succeq0\}=[L,U]\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Lower and upper admissible multiplier bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Certificate Multiplier Interval

assumptions_latex: The quadratic form \(x\mapsto x^\top Bx\) is indefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\top Bx=0\Rightarrow x^\top Ax\ge 0\) if and only if \(A+\mu B\succeq0\) for some \(\mu\in\mathbb R\).

notation.meaning: Real symmetric matrices of order n

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneous equality S-lemma under a two-sided sign condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A,B\in\mathbb S^n\), and suppose that there exist \(x_+,x_-\in\mathbb R^n\) such that \(x_+^\top Bx_+>0\) and \(x_-^\top Bx_-<0\). Then the following statements are equivalent: \[x^\top Bx=0\ \Longrightarrow\ x^\top Ax\ge0\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n,\] and \[\text{there exists }\mu\in\mathbb R\text{ such that }A+\mu B\succeq0.\] The multiplier is unrestricted in sign because the constraint is an equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an indefinite homogeneous equality constraint, nonnegativity of one quadratic form on its zero cone is equivalent to a globally positive-semidefinite unrestricted scalar combination.
knowledge_statements.title: S-Lemma Equality Variant

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The homogeneous equality S-lemma statement is mathematically plausible under the stated two-sided sign condition, and the theorem kind fits the leaf, but no inspectable citation is supplied.

children.title: S-Lemma Interval Variant
children.top_down_role: Quadratic-alternative structure for a two-sided quadratic constraint.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic reparameterization of any two-endpoint certificate, independent of certificate exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\ell<u\) and \(\alpha,\beta\ge0\), \[f-\alpha(h-\ell)-\beta(u-h)=f+\gamma h+c,\qquad \gamma=\beta-\alpha,\quad c=\alpha\ell-\beta u.\] Conversely, \(f+\gamma h+c\) has such a representation exactly when \[c\le-\gamma u\quad\text{if }\gamma\ge0,\qquad c\le-\gamma\ell\quad\text{if }\gamma\le0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two nonnegative endpoint multipliers are equivalent to one free coefficient of the quadratic constraint and a constant satisfying the corresponding endpoint bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The endpoint certificate is equivalent to the stated piecewise-constrained pair \((\gamma,c)\).

notation.meaning: Free constraint coefficient and certificate constant

knowledge_statements.title: Endpoint-Multiplier Reparameterization

assumptions_latex: The set \(\{(h(x),f(x)):x\in\mathbb R^n\}+\mathbb R_+^2\) is convex and closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\ge0\) on \(\{x:\ell\le h(x)\le u\}\) exactly when a nonnegative two-multiplier quadratic certificate exists.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interval certificate stated under explicit joint-range separation hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be quadratic, let \(\ell<u\), and suppose \(\ell<h(\bar x)<u\) for some \(\bar x\). Assume that \(\{(h(x),f(x)):x\in\mathbb R^n\}+\mathbb R_+^2\) is convex and closed. Then \[\ell\le h(x)\le u\ \Longrightarrow\ f(x)\ge0\] holds for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) if and only if there exist \(\alpha,\beta\ge0\) such that \[f(x)-\alpha\bigl(h(x)-\ell\bigr)-\beta\bigl(u-h(x)\bigr)\ge0\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under strict interval feasibility and convex closed joint-range separation, nonnegativity over a quadratic band is equivalent to a global certificate using two nonnegative endpoint multipliers.
knowledge_statements.title: S-Lemma Interval Variant

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits, but the asserted interval S-lemma depends on a specialized convexity-and-closedness hypothesis whose sufficiency cannot be validated without a specific source and locator.

children.title: Equality-to-Interval Transfer
children.top_down_role: Relations between equality-based plus interval-based alternative principles.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equality Certificates Do Not Generally Transfer Back to a Band
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the converse from a certificate at one equality level to a prescribed positive-width interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h(x)=x^2\), \(f(x)=1-2x^2\), \(\tau=0\), and \([\ell,u]=[0,1]\). The equality certificate \(f(x)+2(h(x)-\tau)=1\ge0\) holds globally, so \(f\ge0\) on \(h=\tau\). But \(x=1\) lies in the band \(0\le h(x)\le1\) and satisfies \(f(1)=-1\). Thus a certificate for one equality level need not imply validity on a prescribed band of positive width.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid equality-level certificate does not in general extend to a positive-width quadratic band.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f+2(h-\tau)\ge0\) globally, but \(f(1)<0\) with \(h(1)\in[\ell,u]\).
knowledge_statements.title: Equality Certificates Do Not Generally Transfer Back to a Band
Equality-to-Interval Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic transfer from a band certificate to any level inside the band.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f,h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are quadratic, \(\ell\le\tau\le u\), and \(\alpha,\beta\ge0\). Define \(\mu=\beta-\alpha\) and \(s=\alpha(\tau-\ell)+\beta(u-\tau)\ge0\). Then \[f(x)-\alpha\bigl(h(x)-\ell\bigr)-\beta\bigl(u-h(x)\bigr)=f(x)+\mu\bigl(h(x)-\tau\bigr)-s.\] Consequently, if the left-hand side is nonnegative for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), then \[f(x)+\mu\bigl(h(x)-\tau\bigr)\ge s\ge0\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n,\] and hence \(f(x)\ge s\ge0\) whenever \(h(x)=\tau\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An interval certificate yields a global equality certificate at every level in the interval. The equality multiplier is the difference of the endpoint multipliers, and the interval width supplies a nonnegative surplus.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every interval certificate induces the global equality certificate \(f(x)+(\beta-\alpha)(h(x)-\tau)\ge s\ge0\), where \(s=\alpha(\tau-\ell)+\beta(u-\tau)\).

children.title: Variant Exactness Boundary
children.top_down_role: Exceptional configurations where variant-level exactness weakens or fails.

assumptions_latex: Quadratic implication certificates are sought without a strict-feasibility or two-sided sign hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact equality and interval S-lemma certificates need not exist when the constraint set degenerates and first-order terms are not controlled by the constraint.

notation.meaning: Objective and constraint quadratics in the counterexample

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete degeneracy showing why regularity assumptions cannot simply be omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R\), set \(h(x)=x^2\) and \(f(x)=2x\). The equality implication \[h(x)=0\ \Longrightarrow\ f(x)\ge0\] is true because its feasible set is \(\{0\}\). Nevertheless, no \(\mu\in\mathbb R\) makes \(f(x)+\mu h(x)=2x+\mu x^2\) nonnegative for every \(x\): for every fixed \(\mu\), sufficiently small negative \(x\) makes this expression negative. Hence equality-certificate exactness can fail when the constraint does not take both signs; analogous collapsed-band formulations inherit the obstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a quadratic equality collapses to a point, the implication may hold although no scalar quadratic certificate exists; strict or two-sided feasibility excludes this obstruction.
knowledge_statements.title: Variant Exactness Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equality counterexample is correct and failure_boundary fits the leaf, but the broader claim about analogous collapsed-band formulations lacks cited support.

children.title: S-Lemma Validity Regimes
children.top_down_role: The regularity and exceptional structures controlling validity of quadratic alternatives.

children.title: S-Lemma Regular Regimes
children.top_down_role: Constraint geometries supporting standard quadratic-alternative validity.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(x)\le0\Rightarrow f(x)\ge0\) exactly when \(f(x)+\lambda g(x)\ge0\) globally for some \(\lambda\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical inhomogeneous S-lemma with one inequality and Slater feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be quadratic functions, and assume that \(g(\bar x)<0\) for some \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\). Then the implication \[g(x)\le0\ \Longrightarrow\ f(x)\ge0\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n\] holds if and only if there exists \(\lambda\ge0\) such that \[f(x)+\lambda g(x)\ge0\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n.\] Equivalently, the augmented symmetric matrix representing \(f+\lambda g\) is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a strictly feasible quadratic inequality, validity of a quadratic implication is equivalent to a global nonnegative combination with one nonnegative multiplier.
knowledge_statements.title: S-Lemma Regular Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is the classical one-constraint S-lemma with Slater feasibility, and theorem is the correct kind, but no source or locator is provided.

children.title: S-Lemma Exceptional Regimes
children.top_down_role: Degenerate structures requiring special treatment or admitting failure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient no-Slater regime in which every vacuous implication has a scalar certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write \(f(x)=[x;1]^\top F[x;1]\) and \(g(x)=[x;1]^\top G[x;1]\). If \(G\succ0\), then \(g(x)>0\) for every \(x\), so \(g(x)\le0\Rightarrow f(x)\ge0\) is vacuous. For every \(F\in\mathbb S^{n+1}\), there exists \(\lambda\ge0\) such that \(F+\lambda G\succeq0\), and hence \(f(x)+\lambda g(x)\ge0\) globally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the augmented constraint matrix is positive definite, the empty-sublevel no-Slater regime still admits a scalar certificate for every objective quadratic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\lambda\ge0:F+\lambda G\succeq0\), although no point satisfies \(g(x)<0\).

notation.meaning: Augmented symmetric matrices of the objective and constraint quadratics

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Definite Augmented Constraint Exception

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary-and-sufficient algebraic test for a scalar PSD-pencil certificate when the augmented constraint matrix is positive semidefinite and singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F,G\in\mathbb S^m\), with \(G\succeq0\) singular. Choose orthonormal \(U_0,U_1\) with \(\operatorname{Range}(U_0)=\ker G\), and put \(G_1=U_1^{\mathsf T}GU_1\succ0\) and \(F_{ij}=U_i^{\mathsf T}FU_j\). Then
\[
\exists\lambda\ge0:\ F+\lambda G\succeq0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
F_{00}\succeq0\quad\text{and}\quad\ker(F_{00})\subseteq\ker(F_{10}).
\]
Equivalently, \(F_{10}=F_{10}F_{00}^{\dagger}F_{00}\). Under these conditions every sufficiently large \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfying
\[
F_{11}+\lambda G_1-F_{10}F_{00}^{\dagger}F_{01}\succeq0
\]
provides the certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a singular positive-semidefinite constraint pencil, a scalar PSD certificate exists exactly when the objective is nonnegative on the constraint kernel and its cross block vanishes on null directions of that restriction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\lambda\ge0:F+\lambda G\succeq0\iff F_{00}\succeq0\text{ and }\ker(F_{00})\subseteq\ker(F_{10})\).

notation.meaning: Blocks of F in the kernel/range decomposition of G
Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of the restriction of F to the kernel of G

review_flags: For affine quadratics, application to an S-lemma implication additionally requires respecting the homogenizing slice.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular Positive-Semidefinite Pencil Certificate Test

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible-set nonnegativity alone does not generally imply existence of a scalar S-lemma certificate.

notation.meaning: Objective and constraint in the exceptional example

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degenerate no-Slater regime, illustrated by a one-dimensional obstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Failure of strict feasibility is an exceptional regime in which the classical conclusion is not automatic. For example, on \(\mathbb R\), let \(g(x)=x^2\) and \(f(x)=2x\). Then \(g(x)\le0\) forces \(x=0\), so \(f(x)\ge0\) on the feasible set. However, for every \(\lambda\ge0\), the polynomial \(f(x)+\lambda g(x)=2x+\lambda x^2\) is negative at some sufficiently small negative \(x\). Thus no scalar S-lemma certificate exists despite validity of the implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without strict feasibility, a quadratic implication can hold only because the feasible set is degenerate, while every proposed scalar certificate still fails globally.
knowledge_statements.title: S-Lemma Exceptional Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The example correctly demonstrates failure without strict feasibility, and failure_boundary fits the exceptional-regime leaf, but it has no inspectable citation.

children.title: Regularity-to-Validity Link
children.top_down_role: Dependence of quadratic-alternative validity on constraint regularity.

assumptions_latex: The strict sublevel set \(\{x:g(x)<0\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strict feasibility makes separation exact and yields a nonnegative scalar multiplier certificate for every valid quadratic implication.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation interpretation of the Slater hypothesis in the classical S-lemma.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\mathcal V=\{(g(x),f(x)):x\in\mathbb R^n\}\). If \(g(\bar x)<0\) for some \(\bar x\), then strict feasibility prevents a supporting separator for the forbidden region \(\{(s,t):s\le0,\ t<0\}\) from having zero objective coefficient. Consequently, whenever \(g(x)\le0\) implies \(f(x)\ge0\), the separator can be normalized to \((\lambda,1)\) with \(\lambda\ge0\), giving \[f(x)+\lambda g(x)\ge0\quad\text{for all }x\in\mathbb R^n.\] Thus Slater regularity is the condition converting implication validity into an exact scalar certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict feasible point prevents degenerate separation and allows a valid quadratic implication to be represented by a normalized nonnegative multiplier.
knowledge_statements.title: Regularity-to-Validity Link

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle matches the leaf, but the direct separation claim for the inhomogeneous joint-value set requires a source establishing the necessary separation geometry and normalization.

children.title: Exceptional Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Structural boundary separating valid exceptional cases from invalid ones.

assumptions_latex: The strict feasibility hypothesis of the one-constraint S-lemma is removed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No-Slater degeneracy is a genuine boundary: implication validity may survive while multiplier exactness fails.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp one-dimensional failure after removal of strict feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(g(x)=x^2\) and \(f(x)=2x\) on \(\mathbb R\). The feasible set of \(g(x)\le0\) is \(\{0\}\), and therefore \[g(x)\le0\ \Longrightarrow\ f(x)\ge0.\] Yet no \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfies \(f(x)+\lambda g(x)\ge0\) for all \(x\). Indeed, if \(\lambda=0\), take any \(x<0\); if \(\lambda>0\), take \(-2/\lambda<x<0\). Then \(2x+\lambda x^2=x(2+\lambda x)<0\). The missing strict feasible point is therefore exactly the failed regularity assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The implication for x squared at most zero is valid, but adding any nonnegative multiple of x squared cannot make 2x globally nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.title: Exceptional Failure Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample and its calculations are correct, and counterexample is the exact mathematical role for this failure-boundary leaf, but no citation is supplied.

children.title: Spectral Orthogonality Regimes
children.top_down_role: Quadratic models solved through eigenvalue or orthogonality structure.

children.title: Rayleigh-Quotient Optimization
children.top_down_role: Homogeneous quadratic ratios governed by generalized eigenvalues.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reduction to a Symmetric Eigenvalue Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense direct solution for a positive-definite denominator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=LL^{\mathsf T}\) be a Cholesky factorization and set \(y=L^{\mathsf T}x\). Then \[R_{A,B}(x)=\frac{y^{\mathsf T}(L^{-1}AL^{-\mathsf T})y}{y^{\mathsf T}y}.\] A symmetric eigensolver applied to \(L^{-1}AL^{-\mathsf T}\) returns the generalized eigenvalues, with \(x=L^{-\mathsf T}y\). Standard dense factorization costs \(O(n^3)\) arithmetic operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cholesky whitening converts the generalized quotient into an ordinary symmetric eigenvalue problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generalized eigenproblem reduces to a symmetric eigendecomposition in dense \(O(n^3)\) arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduction to a Symmetric Eigenvalue Problem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact certificates for global generalized-Rayleigh lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(t\in\mathbb R\), \[R_{A,B}(x)\ge t\ \forall x\ne0\iff A-tB\succeq0,\qquad R_{A,B}(x)\le t\ \forall x\ne0\iff tB-A\succeq0.\] Thus the minimum is the largest \(t\) satisfying \(A-tB\succeq0\), and the maximum is the smallest \(t\) satisfying \(tB-A\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global quotient bound is valid exactly when the corresponding shifted pencil is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global quotient bounds are equivalent to positive-semidefinite pencil shifts.
knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Certificates for Rayleigh Bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure when the denominator is not positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A=I_2\) and \(B=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)\), \[R_{A,B}(x)=\frac{x_1^2+x_2^2}{x_1^2-x_2^2}\] is defined off the null cone \(x_1^2=x_2^2\) but is unbounded above and below near that cone. Hence finite extrema need not survive an indefinite denominator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An indefinite denominator can create poles and destroy finite quotient extrema.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quotient is unbounded above and below on its natural domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Indefinite-Denominator Failure Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationary structure on the normalized denominator ellipsoid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A point satisfying \(x^{\mathsf T}Bx=1\) is stationary for \(x^{\mathsf T}Ax\) on that ellipsoid if and only if \[Ax=\lambda Bx,\qquad \lambda=x^{\mathsf T}Ax=R_{A,B}(x).\] Thus every stationary value is a generalized eigenvalue, including nonextreme values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalized stationary points are exactly generalized eigenvectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Stationarity is equivalent to \(Ax=R_{A,B}(x)Bx\).
knowledge_statements.title: Stationary Quotients and Generalized Eigenspaces

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variational characterization of every generalized eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\lambda_1\le\cdots\le\lambda_n\) are the generalized eigenvalues of \((A,B)\), then \[\lambda_k=\min_{\dim S=k}\max_{x\in S\setminus\{0\}}R_{A,B}(x)=\max_{\dim S=n-k+1}\min_{x\in S\setminus\{0\}}R_{A,B}(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every ordered generalized eigenvalue has complementary min–max and max–min characterizations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Both variational expressions equal \(\lambda_k\).

notation.meaning: A linear subspace of the indicated dimension.

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Courant–Fischer Characterization

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The extreme generalized Rayleigh quotients are the smallest and largest generalized eigenvalues of \((A,B)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional symmetric generalized Rayleigh quotient with positive-definite denominator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(B\in\mathbb S^n_{++}\), and define \[R_{A,B}(x)= rac{x^	op Ax}{x^	op Bx}\quad(x
e0).\] If \(\lambda_1\le\cdots\le\lambda_n\) are the eigenvalues of \(B^{-1/2}AB^{-1/2}\), equivalently the generalized eigenvalues satisfying \(Av=\lambda Bv\), then \[\min_{x
e0}R_{A,B}(x)=\lambda_1,\qquad \max_{x
e0}R_{A,B}(x)=\lambda_n.\] A nonzero vector attains either extreme exactly when its image under \(B^{1/2}\) lies in the corresponding eigenspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a positive-definite denominator, minimizing or maximizing a generalized Rayleigh quotient gives the extreme generalized eigenvalues and their eigenspaces.
knowledge_statements.title: Rayleigh-Quotient Optimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-dimensional generalized Rayleigh-quotient theorem is precise and matches the topic, but no authoritative source with a specific locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The standard Rayleigh quotient for a real symmetric matrix and a nonzero vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric and let \(p\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}\). The Rayleigh quotient is \(\rho_H(p)=\frac{p^THp}{p^Tp}\), and \[\lambda_{\min}(H)\le \rho_H(p)\le\lambda_{\max}(H).\] Its minimum and maximum over nonzero \(p\) are attained by eigenvectors associated with \(\lambda_{\min}(H)\) and \(\lambda_{\max}(H)\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Rayleigh quotient of any nonzero vector for a real symmetric matrix lies between its smallest and largest eigenvalues. Its global minimum and maximum are attained at eigenvectors for those extreme eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda_{\min}(H)\le\frac{p^THp}{p^Tp}\le\lambda_{\max}(H),\quad \min_{p\ne0}\rho_H(p)=\lambda_{\min}(H),\quad \max_{p\ne0}\rho_H(p)=\lambda_{\max}(H).

children.title: Orthogonally Constrained Quadratic Programs
children.top_down_role: Structured nonconvex quadratic models with orthogonality-induced exactness regimes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Riemannian Gradient Method with Polar Retraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A feasibility-preserving first-order method for a smooth Stiefel-constrained quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a feasible iterate \(X_j\), compute \[G_j=\nabla q(X_j)-X_j\operatorname{sym}(X_j^\top\nabla q(X_j)),\] choose \(t_j>0\) by Armijo backtracking, and set \[X_{j+1}=(X_j-t_jG_j)\bigl((X_j-t_jG_j)^\top(X_j-t_jG_j)\bigr)^{-1/2}.\] Every iterate is feasible. For a smooth quadratic on the compact Stiefel manifold, standard Armijo parameters imply \(\|G_j\|_F\to0\), and every accumulation point is first-order stationary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Riemannian gradient descent followed by polar retraction preserves orthogonality and converges to stationarity.
assumptions_latex: Armijo backtracking uses fixed admissible parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X_j^\top X_j=I_k\) and \(\|\operatorname{grad}q(X_j)\|_F\to0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Riemannian Gradient Method with Polar Retraction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case iteration bound for retraction-based gradient descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the retraction pullbacks of \(q\) satisfy the standard descent inequality with constant \(L>0\), and use step \(1/L\). If \(q_\star=\min_{X^\top X=I_k}q(X)\), then after \(N\) iterations, \[\min_{0\le j<N}\|\operatorname{grad}q(X_j)\|_F^2\le\frac{2L\bigl(q(X_0)-q_\star\bigr)}{N}.\] Thus an iterate with gradient norm at most \(\varepsilon\) is obtained in \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smooth retraction-based gradient descent reaches an epsilon-stationary orthonormal frame in order epsilon to the minus two iterations.
assumptions_latex: The retraction pullback satisfies an \(L\)-smooth descent inequality along the generated steps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N\ge2L(q(X_0)-q_\star)/\varepsilon^2\) suffices for an \(\varepsilon\)-stationary iterate.

notation.meaning: Global minimum over the Stiefel manifold

knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Stationarity Complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient local curvature tests for a Stiefel-constrained quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be stationary with \(\nabla q(X)=X\Lambda\), \(\Lambda\in\mathbb S^k\), and let \(H\) be the Euclidean Hessian of \(q\) in vectorized coordinates. For each tangent direction \(Z\) satisfying \(X^\top Z+Z^\top X=0\), a local minimum necessarily satisfies \[\operatorname{vec}(Z)^\top H\operatorname{vec}(Z)-\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda Z^\top Z)\ge0.\] Strict positivity for every nonzero tangent \(Z\) is sufficient for a strict local minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lagrangian Hessian must be nonnegative on the Stiefel tangent space, while strict tangent positivity certifies a strict local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Tangent semidefiniteness is necessary, and tangent definiteness is sufficient, for local minimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Tangent-Space Test

knowledge_statements.statement_title: First-Order Stationarity on the Stiefel Manifold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT and tangent-projection characterization for a differentiable quadratic objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=\nabla q(X)\). A feasible \(X\) is first-order stationary exactly when there exists \(\Lambda\in\mathbb S^k\) such that \[G=X\Lambda.\] Equivalently, \[G-X\operatorname{sym}(X^\top G)=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stationarity means that the Euclidean gradient is normal to the Stiefel manifold, equivalently that its tangent projection vanishes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\) is stationary iff \(\nabla q(X)=X\Lambda\) for some symmetric \(\Lambda\).
knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Stationarity on the Stiefel Manifold

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stationarity Does Not Certify Global Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal boundary for first-order certificates on an orthogonality constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n=2\), \(k=1\), and minimize \(q(x)=x_2^2\) subject to \(x^\top x=1\). The feasible points \(x=\pm e_2\) satisfy the projected-gradient stationarity condition, but \(q(\pm e_2)=1\), whereas the global minimum \(0\) is attained at \(x=\pm e_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vanishing Stiefel projected gradient need not identify a minimizer, even for a diagonal quadratic on the unit sphere.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: First-order stationarity alone is not a local or global optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Does Not Certify Global Optimality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General quadratic optimization over an orthonormal frame.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(1\le k\le n\), a Stiefel-constrained quadratic program has the form \[\min_{X\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}}q(X)\quad\text{subject to}\quad X^\top X=I_k,\] where \(q(X)=\tfrac12\operatorname{vec}(X)^\top H\operatorname{vec}(X)+c^\top\operatorname{vec}(X)+d\) and \(H\in\mathbb S^{nk}\). The feasible Stiefel manifold is compact, so every continuous quadratic objective attains its minimum and maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An orthogonally constrained quadratic program optimizes a quadratic matrix objective over the compact set of orthonormal frames.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible set is compact and both extrema of \(q\) are attained.
knowledge_statements.title: Stiefel-Constrained Quadratic Program

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form SVD solution of the nearest-frame quadratic problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\), \[\min_{X^\top X=I_k}\|X-C\|_F^2=k+\|C\|_F^2-2\sum_{i=1}^k\sigma_i(C).\] If \(C=U\Sigma V^\top\) is a thin singular-value decomposition, with orthonormal singular vectors completed when necessary, then \(X_\star=UV^\top\) is optimal. Equivalently, \(X_\star\) maximizes \(\operatorname{tr}(C^\top X)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nearest orthonormal frame is a polar factor obtained from an SVD, and its value is determined by the singular values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X_\star=UV^\top\) solves the nearest-frame problem with the stated value.
knowledge_statements.title: Orthogonal Procrustes Solution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form global solution for a two-sided spectral quadratic over an orthonormal frame.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb S^n\) have eigenvalues \(\alpha_1\le\cdots\le\alpha_n\), let \(B\in\mathbb S^k\) have eigenvalues \(\beta_1\le\cdots\le\beta_k\), and let \(1\le k\le n\). Then
\[
\min_{X^{\mathsf T}X=I_k}\operatorname{tr}(X^{\mathsf T}AXB)
=
\min_{1\le i_1<\cdots<i_k\le n}\ \min_{\pi\in S_k}
\sum_{j=1}^k\alpha_{i_j}\beta_{\pi(j)}.
\]
An optimizer is obtained from eigenvectors of \(A\) indexed by an optimal subset, rotated so that the selected eigenvalues are paired with an eigenbasis of \(B\) according to an optimal permutation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric two-sided trace quadratic over orthonormal frames is solved globally by selecting eigenvalues of the first matrix and optimally pairing them with those of the second.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The global minimum equals the stated minimum over eigenvalue subsets and permutations.

notation.meaning: Ordered eigenvalues of A and B

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Spectral Trace Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Projector SDP for Spectral Trace Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-hull representation for the spectral trace specialization, not for an arbitrary quadratic in vec(X).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(1\le k\le n\), let \(\mathcal P_k=\{XX^{\mathsf T}:X\in\mathbb R^{n\times k},\ X^{\mathsf T}X=I_k\}\). Then \[\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal P_k)=\{Y\in\mathbb S^n:0\preceq Y\preceq I_n,\ \operatorname{tr}Y=k\}.\] Hence, for \(A\in\mathbb S^n\), \[\min_{X^{\mathsf T}X=I_k}\operatorname{tr}(X^{\mathsf T}AX)=\min\{\langle A,Y\rangle:0\preceq Y\preceq I_n,\operatorname{tr}Y=k\}.\] An optimal extreme point is a rank-\(k\) orthogonal projector and can be factored to recover an optimal frame.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank-k orthogonal projectors have the spectrahedral convex hull 0≼Y≼I with trace k, yielding an exact SDP for the spectral trace Stiefel problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal P_k)=\{Y:0\preceq Y\preceq I_n,\operatorname{tr}Y=k\}\), and the stated SDP has the same optimal value.
review_flags: Exactness is restricted to the spectral trace form and does not extend to an arbitrary quadratic in vec(X).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Projector SDP for Spectral Trace Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal–Dual SDP Certificate for Spectral Trace Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit dual of the exact projector SDP for the spectral trace Stiefel specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(1\le k\le n\), the projector relaxation has the primal–dual pair
\[
\min\{\langle A,Y\rangle:0\preceq Y\preceq I,\ \operatorname{tr}Y=k\}
=
\max\{k\alpha-\operatorname{tr}T:T\succeq0,\ A-\alpha I+T\succeq0\}.
\]
Both sides attain their optima. Any primal-feasible \(Y\) and dual-feasible \((\alpha,T)\) with \(\langle A,Y\rangle=k\alpha-\operatorname{tr}T\) certify global optimality. If such an optimal \(Y\) is a rank-\(k\) projector, any factorization \(Y=XX^{\mathsf T}\) with \(X^{\mathsf T}X=I_k\) recovers a globally optimal frame.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matching feasible solutions of the projector SDP and its explicit dual certify the global spectral-trace optimum; a rank-k projector recovers an optimal orthonormal frame.
assumptions_latex: The objective is \(\operatorname{tr}(X^{\mathsf T}AX)\), not an arbitrary quadratic in \(\operatorname{vec}(X)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle A,Y\rangle=k\alpha-\operatorname{tr}T\) for feasible primal and dual data certifies the common global optimum.

notation.meaning: Dual multiplier for the trace constraint.
Positive-semidefinite dual slack associated with \(Y\preceq I\).

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual SDP Certificate for Spectral Trace Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dense Spectral Algorithm for Trace Orthogonality Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic eigensolver realization and dense cost for the spectral trace subclass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(1\le k\le n\), compute \(A=V\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)V^{\mathsf T}\) with \(\lambda_1\le\cdots\le\lambda_n\), and return \(X=[v_1\ \cdots\ v_k]\). Then \(X^{\mathsf T}X=I_k\) and \(X\) globally minimizes \(\operatorname{tr}(X^{\mathsf T}AX)\). A conventional dense symmetric eigendecomposition uses \(O(n^3)\) arithmetic operations and \(O(n^2)\) storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The spectral trace subclass is solved globally by computing a bottom k-dimensional invariant subspace; a dense eigensolver has cubic work and quadratic storage.
assumptions_latex: The complexity statement refers to a conventional dense symmetric eigensolver.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X=[v_1\ \cdots\ v_k]\text{ is globally optimal},\qquad T=O(n^3),\quad S=O(n^2).

notation.meaning: Orthonormal eigenvector associated with the ordered eigenvalue \(\lambda_i\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dense Spectral Algorithm for Trace Orthogonality Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projector Lifting Loses General Stiefel Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal information-loss boundary for extending the exact projector SDP beyond projector-invariant objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Take \(n=k=1\), so the Stiefel constraint is \(x^2=1\), and let \(q(x)=x\). The feasible points \(x=1\) and \(x=-1\) have the same projector \(Y=xx^{\mathsf T}=1\), but \(q(1)=1\) and \(q(-1)=-1\). Therefore a formulation whose only decision variable is \(Y=XX^{\mathsf T}\) cannot represent every quadratic objective in \(\operatorname{vec}(X)\), with affine terms allowed, unless additional orientation information is retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projector XX-transpose loses frame orientation, so its exact SDP representation for spectral trace objectives does not extend to a general Stiefel quadratic.
assumptions_latex: The general Stiefel-QP definition permits affine terms in addition to homogeneous quadratic terms.
The proposed lifting retains only \(Y=XX^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(XX^{\mathsf T}\) does not determine a general \(q(X)\); projector-only exactness requires invariance to the lost frame information.

notation.meaning: Projector variable obtained from an orthonormal frame.

knowledge_statements.title: Projector Lifting Loses General Stiefel Objectives

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The minimum of \(\operatorname{tr}(X^\top AX)\) is the sum of the \(k\) smallest eigenvalues of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stiefel-constrained trace minimization in the symmetric finite-dimensional case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb S^n\) have eigenvalues \(\lambda_1\le\cdots\le\lambda_n\). For \(1\le k\le n\), \[\min_{X\in\mathbb R^{n\times k},\ X^\top X=I_k}\operatorname{tr}(X^\top AX)=\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i.\] Equality holds precisely when the column space of \(X\) is a \(k\)-dimensional invariant subspace assembled from eigenspaces associated with the \(k\) smallest eigenvalues, allowing the usual freedom inside eigenspaces tied at \(\lambda_k\). Replacing the minimum by a maximum selects the \(k\) largest eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An orthonormal k-frame minimizes its quadratic trace by spanning a bottom spectral subspace; the optimum is the sum of the k smallest eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.title: Orthogonally Constrained Quadratic Programs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Ky Fan trace-minimization statement and tied-eigenspace qualification are appropriate for the topic, but the record lacks an inspectable citation.

children.title: Simultaneous-Diagonalization Regimes
children.top_down_role: Joint spectral structure enabling separable or conic reformulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Construction of a Common Orthogonal Eigenbasis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructive diagonalization of a commuting symmetric family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For pairwise-commuting \(A_0,\ldots,A_m\in\mathbb S^n\), diagonalize one matrix and recursively diagonalize the remaining matrices within its invariant eigenspaces. The resulting orthonormal basis simultaneously diagonalizes the family. A straightforward dense implementation is bounded by \(O(mn^3)\) arithmetic operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recursive refinement of common invariant eigenspaces constructs a common orthonormal eigenbasis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The finite procedure produces an orthogonal common diagonalizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Construction of a Common Orthogonal Eigenbasis

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear-Term Boundary of the Squared-Coordinate Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limitation of the homogeneous squared-coordinate reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After \(x=Uy\), an affine-quadratic expression is \[y^{\mathsf T}D_i y+(U^{\mathsf T}c_i)^{\mathsf T}y+\alpha_i.\] The variables \(z_j=y_j^2\) linearize the diagonal quadratic term but lose the signs needed to determine a nonzero linear term. Thus the nonnegative squared-coordinate reformulation is exact for the seed's homogeneous forms, whereas inhomogeneous models require retained signs or additional structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Squared coordinates alone do not encode nonzero affine terms after simultaneous diagonalization.
assumptions_latex: The quadratic matrices share an orthogonal diagonalizer.
At least one transformed linear coefficient may be nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The variables \(z_j=y_j^2\) alone need not represent an inhomogeneous QCQP exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Term Boundary of the Squared-Coordinate Reduction

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A common orthogonal change of variables diagonalizes every quadratic form and converts the homogeneous QCQP into one depending only on squared coordinates.

notation.meaning: Diagonal coefficient matrix for form i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise-commuting real symmetric matrices and homogeneous quadratic models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For real symmetric matrices \(A_0,\ldots,A_m\), pairwise commutation is equivalent to simultaneous orthogonal diagonalizability: there exists an orthogonal matrix \(U\) such that \[U^\top A_iU=D_i=\operatorname{diag}(d_{i1},\ldots,d_{in})\quad(i=0,\ldots,m).\] Under the substitution \(x=Uy\), each homogeneous quadratic form becomes \[x^\top A_ix=\sum_{j=1}^n d_{ij}y_j^2.\] Hence a homogeneous QCQP involving these forms can be represented using \(z_j=y_j^2\ge0\), making every quadratic expression linear in \(z\); recovery of \(y\) requires only choices of coordinate signs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise-commuting symmetric quadratic forms share an orthogonal eigenbasis, after which a homogeneous QCQP becomes linear in the nonnegative squared coordinates.
knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous-Diagonalization Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The simultaneous-diagonalization representation is mathematically standard and fits the topic, but the equivalence and QCQP reformulation have no cited source or locator.

children.title: Positive-Eigenspace Component
children.top_down_role: Spectral component carrying positive quadratic curvature.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Positive Curvature on the Positive Eigenspace
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative curvature bounds intrinsic to the positive spectral subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\) and suppose \(E_+(A)\ne\{0\}\). If \(\lambda_+^{\min}\) and \(\lambda_+^{\max}\) are the smallest and largest positive eigenvalues of \(A\), then every \(u\in E_+(A)\) satisfies \[\lambda_+^{\min}\lVert u\rVert_2^2\le u^{\mathsf T}Au\le\lambda_+^{\max}\lVert u\rVert_2^2.\] Thus the restriction of \(A\) to \(E_+(A)\) is positive definite and coercive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quadratic form is positive definite and coercive on the positive eigenspace, with sharp bounds given by its extreme positive eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_+^{\min}\lVert u\rVert_2^2\le u^{\mathsf T}Au\le\lambda_+^{\max}\lVert u\rVert_2^2\) for all \(u\in E_+(A)\).

notation.meaning: Span of eigenvectors of A having positive eigenvalues.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Positive Curvature on the Positive Eigenspace

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The positive-eigenspace component of \(x\) is its orthogonal projection onto the span of eigenvectors having positive eigenvalues.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the positive eigenspace

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal spectral decomposition for a real symmetric quadratic-form matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=Q\Lambda Q^\top\in\mathbb S^n\), with orthonormal eigenvectors \(q_1,\ldots,q_n\) and eigenvalues \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n\). Define the positive eigenspace and its projector by \[E_+(A)=\operatorname{span}\{q_i:\lambda_i>0\},\qquad P_+=\sum_{\lambda_i>0}q_iq_i^\top.\] For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), its positive-eigenspace component is \[x_+=P_+x=\sum_{\lambda_i>0}(q_i^\top x)q_i.\] Its contribution to the quadratic form is \(x_+^\top Ax_+=\sum_{\lambda_i>0}\lambda_i(q_i^\top x)^2\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positive-eigenspace component is the orthogonal projection onto eigenvectors with positive eigenvalues, and it contributes a nonnegative sum to the quadratic form.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Eigenspace Component

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition, projection formula, and quadratic contribution are internally consistent and fit the terminal container, but no specific source is supplied.

children.title: Negative-Eigenspace Component
children.top_down_role: Spectral component carrying negative quadratic curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Eigenspace Component
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral component carrying all strictly negative curvature of a symmetric quadratic form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, and let \(P_-\) be the orthogonal projector onto the direct sum of eigenspaces of \(Q\) having negative eigenvalues. For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), the negative-eigenspace component is \(x_-:=P_-x\), and the negative-curvature matrix is \(Q_-:=P_-QP_-\). Then \(Q_-\) is negative definite on \(\operatorname{range}(P_-)\), vanishes on its orthogonal complement, and contributes \(x_-^{\mathsf T}Q_-x_-\le 0\) to \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx\), with strict inequality whenever \(x_-\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projection of a vector onto negative-eigenvalue directions contains exactly the quadratic form's strictly concave curvature contribution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_-:=P_-x\) and \(x_-^{\mathsf T}Q_-x_-<0\) for every nonzero \(x_-\in\operatorname{range}(P_-)\).

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the negative eigenspace of Q.
Restriction of Q to its negative eigenspace, extended by zero.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basis-Free and Factorized Negative Spectral Part
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent projector, eigenbasis, and Gram-factor representations of the negative-curvature component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(U_-\) has orthonormal columns spanning the negative eigenspace of symmetric \(Q\), and \(D_-\succ0\) contains the absolute values of the corresponding negative eigenvalues, then \(P_-=U_-U_-^{\mathsf T}\) and \(Q_-=P_-QP_-=-U_-D_-U_-^{\mathsf T}\). Consequently, \(x^{\mathsf T}Q_-x=-\|D_-^{1/2}U_-^{\mathsf T}x\|_2^2\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(Q_-)=\nu_-(Q)\). The operators \(P_-\) and \(Q_-\) are independent of the chosen orthonormal eigenbasis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The negative spectral part is a basis-independent negative Gram matrix whose rank equals the negative inertia and whose quadratic value is minus a squared projected norm.
assumptions_latex: The columns of \(U_-\) form an orthonormal eigenbasis for the negative eigenspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q_-=-U_-D_-U_-^{\mathsf T},\quad x^{\mathsf T}Q_-x=-\|D_-^{1/2}U_-^{\mathsf T}x\|_2^2,\quad \operatorname{rank}(Q_-)=\nu_-(Q).

notation.meaning: Orthonormal eigenbasis matrix for the negative eigenspace.
Positive diagonal matrix of absolute negative eigenvalues.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Free and Factorized Negative Spectral Part

children.title: Null-Eigenspace Component
children.top_down_role: Spectral component carrying zero quadratic curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Null-Eigenspace Component
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral component along directions on which the quadratic term has zero curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, and let \(P_0\) be the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker Q\). For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), the null-eigenspace component is \(x_0:=P_0x\). It satisfies \(Qx_0=0\), so \(x_0^{\mathsf T}Qx_0=0\) and \(x_0^{\mathsf T}Qy=0\) for every \(y\in\mathbb R^n\). Consequently, a quadratic objective \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) depends on \(x_0\) only through the linear term and through feasibility constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The kernel projection contributes no quadratic curvature; it can affect an optimization problem only through linear terms or constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_0:=P_0x\), \(Qx_0=0\), and \(x_0^{\mathsf T}Qy=0\) for all \(y\in\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the kernel of Q.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unboundedness Along an Uncontrolled Null Direction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained quadratic behavior induced by a linear term on the Hessian kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\), where \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\), and let \(P_0\) project orthogonally onto \(\ker Q\). If \(P_0c\ne0\), then \(\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)=-\infty\). If \(P_0c=0\), then \(f(x+z)=f(x)\) for every \(z\in\ker Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero linear component in the Hessian kernel makes an unconstrained quadratic unbounded below; otherwise the objective is constant along every kernel direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_0c\ne0\Rightarrow\inf f=-\infty\), while \(P_0c=0\Rightarrow f(x+z)=f(x)\) for all \(z\in\ker Q\).

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the kernel of Q.

knowledge_statements.title: Unboundedness Along an Uncontrolled Null Direction

children.title: Curvature-Component Coupling
children.top_down_role: Interaction of spectral components under constraints or reformulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Component Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal spectral components decouple in both the quadratic and additive linear objective terms, while feasibility constraints may still couple them.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) have mutually orthogonal spectral projectors \(P_+\), \(P_-\), and \(P_0\), and write \(x=x_++x_-+x_0\), where \(x_s=P_sx\). Spectral invariance and orthogonality give \(x_s^{\mathsf T}Qx_t=0\) whenever \(s\ne t\), and hence \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx=x_+^{\mathsf T}Qx_++x_-^{\mathsf T}Qx_-\). For any \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), the linear term decomposes additively as \(c^{\mathsf T}x=c^{\mathsf T}x_++c^{\mathsf T}x_-+c^{\mathsf T}x_0\). Nevertheless, a general feasible set \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) need not factor as a Cartesian product of its spectral projections, so its constraints may couple \(x_+\), \(x_-\), and \(x_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quadratic form has no cross terms between distinct spectral components, and the linear term is additive across them; general feasibility constraints may nevertheless couple their values.
assumptions_latex: \(P_++P_-+P_0=I\) are the positive, negative, and null spectral projectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_s^{\mathsf T}Qx_t=0\) for \(s\ne t\), while feasibility need not decompose across the three spectral subspaces.

notation.meaning: Positive, negative, and null spectral projectors of Q.

source_refs.locator: 2.2 Convex and Concave Functions p. 35

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2 Convex and Concave Functions p. 35

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient condition under which spectral objective decoupling extends to independent optimization subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_+\oplus E_-\oplus E_0=\mathbb R^n\) be the orthogonal positive, negative, and null spectral decomposition of symmetric \(Q\). If the nonempty feasible set factors as \(F=F_+\times F_-\times F_0\) in these coordinates and \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2c^{\mathsf T}x+d\), then \(q(x_+,x_-,x_0)=q_+(x_+)+q_-(x_-)+q_0(x_0)+d\). If every component infimum is finite, then \(\inf_{x\in F}q(x)=d+\sum_{s\in\{+,-,0\}}\inf_{x_s\in F_s}q_s(x_s)\). Without product feasibility, objective orthogonality alone does not justify independent minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If feasibility factors across the spectral subspaces, their objective contributions can be optimized independently; without that factorization, orthogonality alone is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: \(F=F_+\times F_-\times F_0\) is nonempty in spectral coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{x\in F}q(x)=d+\inf_{F_+}q_++\inf_{F_-}q_-+\inf_{F_0}q_0.

notation.meaning: Feasible component in spectral subspace s.
Objective contribution depending only on spectral component s.

knowledge_statements.title: Separability under Product Spectral Feasibility

children.title: Reduced-Hessian Representations
children.top_down_role: Curvature expressed on feasible null spaces and active faces.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Hessian Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic curvature restricted to an affine feasible space or an active face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax=b\), where \(Q\) is symmetric. Let \(x^0\) satisfy \(Ax^0=b\), and let the columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\). Every feasible point is uniquely represented as \(x=x^0+Zy\), and
\[f(x^0+Zy)=\tfrac12y^{\mathsf T}(Z^{\mathsf T}QZ)y+\bigl(Z^{\mathsf T}(Qx^0+c)\bigr)^{\mathsf T}y+f(x^0).\]
Thus \(Z^{\mathsf T}QZ\) is the reduced Hessian. On an active face, \(A\) is replaced by the matrix of active constraint normals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Null-space coordinates represent feasible curvature by the reduced Hessian, with the same construction applying locally to an active face.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) has full column rank and \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Hessian of the reduced objective in \(y\) is \(Z^{\mathsf T}QZ\).

source_refs.locator: 3.8 The GOP for Quadratic Problems with Linear Constraints p. 95

source_witnesses.locator: 3.8 The GOP for Quadratic Problems with Linear Constraints p. 95

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate invariance of reduced curvature under a change of feasible-direction basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\) and \(\widehat Z\) be full-column-rank matrices with \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\operatorname{range}(\widehat Z)=\ker A\). Then \(\widehat Z=ZT\) for some nonsingular \(T\), and \[\widehat Z^{\mathsf T}Q\widehat Z=T^{\mathsf T}(Z^{\mathsf T}QZ)T.\] Consequently, the two reduced Hessians have identical inertia, and feasible-curvature definiteness is independent of the chosen null-space basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing the null-space basis transforms the reduced Hessian by congruence, preserving inertia and definiteness classifications.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) and \(\widehat Z\) are bases of the same null space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat Z^{\mathsf T}Q\widehat Z=T^{\mathsf T}(Z^{\mathsf T}QZ)T\) for a nonsingular \(T\), so both reduced Hessians have the same inertia.

notation.meaning: Nonsingular change-of-basis matrix in feasible-direction coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Null-Space Basis Congruence and Inertia

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundedness and Minimizers in Reduced Coordinates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification of equality-constrained quadratic minimization after null-space reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under \(x=x^0+Zy\), let \(\phi(y)=\tfrac12y^{\mathsf T}Ry+r^{\mathsf T}y+\gamma\), where \(R=Z^{\mathsf T}QZ\). Then \(\inf_y\phi(y)>-\infty\) if and only if \(R\succeq0\) and \(r\in\operatorname{range}(R)\). In that case \(\arg\min\phi=-R^\dagger r+\ker R\), and the minimizer is unique if and only if \(R\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced quadratic is bounded below exactly when its Hessian is positive semidefinite and its linear term lies in the Hessian range.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) is a basis of their null space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf\phi> -\infty\iff R\succeq0\) and \(r\in\operatorname{range}(R)\), with \(\arg\min\phi=-R^\dagger r+\ker R\).
knowledge_statements.title: Boundedness and Minimizers in Reduced Coordinates

children.title: Spectral-Shift Representations
children.top_down_role: Curvature shifts paired with domain-dependent correction terms.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-Shift Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact decomposition obtained by a nonnegative identity shift that moves the Hessian into the positive-semidefinite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\), where \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), and choose \(\alpha\ge\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(Q)\}\). Then \(Q+\alpha I\succeq0\) and, for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \[f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}(Q+\alpha I)x+c^{\mathsf T}x-\tfrac\alpha2\lVert x\rVert_2^2.\] The first two terms form a convex quadratic, while the final term is concave. Any computable lower bound \(\underline\lambda\le\lambda_{\min}(Q)\) yields a valid nonnegative shift by taking \(\alpha\ge\max\{0,-\underline\lambda\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a sufficiently large nonnegative identity shift makes the Hessian positive semidefinite; subtracting the matching concave squared-norm term preserves the original quadratic exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q+\alpha I\succeq0\) and \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}(Q+\alpha I)x+c^{\mathsf T}x-\tfrac\alpha2\lVert x\rVert_2^2\).

notation.meaning: A computable lower bound on the smallest eigenvalue of Q.

source_refs.locator: 1.1.3 Differential Convex (D.C.) Programming p. 10
2.2 Convex and Concave Functions p. 35

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1.3 Differential Convex (D.C.) Programming p. 10

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp threshold for an identity spectral shift to enter the positive-semidefinite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\), define \(\alpha_*=\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(Q)\}\). For a nonnegative scalar \(\alpha\), \[Q+\alpha I\succeq0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\alpha\ge\alpha_*.\] At \(\alpha=\alpha_*\), the shifted matrix is singular when \(\lambda_{\min}(Q)\le0\); larger shifts remain valid but allocate a larger squared-norm term to the concave correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The negative smallest eigenvalue, truncated at zero, is the smallest uniform shift making the Hessian positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q+\alpha I\succeq0\iff\alpha\ge\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(Q)\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Smallest Uniform Convexifying Shift

children.title: Convex-Concave Quadratic Splits
children.top_down_role: Difference-of-convex representations parameterized by curvature allocation.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Concave Quadratic Splits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Difference-of-convex quadratic representation parameterized by a positive-semidefinite curvature allocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\), where \(Q\) is symmetric. For any symmetric matrix \(S\) satisfying \(S\succeq0\) and \(S-Q\succeq0\), define
\[g(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Sx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d,\qquad h(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}(S-Q)x.\]
Both \(g\) and \(h\) are convex on \(\mathbb R^n\), and \(f=g-h\). Conversely, every quadratic difference-of-convex split retaining the affine term in the first component corresponds to such an allocation matrix \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic is the difference of two convex quadratics whenever its Hessian is expressed as the difference of two positive-semidefinite matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f=g-h\), with \(g\) and \(h\) convex on \(\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: Positive-semidefinite curvature allocated to the convex component.
Convex quadratic components of the difference-of-convex split.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=U\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)U^{\mathsf T}\), with \(Q_+=U\operatorname{diag}(\max\{\lambda_i,0\})U^{\mathsf T}\) and \(Q_-=U\operatorname{diag}(\max\{-\lambda_i,0\})U^{\mathsf T}\). Then \(Q=Q_+-Q_-\), \(Q_+,Q_-\succeq0\), and \(Q_+Q_-=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separating positive and negative eigenvalues gives a DC split with PSD components on orthogonal spectral subspaces.

notation.meaning: Magnitude of the negative spectral part of Q.

children.title: Quadratic-to-Bilinear Transformations
children.top_down_role: Variable duplication and block partitioning exposing product structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-to-Bilinear Transformations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact variable-duplication representation exposing a quadratic form as a bilinear product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). The quadratic program
\[\min\{x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in F\}\]
is equivalent to the bilinear program
\[\min\{x^{\mathsf T}Qy+c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in F,\ y=x\}.\]
The equality \(y=x\) gives a value-preserving bijection between feasible points. More generally, after partitioning \(x=(u,v)\), off-diagonal quadratic blocks become bilinear terms such as \(u^{\mathsf T}Q_{uv}v\); duplicating selected blocks isolates these products for bilinear relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicating variables and imposing equality converts quadratic products into bilinear products without changing feasible solutions or objective values.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the original feasible set.
The duplication constraint \(y=x\) is imposed exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx=x^{\mathsf T}Qy\) on \(\{(x,y):y=x\}\), so the two optimization problems have equal optimal values.

notation.meaning: Duplicate of the original decision vector x.
Cross block of Q under a variable partition.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 Bilinear Programming Problems p. 69

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Bilinear Programming Problems p. 69

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact duplication and a bilinear relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(R\supseteq\{(x,x):x\in F\}\), \[\min_{(x,y)\in R}x^{\mathsf T}Qy+c^{\mathsf T}x\leq\min_{x\in F}x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x.\] Equality need not hold when \(y=x\) is relaxed: for \(F=[-1,1]\), \(Q=[1]\), and \(c=0\), the quadratic minimum is \(0\), whereas \(\min_{x,y\in[-1,1]}xy=-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplication is exact only while consistency is enforced; relaxing it can produce a strict lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_R x^{\mathsf T}Qy+c^{\mathsf T}x\leq\min_F x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\), with possible strict inequality.

notation.meaning: Relaxed feasible set for original and duplicate variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Exactness Requires Duplication Consistency

children.title: Separable-Nonconvexity Reductions
children.top_down_role: Reformulations concentrating nonconvexity into univariate or low-dimensional terms.

knowledge_statements.title: Separable-Nonconvexity Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral reformulation concentrating negative curvature into independent univariate quadratic terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q=Q_+-UDU^{\mathsf T}\), where \(Q_+\succeq0\), the columns of \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) are orthonormal negative-eigenvalue directions, and \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_r)\) with \(d_i>0\). Introducing \(t=U^{\mathsf T}x\) gives the exact representation
\[\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Q_+x+c^{\mathsf T}x-\tfrac12\sum_{i=1}^r d_it_i^2,\qquad t=U^{\mathsf T}x.\]
Thus all nonconvexity is confined to \(r\) separable concave univariate terms, where \(r\) is the number of negative eigenvalues counted with multiplicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative curvature can be isolated into one concave square per negative eigenvalue, leaving a convex quadratic in the original variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under \(t=U^{\mathsf T}x\), the only nonconvex terms are \(-\tfrac12d_it_i^2\) for \(i=1,\ldots,r\).

notation.meaning: Positive diagonal matrix of negative-eigenvalue magnitudes.

source_refs.locator: 3.8 The GOP for Quadratic Problems with Linear Constraints p. 95

source_witnesses.locator: 3.8 The GOP for Quadratic Problems with Linear Constraints p. 95

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimal Dimension of a PSD-Remainder Nonconvex Core
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp inertia bound for projected-coordinate reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Q=P-VSV^{\mathsf T}\), where \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\), \(P\succeq0\), \(S\succeq0\), and \(V\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\), then \[n_-(Q)\leq\operatorname{rank}(VSV^{\mathsf T})\leq k.\] Hence any PSD-remainder representation confining negative curvature to \(k\) projected coordinates requires \(k\geq n_-(Q)\); the seed's negative-eigenspace construction attains equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative inertia is the minimum number of projected coordinates needed to contain all negative curvature while retaining a positive-semidefinite remainder.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k\geq n_-(Q)\), with equality attained by the spectral construction.

notation.meaning: Number of negative eigenvalues counted with multiplicity.
Projected coordinates containing the nonconvex core.

children.title: Homogeneous Quadratic Lifting
children.top_down_role: Homogenized matrix views underlying conic relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Homogeneous Quadratic Lifting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogenization of affine quadratics followed by a rank-one symmetric-matrix lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\), define \(z=(1,x^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}\) and
\[H=\begin{pmatrix}d&c^{\mathsf T}/2\\c/2&Q\end{pmatrix}.\]
Then \(f(x)=z^{\mathsf T}Hz=\langle H,Z\rangle\) with \(Z=zz^{\mathsf T}\). The lifted matrix satisfies \(Z\succeq0\), \(Z_{00}=1\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(Z)=1\). Conversely, every matrix satisfying these three conditions has the form \((1,x^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}(1,x^{\mathsf T})\) for a unique \(x\), so the lift is exact before rank relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Appending a constant coordinate makes an affine quadratic homogeneous and represents it linearly over a positive-semidefinite rank-one matrix.
assumptions_latex: The homogenizing coordinate is fixed to one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)=\langle H,Z\rangle\) with \(Z\succeq0\), \(Z_{00}=1\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(Z)=1\).

notation.meaning: Homogenized vector with leading coordinate one.

source_refs.locator: 2.13.3 Conic Programming p. 80

source_witnesses.locator: 2.13.3 Conic Programming p. 80

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Free Homogenizing Coordinate and Dehomogenization Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneous extension before fixing the normalization coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\), define \[f^{\mathrm h}(t,y)=y^{\mathsf T}Qy+t c^{\mathsf T}y+d t^2.\] Then \(f^{\mathrm h}\) is homogeneous of degree two, \(f^{\mathrm h}(1,x)=f(x)\), and \(f^{\mathrm h}(t,y)=t^2f(y/t)\) for \(t\ne0\). Points with \(t=0\) cannot be dehomogenized into finite affine points and satisfy \(f^{\mathrm h}(0,y)=y^{\mathsf T}Qy\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A free homogenizing coordinate yields a degree-two form; nonzero coordinates recover the original quadratic, while zero-coordinate points lie outside the affine chart.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f^{\mathrm h}(t,y)=t^2f(y/t)\) for \(t\ne0\), while \(t=0\) has no affine dehomogenization.
knowledge_statements.title: Free Homogenizing Coordinate and Dehomogenization Boundary

children.title: Product-Variable Lifting
children.top_down_role: Explicit product systems underlying linearization and consistency relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Product-Variable Lifting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact linearization of quadratic expressions by explicit variables for pairwise products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), introduce symmetric variables \(X_{ij}\) intended to satisfy \(X_{ij}=x_ix_j\). Then every quadratic function becomes affine: \[x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d=\langle Q,X\rangle+c^{\mathsf T}x+d.\] The lifted formulation is exact when all product-consistency equations \(X_{ij}=x_ix_j\) are retained, equivalently when \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\). Replacing these nonlinear equations by valid convex envelopes or conic constraints produces a relaxation; therefore, linearity of the lifted objective alone does not imply equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable for each pairwise product makes every quadratic expression affine; exactness requires retaining all nonlinear product-consistency conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(X_{ij}=x_ix_j\) for all \(i,j\), then \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx=\langle Q,X\rangle\).

notation.meaning: Lifted variable representing the product of coordinates i and j.
Trace inner product of Q and X.

children.title: Rank-Constrained Conic Representations
children.top_down_role: Exact lifted models whose remaining nonconvexity is concentrated in rank.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Constrained Conic Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact semidefinite lift whose sole generic nonconvex constraint is rank one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(X\in\mathbb S^n\). The identity \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) is equivalent to
\[Y:=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,\qquad \operatorname{rank}(Y)=1.\]
Accordingly, a quadratically constrained quadratic program becomes an exact rank-constrained semidefinite program by replacing each expression \(x^{\mathsf T}Q_kx+c_k^{\mathsf T}x+d_k\) with \(\langle Q_k,X\rangle+c_k^{\mathsf T}x+d_k\) and imposing the displayed conditions. Dropping only the rank constraint yields the standard semidefinite relaxation, which can admit matrices not generated by any vector \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic programs admit exact positive-semidefinite lifts when the lifted moment matrix is constrained to rank one; deleting rank gives a relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The leading entry of \(Y\) is fixed to one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) if and only if \(Y\succeq0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)=1\).

notation.meaning: Space of real symmetric n-by-n matrices.
Matrix representing pairwise products of x.

source_refs.locator: 2.13.3 Conic Programming p. 80

source_witnesses.locator: 2.13.3 Conic Programming p. 80

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact distinction between the PSD lifted relaxation and rank-one product consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Y=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\), \(Y\succeq0\) is equivalent to \(X-xx^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\). Thus deleting rank one permits a positive-semidefinite slack \(W:=X-xx^{\mathsf T}\), and exact product consistency holds if and only if \(W=0\). For example, \(x=0\) and \(X=I\) satisfy \(Y\succeq0\) but not \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The PSD relaxation permits a nonzero positive-semidefinite slack between X and xx-transpose; zero slack is exactly product consistency.
assumptions_latex: The leading entry of \(Y\) equals one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y\succeq0\iff X-xx^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\), and exactness holds iff \(X-xx^{\mathsf T}=0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Relaxation Gap

children.title: Linear-Complementarity Connection
children.top_down_role: Quadratic-programming stationarity represented through complementarity structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Indefinite LCP Stationarity Need Not Give a Minimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smallest example separating LCP stationarity from local and global minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{-\tfrac12x^2:x\ge0\}\), the LCP data are \(Q=-1\) and \(c=0\). The point \(x=0\), \(w=Qx+c=0\) satisfies \(x\ge0\), \(w\ge0\), and \(xw=0\), yet every \(x>0\) has objective value \(-\tfrac12x^2<0\). Thus this LCP solution is not a local minimizer, and the quadratic program is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a concave one-variable quadratic on the nonnegative ray, zero solves the stationarity LCP but is not even a local minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x,w)=(0,0)\text{ solves the LCP but }x=0\text{ is not a local minimizer}.
knowledge_statements.title: Indefinite LCP Stationarity Need Not Give a Minimum
Linear-Complementarity Connection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT stationarity for a nonnegativity-constrained quadratic program written as a linear complementarity problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x:x\ge0\}\) with symmetric \(Q\). Its first-order stationarity conditions are the linear complementarity system
\[w=Qx+c,\qquad x\ge0,\qquad w\ge0,\qquad x^{\mathsf T}w=0.\]
Thus every local minimizer satisfies the linear complementarity problem with matrix \(Q\) and vector \(c\). Conversely, every solution of this system is a KKT stationary point. If \(Q\succeq0\), stationarity is sufficient for global optimality; for indefinite \(Q\), an LCP solution alone need not be locally or globally minimizing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative quadratic-program stationarity is an LCP; it characterizes global minimizers only under convexity, not for a general indefinite Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: KKT stationarity is equivalent to \(w=Qx+c\), \(x\ge0\), \(w\ge0\), and \(x^{\mathsf T}w=0\).

notation.meaning: Stationarity slack or complementary dual vector.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The LCP formulation and convexity boundary are mathematically standard and fit the target, but the record supplies no citation or inspectable locator. An authoritative source covering QP KKT conditions, their LCP form, and the indefinite-case limitation is required.

children.title: Active-Face Disjunctive Representations
children.top_down_role: Finite unions indexed by active faces or complementarity patterns.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case combinatorial size of the exact active-face union.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m\) complementarity pairs, the standard pattern index set has \(2^m\) subsets \(I\subseteq[m]\). All corresponding coordinate faces \(F_I\) are distinct: each \(F_I\) contains a point with \(s_i>0,y_i=0\) for \(i\notin I\) and \(s_i=0,y_i>0\) for \(i\in I\), and that point belongs to no other pattern face. Thus exact face enumeration is finite but can require exponentially many disjuncts before additional constraints eliminate patterns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact complementarity union can have 2 to the m distinct faces, so finite pattern enumeration is not itself a polynomial-time method.
assumptions_latex: No additional constraints eliminate a coordinate pattern.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\{F_I:I\subseteq[m]\}|=2^m.

notation.meaning: Coordinate face selected by complementarity pattern I.

knowledge_statements.title: Exponential Size of Complementarity-Pattern Enumeration

assumptions_latex: The complementarity variables satisfy \(s,y\in\mathbb{R}^m_+\) and \(s_i y_i=0\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal C=\bigcup_{I\subseteq[m]}F_I\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite active-face representation of a nonnegative complementarity system.

source_refs.locator: 1.6.2 Face and Extreme Point p. 21

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(I\subseteq[m]\), define \[F_I:=\{(s,y)\in\mathbb R^{2m}_+:s_i=0\ \text{for all }i\in I,\ y_i=0\ \text{for all }i\notin I\}.\] Then the complementarity set has the finite disjunctive representation \[\mathcal C:=\{(s,y)\in\mathbb R^{2m}_+:s_i y_i=0\ \text{for every }i\}=\bigcup_{I\subseteq[m]}F_I.\] Additional constraints may be intersected with every \(F_I\); the resulting union remains exact, although distinct faces may overlap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite complementarity system is exactly the union of faces obtained by choosing, for each index, whether the slack or its complementary variable is zero.
