children.title: Global QP Bounding Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Convex, polyhedral, semidefinite, Lagrangian, and exact-conic bounding families for indefinite quadratic models.

children.title: Convex Quadratic Underestimators
children.top_down_role: Domain-dependent convex quadratic lower models for indefinite objectives.

children.title: alphaBB Convexification
children.top_down_role: Box-valid diagonal perturbation bounds and their parameter-selection families.

children.title: Eigenvalue-Based alphaBB Parameters
children.top_down_role: Spectral parameter-selection families for valid convex underestimation.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha=\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(Q)\}\) yields a convex underestimator.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform spectral alphaBB rule for a quadratic objective on a box.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute \(\lambda_{\min}(Q)\), set \(\alpha:=\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(Q)\}\), and define \[f_\alpha(x):=f(x)-\alpha\sum_{i=1}^n(u_i-x_i)(x_i-\ell_i).\] Because each box product is nonnegative, \(f_\alpha(x)\le f(x)\) on \([\ell,u]\). Moreover, \(Q+\alpha I\succeq0\), so the Hessian \(2(Q+\alpha I)\) is positive semidefinite and \(f_\alpha\) is convex. Output \(\alpha\) and \(f_\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shift every diagonal curvature by the negative smallest eigenvalue, when needed; the box correction then gives a convex quadratic underestimator.
knowledge_statements.title: Eigenvalue-Based alphaBB Parameters

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality of the eigenvalue rule among nonnegative uniform diagonal shifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Q=Q^\top\), the nonnegative uniform shifts satisfying \(Q+\rho I\succeq0\) form \([\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(Q)\},\infty)\). Thus \(\rho_*:=\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(Q)\}\) is the unique least feasible uniform shift.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The negative smallest eigenvalue, truncated at zero, is the least nonnegative uniform shift that convexifies the quadratic matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q+\rho I\succeq0\iff \rho\ge\rho_*:=\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(Q)\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Least Uniform Spectral Shift

children.title: Structure-Aware alphaBB Parameters
children.top_down_role: Scaling and structure-aware refinements of diagonal perturbation bounds.

children.title: Scaled alphaBB Parameters
children.top_down_role: Parameter choices adapted through variable or domain scaling.

assumptions_latex: The objective domain is the finite box \([\ell,u]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scaled row-sum parameters satisfy \(Q+\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled Gershgorin rule for coordinatewise alphaBB parameters.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(d\in\mathbb R^n_{++}\) and set \[\alpha_i:=\max\left\{0,-Q_{ii}+\sum_{j\ne i}|Q_{ij}|\frac{d_j}{d_i}\right\},\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.\] The matrix \(D^{-1}(Q+\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha))D\) has nonnegative, row-diagonally-dominant Gershgorin discs; since it is similar to the symmetric matrix \(Q+\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\), the latter is positive semidefinite. Hence \[f_\alpha(x):=f(x)-\sum_i\alpha_i(u_i-x_i)(x_i-\ell_i)\] is a convex underestimator on the box. Output \(d\), \(\alpha\), and \(f_\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive diagonal scaling produces coordinatewise Gershgorin shifts whose box correction is both valid and convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaled alphaBB Parameters

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Redundancy and unscaled specialization of the scaled Gershgorin parameter rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(d\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\) and \(\tau>0\), the scaled Gershgorin parameters satisfy \(\alpha(\tau d)=\alpha(d)\). Thus the rule depends only on ratios \(d_j/d_i\). Setting \(d=\mathbf1\) gives \(\alpha_i=\max\{0,-Q_{ii}+\sum_{j\ne i}|Q_{ij}|\}\), the ordinary unscaled Gershgorin choice.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Only relative diagonal scaling matters, and the all-ones scaling recovers the ordinary Gershgorin parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha(\tau d)=\alpha(d)\) for every \(\tau>0\), and \(d=\mathbf1\) yields the unscaled row-sum rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Projective Scaling Invariance

children.title: Tightened alphaBB Parameters
children.top_down_role: Structure-aware parameter refinements yielding stronger diagonal perturbation bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Tightened alphaBB Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semidefinite tightening minimizing a boxwise correction-gap bound after fixed coordinates have been eliminated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve the convex semidefinite problem \[\min_{\alpha\in\mathbb R^n_+}G(\alpha):=\frac14\sum_{i=1}^n w_i^2\alpha_i\quad\text{subject to}\quad Q+\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0.\] For every feasible \(\alpha\) and every \(x\in[\ell,u]\), \[0\le f(x)-f_\alpha(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(u_i-x_i)(x_i-\ell_i)\le G(\alpha).\] Because \(w_i>0\) for every retained coordinate, the problem has an optimizer \(\alpha^*\). Return \(\alpha^*\) and the associated convex underestimator \(f_{\alpha^*}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After eliminating fixed coordinates, choose nonnegative diagonal shifts by semidefinite optimization to minimize the stated alphaBB correction-gap bound over the box.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in[\ell,u]\subset\mathbb R^n\), fixed coordinates have been eliminated, and \(w_i:=u_i-\ell_i>0\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimizer \(\alpha^*\) exists and minimizes \(G(\alpha)=\frac14\sum_iw_i^2\alpha_i\) over all nonnegative shifts satisfying \(Q+\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: Positive width of retained box coordinate i

source_refs.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247
2.14 Semidefinite Programming p. 81

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247
2.14 Semidefinite Programming p. 81

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semidefinite dual certificate for the minimum width-weighted alphaBB correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c_i=w_i^2/4>0\). The problem \[\min_{\alpha\ge0}\{c^\top\alpha:Q+\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\}\] has dual \[\max_{X\succeq0}\{-\langle Q,X\rangle:\operatorname{diag}(X)\le c\}.\] A sufficiently large strictly positive \(\alpha\) makes the primal matrix positive definite, so semidefinite strong duality holds and both optimal values are attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The best width-weighted diagonal shift has an SDP dual with a PSD matrix whose diagonal is bounded by the width weights, yielding matching optimality certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{\alpha\ge0,\,Q+\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0}c^\top\alpha=\max_{X\succeq0,\,\operatorname{diag}(X)\le c}-\langle Q,X\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.title: Dual of Diagonal-Shift Tightening

children.title: Scaling-Aware Tightening
children.top_down_role: Interaction between scaling choices plus parameter-strengthening opportunities.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Aware Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization of diagonal scaling using the boxwise alphaBB gap criterion after fixed coordinates have been eliminated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(d\in\mathbb R^n_{++}\), define \[\alpha_i(d):=\max\left\{0,-Q_{ii}+\sum_{j\ne i}|Q_{ij}|\frac{d_j}{d_i}\right\},\qquad G(d):=\frac14\sum_{i=1}^n w_i^2\alpha_i(d).\] Remove the immaterial common scale by imposing \(\prod_{i=1}^n d_i=1\), and minimize \(G(d)\) over positive \(d\). Every feasible scaling induces \(Q+\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha(d))\succeq0\), so its alphaBB correction is a convex underestimator with certified gap at most \(G(d)\). Return a minimizing scaling and its induced parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After eliminating fixed coordinates, optimize the positive diagonal scaling against the box widths to obtain the smallest certified gap within the scaled Gershgorin family.
assumptions_latex: Fixed coordinates have been eliminated, so \(w_i:=u_i-\ell_i>0\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A minimizing normalized scaling selects the smallest certified gap bound within the stated scaled Gershgorin family.

notation.meaning: Coordinatewise parameters induced by scaling d
Positive width of retained box coordinate i

source_refs.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex reparameterization of scaling-aware alphaBB gap minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(d_i=e^{y_i}\). Then \(\prod_i d_i=1\) is equivalent to \(\sum_i y_i=0\), and \[G(e^y)=\frac14\sum_i w_i^2\max\left\{0,-Q_{ii}+\sum_{j\ne i}|Q_{ij}|e^{y_j-y_i}\right\}\] is convex in \(y\). Thus scaling-aware tightening is a convex optimization problem on \(\{y:\sum_i y_i=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Logarithmic scaling turns the normalized scaling search into a convex optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\mapsto G(e^y)\) is convex and \(\prod_i d_i=1\iff\sum_i y_i=0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Log-Scaling Formulation

children.title: Parameter-Quality Boundary
children.top_down_role: Regimes where refined parameters materially improve or fail to improve underestimators.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Quality Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary separating underestimation from convexification on a full-dimensional box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[f_\alpha(x):=f(x)-\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(u_i-x_i)(x_i-\ell_i).\] For \(\alpha\in\mathbb R^n_+\), one has \(f_\alpha(x)\le f(x)\) throughout \([\ell,u]\). On the full-dimensional box, \(f_\alpha\) is convex if and only if \[Q+\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0.\] Consequently, a nonnegative parameter vector may define a valid underestimator while failing to define a convex underestimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a full-dimensional box, nonnegative parameters always give an underestimator, but they give a convex underestimator exactly when the diagonally shifted quadratic matrix is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Underestimation holds for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb R^n_+\), whereas convexity holds exactly when \(Q+\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\).

source_refs.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualification of the ambient PSD test when some box coordinates are fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:=\{i:\ell_i<u_i\}\) and \(Q_\alpha:=Q+\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\). On a box with fixed coordinates, convexity of \(f_\alpha\) restricted to the box is equivalent to \((Q_\alpha)_{FF}\succeq0\), not necessarily to \(Q_\alpha\succeq0\). For \(i\notin F\), the correction \(\alpha_i(u_i-x_i)(x_i-\ell_i)\) vanishes identically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a degenerate box, only the shifted principal matrix on free coordinates controls convexity, and shifts on fixed coordinates have no effect.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_\alpha\text{ is convex on }[\ell,u]\iff (Q+\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha))_{FF}\succeq0.
knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate-Box Convexity Boundary

children.title: Eigenvalue-Shift Convexification
children.top_down_role: Uniform spectral shifts combined with bounded-domain corrections.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The shifted-and-corrected function is a convex underestimator of the original quadratic.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform eigenvalue shift with an exact box-boundary correction.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The eigenvalue-shift underestimator is \[\underline f_\rho(x):=f(x)-\rho\sum_{i=1}^n(u_i-x_i)(x_i-\ell_i).\] On the box, every subtracted product is nonnegative, so \(\underline f_\rho(x)\le f(x)\). Its quadratic matrix is \(Q+\rho I\), which is positive semidefinite under the stated spectral condition; hence \(\underline f_\rho\) is convex. The correction vanishes at every box vertex, so \(\underline f_\rho\) and \(f\) agree there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform eigenvalue shift plus a nonnegative box correction yields a convex underestimator that agrees with the quadratic at box vertices.
knowledge_statements.title: Eigenvalue-Shift Convexification

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact pointwise and worst-case discrepancy introduced by the uniform box correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(w_i:=u_i-\ell_i\) and \(\rho\ge0\), \[f(x)-\underline f_\rho(x)=\rho\sum_{i=1}^n(u_i-x_i)(x_i-\ell_i).\] Hence \[0\le f(x)-\underline f_\rho(x)\le\frac{\rho}{4}\sum_{i=1}^n w_i^2,\] with equality at the box midpoint \(x=(\ell+u)/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The uniform-shift correction has exact maximum one quarter of rho times the sum of squared box widths, attained at the midpoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_{x\in[\ell,u]}(f(x)-\underline f_\rho(x))=\frac\rho4\sum_i(u_i-\ell_i)^2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Uniform-Shift Correction Gap

children.title: Separable Diagonal Convexification
children.top_down_role: Coordinatewise curvature allocation producing separable convex bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Separable Diagonal Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal curvature allocation using separable coordinatewise box corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r_i(t):=\delta_i(u_i-t)(t-\ell_i)\), define \[\underline f_\delta(x):=f(x)-\sum_{i=1}^n r_i(x_i).\] Each \(r_i\) is nonnegative on \([\ell_i,u_i]\), so \(\underline f_\delta(x)\le f(x)\) throughout the box. If \(Q+\operatorname{Diag}(\delta)\succeq0\), then \(\underline f_\delta\) is a convex quadratic underestimator. The correction \(\sum_i r_i(x_i)\) is separable, although \(\underline f_\delta\) need not be separable when \(Q\) has off-diagonal entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocate curvature by coordinate and subtract separable box products; positive semidefiniteness of the shifted matrix gives a convex quadratic underestimator, while only the correction is necessarily separable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coordinatewise separable correction defines a convex quadratic underestimator \(\underline f_\delta\le f\) on the box.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247
4.4 DC Representation of Separable Functions p. 110

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247
4.4 DC Representation of Separable Functions p. 110

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact maximum discrepancy for a fixed nonnegative coordinatewise curvature allocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(w_i:=u_i-\ell_i\) and \(\delta\ge0\). Then \[f(x)-\underline f_\delta(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\delta_i(u_i-x_i)(x_i-\ell_i),\] and \[0\le f(x)-\underline f_\delta(x)\le\frac14\sum_{i=1}^n\delta_iw_i^2.\] The upper bound is attained by placing every coordinate with \(\delta_i>0\) at its interval midpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For fixed diagonal shifts, the exact maximum separable correction is one quarter of their width-squared weighted sum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_{x\in[\ell,u]}(f(x)-\underline f_\delta(x))=\frac14\sum_i\delta_i(u_i-\ell_i)^2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Separable-Correction Gap

children.title: Product-Envelope Relaxation Family
children.top_down_role: Convex-hull and lifted-linear bounds for quadratic products over bounded domains.

children.title: McCormick Bilinear Envelopes
children.top_down_role: Termwise convexification of bilinear products over boxes.

assumptions_latex: The lifted variable \(w\) represents the product \(xy\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The four McCormick inequalities describe \(\operatorname{conv}\{(x,y,xy)\}\) over the rectangle.

notation.meaning: Convex hull of the bilinear graph

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex hull of one bilinear graph over a rectangle.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 Bilinear Programming Problems p. 69

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The convex hull of the bilinear graph over the rectangle is the polytope \(\mathcal M\) defined by the variable bounds and \[\begin{aligned}w&\ge \ell_x y+\ell_y x-\ell_x\ell_y, &w&\ge u_x y+u_y x-u_xu_y,\\ w&\le u_x y+\ell_y x-u_x\ell_y, &w&\le \ell_x y+u_y x-\ell_xu_y.\end{aligned}\] Precisely, \[\mathcal M=\operatorname{conv}\{(x,y,w):\ell_x\le x\le u_x,\ \ell_y\le y\le u_y,\ w=xy\}.\] Applying these inequalities termwise gives a linear relaxation of box-constrained quadratic products.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Four linear inequalities give the exact convex hull of one bilinear product over a rectangle and can be imposed termwise in lifted quadratic models.
knowledge_statements.title: McCormick Bilinear Envelopes

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Bilinear Programming Problems p. 69

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Bound Requirement and Termwise Exactness Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exactness for one product and relaxation of a coupled product system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The standard four-facet McCormick formulation requires finite lower and upper bounds for both factors. It is the exact convex hull of one bilinear graph over the resulting rectangle, but imposing such envelopes independently on several products need not describe the convex hull of their joint graph because shared-factor and higher-order consistency relations may be missing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: McCormick is exact for one finitely bounded product, but independent termwise envelopes can be inexact for coupled products and require finite factor bounds.
assumptions_latex: Multiple lifted products may share original variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Single-product hull exactness does not imply joint-product hull exactness, and finite factor bounds are required for the standard four-facet formulation.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Bound Requirement and Termwise Exactness Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact McCormick Error on a Rectangle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp dependence of a single bilinear envelope on factor widths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Delta_x=u_x-\ell_x\) and \(\Delta_y=u_y-\ell_y\). For the McCormick convex underestimator \(\underline m\) and concave overestimator \(\overline m\) of \(xy\),
\[
\max(xy-\underline m)=\frac{\Delta_x\Delta_y}{4},
\qquad
\max(\overline m-xy)=\frac{\Delta_x\Delta_y}{4},
\]
where both maxima are over the rectangle. The maximum vertical width \(\overline m-\underline m\) is \(\Delta_x\Delta_y/2\). Hence bound contraction monotonically strengthens the envelope, and the envelope is exact when either factor is fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each one-sided McCormick error is one quarter of the product of the interval widths; the envelope becomes exact when either interval has zero width.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max(xy-\underline m)=\max(\overline m-xy)=\Delta_x\Delta_y/4\) and \(\max(\overline m-\underline m)=\Delta_x\Delta_y/2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact McCormick Error on a Rectangle

children.title: Reformulation-Linearization Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Lifted linear bounds strengthened by products of valid relations.

children.title: First-Level RLT Bounds
children.top_down_role: Foundational lifted consistency bounds for quadratic products.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Linearized products of pairs of valid affine slacks form the first-level RLT relaxation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise-slack convention for level-one RLT on a bounded polyhedron.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every pair \(r,s\), validity of \(g_r(x)g_s(x)\ge0\) on \(P\) gives, after replacing \(x_ix_j\) by \(X_{ij}\), \[b_rb_s-b_s a_r^\top x-b_r a_s^\top x+\langle a_r a_s^\top,X\rangle\ge0.\] The first-level RLT relaxation consists of \(x\in P\), symmetry of \(X\), and these linearized pair-product inequalities, including products involving the box-defining slacks when bounds are present. Every point \((x,xx^\top)\) with \(x\in P\) satisfies the system, so optimizing the lifted quadratic objective over it gives a valid relaxation bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiply pairs of nonnegative defining slacks, replace each quadratic monomial by a lifted variable, and impose the resulting linear inequalities to obtain a valid bound.
knowledge_statements.title: First-Level RLT Bounds

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Box RLT Recovers Pairwise McCormick Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural equivalence between bound-slack products and pairwise product envelopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For finite bounds \(\ell_i\le x_i\le u_i\) and \(\ell_j\le x_j\le u_j\), linearizing the four valid products
\[
(x_i-\ell_i)(x_j-\ell_j),\quad
(u_i-x_i)(u_j-x_j),\quad
(u_i-x_i)(x_j-\ell_j),\quad
(x_i-\ell_i)(u_j-x_j)
\]
with \(X_{ij}\) replacing \(x_ix_j\) yields exactly the four McCormick inequalities for \(X_{ij}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a box, pairwise products of lower- and upper-bound slacks linearize exactly to the four McCormick inequalities.
assumptions_latex: Both variables have finite lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bound-slack portion of first-level RLT equals the pairwise McCormick system.
knowledge_statements.title: Box RLT Recovers Pairwise McCormick Inequalities

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-derived lifted consistency equations at the foundational RLT level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(h_t(x)=d_t-c_t^{\mathsf T}x=0\) is a valid affine equality, then for every selected affine coordinate factor or defining affine slack \(s(x)\) used at the first RLT level,
\[
h_t(x)s(x)=0
\]
is valid. Expanding and replacing each \(x_ix_j\) by \(X_{ij}\) gives a linear equality in \((x,X)\). These equations may be imposed together with linearized products \(g_r(x)g_s(x)\ge0\) of nonnegative inequality slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: First-level RLT can multiply valid affine equalities by first-level affine factors and linearize the products into lifted consistency equations.
assumptions_latex: \(h_t(x)=0\) is valid on the original feasible set.
\(s(x)\) is an affine factor selected by the first-level convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal L(h_t s)=0\) is valid for every selected first-level affine factor \(s\).
knowledge_statements.title: First-Level Products Involving Affine Equalities

children.title: RLT Product Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Successively strengthened product-relation families.

children.title: RLT Hierarchy Levels
children.top_down_role: Successive levels of reformulation-linearization strength.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Level definition and monotone lower-bound ordering under an explicitly declared product-family convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix nested families \(\mathcal F_1\subseteq\mathcal F_2\subseteq\cdots\) of valid products of nonnegative affine slacks, and define level \(d\) to impose consistent linearizations of every product in \(\mathcal F_d\) while retaining all earlier relations. If \(R_d\) is the resulting lifted region and \(L_d\) the minimum of a consistently lifted objective, then \[\pi_d(R_{d+1})\subseteq R_d,\qquad L_d\le L_{d+1}\le f^*.\] The index \(d\) has no convention-independent degree meaning; that meaning must be declared through \(\mathcal F_d\). Nesting alone does not imply strict improvement or convergence to \(f^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An RLT hierarchy is well defined once its nested product families are declared. Retaining earlier relations gives nested relaxations and nondecreasing lower bounds, but nesting alone gives neither strict gain nor convergence.
assumptions_latex: \text{the objective and shared monomials are lifted consistently}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Handelman–RLT Asymptotic Convergence on a Polytope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence of the full slack-product hierarchy under compact full-dimensional polyhedral assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x:g_i(x)\ge0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) be a compact polytope with nonempty interior, where the \(g_i\) are affine, and let \(f\) be a polynomial. Define \(L_d\) as the largest \(\gamma\) admitting \(f(x)-\gamma=\sum_{|\alpha|\le d}c_\alpha\prod_{i=1}^m g_i(x)^{\alpha_i}\), with \(c_\alpha\ge0\). Then \(L_d\) is nondecreasing and converges to \(f^*=\min_{x\in P}f(x)\). Equivalently, every \(\gamma<f^*\) has such a certificate at some finite degree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact full-dimensional polytope, the full nonnegative slack-product hierarchy gives monotone lower bounds converging to the polynomial minimum; every strict lower bound has a finite certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a compact polytope with nonempty interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_d\uparrow f^*\), and for every \(\gamma<f^*\) there is a finite-degree representation \(f-\gamma=\sum c_\alpha g^\alpha\) with \(c_\alpha\ge0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\) be a finite family of index tuples. For every \(S=(r_1,\ldots,r_t)\in\mathcal F\), the polynomial inequality \[\prod_{q=1}^t g_{r_q}(x)\ge0\] is valid on the feasible set. Expanding the product and applying the monomial substitution \(\mathcal L(x^\gamma)=z_\gamma\) gives the linear lifted inequality \[\mathcal L\left(\prod_{q=1}^t g_{r_q}(x)\right)\ge0.\] Thus a constraint-product family is represented by the collection of these linearizations. If \(\mathcal F_1\subseteq\mathcal F_2\), the relaxation generated by \(\mathcal F_2\) is contained in that generated by \(\mathcal F_1\).

children.title: Marginal-Strength Boundary
children.top_down_role: Regimes where additional lifted relations yield limited bound improvement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary between no improvement and strict improvement when one nested RLT relaxation replaces another.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq R\) be nonempty compact convex projected relaxation sets and let \(L\) be linear. For minimization, the added level has zero marginal strength for \(L\) exactly when \[\min_{z\in S}L(z)=\min_{z\in R}L(z),\] and has strict marginal strength exactly when the left side is larger. Moreover, \(S=R\) if and only if these minima agree for every linear objective. Thus proper inclusion guarantees improvement for some separating linear objective, but not for every specified objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nested level improves a fixed bound exactly when its optimum is strictly larger. Equality of the sets is equivalent to equality for every linear objective, while proper inclusion need not improve a particular objective.
assumptions_latex: S\text{ and }R\text{ are compact and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_S L>\min_R L\iff\text{strict marginal improvement for }L
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Specific and Uniform Marginal Strength
Marginal-Strength Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion distinguishing redundant and strictly strengthening successive RLT levels for a fixed objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem with lifted linear objective \(L\), let \(R_d\) and \(R_{d+1}\) be successive nonempty RLT relaxations and let \(\pi_d(R_{d+1})\subseteq R_d\) be the higher-level projection. The next level has zero marginal strength for this objective exactly when \(\inf_{z\in\pi_d(R_{d+1})}L(z)=\inf_{z\in R_d}L(z)\). It is strictly stronger for the objective exactly when the left-hand infimum is larger. Objective-independent redundancy holds when \(\pi_d(R_{d+1})=R_d\); proper inclusion alone does not guarantee a strict improvement for every objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A new RLT level improves a given lower bound exactly when minimizing the lifted objective over its projection yields a strictly larger value.
assumptions_latex: L\text{ is a finite-valued linear objective on }R_d
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{z\in\pi_d(R_{d+1})}L(z)>\inf_{z\in R_d}L(z)\iff\text{strict marginal strengthening for }L

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The objective-dependent equality/strict-inequality criterion is mathematically coherent and the content kind condition fits the boundary leaf, but the record supplies no evidence for its RLT interpretation or the objective-independent redundancy assertion.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \([\ell,u]\subset\mathbb R^n\) be partitioned into finitely many boxes \(B_k=[\ell^k,u^k]\), and let \(i\ne j\). For \(w=x_ix_j\), let \(M_k\) be the four-inequality McCormick polytope on \(B_k\), including the restrictions \(x\in B_k\). A box-selection disjunctive formulation with integral selectors projects onto \(\bigcup_k M_k\); an ideal continuous relaxation of that disjunction projects onto \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_kM_k)\). Both sets are contained in the McCormick envelope \(M(\ell,u)\) over the original box. For a sequence of partitions whose maximum box diameter tends to zero, \(\sup\{|w-x_ix_j|:(x,w)\in\bigcup_kM_k\}\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Applying McCormick inequalities separately on partition boxes gives a disjunctive union that tightens the global envelope and converges to the bilinear graph as the mesh vanishes; the ideal continuous relaxation is the convex hull of that union.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Piecewise Envelopes for a Univariate Square
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partition-dependent lower and upper representation of a univariate quadratic graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On an interval \([a,b]\), the convex hull of the graph \(w=x^2\) is
\[
a\le x\le b,
\qquad x^2\le w\le(a+b)x-ab.
\]
The secant overestimator has sharp error
\[
\max_{x\in[a,b]}\big((a+b)x-ab-x^2\big)=\frac{(b-a)^2}{4}.
\]
Applying this hull on every selected cell of a finite interval partition gives a piecewise convex relaxation contained in the original-interval hull, and its maximum graph error tends to zero with the partition mesh.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A square is bounded below by its convex graph and above by its secant; recomputing this hull on partition intervals strengthens the relaxation with quadratic error decay.
assumptions_latex: Partition cells are closed intervals with disjoint interiors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^2\le w\le(a+b)x-ab\), with maximum upper error \((b-a)^2/4\); the cellwise error vanishes with the mesh.

knowledge_statements.title: Basic Shor Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard lifted SDP relaxation of a real QCQP in minimization form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(x^\top Q_0x+2q_0^\top x+c_0\) subject to \(x^\top Q_i x+2q_i^\top x+c_i\le 0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). The basic Shor relaxation replaces \(xx^\top\) by \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) and solves the semidefinite program with objective \(\langle Q_0,X\rangle+2q_0^\top x+c_0\), constraints \(\langle Q_i,X\rangle+2q_i^\top x+c_i\le0\), and \(\begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\). Dropping \(X=xx^\top\) makes its optimum a lower bound on the QCQP optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Shor relaxation linearizes every quadratic term in a matrix variable and replaces the rank-one identity by one positive-semidefinite block constraint.
assumptions_latex: Q_i\in\mathbb S^n,\ q_i\in\mathbb R^n,\ c_i\in\mathbb R

knowledge_statements.title: Chordal Semidefinite Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-semidefinite completion characterization for chordal sparsity patterns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be chordal, let \(C_1,\ldots,C_p\) be its maximal cliques, and let \(Z\) be a symmetric partial matrix whose diagonal and edge entries are specified consistently. Then \(Z\) admits a completion \(\widehat Z\succeq0\) if and only if every fully specified principal clique matrix \(Z[C_k,C_k]\) is positive semidefinite. Consequently, when an SDP depends only on entries specified by \(G\), its global positive-semidefinite constraint may be represented by maximal-clique PSD constraints plus shared-entry consistency, without changing the projected feasible set or optimal bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For chordal sparsity, consistent positive-semidefinite maximal-clique blocks are exactly the partial matrices having a global positive-semidefinite completion.

Z\text{ is a symmetric partial matrix specified on the diagonal and }E

children.title: Clique-Overlap Consistency
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of local matrix blocks across shared clique variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Overlap Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility condition for independently represented clique moment matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z^1,\ldots,Z^p\) be symmetric matrices indexed by cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_p\). Clique-overlap consistency requires \(Z^k[C_k\cap C_\ell,C_k\cap C_\ell]=Z^\ell[C_k\cap C_\ell,C_k\cap C_\ell]\) for every pair \(k,\ell\) with nonempty intersection. Equivalently, every matrix entry indexed by two vertices belonging to multiple cliques has one common value. Under the running-intersection property, it suffices to impose these equalities on adjacent cliques of a clique tree; the resulting local matrices define one well-defined partial global matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local clique matrices are consistent when they assign identical values to every entry shared on clique intersections; clique-tree edge equalities suffice under running intersection.
assumptions_latex: \{C_k\}\text{ has the running-intersection property for the clique-tree reduction}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Z^k[C_k\cap C_\ell,C_k\cap C_\ell]=Z^\ell[C_k\cap C_\ell,C_k\cap C_\ell]

notation.meaning: local symmetric matrix on clique k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Pairwise overlap equality and the clique-tree reduction under running intersection are mathematically plausible and condition is the correct content kind, but the record has no citation supporting the adjacent-clique sufficiency claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse-Decomposition Exactness Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chordality marks when clique PSD constraints characterize global PSD completability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a chordal sparsity graph, maximal-clique positive-semidefinite constraints with overlap consistency exactly characterize partial matrices having a global positive-semidefinite completion. Without chordality, maximal-clique constraints can be insufficient. On the chordless four-cycle \(1-2-3-4-1\), specify \(Z_{ii}=1\), \(Z_{12}=Z_{23}=Z_{34}=1\), and \(Z_{41}=-1\). Every specified edge block is positive semidefinite, yet no global positive-semidefinite completion exists: a Gram realization of the three unit inner products forces all four unit vectors equal, contradicting the last inner product. Thus chordal extension or additional constraints are necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clique PSD constraints are exact for chordal patterns, but a chordless four-cycle already admits locally PSD edge blocks with no global PSD completion.
assumptions_latex: G\text{ is the sparsity graph of a symmetric partial matrix}
\text{local PSD constraints are imposed on maximal cliques}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ chordal implies exact PSD-completion characterization; nonchordal }G\text{ need not}

children.title: SDP Rank Diagnostics

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rank decomposition of a normalized positive-semidefinite Shor moment matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\), let \(R=X-xx^\top\). Then \(R\succeq0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(Z)=1+\operatorname{rank}(R)\). Thus \(Z\) has rank one exactly when \(R=0\). Quantities such as \(\operatorname{tr}(R)\) and \(\|R\|_2\) measure rank-one failure, but constitute numerical certificates only with declared feasibility, scaling, and arithmetic-error tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The rank excess of a normalized moment matrix equals the rank of its PSD Schur residual; residual norms are only tolerance-dependent numerical diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R:=X-xx^\top\succeq0,\quad \operatorname{rank}(Z)=1+\operatorname{rank}(R),\quad \operatorname{rank}(Z)=1\iff R=0

notation.meaning: Schur residual measuring violation of the lifted product identity
spectral norm of the Schur residual

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and numerical rank tests for a Shor moment matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z^\star=\begin{pmatrix}1&(x^\star)^\top\\x^\star&X^\star\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\) be an optimal Shor moment matrix. In exact arithmetic, \(\operatorname{rank}(Z^\star)=1\) is equivalent to \(X^\star=x^\star(x^\star)^\top\), and therefore certifies satisfaction of the dropped rank constraint. Numerically, ordered eigenvalues \(\lambda_1\ge\lambda_2\ge\cdots\ge0\) may be inspected through \(\lambda_2/\max\{1,\lambda_1\}\); a small ratio is evidence of near rank one but is not an exact certificate without feasibility and error bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal lifted matrix has exact rank one precisely when its lifted block equals xxᵀ; eigenvalue ratios provide only numerical diagnostics.
assumptions_latex: Z^\star\text{ is optimal for the SDP relaxation}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}(Z^\star)=1\iff X^\star=x^\star(x^\star)^\top

knowledge_statements.title: SDP Exactness Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori equality test between an SDP lower bound and a feasible QCQP value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization QCQP, let \(v_{\mathrm{SDP}}\) be a valid semidefinite lower bound. If a recovered point \(\bar x\) satisfies every original constraint and its objective value obeys \(f(\bar x)=v_{\mathrm{SDP}}\), then \(\bar x\) is globally optimal and the relaxation is exact. With numerical tolerances, verified inequalities \(f(\bar x)-v_{\mathrm{SDP}}\le\varepsilon\) and original feasibility certify an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal point, provided the reported SDP value is itself a rigorously valid lower bound. Rank one is a common sufficient recovery diagnostic but is not required for equality of optimal values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible original point matching the rigorous SDP lower bound certifies global optimality and value exactness; a bounded gap certifies corresponding approximate optimality.

notation.meaning: Optimal values over the relaxed and rank-one lifted sets

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict nonexactness criterion for a compact rank relaxation of a minimization problem.

source_refs.locator: 2.14 Semidefinite Programming p. 81

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal R\) be a nonempty compact set of feasible rank-one lifts, and let \(\mathcal S\supseteq\mathcal R\) be a compact convex relaxation. For \(C\) in the same finite-dimensional inner-product space, define
\[
v_{\mathcal S}=\min_{Y\in\mathcal S}\langle C,Y\rangle,
\qquad
v_{\mathcal R}=\min_{Y\in\mathcal R}\langle C,Y\rangle,
\qquad
F=\operatorname*{argmin}_{Y\in\mathcal S}\langle C,Y\rangle.
\]
Then
\[
F\cap\mathcal R=\varnothing\quad\Longrightarrow\quad v_{\mathcal S}<v_{\mathcal R}.
\]
Equivalently, equality \(v_{\mathcal S}=v_{\mathcal R}\) implies \(F\cap\mathcal R\neq\varnothing\), although \(F\) may also contain higher-rank points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a compact lifted relaxation, absence of feasible rank-one lifts from its optimal face is equivalent to a strict relaxation-value gap; equality of attained values forces at least one feasible rank-one lift in that face.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonexact Lifted Faces

children.title: Quadratic Lagrangian Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Multiplier-based bounds for quadratic constraints and side relations.

assumptions_latex: The primal feasible set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(\lambda,\nu)\leq d^*\leq p^*\) for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\) and \(\nu\in\mathbb R^p\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier lower bound for an inequality- and equality-constrained quadratic minimization problem.

source_refs.locator: 5.2 Convex Programming and Duality p. 315
source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be quadratic for \(i=0,\ldots,m\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and let \(b\in\mathbb R^p\). Consider
\[
p^*=\inf\{q_0(x):q_i(x)\leq0\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,m,\ Ax=b\}.
\]
For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\) and \(\nu\in\mathbb R^p\), define
\[
L(x,\lambda,\nu)=q_0(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_iq_i(x)+\nu^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b),
\qquad
g(\lambda,\nu)=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}L(x,\lambda,\nu),
\]
and
\[
d^*=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m,\,\nu\in\mathbb R^p}g(\lambda,\nu).
\]
Weak duality gives \(g(\lambda,nu)\leq d^*\leq p^*\) for every admissible multiplier pair. Every pair for which \(g(\lambda,\nu)\) is finite therefore supplies a global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing quadratic inequalities and linear equalities yields an unconstrained quadratic subproblem whose infimum is a global lower bound; maximizing over the admissible multipliers gives the Lagrangian relaxation value.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Lagrangian Relaxations

source_witnesses.locator: 5.2 Convex Programming and Duality p. 315
source_witnesses.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Evaluation of a Quadratic Lagrangian
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form value and finiteness test for a fixed-multiplier quadratic subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Write the quadratic Lagrangian at fixed multipliers as
\[
L(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Hx+2h^{\mathsf T}x+c,
\qquad H\in\mathbb S^n.
\]
Then
\[
\inf_x L(x)=
\begin{cases}
c-h^{\mathsf T}H^\dagger h,&H\succeq0\text{ and }h\in\operatorname{Range}(H),\\
-\infty,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
When finite, its minimizers form \(-H^\dagger h+\ker H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic Lagrangian has a finite infimum exactly when its Hessian is positive semidefinite and its linear coefficient lies in the Hessian range; the pseudoinverse then gives its value and minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_xL(x)=c-h^{\mathsf T}H^\dagger h\) exactly when \(H\succeq0\) and \(h\in\operatorname{Range}(H)\); otherwise it equals \(-\infty\).

notation.meaning: Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of the aggregated Hessian
Null space of the aggregated Hessian

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong-Duality Boundary for Nonconvex Quadratic Lagrangian Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of the multiplier bound without an applicable exactness theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonconvex QCQP, weak duality always gives \(d^*\le p^*\), but primal feasibility and boundedness alone imply neither equality nor attainment of \(d^*\). Zero duality gap requires additional structure, such as convexity with an appropriate constraint qualification or a specialized exact quadratic certificate. Outside such regimes a positive Lagrangian duality gap or nonattainment may occur.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quadratic Lagrangian bound is always valid, but a generic nonconvex QCQP need not have zero gap or an attained best multiplier.
assumptions_latex: No convex constraint qualification or specialized exactness theorem is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only \(d^*\le p^*\) is guaranteed in general; equality and dual attainment require additional hypotheses.

assumptions_latex: The feasible region is the standard simplex \(\{x\in\mathbb R_+^n:e^{\mathsf T}x=1\}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact copositive dual representation of standard quadratic optimization on the simplex.

source_refs.locator: 2.13.3 Conic Programming p. 80

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(e=(1,\ldots,1)^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^n\). Define
\[
\operatorname{COP}_n=\{M\in\mathbb S^n:z^{\mathsf T}Mz\geq0\text{ for every }z\in\mathbb R_+^n\}.
\]
For the standard quadratic program
\[
p^*=\min\{x^{\mathsf T}Qx:e^{\mathsf T}x=1,\ x\in\mathbb R_+^n\},
\]
the exact copositive representation is
\[
p^*=\max\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:Q-\gamma ee^{\mathsf T}\in\operatorname{COP}_n\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing a quadratic form on the standard simplex equals maximizing a scalar whose associated shift of the quadratic matrix is copositive.
knowledge_statements.title: Copositive Reformulations

source_witnesses.locator: 2.13.3 Conic Programming p. 80

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent normalized membership and interior tests for the copositive cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(M\in\mathbb S^n\), homogeneity gives
\[
M\in\operatorname{COP}_n\iff \min\{x^{\mathsf T}Mx:x\geq0,\ e^{\mathsf T}x=1\}\geq0.
\]
Moreover, \(M\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{COP}_n)\) if and only if this minimum is strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Copositivity can be tested on the standard simplex, and strict positivity there characterizes the cone interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\in\operatorname{COP}_n\iff\min_{x\ge0,\ e^{\mathsf T}x=1}x^{\mathsf T}Mx\ge0\), with strict inequality characterizing \(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{COP}_n)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Simplex Characterization of Copositivity

source_refs.locator: 2.13.3 Conic Programming p. 80

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\), let \(e=(1,\ldots,1)^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^n\), and define
\[
\operatorname{CP}_n=\operatorname{cone}\{xx^{\mathsf T}:x\in\mathbb R_+^n\}.
\]
The standard quadratic program has the exact completely positive formulation
\[
\min\{x^{\mathsf T}Qx:e^{\mathsf T}x=1,\ x\in\mathbb R_+^n\}
=
\min\{\langle Q,X\rangle:\langle ee^{\mathsf T},X\rangle=1,\ X\in\operatorname{CP}_n\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic program on the standard simplex is exactly a linear conic program over the completely positive cone with one normalization constraint.

source_witnesses.locator: 2.13.3 Conic Programming p. 80

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of a simplex optimizer from a normalized completely positive factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\operatorname{CP}_n\) satisfy \(\langle ee^{\mathsf T},X\rangle=1\), and let \(X=\sum_{r=1}^Nz_rz_r^{\mathsf T}\) with \(z_r\ge0\). Put \(\alpha_r=e^{\mathsf T}z_r\) and, for \(\alpha_r>0\), \(x_r=z_r/\alpha_r\). Then \[X=\sum_{r:\alpha_r>0}\alpha_r^2x_rx_r^{\mathsf T},\qquad \sum_r\alpha_r^2=1,\qquad x_r\ge0,\ e^{\mathsf T}x_r=1.\] Therefore some \(x_r\) satisfies \(x_r^{\mathsf T}Qx_r\le\langle Q,X\rangle\); if \(X\) is optimal, such an \(x_r\) is an optimal simplex solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized completely positive factorization is a convex combination of simplex rank-one lifts and contains a simplex point no worse than its conic objective.
assumptions_latex: A finite nonnegative factorization of \(X\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists r:\ x_r\ge0,\ e^{\mathsf T}x_r=1,\quad x_r^{\mathsf T}Qx_r\le\langle Q,X\rangle.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative factor in a completely positive decomposition.

children.title: Cone-Duality Interface
children.top_down_role: Dual relationship connecting the two nonnegative matrix-cone views.

assumptions_latex: The ambient space is \(\mathbb S^n\) with the trace inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{CP}_n^*=\operatorname{COP}_n\), and the displayed completely positive primal and copositive dual have the same optimal value.

notation.meaning: Dual cone of K under the trace inner product

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trace-duality relation connecting completely positive primal models and copositive dual bounds for the standard quadratic program.

source_refs.locator: 2.13.3 Conic Programming p. 80
6. Duality in Global Optimization p. 167

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the trace inner product on \(\mathbb S^n\), the completely positive and copositive cones satisfy
\[
\operatorname{CP}_n^*=\operatorname{COP}_n.
\]
For \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(e=(1,\ldots,1)^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^n\), the conic dual pair associated with the standard quadratic program is
\[
\min\{\langle Q,X\rangle:\langle ee^{\mathsf T},X\rangle=1,\ X\in\operatorname{CP}_n\}
\]
and
\[
\max\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:Q-\gamma ee^{\mathsf T}\in\operatorname{COP}_n\}.
\]
Weak duality holds for this pair, and both displayed optimal values equal the minimum of \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx\) over \(\{x\in\mathbb R_+^n:e^{\mathsf T}x=1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The copositive cone is dual to the completely positive cone, and the corresponding lifted primal and scalar copositive dual both represent the standard quadratic-program value.
knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Duality Interface

source_witnesses.locator: 2.13.3 Conic Programming p. 80
6. Duality in Global Optimization p. 167

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual certificate for standard quadratic optimization on the simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\ge0\), \(e^{\mathsf T}x=1\), and let \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\) satisfy \(S:=Q-\gamma ee^{\mathsf T}\in\operatorname{COP}_n\). Then \[x^{\mathsf T}Qx-\gamma=x^{\mathsf T}Sx\ge0.\] Thus \(\gamma\) is a global lower bound. If \(x^{\mathsf T}Sx=0\), then \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx=\gamma\) and \(x\) is globally optimal. For a normalized completely positive primal point \(X\), \(\langle S,X\rangle=0\) is the corresponding complementary zero-gap condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A copositive slack certifies a global lower bound; equality with a feasible simplex point or normalized CP lift certifies global optimality.
assumptions_latex: For the lifted condition, \(X\in\operatorname{CP}_n\) and \(\langle ee^{\mathsf T},X\rangle=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \gamma\le p^*,\qquad x^{\mathsf T}Sx=0\Longrightarrow x^{\mathsf T}Qx=p^*=\gamma.
knowledge_statements.title: Copositive Lower-Bound and Zero-Gap Certificate

children.title: Exact-Conic Representation Boundary
children.top_down_role: Modeling regimes controlling availability or usefulness of exact cone representations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complexity Barrier to Tractable Exact Copositive Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computational boundary for treating exact copositive membership as a tractable primitive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Deciding whether a rational symmetric matrix \(M\) is copositive is co-NP-complete when the dimension is part of the input. Consequently, a polynomial-time exact membership algorithm for \(\operatorname{COP}_n\) in variable dimension would imply \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\). Thus an exact copositive reformulation preserves mathematical equivalence but does not generically produce a polynomial-time conic method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact copositive reformulations are generally intractable because rational copositivity testing is co-NP-complete.
assumptions_latex: The matrix dimension is part of the input.
Matrix entries are rational and binary encoded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact \(\operatorname{COP}_n\)-membership is co-NP-complete in variable dimension; a generic polynomial-time membership algorithm would imply \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Complexity Barrier to Tractable Exact Copositive Models

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Explicit Order-Five DNN Matrix Outside the Completely Positive Cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete witness in the first dimension where DNN strictly contains CP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A(C_5)\) be the adjacency matrix of the chordless five-cycle and let \(\alpha=(\sqrt5-1)/2\). Then \[X=I_5+\alpha A(C_5)\] is positive semidefinite and entrywise nonnegative, but is not completely positive. Hence \(X\in\operatorname{DNN}_5\setminus\operatorname{CP}_5\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identity plus the reciprocal golden ratio times the five-cycle adjacency matrix is doubly nonnegative but not completely positive.
assumptions_latex: \(A(C_5)\) is the adjacency matrix of the chordless five-cycle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\in\operatorname{DNN}_5\setminus\operatorname{CP}_5\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual cone induced by the doubly nonnegative outer approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbb N_n\) be the cone of entrywise nonnegative symmetric matrices and \(\operatorname{SPN}_n=\mathbb S_+^n+\mathbb N_n\). Under the trace inner product, \[\operatorname{DNN}_n^*=\operatorname{SPN}_n.\] Since \(\operatorname{CP}_n\subseteq\operatorname{DNN}_n\), dual inclusion gives \[\operatorname{SPN}_n\subseteq\operatorname{COP}_n.\] Thus a DNN outer relaxation of a completely positive primal model corresponds to restricting copositive dual certificates to PSD-plus-nonnegative matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual of the doubly nonnegative cone is the PSD-plus-nonnegative cone, an inner approximation of the copositive cone.
assumptions_latex: All cones lie in the finite-dimensional space of real symmetric matrices with the trace inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{DNN}_n^*=\operatorname{SPN}_n\subseteq\operatorname{COP}_n\).
knowledge_statements.title: DNN–SPN Surrogate Duality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp dimension threshold for replacing complete positivity by double nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\operatorname{DNN}_n=\mathbb S_+^n\cap\mathbb R_+^{n\times n}\), \[\operatorname{CP}_n=\operatorname{DNN}_n\quad(n\le4),\qquad \operatorname{CP}_n\subsetneq\operatorname{DNN}_n\quad(n\ge5).\] Thus the DNN replacement is universally exact through order four and is only an outer relaxation from order five onward.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete positivity equals positive semidefiniteness plus entrywise nonnegativity through dimension four, with strict containment beginning in dimension five.
assumptions_latex: Entrywise inequalities use the standard nonnegative orthant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{CP}_n=\operatorname{DNN}_n\) exactly for \(n\le4\).
knowledge_statements.title: Sharp CP–DNN Dimension Boundary
Exact-Conic Representation Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp dimension boundary for replacing complete positivity by double nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the doubly nonnegative cone by \(\operatorname{DNN}_n=\mathbb S_+^n\cap\mathbb R_+^{n\times n}\). Then
\[
\operatorname{CP}_n=\operatorname{DNN}_n\quad\text{for }n\leq4,
\qquad
\operatorname{CP}_n\subsetneq\operatorname{DNN}_n\quad\text{for }n\geq5.
\]
Hence replacing \(X\in\operatorname{CP}_n\) by the tractable constraints \(X\succeq0\) and \(X\geq0\) preserves every completely positive linear optimization model in dimensions at most four. From dimension five onward the replacement is only an outer relaxation and can yield a strictly smaller value in minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete positivity equals positive semidefiniteness plus entrywise nonnegativity through dimension four, but the latter cone becomes strictly larger from dimension five onward.
assumptions_latex: Entrywise inequalities use the standard nonnegative orthant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{CP}_n=\operatorname{DNN}_n\) iff \(n\leq4\); universal DNN exactness fails for \(n\geq5\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dimension boundary is a specialized nontrivial theorem and the failure-boundary kind is appropriate, but the record supplies no source. An authoritative locator supporting both equality for n at most 4 and strict inclusion for n at least 5 is required.

children.title: Tractable Copositive-Cone Approximations
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral and semidefinite approximations to exact but difficult conic models.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SOS Inner Hierarchy for the Copositive Cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested semidefinite sufficient conditions for copositivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(M\in\mathbb S^n\), define
\[
p_M(y)=\sum_{i,j=1}^n M_{ij}y_i^2y_j^2.
\]
For \(r\in\mathbb Z_+\), let
\[
\mathcal K_n^{(r)}=\left\{M:\left(\sum_{i=1}^ny_i^2\right)^r p_M(y)\text{ is a sum of squares}\right\}.
\]
Then
\[
\mathcal K_n^{(0)}\subseteq\mathcal K_n^{(1)}\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\operatorname{COP}_n.
\]
Every fixed level is semidefinite representable, and every strictly copositive matrix belongs to some level. Thus
\[
\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{COP}_n)\subseteq\bigcup_{r\ge0}\mathcal K_n^{(r)}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increasing-degree SOS tests give nested SDP-representable inner approximations that eventually contain every strictly copositive matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal K_n^{(r)}\subseteq\mathcal K_n^{(r+1)}\subseteq\operatorname{COP}_n\) and \(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{COP}_n)\subseteq\bigcup_r\mathcal K_n^{(r)}\).

notation.meaning: Level-r SOS inner approximation of the copositive cone

knowledge_statements.title: SOS Inner Hierarchy for the Copositive Cone

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SOS Copositivity Level Size and Boundary Limitation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense Gram-matrix growth and the distinction between interior capture and boundary finite convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At level \(r\), \((\sum_i y_i^2)^r p_M(y)\) has degree \(2r+4\) and admits a homogeneous Gram representation over monomials of degree \(r+2\). The direct dense formulation therefore uses a positive-semidefinite matrix of order \(N_{n,r}=\binom{n+r+1}{r+2}\), with coefficient-matching equations indexed by at most \(\binom{n+2r+3}{2r+4}\) monomials. These quantities are polynomial in \(n\) for fixed \(r\) but grow combinatorially with the level. Interior finite capture does not imply finite-level capture of every boundary matrix in \(\operatorname{COP}_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dense SOS hierarchy has rapidly growing Gram matrices; it finitely captures every strictly copositive matrix but has no universal finite-level guarantee on the cone boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{n,r}=\binom{n+r+1}{r+2}\), and \(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{COP}_n)\subseteq\bigcup_r\mathcal K_n^{(r)}\) does not imply \(\operatorname{COP}_n=\bigcup_r\mathcal K_n^{(r)}\).

notation.meaning: Order of the direct homogeneous SOS Gram matrix.

review_flags: Counts describe the direct dense homogeneous Gram formulation; sparsity or symmetry can reduce size.
knowledge_statements.title: SOS Copositivity Level Size and Boundary Limitation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mesh-refined polyhedral sufficient conditions for copositivity on the simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal T\) be a finite simplicial partition of \(\Delta_{n-1}\), and define \(\mathcal P(\mathcal T)=\{M\in\mathbb S^n:u^{\mathsf T}Mv\ge0\text{ for every pair of vertices }u,v\text{ of every }S\in\mathcal T\}\). Then \(\mathcal P(\mathcal T)\) is a polyhedral cone contained in \(\operatorname{COP}_n\). If \(\mathcal T'\) refines \(\mathcal T\), then \(\mathcal P(\mathcal T)\subseteq\mathcal P(\mathcal T')\). Along partitions whose mesh tends to zero, every strictly copositive matrix belongs to all sufficiently fine approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative bilinear products between vertices of each simplex define nested polyhedral inner approximations that eventually capture every strictly copositive matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal T\) is a finite simplicial partition of \(\Delta_{n-1}\).
The maximum simplex diameter tends to zero along the refinement sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P(\mathcal T)\subseteq\operatorname{COP}_n\), and \(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{COP}_n)\subseteq\bigcup_{\mathcal T}\mathcal P(\mathcal T)\) along mesh-refining partitions.

notation.meaning: Polyhedral inner approximation defined by simplex-vertex pairs.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplicial Polyhedral Inner Approximations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Level-by-level use of tractable inner approximations of a copositive dual cone to obtain certified lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a conic minimization problem whose exact lower-bounding dual is \[v^*=\sup\{b^{\mathsf T}y:C-\mathcal A^*y\in\operatorname{COP}_n\}.\] Let \(\mathcal K_n^{(0)}\subseteq\mathcal K_n^{(1)}\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\operatorname{COP}_n\) be SDP-representable inner approximations. At level \(r\), solve \[d_r=\sup\{b^{\mathsf T}y:C-\mathcal A^*y\in\mathcal K_n^{(r)}\}.\] Every verified feasible \(y_r\) certifies \(b^{\mathsf T}y_r\le v^*\), and \(d_r\le d_{r+1}\le v^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successive SDP-representable inner approximations of the copositive dual cone produce monotone lower bounds when cone feasibility and objective values are rigorously verified.
assumptions_latex: The displayed copositive dual exactly represents, or is a valid lower-bounding dual for, the original minimization problem.
Reported cone feasibility and objective values are rigorously verified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_r\le d_{r+1}\le v^*\), and each verified level-\(r\) feasible point supplies a valid lower bound.

notation.meaning: Adjoint of the linear conic constraint map.
Optimal lower bound at hierarchy level r.

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Copositive Inner-Hierarchy Bounding Procedure
Tractable Copositive-Cone Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semidefinite inner and outer approximations for the copositive–completely-positive cone pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathbb N^n\) denote the cone of entrywise nonnegative symmetric matrices. The tractable inclusions
\[
\operatorname{CP}_n\subseteq\operatorname{DNN}_n:=\mathbb S_+^n\cap\mathbb N^n,
\qquad
\mathbb S_+^n+\mathbb N^n=\operatorname{DNN}_n^*\subseteq\operatorname{COP}_n
\]
produce paired semidefinite relaxations. For a completely positive minimization model, replacing \(\operatorname{CP}_n\) by \(\operatorname{DNN}_n\) gives a lower bound. Equivalently, restricting its copositive dual slack to \(\mathbb S_+^n+\mathbb N^n\) gives a tractable dual bound. Tighter nested cone approximations yield monotonically stronger bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Doubly nonnegative outer approximations and positive-semidefinite-plus-nonnegative inner approximations form a tractable dual pair that supplies lower bounds for completely positive minimization.
assumptions_latex: The primal problem is a minimization over \(\operatorname{CP}_n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{CP}_n\subseteq\operatorname{DNN}_n\) and \(\operatorname{DNN}_n^*=\mathbb S_+^n+\mathbb N^n\subseteq\operatorname{COP}_n\).

source_refs.locator: 2.14 Semidefinite Programming p. 81

children.title: Relaxation Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural causes of weak, unstable, or unrealizable relaxation solutions.

children.title: Large Relaxation Gaps
children.top_down_role: Weak convex or conic approximations relative to the original quadratic geometry.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-variable family with an unbounded additive gap for the basic bilinear McCormick relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M>0\), consider \[p_M=\min\{-xy:x+y=0,\ -M\le x,y\le M\}.\] Its optimal value is \(p_M=0\). If \(w=xy\) is replaced solely by the four McCormick inequalities on \([-M,M]^2\), the relaxed optimal value is \(p_M^{\mathrm{Mc}}=-M^2\). Consequently, \[p_M-p_M^{\mathrm{Mc}}=M^2\to\infty.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-variable equality-constrained quadratic has value zero, while its basic McCormick relaxation has value minus M squared, producing an unbounded additive gap.
assumptions_latex: \text{the equality }w=xy\text{ is replaced only by its four box McCormick inequalities}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_M-p_M^{\mathrm{Mc}}=M^2\to\infty
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratically Growing McCormick Gap
Large Relaxation Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A two-variable McCormick relaxation whose additive gap grows quadratically with domain radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(M>0\), consider
\[
p_M=\min\{-xy:x+y=0,\ -M\leq x,y\leq M\}.
\]
Since \(y=-x\), the original objective is \(x^2\), so \(p_M=0\). Introduce \(w\) for \(xy\) and impose the four McCormick inequalities over \([-M,M]^2\). The point \((x,y,w)=(0,0,M^2)\) satisfies those inequalities and \(x+y=0\); moreover they imply \(w\leq M^2\). Therefore the relaxed minimum of \(-w\) is \(-M^2\), and the additive lower-bound gap equals \(M^2\), becoming arbitrarily large as \(M\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bilinear McCormick relaxation can have gap M squared: the original constrained problem has value zero while its relaxation has value minus M squared.
assumptions_latex: The bilinear equality \(w=xy\) is replaced only by its four box McCormick inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_M-p_M^{\mathrm{Mc}}=M^2\to\infty\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The constructed McCormick example is mathematically plausible and the counterexample kind fits the leaf, but it has no citation and its statement contains a derivation. A source or independently inspectable verifier record is required before the mathematical version can be accepted.

children.title: Domain-Scaling Sensitivity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Deterioration of envelopes and conditioning under loose or poorly scaled bounds.

children.title: Domain Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Dependence of relaxation strength on domain width or bounding geometry.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Weakening on a Larger Interval
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal family showing that convex-envelope domain antitonicity can be strict.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<a<b\), let \(f(x)=-x^2\), \(K_1=[-a,a]\), and \(K_2=[-b,b]\). Then \[\operatorname{vex}_{K_1}f(x)=-a^2,\qquad \operatorname{vex}_{K_2}f(x)=-b^2\quad(x\in K_1),\] so the envelope obtained on the larger domain is strictly weaker throughout \(K_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the concave quadratic minus x squared, enlarging a symmetric interval from radius a to radius b strictly lowers the convex envelope on the entire smaller interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{vex}_{[-b,b]}(-x^2)<\operatorname{vex}_{[-a,a]}(-x^2)\text{ on }[-a,a]
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Weakening on a Larger Interval

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise dependence of the convex envelope on nested compact construction domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_1\subseteq K_2\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty compact convex sets and let \(f:K_2\to\mathbb R\) be continuous. If \(\operatorname{vex}_K f\) denotes the greatest convex underestimator of \(f\) on \(K\), then \[\operatorname{vex}_{K_2}f(x)\le \operatorname{vex}_{K_1}f(x)\le f(x)\qquad(x\in K_1).\] Hence enlarging the construction domain cannot strengthen the convex envelope on the retained domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuous function on nested compact convex domains, the convex envelope constructed on the larger domain is no stronger when restricted to the smaller domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{vex}_{K_2}f|_{K_1}\le\operatorname{vex}_{K_1}f\le f|_{K_1}

notation.meaning: convex envelope of f on K

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Envelope Antitonicity Under Domain Enlargement
Domain Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic dependence of convex-envelope lower bounds on the chosen relaxation domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K_1\subseteq K_2\subset\mathbb R^n\) be compact convex sets and let \(f:K_2\to\mathbb R\). Write \(\operatorname{vex}_{K}f\) for the greatest convex function on \(K\) that does not exceed \(f\). Then, for every \(x\in K_1\),
\[
\operatorname{vex}_{K_2}f(x)\leq\operatorname{vex}_{K_1}f(x)\leq f(x).
\]
Thus enlarging the domain used to construct a convex underestimator cannot strengthen its pointwise lower bound on the original smaller domain. Equality need not hold, so domain selection can change relaxation quality even when the optimization points of interest remain in \(K_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex envelope built on a larger domain is no greater on a nested smaller domain, so enlarging bounds can only weaken this pointwise underestimator.
assumptions_latex: \(K_1\subseteq K_2\) are nonempty compact convex sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{vex}_{K_2}f|_{K_1}\leq\operatorname{vex}_{K_1}f\leq f|_{K_1}\).

notation.meaning: Convex envelope of f over K

children.title: Scaling Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Dependence of relaxation quality plus conditioning on variable or constraint scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine invariance of exact lifted models and the source of scaling-dependent implementations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular and substitute \(x=Dz\) in a quadratic program. Under the lifted correspondence \(X=DZD^{\mathsf T}\), rank-one identities are preserved because \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) if and only if \(Z=zz^{\mathsf T}\). Moreover,
\[
\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}
=
\operatorname{diag}(1,D)
\begin{pmatrix}1&z^{\mathsf T}\\z&Z\end{pmatrix}
\operatorname{diag}(1,D)^{\mathsf T},
\]
so positive semidefiniteness is preserved. Hence an exactly transformed lifted conic relaxation has the same optimal value and rank-exactness status. Scaling sensitivity arises when bounds, approximation cones, tolerances, or coefficients are not transformed equivariantly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonsingular variable scaling preserves exact lifted values and rank conditions under congruent transformation; observed scaling sensitivity comes from non-equivariant approximations or numerical conventions.
assumptions_latex: Every objective, constraint, and lifted variable is transformed consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact congruent scaling preserves feasibility, optimal value, and rank-one recoverability.

notation.meaning: Lifted matrices before and after scaling

children.title: Loose-Bound Deterioration
children.top_down_role: Loss of envelope strength under weak variable bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact maximum vertical width of the four-facet bilinear McCormick relaxation under finite bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(w=xy\) on \([\ell_x,u_x]\times[\ell_y,u_y]\), let \(w_L\) be the maximum of the two McCormick lower planes and \(w_U\) the minimum of the two upper planes. Then \[\max_{(x,y)}\bigl(w_U(x,y)-w_L(x,y)\bigr)=\frac{(u_x-\ell_x)(u_y-\ell_y)}{2},\] attained at the rectangle center. Thus the maximum vertical relaxation width grows linearly in either factor width and quadratically under a common dilation of both widths.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum vertical width of a four-facet bilinear McCormick relaxation is half the product of the two factor-bound widths and is attained at the box center.
assumptions_latex: \text{only the four standard McCormick inequalities constrain }w
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max(w_U-w_L)=\tfrac12(u_x-\ell_x)(u_y-\ell_y)
knowledge_statements.title: Exact McCormick Width Deterioration
Loose-Bound Deterioration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact dependence of McCormick-envelope width on bilinear variable-bound widths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(w=xy\) on the rectangle \([\ell_x,u_x]\times[\ell_y,u_y]\), let \(w_L(x,y)\) be the maximum of the two McCormick lower planes and \(w_U(x,y)\) the minimum of the two upper planes. Then
\[
\max_{(x,y)}\bigl(w_U(x,y)-w_L(x,y)\bigr)
=\frac{(u_x-\ell_x)(u_y-\ell_y)}{2}.
\]
The maximum is attained at the rectangle center. Consequently, doubling either bound width doubles the largest permitted vertical discrepancy, while doubling both widths multiplies it by four. Loose variable bounds therefore directly deteriorate bilinear relaxation strength.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum vertical width of a bilinear McCormick relaxation equals half the product of the two variable-bound widths, quantifying deterioration from loose bounds.
assumptions_latex: Only the four standard McCormick inequalities describe the lifted bilinear term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max(w_U-w_L)=\tfrac12(u_x-\ell_x)(u_y-\ell_y)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact maximum-width formula is a nontrivial quantitative claim and the property kind fits, but no source or inspectable verifier evidence is supplied. A specific authoritative locator is required.

children.title: Conditioning Degradation
children.top_down_role: Numerical fragility induced by poorly balanced model scales.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning Degradation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent diagonal scaling can make a quadratic Hessian arbitrarily ill-conditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the positive-definite quadratic \(f(x)=x^{\mathsf T}x\) and the nonsingular change of variables \(x=D_sz\), where \(D_s=\operatorname{diag}(1,s)\) and \(s\geq1\). In the new variables,
\[
f(D_sz)=z^{\mathsf T}D_s^{\mathsf T}D_sz=z_1^2+s^2z_2^2,
\qquad
\kappa_2(D_s^{\mathsf T}D_s)=s^2.
\]
Thus mathematically equivalent quadratic programs can have arbitrarily different Hessian condition numbers as \(s\to\infty\). Finite-precision linear algebra, feasibility tests, and stopping rules may consequently degrade even though an exactly transformed conic or lifted formulation retains the same optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A diagonal change of variables leaves the optimization problem equivalent but can increase the Hessian condition number to s squared, causing arbitrarily severe numerical degradation.
assumptions_latex: Conditioning is measured by the spectral condition number.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(D_s^{\mathsf T}D_s)=s^2\to\infty\) as \(s\to\infty\).

children.title: Lifted Realizability Failures
children.top_down_role: Lifted relaxation points that do not represent realizable quadratic products.

children.title: Lifted Rank Loss
children.top_down_role: Relaxation solutions whose matrix rank prevents direct quadratic recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Rank Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a first-order semidefinite lift to represent one original quadratic point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(X\in\mathbb S^n\), and \(Y=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\). The lifted pair is realizable by the original quadratic products precisely when \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\), equivalently \(Y=(1,x^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}(1,x^{\mathsf T})\) and \(\operatorname{rank}Y=1\). Hence any feasible relaxed point with \(\operatorname{rank}Y>1\) has lost lifted realizability: it may yield a valid relaxation bound, but it cannot be interpreted as a single feasible original point without a rank-recovery step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite lifted solution represents one original point exactly only at rank one; higher rank is a relaxation artifact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\iff\operatorname{rank}Y=1\); thus \(\operatorname{rank}Y>1\) certifies rank loss.

notation.meaning: lifted matrix intended to equal the quadratic product matrix

source_refs.locator: 5. Approximation Algorithms in Quadratic Programming p. 38

children.title: Product-Consistency Loss
children.top_down_role: Lifted product values lacking joint consistency with original variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Product-Consistency Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Entrywise failure of lifted variables to equal the products they replace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and a symmetric lifted matrix \(X\), define the product residuals by \(r_{ij}=X_{ij}-x_i x_j\) for \(1\le i\le j\le n\). The lift is product-consistent exactly when every residual vanishes. If \(r_{ij}\ne0\) for at least one pair, evaluation of a quadratic coefficient multiplying \(X_{ij}\) need not agree with evaluation at \(x\); consequently the relaxed objective or constraints describe a point outside the graph of the quadratic product map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lifted variables lose product consistency whenever some matrix entry differs from the corresponding product of original variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,X)\) is product-consistent iff \(X_{ij}=x_i x_j\) for all \(i,j\).
