source_witnesses.locator: 5. Approximation Algorithms in Quadratic Programming p. 38

children.title: Quadratic Realizability Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Structural checks for whether lifted values represent an original-space quadratic point.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Realizability Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual and spectral tests for deciding whether a lifted point represents one quadratic point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(X\in\mathbb S^n\), form \(D=X-xx^{\mathsf T}\). Exact quadratic realizability holds if and only if \(D=0\). If the homogenized matrix \(Y=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\) is positive semidefinite, its Schur complement gives \(D\succeq0\); in that case any one of \(\operatorname{tr}D=0\), \(\lVert D\rVert_{\mathrm F}=0\), or \(\lambda_{\max}(D)=0\) is an equivalent, directly checkable certificate of realizability. Positive values quantify nonrealizability rather than prove feasibility of an original point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtract the outer product from the lifted matrix; zero residual certifies exact realizability, while a positive residual diagnoses relaxation slack.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D=0\iff X=xx^{\mathsf T}\); under \(D\succeq0\), this is equivalent to \(\operatorname{tr}D=0\).

source_refs.locator: 5. Approximation Algorithms in Quadratic Programming p. 38

children.title: Rank-Product Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Cases where favorable rank evidence conflicts with product-level consistency, or conversely.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank-One Product Block Can Still Be Inconsistent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample to using rank one of the product block X as a surrogate for rank one of the full normalized moment matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\ge2\), choose a nonzero \(u\in[-1,1]^n\), and set \(x=0\), \(X=uu^{\mathsf T}\). Then \(X\succeq0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}X=1\), while \(Y=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&uu^{\mathsf T}\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\) has rank two. Moreover \(X\ne xx^{\mathsf T}=0\), although the usual diagonal box bounds \(X_{ii}\le1\) hold. Thus rank one of \(X\) is not a product-consistency certificate for the inhomogeneous lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-one lifted product block can satisfy PSD and box bounds while the full moment matrix has rank two and the products are inconsistent with the first moments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}X=1\) but \(\operatorname{rank}Y=2\) and \(X\ne xx^{\mathsf T}\).

notation.meaning: nonzero vector generating the rank-one product block

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-One Product Block Can Still Be Inconsistent

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact compatibility relation showing that genuine disagreement is impossible when both tests use the full normalized lift and all product equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(X\in\mathbb S^n\), \(Y=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\), and \(D=X-xx^{\mathsf T}\), one has \(\operatorname{rank}Y=1+\operatorname{rank}D\). Hence \(\operatorname{rank}Y=1\) if and only if \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\). Exact full-moment rank evidence therefore cannot conflict with complete product consistency; apparent conflict must arise from testing \(X\) rather than \(Y\), checking only selected products, using numerical tolerances, or changing the normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full normalized moment rank and complete product consistency agree exactly; mismatches arise only from partial, surrogate, numerical, or differently normalized evidence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}Y=1+\operatorname{rank}(X-xx^{\mathsf T})\), so \(\operatorname{rank}Y=1\iff X=xx^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Full-Moment Rank–Product Compatibility
Rank-Product Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete semidefinite-feasible lift that has neither rank one nor correct products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On the box \([-1,1]^n\) with \(n\ge1\), take \(x=0\) and \(X=I_n\). Then \(Y=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&I_n\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\), and the usual diagonal bounds \(X_{ii}\le1\) hold. Nevertheless \(xx^{\mathsf T}=0\ne I_n=X\), while \(\operatorname{rank}Y=n+1\). Thus positive semidefiniteness and elementary box-derived bounds do not force either rank-one structure or product consistency; the relaxed point cannot be generated by any single original vector having first moment \(x=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lifted point with zero vector and identity product matrix satisfies basic semidefinite and box bounds but is not quadratically realizable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y\succeq0\) but \(X\ne xx^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\operatorname{rank}Y=n+1\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is algebraically correct and the content kind fits, but the record supplies no evidence reference or explicit standard-field rationale for this nontrivial claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Extreme-Point Ranking Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite vertex-ranking scheme for minimizing a concave quadratic over a bounded polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty compact polytope, let \(q:P\to\mathbb R\) be a concave quadratic, and let \(V(P)\) be the finite vertex set of \(P\). Maintain an incumbent value \(U\), a set \(R\subseteq V(P)\) of unprocessed vertices, and a priority key \(\rho:R\to\mathbb R\). Repeatedly select a vertex of highest priority and evaluate its objective value, updating \(U\). A subset \(D\subseteq R\) may be discarded only when a certified bound \(b(D)\le\min_{v\in D}q(v)\) satisfies \(b(D)\ge U\). Stop after every vertex has been evaluated or validly discarded. Since a concave function attains its minimum over a compact polytope at a vertex, the final incumbent is a global minimum of \(q\) over \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank and evaluate the vertices of the polytope, discarding a group only when a valid lower bound proves that none of its vertices can improve the incumbent; the final incumbent is globally optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty compact polytope.
Every discarded subset \(D\) has a certified bound \(b(D)\le\min_{v\in D}q(v)\) with \(b(D)\ge U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned vertex \(v^*\in V(P)\) satisfies \(q(v^*)=\min_{x\in P}q(x)\).

notation.meaning: finite vertex set of the polytope
priority key on the unprocessed vertices
certified lower bound on the objective values of vertices in D

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Output-size boundary for extreme-point ranking without effective subset pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An extreme-point ranking method that has no valid discard certificate for any unevaluated vertex must evaluate every vertex of \(P\) before certifying the minimum. Thus its number of objective evaluations is \(|V(P)|\). For \(P=[0,1]^n\), \(|V(P)|=2^n\), so exhaustive ranking can require exponentially many evaluations in the dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without effective pruning, vertex ranking degenerates to enumeration and can require exponentially many evaluations.
assumptions_latex: Optimality is certified only by evaluating a vertex or discarding it through a valid bound.
No unevaluated vertex can be validly discarded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{eval}}=|V(P)|,\qquad N_{\mathrm{eval}}=2^n\text{ for }P=[0,1]^n.

children.title: Concave-QP Cutting-Plane Methods

knowledge_statements.title: Concave-QP Cutting-Plane Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-approximation cutting-plane scheme for a concave quadratic on a compact polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a compact polytope \(P\), a concave quadratic \(q\), tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), and an initial polyhedral underestimator \(m_0\le q\) on \(P\). At iteration \(k\), solve \(L_k=\min_{x\in P}m_k(x)\), evaluate a minimizer \(x^k\), and update the incumbent \(U_k\) using \(q(x^k)\). If \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\), return the incumbent. Otherwise obtain a valid affine or piecewise-affine cut that remains below \(q\) and raises the model near \(x^k\), define \(m_{k+1}\) as the maximum of the old model and the new cut, and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly strengthen a polyhedral lower model of the concave quadratic until its lower bound meets the incumbent within tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Every generated cut is a valid global underestimator on \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, the returned \(\bar x\in P\) satisfies \(q(\bar x)-\min_{x\in P}q(x)\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: current lower and incumbent upper bounds

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Concave Tangents Are Invalid Lower Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direction-of-support boundary for lower-approximation cutting-plane methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For differentiable concave q and x^k\in P, q(x)\le q(x^k)+\nabla q(x^k)^\top(x-x^k) for every x\in P. The tangent is therefore a global overestimator, not a valid lower cut, unless it coincides with q on P. Lower approximation requires certified underestimators such as valid secants or localized convex-envelope pieces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tangents to a concave quadratic lie above it and ordinarily cannot serve as lower-bounding cuts.
assumptions_latex: q\text{ is differentiable and concave on }P
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q(x)\le q(x^k)+\nabla q(x^k)^\top(x-x^k)\quad\forall x\in P.
knowledge_statements.title: Concave Tangents Are Invalid Lower Cuts

knowledge_statements.title: Concave-QP Partition Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-and-bound partition algorithm using cellwise lower envelopes of a concave quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a compact polytope \(P\), concave quadratic \(q\), tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), and an initial finite partition \(\mathcal P_0\). For every cell \(C\), compute a valid lower bound \(L(C)\) and a feasible sample value. Maintain the best sample value \(U\). Select a cell with smallest \(L(C)\); discard it if \(L(C)\ge U-\varepsilon\), otherwise split it into finitely many smaller cells, compute their bounds and samples, and update \(U\). Stop when no active cell has lower bound below \(U-\varepsilon\), returning the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition the feasible region, refine the cell with the best lower bound, and prune cells unable to improve the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: Along every infinite refinement chain, cell diameters tend to zero and bound gaps vanish.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned \(\bar x\in P\) satisfies \(q(\bar x)-\min_{x\in P}q(x)\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: valid lower bound on cell C

knowledge_statements.title: Localized Concave-QP Envelopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex envelope of a concave quadratic restricted to a simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_n\}\) be an \(n\)-simplex and let \(q:S\to\mathbb R\) be concave. Every \(x\in S\) has unique barycentric coordinates \(\lambda_i(x)\ge0\) with \(\sum_{i=0}^n\lambda_i(x)=1\). The convex envelope of \(q\) on \(S\) is the affine vertex interpolant
\[\operatorname{vex}_S q(x)=\sum_{i=0}^n\lambda_i(x)q(v_i).\]
Thus minimizing this localized envelope over any polyhedral subset of \(S\) is a linear program and supplies a valid lower bound for minimizing \(q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a simplex, the convex envelope of a concave quadratic is the affine function interpolating its vertex values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{vex}_S q(x)=\sum_{i=0}^n\lambda_i(x)q(v_i)\le q(x)\) for every \(x\in S\).

notation.meaning: barycentric coordinate of x at vertex i
convex envelope of q over S

source_witnesses.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polytope Vertex-Lifting Formula for the Convex Envelope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact localized convex envelope of a concave quadratic on a polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let P=\operatorname{conv}(V) be a compact polytope with finite vertex set V, and let q be concave on P. Then \operatorname{vex}_Pq(x)=\min\{\sum_{v\in V}\lambda_vq(v):\sum_{v\in V}\lambda_vv=x,\ \sum_{v\in V}\lambda_v=1,\ \lambda_v\ge0\}. Equivalently, its graph is the lower convex hull induced by the lifted vertex values (v,q(v)). The formula is a linear program in \lambda and reduces to affine vertex interpolation on a simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a polytope, the convex envelope of a concave quadratic is obtained from the lower convex hull of its lifted vertex values.
assumptions_latex: P=\operatorname{conv}(V)\text{ is a nonempty compact polytope}
q\text{ is concave and finite on }P
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{vex}_Pq(x)=\min_{\lambda\ge0}\left\{\sum_{v\in V}\lambda_vq(v):\sum_v\lambda_vv=x,\ \sum_v\lambda_v=1\right\}.

notation.meaning: finite vertex set of the polytope
convex-combination weight assigned to vertex v
convex envelope of q over P

children.title: Partition-Envelope Coupling
children.top_down_role: Dependence of local bound strength on partition geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Envelope Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic strengthening obtained by recomputing concave envelopes after partition refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal P\) be a finite partition of compact \(P\), and on each cell \(C\in\mathcal P\) let \(e_C\le q\) be the convex envelope of a concave quadratic restricted to \(C\). Define \(L(\mathcal P)=\min_{C\in\mathcal P}\min_{x\in C}e_C(x)\). If \(\mathcal P'\) refines \(\mathcal P\) and exact cell envelopes are recomputed, restriction of every coarse envelope remains a valid underestimator on each child. Therefore
\[L(\mathcal P)\le L(\mathcal P')\le\min_{x\in P}q(x).\]
The global lower bound is consequently monotone under refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recomputing exact cell envelopes after refinement can only raise the global lower bound, never invalidate it.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is compact and \(\mathcal P'\) is a finite refinement of \(\mathcal P\).
Each cell model is the exact convex envelope of \(q\) on that cell.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(\mathcal P)\le L(\mathcal P')\le\min_{x\in P}q(x)\).

notation.meaning: localized convex envelope on cell C

source_refs.locator: 2.4.2 Convergence of Multivariate Rectangular Partition Methods p. 97

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4.2 Convergence of Multivariate Rectangular Partition Methods p. 97

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Cell Envelopes Make the Scalar Bound Partition-Independent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness boundary for the scalar partition bound defined in the seed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every nonempty cell \(C\), let \(e_C=\operatorname{conv}_C q\) be the exact convex envelope of \(q\) on \(C\). Since the constant function \(\min_{x\in C}q(x)\) is a convex underestimator and \(e_C\le q\), one has \[\min_{x\in C}e_C(x)=\min_{x\in C}q(x).\] Consequently, for every finite partition \(\mathcal P\) of \(P\), \[L(\mathcal P)=\min_{C\in\mathcal P}\min_{x\in C}e_C(x)=\min_{x\in P}q(x).\] Thus the seed's monotonicity inequalities hold with equality throughout; nontrivial strengthening requires an inexact envelope, additional relaxation variables, or a relaxation domain differing from the set over which the envelope minimum is taken.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With exact cell envelopes minimized over the same cells, the partition lower bound already equals the true minimum and cannot improve under refinement.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\) is a finite partition of \(P\) into nonempty cells.
\(e_C\) is the exact convex envelope of \(q\) on each cell \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L(\mathcal P)=\min_{x\in P}q(x)\text{ for every }\mathcal P.

notation.meaning: exact convex envelope of q on C

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Cell Envelopes Make the Scalar Bound Partition-Independent

children.title: Refinement-Efficiency Boundary
children.top_down_role: Regimes where additional partition refinement yields insufficient envelope improvement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Uniform-Grid Error and Cell Count for a Separable Concave Quadratic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit curse-of-dimensionality boundary for uniform rectangular refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=-\frac{M}{2}\lVert x\rVert_2^2\) on \([0,L]^n\), where \(M,L>0\), and divide every coordinate into \(m\) equal intervals. On each resulting cube of side \(h=L/m\), the exact convex envelope is the sum of the coordinate secants, and its maximum pointwise error is \[\max_x\bigl(q(x)-\operatorname{conv}q(x)\bigr)=\frac{nMh^2}{8}=\frac{nML^2}{8m^2}.\] Hence an error at most \(\varepsilon>0\) is obtained exactly when \[m\ge L\sqrt{\frac{nM}{8\varepsilon}},\] up to integer rounding, and the uniform partition then contains \[N(\varepsilon)=\left\lceil L\sqrt{\frac{nM}{8\varepsilon}}\right\rceil^n\] cells.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a separable concave quadratic, uniform envelope error decreases quadratically with cell width but the required number of cells grows exponentially with dimension.
assumptions_latex: Every coordinate is divided into the same number \(m\) of equal intervals.
Exact cellwise convex envelopes are used and error is measured pointwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N(\varepsilon)=\left\lceil L\sqrt{nM/(8\varepsilon)}\right\rceil^n.

notation.meaning: uniform cell count required for pointwise error at most epsilon

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Uniform-Grid Error and Cell Count for a Separable Concave Quadratic
Refinement-Efficiency Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curse-of-dimensionality boundary for uniform spatial refinement of quadratic envelope errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a cube of side length \(L\) in \(\mathbb R^n\), partitioned uniformly into cells of side at most \(h\). The partition contains at least \(\lceil L/h\rceil^n\) cells. For a concave quadratic with curvature scale \(M=\lVert-Q\rVert_2\), standard localized interpolation-envelope errors scale as \(O(Mnh^2)\). Thus enforcing a uniform error target \(\varepsilon\) by mesh width alone requires \(h=O(\sqrt{\varepsilon/(Mn)})\) and, in the full-curvature worst case, on the order of \((L\sqrt{Mn/\varepsilon})^n\) cells. Uniform refinement is therefore exponentially sensitive to dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform partition refinement needs exponentially many cells in dimension, even though local quadratic-envelope error decreases quadratically with cell width.
assumptions_latex: The domain is an \(n\)-dimensional cube of side length \(L>0\).
Refinement is uniform and cellwise envelope error is controlled through diameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N(\varepsilon)=O\!\left((L\sqrt{Mn/\varepsilon})^n\right)\) cells suffice under the stated error model, exhibiting exponential dimension dependence.

notation.meaning: spectral curvature scale of the concave quadratic
number of uniform cells at target error

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-QP Node Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Box-local convex quadratic underestimator obtained by diagonal spectral shifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\) on a node box \([l,u]\), choose \(\alpha\ge\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(Q)\}\). Since \(Q+\alpha I\succeq0\) and the chord of \(-\alpha x_i^2\) on \([l_i,u_i]\) is \(-\alpha((l_i+u_i)x_i-l_i u_i)\), the function
\[\underline q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}(Q+\alpha I)x+c^{\mathsf T}x+d-\alpha\sum_i((l_i+u_i)x_i-l_i u_i)\]
is convex and satisfies \(\underline q(x)\le q(x)\) throughout the box. Minimizing it over convex node constraints yields a valid node lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shift the Hessian to positive semidefinite and replace the resulting concave square terms by box chords to obtain a convex node bound.
assumptions_latex: The node feasible set is convex and contained in \([l,u]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min \underline q\le\min q\) over the node feasible set, and computing \(\min\underline q\) is a convex quadratic program.

notation.meaning: convex quadratic underestimator on the node box

9.3.1 Biconvex and Convex-Concave Programming p. 190

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1.3 Differential Convex (D.C.) Programming p. 10

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise and uniform error of the seed's diagonal-shift underestimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the seed underestimator \(\underline q\),\[q(x)-\underline q(x)=\alpha\sum_{i=1}^n(x_i-l_i)(u_i-x_i),\]and therefore\[0\le q(x)-\underline q(x)\le\frac{\alpha}{4}\sum_{i=1}^n(u_i-l_i)^2.\]It is exact at every box vertex and becomes uniformly exact along boxes whose maximum side length tends to zero, provided the chosen shifts remain bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The spectral-shift bound has an explicit width-squared error, is exact at box vertices, and is locally consistent under shrinking boxes and bounded shifts.
assumptions_latex: The seed construction uses a nonnegative scalar shift \(\alpha\).
For a sequence of boxes, the selected shifts are uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{x\in[l,u]}(q(x)-\underline q(x))\le\frac{\alpha}{4}\sum_i(u_i-l_i)^2.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-Shift Underestimation Error

children.title: Linearized Node Bounds
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral node relaxations derived from product envelopes and cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Linearized Node Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP node relaxation using McCormick inequalities and finite tangent cuts for squares.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On a node box \([l,u]\), replace every product \(x_i x_j\) by \(X_{ij}\). For \(i<j\), impose the four McCormick inequalities
\[X_{ij}\ge l_i x_j+l_j x_i-l_i l_j,\quad X_{ij}\ge u_i x_j+u_j x_i-u_i u_j,\]
\[X_{ij}\le u_i x_j+l_j x_i-u_i l_j,\quad X_{ij}\le l_i x_j+u_j x_i-l_i u_j.\]
For squares impose \(X_{ii}\le(l_i+u_i)x_i-l_i u_i\) and tangent cuts \(X_{ii}\ge2t x_i-t^2\) for selected \(t\in[l_i,u_i]\). Substituting \(X\) into the quadratic objective and constraints produces an LP relaxation whose optimum is a valid node lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lift quadratic products and bound their graphs with McCormick inequalities and square tangents, producing a polyhedral node relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(l_i\le x_i\le u_i\) with finite bounds for every variable.
The lifted LP retains all original linear node constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every original node-feasible point lifts into the stated polyhedron, so the LP optimum is no greater than the original node optimum.

notation.meaning: lifted variable representing the product of variables i and j
selected tangency point for a square lower cut

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Termwise Exactness Does Not Imply Joint Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit incompatibility among individually exact product envelopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \([0,1]^3\), the lifted point\[x_1=x_2=x_3=\tfrac12,\qquad X_{ii}=\tfrac12,\qquad X_{ij}=0\ (i\ne j)\]satisfies the exact individual convex-hull descriptions for every square and every bilinear product. It is not in \(\operatorname{conv}\{(x,xx^{\mathsf T}):x\in[0,1]^3\}\): the equalities \(X_{ii}=x_i\) force each coordinate to be binary almost surely in any representing mixture, while \(X_{ij}=0\) forces at most one coordinate to equal one, contradicting \(\sum_i x_i=3/2\). Thus pairwise-exact envelopes can omit joint compatibility conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A three-variable lifted point satisfies every individual product hull but not the joint quadratic-product hull.
assumptions_latex: Individual square and bilinear convex-hull constraints are imposed termwise on \([0,1]^3\).
No global positive-semidefinite or higher-order compatibility constraint is added.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigcap_{i\le j}\mathcal M_{ij}\supsetneq\operatorname{conv}\{(x,xx^{\mathsf T}):x\in[0,1]^3\}.

notation.meaning: Exact individual lifted-product hull for indices i,j.

knowledge_statements.title: Termwise Exactness Does Not Imply Joint Exactness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonicity and limiting exactness of square tangent cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty finite \(T_i\subset[l_i,u_i]\), impose \(X_{ii}\ge2tx_i-t^2\) for every \(t\in T_i\). Enlarging \(T_i\) shrinks the lifted LP feasible set and cannot decrease its minimization lower bound. Moreover,\[x_i^2-\max_{t\in T_i}(2tx_i-t^2)=\min_{t\in T_i}(x_i-t)^2.\]Hence the square lower approximation converges uniformly to \(x_i^2\) as the fill distance of \(T_i\) tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding square tangents monotonically strengthens the LP, and the approximation error is the squared distance to the nearest tangency point.
assumptions_latex: The lifted objective is minimized over the resulting outer approximation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_i\subseteq T_i'\Rightarrow L(T_i)\le L(T_i'),\qquad \sup_{x_i}\left(x_i^2-\max_{t\in T_i}(2tx_i-t^2)\right)=h(T_i)^2.

notation.meaning: Fill distance of the tangency set.
LP lower bound using those tangents.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested Tangent-Cut Strengthening

children.title: Semidefinite Node Bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Node Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shor-type matrix lifting over a bounded node, with optional valid strengthening constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2c^{\mathsf T}x\) over a node-feasible set contained in \(B=[l,u]\). Introduce \(X\) to represent \(xx^{\mathsf T}\), replace the rank-one equality by \[Y=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,\] and impose every available linear constraint valid for \((x,xx^{\mathsf T})\), including \(l_i\le x_i\le u_i\) and \(X_{ii}\le(l_i+u_i)x_i-l_iu_i\). The semidefinite node bound is \[L_B^{\rm SDP}=\min\{\langle Q,X\rangle+2c^{\mathsf T}x:(x,X)\text{ satisfies these constraints}\}.\] Valid RLT or stationarity-derived linear constraints may be added without invalidating the bound. Then \(L_B^{\rm SDP}\) does not exceed the node optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lift quadratic products to a positive-semidefinite matrix and drop rank one. Box, RLT, or valid stationarity constraints strengthen the resulting rigorous node lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The original node-feasible set is nonempty and contained in \([l,u]\).
Every added strengthening constraint is valid for \((x,xx^{\mathsf T})\) at the node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_B^{\rm SDP}\le \min\{x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2c^{\mathsf T}x:x\text{ is node-feasible}\}\).

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the node SDP relaxation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal recovery and closure from a rank-one optimal node moment matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x^*,X^*)\) attain the node SDP optimum and let\[Y^*=\begin{pmatrix}1&(x^*)^{\mathsf T}\\x^*&X^*\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.\]If \(\operatorname{rank}(Y^*)=1\), then \(X^*=x^*(x^*)^{\mathsf T}\). If the rank-one lifted constraints coincide with the original node constraints, the recovered \(x^*\) is original-node feasible and its objective equals the SDP lower bound; it is therefore node-optimal and supplies a realizability-fathoming witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal rank-one node moment matrix recovers an original feasible optimizer and certifies exactness.
assumptions_latex: The node SDP optimum is attained.
The leading entry of \(Y^*\) is one.
At rank one, the lifted constraints represent the original node constraints exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}(Y^*)=1\Rightarrow X^*=x^*(x^*)^{\mathsf T},\quad f(x^*)=L_B^{\rm SDP}=f_B^*.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-One Node Exactness Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordering of node SDP bounds under valid added constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal S_1\subseteq\mathcal S_0\) be obtained from a basic node SDP feasible set by adding constraints valid for every exact node lift. For minimization,\[L_0=\min_{\mathcal S_0}\langle Q,X\rangle+2c^{\mathsf T}x\le L_1=\min_{\mathcal S_1}\langle Q,X\rangle+2c^{\mathsf T}x\le f_B^*.\]Thus valid box, RLT, or stationarity constraints cannot weaken the bound, although strict improvement and rank-one recovery are not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid tightening raises or preserves an SDP node lower bound but need not make it exact.
assumptions_latex: Every exact feasible lift remains in \(\mathcal S_1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_0\le L_1\le f_B^*.

notation.meaning: Basic and strengthened SDP feasible sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary branching on one coordinate of a bounded continuous-QP node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a current box \(B=[l,u]\), choose a coordinate \(k\) with \(l_k<u_k\) and a split point \(s\in(l_k,u_k)\). Form two children \[B^-=[l,u^-],\qquad B^+=[l^+,u],\] where \(u^-_k=s\), \(l^+_k=s\), and all other bounds remain unchanged. Intersect each child with the node constraints, compute its relaxation bound, and discard it only through a valid fathoming rule. The children cover the parent because \(B=B^-\cup B^+\); their interiors are disjoint in coordinate \(k\). Repeated branching is exhaustive when every infinite branch has coordinate widths tending to zero in all directions relevant to relaxation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split one bounded variable at an interior point, solve the two child relaxations, and continue until relevant coordinate widths vanish or valid fathoming applies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B=B^-\cup B^+\) and \(\operatorname{int}(B^-)\cap\operatorname{int}(B^+)=\varnothing\).

children.title: Box Branching
children.top_down_role: Subdivision regimes acting on multidimensional boxes or selected box faces.

knowledge_statements.title: Box Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite hyperrectangular partition of a continuous-QP search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a bounded node box \(B=[l,u]\), choose a finite family of nonempty closed axis-aligned boxes \(B^1,\ldots,B^r\subseteq B\) satisfying \[B=\bigcup_{j=1}^r B^j,\qquad \operatorname{int}(B^j)\cap\operatorname{int}(B^h)=\varnothing\quad(j\ne h).\] If \(F\) denotes the original constraint set, create a child feasible region \(F\cap B^j\) for each \(j\). Before fathoming, these children satisfy \[F\cap B=\bigcup_{j=1}^r(F\cap B^j).\] Compute a valid lower bound for each child and discard a child only through a valid fathoming rule. A standard realization introduces interior breakpoints on selected coordinates and uses the Cartesian products of the resulting subintervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition the parent box into finitely many interior-disjoint child boxes. Their constrained regions cover the parent feasible region before fathoming; afterward, only children removed by valid fathoming certificates may be omitted.
assumptions_latex: Each \(B^j\) is a nonempty closed axis-aligned box contained in \(B\).
The boxes cover \(B\), and every subsequent child deletion uses a valid fathoming rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\cap B=\bigcup_{j=1}^r(F\cap B^j)\) before fathoming.

source_refs.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

source_witnesses.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric localization condition for nested descendants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B^0\supseteq B^1\supseteq\cdots\) be nonempty compact child boxes from valid box partitions. If \(\operatorname{diam}(B^k)\to0\), then there is a unique \(\bar x\) with \(\bigcap_kB^k=\{\bar x\}\). Any node relaxation whose uniform error is bounded by \(\omega(\operatorname{diam}B)\), where \(\omega(t)\to0\), is locally exact along this branch. Valid partitioning alone does not imply this shrinking condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested nonempty compact child boxes with vanishing diameter localize to one point; coverage alone does not guarantee such shrinking.
assumptions_latex: Every child box is nonempty, compact, and contained in its parent.
For the relaxation assertion, the error has a vanishing diameter modulus.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{diam}(B^k)\to0\Rightarrow\bigcap_kB^k=\{\bar x\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Exhaustive Shrinking Box Refinement

children.title: Coordinate-Selection Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural criteria distinguishing candidate branching coordinates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic nonstarvation of persistently eligible coordinates along a nested box branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_t=[l^t,u^t]\) be nested boxes and let \(k_t\) be the coordinate split at step \(t\). A regime is essentially cyclic with window \(M\) if every coordinate that remains eligible throughout \(t,\ldots,t+M-1\) is selected at least once in that window. Hence a coordinate that is persistently nondegenerate cannot be permanently starved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An essentially cyclic regime selects every coordinate that remains eligible throughout each fixed-length window.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(l_i^s<u_i^s\ \forall s\in\{t,\ldots,t+M-1\}\bigr)\Longrightarrow i\in\{k_t,\ldots,k_{t+M-1}\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Essentially Cyclic Coordinate Selection

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Width Contraction Under Fair Balanced Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-depth bound from essentially cyclic selection and uniformly interior splits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose splitting coordinate \(i\) leaves the followed child with width at most \((1-\eta)\) times its parent width, where \(0<\eta\le1/2\). After \(N_i(t)\) such splits, \[w_i^t\le(1-\eta)^{N_i(t)}w_i^0.\] Thus \(N_i(t)\ge\lceil\log(w_i^0/\varepsilon)/[-\log(1-\eta)]\rceil\) implies \(w_i^t\le\varepsilon\). Under an essentially cyclic window \(M\), every persistently eligible coordinate receives the required splits within at most \(M\) times this split count.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly interior splits contract selected widths geometrically, and an essentially cyclic schedule converts split counts into branch-depth bounds.
assumptions_latex: Every selected-coordinate child width is at most \((1-\eta)w_i^t\).
Selection is essentially cyclic with window \(M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_i(t)\to\infty\Longrightarrow w_i^t\to0.

notation.meaning: Width of coordinate i at step t.
Number of splits of coordinate i through step t.

knowledge_statements.title: Width Contraction Under Fair Balanced Splitting

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested-box example in which repeatedly splitting an irrelevant coordinate leaves a positive quadratic-envelope error unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_t=[0,2^{-t}]\times[0,1]\) and consider the concave quadratic term \(q(x)=-x_2^2\). Its convex envelope over every \(B_t\) is \(\operatorname{vex}_{B_t}q(x)=-x_2\), so \[\sup_{x\in B_t}\bigl(q(x)-\operatorname{vex}_{B_t}q(x)\bigr)=\sup_{0\le x_2\le1}x_2(1-x_2)=\tfrac14.\] Thus the schedule that always bisects coordinate \(1\) produces nested boxes with \(w_1^t\to0\) but permanently starves coordinate \(2\), and the envelope error does not converge to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly splitting one coordinate can leave a positive relaxation error unchanged in an ignored coordinate, so unfair coordinate selection need not yield asymptotically exact envelopes.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation replaces \(-x_2^2\) by its convex envelope over the current box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w_1^t\to0\quad\text{but}\quad\sup_{x\in B_t}\bigl(q(x)-\operatorname{vex}_{B_t}q(x)\bigr)=\tfrac14\ \text{for every }t.

notation.meaning: Convex envelope of the quadratic term on the current box.
Width of coordinate i in box \(B_t\).

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Starvation Prevents Envelope Exactness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Width-, Error-, and Strong-Branching Coordinate Scores
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical coordinate-scoring variants for binary branching on a bounded node box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node \(B=[l,u]\), score each eligible coordinate \(i\) with \(l_i<u_i\). Longest-edge selection uses \(\sigma_i=u_i-l_i\). Error selection uses a valid or computed coordinate contribution \(e_i(B)\) to relaxation weakness. Strong branching tentatively forms the two children and may use \[\sigma_i=\min\{L_i^-,L_i^+\}-L(B),\] where \(L(B)\) and \(L_i^\pm\) are valid parent and tentative child lower bounds. Select a maximizer using a fixed tie rule, then pass that coordinate to the variable-branching operation. For convergence, the selection policy must not permanently starve coordinates retaining positive unresolved error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinates may be selected by width, modeled relaxation error, or tentative child-bound improvement, subject to nonstarvation of persistent error.
assumptions_latex: Scores are finite for eligible coordinates.
Tentative child scores use consistently computed valid lower bounds when interpreted as bound improvements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{i:l_i<u_i}\sigma_i(B)\), subject to the stated nonstarvation requirement.

notation.meaning: Tentative lower bounds for the two children of coordinate \(i\).

knowledge_statements.title: Width-, Error-, and Strong-Branching Coordinate Scores

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Error-Fair Balanced Selection Gives Relaxation Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional convergence for coordinatewise width-controlled relaxation errors along a nested branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let nested boxes \(B_t\) have widths \(w_i^t\), and suppose \[0\le G(B_t)\le\sum_{i=1}^n c_i(w_i^t)^{p_i},\qquad c_i\ge0,\quad p_i>0.\] If every coordinate with persistent positive contribution is selected infinitely often and each selected width contracts by a factor at most \(1-\eta\), for fixed \(0<\eta\le1/2\), then every contributing width tends to zero and \(G(B_t)\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fair balanced refinement makes a separable width-controlled relaxation asymptotically exact.
assumptions_latex: The displayed finite coordinatewise error bound holds.
Every persistently positive error contribution is selected infinitely often.
Selected widths contract by the fixed factor \(1-\eta\).

notation.meaning: Node relaxation gap controlled by coordinate widths.
Coordinatewise error constants and positive exponents.

knowledge_statements.title: Error-Fair Balanced Selection Gives Relaxation Exactness
Coordinate-Selection Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rules for choosing the coordinate used by box branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node \(B=[l,u]\), assign each eligible coordinate \(i\) a score \(\sigma_i(B)\). A longest-edge regime uses \(\sigma_i=u_i-l_i\); a relaxation-error regime uses a certified or computed contribution of coordinate \(i\) to the node relaxation gap; and a strong-branching regime tentatively splits each candidate and scores the predicted child-bound improvement. Select \[k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{i:l_i<u_i}\sigma_i(B),\] resolve ties deterministically, choose an interior split point, and create the corresponding children. For convergence, the regime must be exhaustive: along every infinite nested-node sequence, no coordinate whose unresolved relaxation error stays positive may be neglected indefinitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Score eligible coordinates by width, relaxation error, or tentative bound improvement, branch on a maximizer, and enforce fairness for coordinates retaining positive relaxation error.
assumptions_latex: \(B=[l,u]\) is a nondegenerate bounded node box.
Scores are finite and comparable for every eligible coordinate.
Tie-breaking and split-point rules are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{i:l_i<u_i}\sigma_i(B)\), subject to the stated exhaustiveness requirement.

notation.meaning: Branching score for coordinate i at box B.

children.title: Box-Geometry Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Dependence of branching effectiveness on domain shape plus scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Box-Geometry Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact dependence of elementary quadratic-envelope gaps on box side lengths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_i\in[l_i,u_i]\) and \(x_j\in[l_j,u_j]\). For the McCormick relaxation of \(w=x_ix_j\), the largest vertical separation between its convex and concave piecewise-linear envelopes over the rectangle equals \[\frac{(u_i-l_i)(u_j-l_j)}{2},\] while the largest one-sided deviation of either envelope from the bilinear graph equals \((u_i-l_i)(u_j-l_j)/4\). For the secant overestimator of \(w=x_i^2\), the maximum deviation from the graph is \((u_i-l_i)^2/4\). Consequently, shrinking a side participating in a quadratic term reduces its envelope error linearly for bilinear terms and quadratically for a repeated-variable square term.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic-envelope weakness is controlled by box widths: bilinear one-sided error is one quarter of the width product, while square secant error is one quarter of width squared.
assumptions_latex: Standard McCormick envelopes are used for \(x_ix_j\).
The chord through the interval endpoints is used for the square overestimator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_{ij}^{\rm one\text{-}sided}=\frac14(u_i-l_i)(u_j-l_j)\) and \(\Delta_{ii}^{\rm sec}=\frac14(u_i-l_i)^2\).

notation.meaning: Maximum deviation of one McCormick envelope from the bilinear graph.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 Bilinear Programming Problems p. 69

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Bilinear Programming Problems p. 69

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Raw widths are unit-dependent whereas coefficient-weighted error terms are invariant under diagonal rescaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under \(x_i=s_i z_i+r_i\) with \(s_i\ne0\), widths satisfy \(d_i^z=d_i^x/|s_i|\), while the coefficient of \(z_iz_j\) is \(a_{ij}^z=a_{ij}^xs_is_j\). Hence\[|a_{ij}^z|d_i^zd_j^z=|a_{ij}^x|d_i^xd_j^x,\qquad |a_{ii}^z|(d_i^z)^2=|a_{ii}^x|(d_i^x)^2.\]Raw longest-side comparisons therefore depend on units, whereas consistently coefficient-weighted envelope-error measures do not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Raw box widths depend on units, while coefficient-weighted width products are invariant under diagonal rescaling.
assumptions_latex: The coordinate transformation is diagonal and nonsingular.
Coefficients and bounds are transformed consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |a_{ij}^z|d_i^zd_j^z=|a_{ij}^x|d_i^xd_j^x.
knowledge_statements.title: Absolute-Width Scaling Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregate geometry bound for a standard termwise quadratic underestimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let\[q(x)=\sum_{i<j}a_{ij}x_ix_j+\sum_i a_{ii}x_i^2+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\]on \([l,u]\), with \(d_i=u_i-l_i\). For each bilinear term use the McCormick side giving a lower estimator after multiplication by \(a_{ij}\). For \(a_{ii}<0\), use the square secant after multiplication; for \(a_{ii}\ge0\), retain the convex square exactly. Then\[0\le q(x)-\underline q(x)\le\frac14\sum_{i<j}|a_{ij}|d_id_j+\frac14\sum_{i:a_{ii}<0}|a_{ii}|d_i^2.\]The same expression with all diagonal absolute values is a valid looser bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A standard termwise quadratic underestimator has a coefficient-weighted error bounded by width products and squared widths.
assumptions_latex: Every off-diagonal product is counted once.
Positive square terms are retained exactly and negative square terms use their secant-based lower estimator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q(x)-\underline q(x)\le\frac14\sum_{i<j}|a_{ij}|d_id_j+\frac14\sum_{i:a_{ii}<0}|a_{ii}|d_i^2.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Weighted Aggregate Envelope Error

children.title: Bilinear-Term Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching directed at product-envelope error.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Policy-independent core algorithm, excluding unsupported specialized scoring formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node whose relaxation contains \(w_{ij}\) for \(x_ix_j\), select a term with nonzero product-envelope error and choose one factor having positive interval width. Split that factor at an interior point, form children covering the parent interval, rebuild every affected product envelope on each child, and apply only valid fathoming. Residual size, coefficient-weighted residual, predicted envelope-gap reduction, and factor width are admissible selection heuristics, but none is required for validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose an inexact bilinear term, split a nondegenerate factor interval, and rebuild the affected envelopes in covering child nodes.
assumptions_latex: Both product factors have finite bounds.
The chosen factor has positive width and the split is interior.
Child intervals cover the parent interval.
Affected envelopes are rebuilt using the child bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B=B^-\cup B^+\text{ and each child McCormick relaxation remains a valid outer approximation}.
knowledge_statements.title: Envelope-Error-Directed Bilinear Branching

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition ensuring all selected product-envelope errors vanish along a retained branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nested node boxes \(B^k=[l^k,u^k]\), suppose every relaxed bilinear term satisfies\[(u_i^k-l_i^k)(u_j^k-l_j^k)\to0.\]Because its maximum one-sided McCormick error is one quarter of this product, every product-envelope error tends to zero. The bilinear component of the relaxation is therefore locally consistent along the branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bilinear branching is envelope-consistent when every relevant factor-width product tends to zero.
assumptions_latex: Standard McCormick envelopes are rebuilt after branching.
The width-product condition holds for every relaxed bilinear term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall(i,j),\ d_i^kd_j^k\to0\Rightarrow\max|w_{ij}-x_ix_j|\to0.

notation.meaning: Width of factor i at node k.

knowledge_statements.title: Bilinear-Branching Consistency Condition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of consistency when a selection rule indefinitely ignores another inexact product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two independent relaxed products \(x_1x_2\) and \(x_3x_4\) on positive-width intervals. A rule that repeatedly branches only factors of \(x_1x_2\) while never shrinking either interval of \(x_3x_4\) leaves the latter term's maximum McCormick error equal to \(\tfrac14d_3d_4>0\). Thus repeated product-directed branching is not sufficient for consistency unless every persistently inexact relevant product is eventually refined or its factor-width product otherwise vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A term-selection rule can fail by starving another product whose envelope error then remains positive.
assumptions_latex: The intervals of \(x_3\) and \(x_4\) retain fixed positive widths.
The product \(x_3x_4\) remains in the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_3^kd_4^k=d_3^0d_4^0>0\Rightarrow\Delta_{34}^k\not\to0.

notation.meaning: Maximum one-sided McCormick error for product \(x_3x_4\).

knowledge_statements.title: Product-Starvation Failure
Bilinear-Term Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branching chosen to reduce the largest weighted product-envelope error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the node relaxation contains lifted products \(w_{ij}\) for terms \(q_{ij}x_ix_j\). At its solution \((\bar x,\bar w)\), compute violations \(e_{ij}=|\bar w_{ij}-\bar x_i\bar x_j|\) and select \[(i,j)\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{(p,q)}|q_{pq}|e_{pq}.\] Choose \(k\in\{i,j\}\) having positive width and, commonly, the larger width or predicted reduction in the product-envelope gap. Split the interval of \(x_k\) at an interior point, rebuild the product envelopes on each child box, solve the child relaxations, and apply valid fathoming. If all selected product widths are driven to zero, the associated McCormick relaxation errors vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the weighted bilinear term with the largest lifted-product discrepancy, branch on one of its factors, and rebuild tighter product envelopes in the children.
assumptions_latex: Every selected product has finite factor bounds.
The relaxation explicitly represents \(w_{ij}\) and supplies a node solution.
The split point lies strictly inside the selected factor interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((u_i-l_i)(u_j-l_j)\to0\) implies the McCormick error for \(x_ix_j\) tends to \(0\).

notation.meaning: Lifted representative of product x_i x_j.
Product inconsistency at the relaxation solution.

children.title: Negative-Eigenspace Branching
children.top_down_role: Partitions focused on directions responsible for nonconvex curvature.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite projection bounds required by secant-based negative-direction branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda>0\), no finite affine function \(\ell(y)=\alpha y+\beta\) satisfies \(\ell(y)\le-\lambda y^2\) for every \(y\in\mathbb R\). Consequently, a two-endpoint secant underestimator and its width-based error bound require finite valid bounds on the projected negative-curvature coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A concave quadratic has no global affine underestimator on the real line, so secant-based directional branching requires finite projection bounds.
assumptions_latex: The projected domain contains the entire real line.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nexists(\alpha,\beta)\in\mathbb R^2:\ \alpha y+\beta\le-\lambda y^2\quad\forall y\in\mathbb R.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded-Projection Secant Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact envelope error for one bounded negative-eigenvalue coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda>0\) and \(y\in[a,b]\), the convex envelope of \(-\lambda y^2\) is its secant \[s(y)=-\lambda(a+b)y+\lambda ab.\] Its pointwise error is \[ -\lambda y^2-s(y)=\lambda(y-a)(b-y),\] so \[\max_{y\in[a,b]}[-\lambda y^2-s(y)]=\frac{\lambda}{4}(b-a)^2.\] Exhaustive shrinking of the interval therefore eliminates this directional envelope error quadratically in its width.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum secant error in a bounded negative-eigenvalue direction is one quarter of the eigenvalue magnitude times squared interval width.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_{y\in[a,b]}[-\lambda y^2-s(y)]=\lambda(b-a)^2/4.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Negative-Direction Secant Error

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional branching on a finitely bounded negative-curvature projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=Q_+-\sum_{r=1}^m\lambda_rv_rv_r^{\mathsf T}\), with \(Q_+\succeq0\), \(\lambda_r>0\), and orthonormal \(v_r\). At a node with finite valid bounds \(a_r\le v_r^{\mathsf T}x\le b_r\), choose an unresolved direction, for example a maximizer of \(\lambda_r(b_r-a_r)^2/4\), and choose \(s\in(a_r,b_r)\). Create children by adding respectively \(v_r^{\mathsf T}x\le s\) and \(v_r^{\mathsf T}x\ge s\). These complementary halfspaces cover the parent feasible set. Recompute projection bounds and lower relaxations in each child.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch on a bounded negative-eigenvalue projection by complementary halfspaces, preferably targeting a large exact secant error.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\) has at least one negative eigenvalue.
Finite valid bounds on the selected projection are available.
The split point is strictly interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two children cover the parent feasible set and reduce the selected projection interval.
knowledge_statements.title: Complementary-Halfspace Negative-Eigenspace Branching

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregate secant error for independently bounded spectral coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \[q_-(y)=-\sum_{r=1}^m\lambda_r y_r^2,\qquad \lambda_r>0,
\qquad y\in\prod_{r=1}^m[a_r,b_r],\] the convex envelope is the sum of the coordinate secants and \[\max_y\bigl(q_-(y)-\operatorname{vex}q_-(y)\bigr)=\frac14\sum_{r=1}^m\lambda_r(b_r-a_r)^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a product of bounded spectral intervals, total negative-eigenspace secant error is the sum of the one-dimensional errors.
assumptions_latex: The envelope domain is the Cartesian product of the projected intervals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E=\frac14\sum_r\lambda_r(b_r-a_r)^2\).

notation.meaning: Separable concave quadratic carried by the negative eigenspace.

knowledge_statements.title: Total Separable Negative-Eigenspace Envelope Error

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fair Directional Refinement Eliminates Spectral Envelope Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional convergence under balanced nonstarving refinement of negative-curvature projections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(w_r^t=b_r^t-a_r^t\). Suppose every direction with persistent positive error \(\lambda_r(w_r^t)^2/4\) is selected infinitely often and each selected child satisfies \(w_r^{t+1}\le(1-\eta)w_r^t\) for fixed \(0<\eta\le1/2\). Then \[\sum_{r=1}^m\frac{\lambda_r}{4}(w_r^t)^2\longrightarrow0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Balanced nonstarving refinement of all unresolved negative-curvature projections drives their total secant error to zero.
assumptions_latex: There are finitely many negative-eigenvalue directions.
All initial projected intervals are finite.
Selection is fair for every direction retaining positive error.
Each selected interval contracts by the fixed factor \(1-\eta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_r\lambda_r(w_r^t)^2/4\to0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Fair Directional Refinement Eliminates Spectral Envelope Error
Negative-Eigenspace Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional branching on coordinates induced by negative curvature of the quadratic form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=Q_+-\sum_{r=1}^m\lambda_rv_rv_r^{\mathsf T}\), where \(Q_+\succeq0\), \(\lambda_r>0\), and the \(v_r\) are orthonormal negative-eigenvalue directions. Introduce \(y_r=v_r^{\mathsf T}x\) and obtain valid node bounds \(a_r\le y_r\le b_r\). Score unresolved directions, for example by \(\lambda_r(b_r-a_r)^2\), select a maximizer, and split its interval at \(s\in(a_r,b_r)\). The two children add respectively \(v_r^{\mathsf T}x\le s\) and \(v_r^{\mathsf T}x\ge s\). Recompute bounds and relaxations. Shrinking every negatively curved directional interval to zero eliminates the separable concave-quadratic envelope error caused by \(-\lambda_ry_r^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonalize the negative curvature, choose a weighted unresolved eigen-direction, and branch by two half-space cuts on its projected coordinate.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\) has at least one negative eigenvalue.
Finite valid bounds on each selected projection \(v_r^{\mathsf T}x\) are available.
The directional split is strictly interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b_r-a_r\to0\) for all \(r\) implies the negative-eigenspace envelope error tends to \(0\).

notation.meaning: Magnitude of the associated negative eigenvalue.

children.title: Node Selection-Fathoming Calculus
children.top_down_role: Search ordering and rigorous elimination of nodes by status or dominance.

children.title: Node Ordering Policy Family
children.top_down_role: Canonical node-ordering families and their hybrids.

children.title: Best-Bound Node Selection
children.top_down_role: Node ordering driven by relaxation-bound priority.

knowledge_statements.title: Best-Bound Node Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-node ordering by the smallest valid lower bound for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain an active-node set \(\mathcal A\), a valid lower bound \(L_N\) for each \(N\in\mathcal A\), and an incumbent value \(U\). After applying valid fathoming tests, if \(\mathcal A\ne\varnothing\), define \[L=\min_{N\in\mathcal A}L_N\] and select \[N^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{N\in\mathcal A}L_N,\] using a fixed tie-breaking rule. Process \(N^*\) and insert its unfathomed children with valid bounds. For an absolute tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), gap termination is valid when \(U<+\infty\) and \(U-L\le\varepsilon\). If \(\mathcal A=\varnothing\), termination is instead justified by the accumulated valid fathoming certificates, with the outcome determined by whether a feasible incumbent exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Process an active node with the smallest valid lower bound. Use the incumbent-to-active-bound gap only when the active set is nonempty and a finite incumbent exists; an empty active set is handled through the accumulated fathoming certificates.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
Every active node \(N\) has a valid lower bound \(L_N\).
\(U\) is the value of a feasible incumbent or \(+\infty\) if none exists.
Every removed node is covered by a valid fathoming certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\mathcal A\ne\varnothing\), then \(L_{N^*}=L=\min_{N\in\mathcal A}L_N\).

notation.meaning: Valid lower bound for node N.
Minimum lower bound over a nonempty active-node set.

children.title: Depth-Oriented Node Selection
children.top_down_role: Node ordering favoring deeper exploration of the search tree.

knowledge_statements.title: Depth-Oriented Node Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-node ordering favoring the deepest available search-tree node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each node \(N\) in a nonempty active set \(\mathcal A\), let \(d_N\) be its finite depth in the spatial-search tree. After applying valid fathoming tests, select \[N^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{N\in\mathcal A}d_N,\] resolving ties by a fixed rule such as smallest lower bound or last-in-first-out order. Process \(N^*\), update the incumbent from any feasible point found, and insert its unfathomed children into \(\mathcal A\). This rule favors continued exploration of deep branches, but by itself it does not guarantee fairness or prevent indefinite postponement of shallower active nodes; any required global-convergence fairness must be supplied by an additional scheduling condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Process a deepest active node using a fixed tie-breaker. This favors continued exploration of a branch but does not by itself guarantee fair processing of shallower nodes or global convergence.
assumptions_latex: The active search structure is a rooted tree, and every \(N\in\mathcal A\) has finite depth \(d_N\).
All node deletions use valid fathoming certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{N^*}=\max_{N\in\mathcal A}d_N\).

source_refs.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

source_witnesses.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

children.title: Hybrid Node Selection
children.top_down_role: Ordering regimes combining bound priority with depth preference.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General node-ordering schedule combining the two sibling priority rules without asserting convergence from scheduling alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A_t\) be the nonempty active set at iteration \(t\), with valid lower bounds \(L_N\) and depths \(d_N\). Choose a prescribed index set \(B\subseteq\mathbb N\). After valid fathoming, select \[N_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{N\in\mathcal A_t}L_N\quad\text{when }t\in B,\] and select \[N_t\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{N\in\mathcal A_t}d_N\quad\text{when }t\notin B,\] using specified tie rules. Periodic alternation, finite depth-oriented phases followed by a best-bound step, and event-triggered switching are instances once \(B\) is fixed by the corresponding schedule. The schedule combines the component priorities but does not by itself supply a global-convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid schedule uses best-bound selection on specified iterations and deepest-node selection on the others; periodic and event-triggered switching are instances.
assumptions_latex: Each selected node belongs to a nonempty active set and has a valid lower bound and finite depth.
Valid fathoming is applied before selection.
The schedule and tie-breaking rules are specified independently of any claimed convergence result.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: t\in B\Rightarrow L_{N_t}=\min_{N\in\mathcal A_t}L_N,\qquad t\notin B\Rightarrow d_{N_t}=\max_{N\in\mathcal A_t}d_N.

notation.meaning: Valid node lower bound and tree depth.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduled Best-Bound and Depth Hybrid

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Recurrent Best-Bound Steps Do Not Imply General Fairness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp scheduling boundary for starvation claims in hybrids with infinitely recurring best-bound iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Even if \(B\) is infinite, recurrent best-bound iterations do not ensure that every persistent active node is eventually selected. Such recurrence protects only nodes that continue to attain the minimum active lower bound, and then only under a tie rule fair among persistent minimizers. A persistent node whose bound is always strictly above another active bound can remain unselected at every best-bound iteration and can also be bypassed by the depth-oriented steps. Therefore general fairness or global convergence requires additional scheduling and refinement assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infinitely many best-bound steps do not prevent starvation of every active node; fairness among persistent minimum-bound nodes and further convergence assumptions are still required.
assumptions_latex: Nodes not selected remain active unless valid fathoming removes them.
No fairness condition beyond the stated component priorities is presumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |B|=\infty\not\Rightarrow\text{every persistent active node is eventually selected}.
knowledge_statements.title: Recurrent Best-Bound Steps Do Not Imply General Fairness
Hybrid Node Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node ordering alternating incumbent-seeking depth and global-bound improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain active nodes with depths \(d_N\), lower bounds \(L_N\), and an incumbent \(U\). Fix a deterministic schedule with infinitely many best-bound iterations. On a best-bound iteration select a node minimizing \(L_N\); otherwise select a deepest node, optionally restricted to descendants of a designated incumbent-seeking node. Apply valid fathoming before selection, process the chosen node, update \(U\), and insert all unfathomed children. A common schedule performs one best-bound iteration after every \(p\) depth-oriented iterations. Because best-bound iterations recur indefinitely and ties are resolved fairly, the hybrid cannot permanently ignore an active node defining the global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate depth-oriented incumbent search with recurrent best-bound steps, retaining valid fathoming and fairness so global-bound-defining nodes cannot be ignored forever.
assumptions_latex: Every active node has a valid lower bound and finite depth.
Best-bound iterations occur infinitely often unless the algorithm terminates.
Tie-breaking is fair among persistent minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\#\{t:\text{iteration }t\text{ uses best-bound selection}\}=\infty\) whenever infinitely many iterations occur.

notation.meaning: Number of depth-oriented steps per best-bound step.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The periodic hybrid is plausible, but the exact schedule and starvation claim are not supported by the supplied locator. Recurrent best-bound iterations and fair ties only protect nodes that persist as lower-bound minimizers; the statement needs a direct convergence source and that qualification.

children.title: Ordering-Performance Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs among bound progress, incumbent discovery, memory, plus tree exploration.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract valid search trees showing that neither bound priority nor depth preference uniformly minimizes processed nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There are finite valid branch-and-bound trees on which best-bound processes fewer nodes than a depth-oriented policy: after the root, a node \(B\) with lower bound \(0\) immediately yields an incumbent \(U=1\), while a deep subtree \(A\) has lower bounds at least \(1\); best-bound selects \(B\) and then fathoms \(A\), whereas depth preference may traverse \(A\) first. Conversely, there are trees with two root children of equal lower bound \(0\), where one child immediately yields \(U=0\) and the other begins an arbitrarily large zero-bound subtree. A best-bound tie rule may enter the large subtree, while a depth-oriented tie rule selecting the incumbent child first permits the entire other subtree to be fathomed. Thus no one of these ordering regimes uniformly minimizes processed nodes over all valid labeled search trees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different valid search trees favor different node orderings, so neither best-bound nor depth preference universally minimizes processed nodes.
assumptions_latex: Lower-bound labels are valid for their subtrees.
Nodes with lower bound at least the incumbent may be fathomed.
The compared policies use the indicated deterministic tie choices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nexists\,P\in\{\text{best-bound},\text{depth-oriented}\}\ \forall T:\ N_P(T)\le N_{P'}(T).

notation.meaning: Number of processed nodes under policy P on labeled tree T.

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Ordering Nondominance Families

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates branch-and-bound correctness from the amount and sequence of search work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two spatial branch-and-bound executions using identical exhaustive branching, valid node lower bounds, sound fathoming, and the same termination test, but different active-node orderings. Whenever either execution terminates with a finite incumbent \(U\) and active-node lower bound \(L\) satisfying \(U-L\le\varepsilon\), its incumbent is \(\varepsilon\)-globally optimal, independently of the ordering. For an infinite execution, ordering-independent convergence additionally requires fairness or another condition preventing indefinitely relevant nodes from being starved. The ordering can nevertheless change when incumbents and global bounds improve and therefore which nodes are processed before termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid gap certificates do not depend on node order, but convergence requires nonstarvation and the amount of work can depend strongly on the ordering.
assumptions_latex: All node bounds and fathoming rules are valid.
For asymptotic convergence, the ordering does not permanently starve relevant active nodes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U-L\le\varepsilon\Rightarrow f(\hat x)-f^*\le\varepsilon\text{ for every ordering satisfying the stated search conditions}.

notation.meaning: Minimum valid lower bound over active nodes.

knowledge_statements.title: Ordering-Invariant Validity and Ordering-Dependent Work
Ordering-Performance Tradeoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness is ordering-invariant under fairness, but search effort and incumbent discovery are not.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a spatial branch-and-bound method use the same exhaustive branching rule, valid node bounds, and sound fathoming tests under two fair active-node orderings. If both methods continue until \(U-L\le\varepsilon\), either ordering yields a valid \(\varepsilon\)-global solution certificate. Their computational behavior may nevertheless differ: best-bound selection immediately processes a node attaining \(L=\min_{N\in\mathcal A}L_N\), whereas depth orientation may reach feasible leaves and improve \(U\) sooner. No ordering universally minimizes processed nodes, because the effect of a tighter lower bound or incumbent depends on the unexplored tree. Hybrid policies trade recurrent global-bound progress against rapid incumbent search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fair node orderings preserve branch-and-bound correctness, but best-bound favors lower-bound progress, depth orientation favors incumbent discovery, and neither universally minimizes work.
assumptions_latex: Branching is exhaustive and every node bound and fathoming test is valid.
Termination requires an incumbent-to-global-bound gap at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U-L\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(f(\hat x)-f^*\le\varepsilon\), independently of the fair node ordering.

notation.meaning: Minimum lower bound over active nodes.

source_refs.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39
