children.title: Node Elimination Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Node elimination through feasibility status and incumbent comparison.

children.title: Infeasibility Fathoming
children.top_down_role: Node elimination based on certified absence of feasible descendants.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility Fathoming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node elimination from an infeasible outer relaxation, with a Farkas certificate in the linear case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_N\) be the original feasible set restricted to node \(N\), and let \(R_N\supseteq F_N\) be its relaxation. If \(R_N=\varnothing\), then \(F_N=\varnothing\), so the node may be fathomed without losing a feasible or globally optimal point. For a linear relaxation \(R_N=\{z:A_Nz\le b_N\}\), a directly checkable infeasibility certificate is a vector \(y\) satisfying \[y\ge0,\qquad A_N^{\mathsf T}y=0,\qquad b_N^{\mathsf T}y<0.\] Indeed, these displayed relations are incompatible with any \(z\) satisfying \(A_Nz\le b_N\). Numerical solver status alone is not a mathematical certificate unless accompanied by a validated ray or another rigorous infeasibility test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fathom a node when an outer relaxation is empty. For linear relaxations, a nonnegative Farkas ray with zero combined coefficients and negative combined right side certifies emptiness.
assumptions_latex: Certificate equalities and inequalities are validated exactly or with rigorous error bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_N=\varnothing\Rightarrow F_N=\varnothing\), hence node \(N\) is safely fathomed.

notation.meaning: Original feasible region within node N.
Outer relaxation of the node feasible region.

source_refs.locator: 2.13.3 Conic Programming p. 80
7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

source_witnesses.locator: 2.13.3 Conic Programming p. 80
7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

children.title: Bound-Dominance Fathoming
children.top_down_role: Node elimination when its valid bound cannot improve the incumbent.

assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb N\), \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(F\subseteq X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
\(L(R)\) is a valid lower bound on \(F\cap R\).
\(U\) is attained by a known point \(\bar x\in F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\) is safely fathomed when \(L(R)\geq U-\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Valid lower bound for the objective over the feasible portion of the node.
Objective value of the incumbent feasible point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incumbent-based closure of a minimization node using a valid relaxation lower bound.

source_refs.locator: 3.6 Finite epsilon-Convergence and epsilon-Global Optimality p. 87

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb N\), \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(F\subseteq X\), \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). Consider minimizing \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) over \(F\), and let \(R\subseteq X\) be a branch-and-bound node. Suppose \(L(R)\leq\inf\{f(x):x\in F\cap R\}\), while \(U=f(\bar x)\) for a known \(\bar x\in F\). For an absolute tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), the inequality \[L(R)\geq U-\varepsilon\] certifies that every \(x\in F\cap R\) satisfies \(f(x)\geq U-\varepsilon\). Hence \(R\) may be fathomed without excluding any point capable of improving the incumbent by more than \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node is safely discarded when its valid lower bound is no smaller than the incumbent value minus the prescribed absolute tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Dominance Fathoming

source_witnesses.locator: 3.6 Finite epsilon-Convergence and epsilon-Global Optimality p. 87

children.title: Fathoming-Certificate Strength
children.top_down_role: Comparative rigor plus decisiveness of node-elimination evidence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extensional comparison of sound node-elimination predicates on one fixed class of node states, excluding computational cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal N\) be a fixed class of node states and let \(C_1,C_2:\mathcal N\to\{0,1\}\) be sound fathoming predicates. Define \(C_1\succeq C_2\) when \[C_2(s)=1\Longrightarrow C_1(s)=1\qquad\text{for every }s\in\mathcal N.\] Equivalently, the acceptance set of \(C_2\) is contained in that of \(C_1\). Strength is strict when the inclusion is strict, and the predicates are extensionally equivalent when both implications hold. This ordering measures decisiveness only and does not compare the cost of producing or validating the certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One sound fathoming predicate is logically stronger when it safely closes every node closed by the other on the same state class; this does not compare computational cost.
assumptions_latex: \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) are sound on the same fixed node-state class \(\mathcal N\).
Certificate strength is interpreted extensionally, independently of evaluation cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_1\succeq C_2\iff\{s\in\mathcal N:C_2(s)=1\}\subseteq\{s\in\mathcal N:C_1(s)=1\}.

notation.meaning: Fixed class of compared node states.

knowledge_statements.title: Logical Strength of Fathoming Predicates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotonicity under Stronger Valid Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength comparison of bound-dominance predicates using a common node-state class and cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(s\in\mathcal N\), let \(L_1(s)\) and \(L_2(s)\) be valid lower bounds with \(L_1(s)\ge L_2(s)\), and let both tests use the same cutoff \(\tau(s)\). If \(C_i(s)=1\) exactly when \(L_i(s)\ge\tau(s)\), then \[C_2(s)=1\Longrightarrow C_1(s)=1.\] Consequently, the predicate using \(L_1\) is at least as strong as the predicate using \(L_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a common cutoff, a pointwise larger valid lower bound gives an at-least-as-decisive bound-dominance certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(L_1(s)\) and \(L_2(s)\) are valid bounds for the same node state.
Both predicates use the same cutoff \(\tau(s)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_1\succeq C_2\).

notation.meaning: Valid lower bound used by predicate i.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity under Stronger Valid Lower Bounds

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Incomparability of Infeasibility and Bound-Dominance Predicates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical comparison of the two principal sibling elimination mechanisms on a state class containing both relevant witness types.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the compared class contains an infeasible node that is certified empty but for which bound dominance is not established, and also a feasible node whose valid lower bound satisfies \(L(N)\ge U-\varepsilon\). The first node is closed by infeasibility but not by the stated bound-dominance predicate, whereas the second is closed by bound dominance and cannot be certified empty. Thus neither predicate is logically stronger than the other on this class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infeasibility and bound dominance are generally incomparable because each can close nodes that the other cannot.
assumptions_latex: The state class contains a certified-infeasible node without an established bound-dominance certificate.
The state class contains a feasible node satisfying \(L(N)\ge U-\varepsilon\).
Both predicates are sound on the compared class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_{\mathrm{inf}}\not\succeq C_{\mathrm{bd}}\quad\text{and}\quad C_{\mathrm{bd}}\not\succeq C_{\mathrm{inf}}.
knowledge_statements.title: Incomparability of Infeasibility and Bound-Dominance Predicates
Fathoming-Certificate Strength
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical comparison of safe node-elimination predicates on a fixed problem class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal N\) be a class of branch-and-bound node states and let \(C_1,C_2:\mathcal N\to\{0,1\}\) be sound fathoming predicates, where \(C_i(s)=1\) authorizes elimination of the node represented by \(s\). Certificate \(C_1\) is at least as strong as \(C_2\) on \(\mathcal N\) precisely when \[\{s\in\mathcal N:C_2(s)=1\}\subseteq\{s\in\mathcal N:C_1(s)=1\}.\] It is strictly stronger when this inclusion is strict. Two certificates are equivalent on \(\mathcal N\) when both inclusions hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One sound fathoming certificate is stronger than another when it closes every node closed by the other, and possibly additional nodes.
assumptions_latex: \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) are sound on the same node-state class \(\mathcal N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_1\succeq C_2\) exactly when \(C_2(s)=1\Rightarrow C_1(s)=1\) for every \(s\in\mathcal N\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed ordering of sound Boolean certificates is mathematically coherent and definition is the correct content kind, but the nonstandard local terminology and exact formalization have no cited source or explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: Ambiguous Elimination Boundary
children.top_down_role: Nodes lacking sufficient evidence for either feasibility-based or dominance-based elimination.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a bound-dominance decision when a rigorous enclosure of the exact valid node bound crosses the incumbent cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the exact valid node lower bound satisfy \(L(R)\in[\underline L_R,\overline L_R]\), and let \(\tau=U-\varepsilon\) be the bound-dominance cutoff. If \(\underline L_R\ge\tau\), dominance fathoming is certified. If \(\overline L_R<\tau\), the bound is certified not to establish dominance. When \(\underline L_R<\tau\le\overline L_R\), the enclosure admits exact-bound values on both sides of the cutoff, so it supports neither conclusion and the node cannot safely be eliminated from this comparison alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rigorous bound enclosure that straddles the incumbent cutoff cannot by itself certify either bound-dominance fathoming or its failure.
assumptions_latex: \(L(R)\) is a valid lower bound and \(L(R)\in[\underline L_R,\overline L_R]\) is rigorously certified.
\(U\) is a feasible incumbent value and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
The cutoff convention is fathoming when \(L(R)\ge U-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline L_R<U-\varepsilon\le\overline L_R\) is an ambiguous bound-dominance region.

notation.meaning: Certified lower and upper endpoints enclosing the exact valid node bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Certified-Bound Enclosure Straddling Boundary
Ambiguous Elimination Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical uncertainty region in which bound dominance cannot certify node elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a computed node bound \(\widehat L(R)\) have a certified error radius \(\delta_R\geq0\), so that the exact valid bound \(L(R)\) is known only to lie in \([\widehat L(R)-\delta_R,\widehat L(R)+\delta_R]\). Given incumbent \(U\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), bound-dominance fathoming is certified if \(\widehat L(R)-\delta_R\geq U-\varepsilon\), and non-dominance is certified if \(\widehat L(R)+\delta_R<U-\varepsilon\). If \[\widehat L(R)-\delta_R<U-\varepsilon\leq\widehat L(R)+\delta_R,\] the available enclosure supports neither conclusion; eliminating \(R\) solely from \(\widehat L(R)\) is unsafe.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the certified bound-error interval crosses the incumbent cutoff, neither elimination nor non-elimination follows from that bound computation alone.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is a feasible incumbent value and \(\varepsilon\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An enclosure straddling \(U-\varepsilon\) is an ambiguous elimination boundary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The interval test is internally coherent and failure_boundary fits the terminal container, but the certified-error variant has no source supporting its precise enclosure assumptions and strict versus non-strict cutoff conventions.

children.title: Relaxation-Exactness Fathoming
children.top_down_role: Node closure when relaxation structure certifies realizability or optimality.

assumptions_latex: The relaxation optimum \(L(R)\) is a valid lower bound on the original node optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\) is optimal on \(F\cap R\), and \(R\) may be fathomed after the incumbent update.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node closure when a relaxation optimizer is realizable by the original quadratic program.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(f:F\to\mathbb R\) be the original objective, and let \(R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a node. Suppose a valid relaxation has feasible region \(\mathcal R(R)\), objective \(\phi:\mathcal R(R)\to\mathbb R\), and attained optimum \[L(R)=\min\{\phi(y):y\in\mathcal R(R)\}\leq\inf\{f(x):x\in F\cap R\}.\] If an optimal relaxation point \(y^*\in\mathcal R(R)\) yields a point \(x^*\in F\cap R\) satisfying \(\phi(y^*)=f(x^*)\), then \[L(R)=f(x^*)=\min\{f(x):x\in F\cap R\}.\] Thus \(x^*\) is node-optimal. After updating the incumbent with \(f(x^*)\), the node may be fathomed because its relaxation lower bound is attained by an original feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a valid relaxation optimum maps to an original feasible point with the same value, that point is node-optimal and the node may be closed.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Exactness Fathoming

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Value Exactness Without a Realizability Witness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits exactness fathoming when only equality of optimal values is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v_R\) be the relaxation optimum and \(v_N\) the original node optimum. Equality \(v_R=v_N\) alone does not recover an original feasible optimizer or provide an incumbent. Without a certified relaxation optimizer representing some \(x\in F\cap R\) with objective \(v_R\), realizability-based fathoming cannot be invoked. If an independently certified incumbent satisfies \(U=v_R\), ordinary bound-dominance fathoming is valid instead.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Value equality alone does not recover a feasible optimizer; realizability or an independent matching incumbent is still needed for node closure.
assumptions_latex: No relaxation optimizer has been certified as an original feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v_R=v_N\not\Rightarrow\text{recoverability},\qquad U=v_R\Rightarrow\text{bound-dominance fathoming}.
knowledge_statements.title: Value Exactness Without a Realizability Witness

knowledge_statements.title: Localized Bound Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic exactness of node lower bounds under localization around any retained point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and let \(L(R)\) be a valid lower bound for every compact node \(R\subseteq X\). The bound scheme is locally consistent on \(F\) if, for every \(x\in F\) and every nested sequence \(R_1\supseteq R_2\supseteq\cdots\) with \(x\in R_k\) and \(\operatorname{diam}(R_k)\to0\), \[f(x)-L(R_k)\longrightarrow0.\] For continuous \(f\), this condition states that localization removes the relaxation underestimation at every feasible limiting point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower-bounding scheme is locally consistent when its gap at every feasible point vanishes along every nested node sequence shrinking to that point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{diam}(R_k)\to0\) and \(x\in R_k\) imply \(L(R_k)\to f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Valid lower bound associated with node R.
Diameter of a node in the ambient norm.

source_refs.locator: 2.2 Convergence Properties of Adaptive Partition Algorithms p. 59

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2 Convergence Properties of Adaptive Partition Algorithms p. 59

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Diameter-Modulus Criterion for Local Bound Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient condition converting a node-diameter relaxation-error estimate into local consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L(R)\leq\inf_{z\in F\cap R}f(z)\) for every compact node with \(F\cap R\neq\varnothing\). Suppose \(\omega:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)\) satisfies \(\omega(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\) and \[0\leq\inf_{z\in F\cap R}f(z)-L(R)\leq\omega(\operatorname{diam}R).\] If \(f\) is continuous, then every nested sequence \(R_k\ni x\in F\) with \(\operatorname{diam}(R_k)\to0\) satisfies \(L(R_k)\to f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid node bound whose relaxation error is controlled by a modulus vanishing with node diameter is locally consistent.
assumptions_latex: \(\omega(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\) and bounds the node relaxation gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in R_k\) and \(\operatorname{diam}(R_k)\to0\) imply \(L(R_k)\to f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Valid lower bound on node R.

knowledge_statements.title: Diameter-Modulus Criterion for Local Bound Consistency

children.title: Exhaustive Partition Refinement
children.top_down_role: Coverage and shrinking behavior across persistent search regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Exhaustive Partition Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Refinement condition excluding persistent positive-diameter regions from an infinite search path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A branching rule on compact nodes is exhaustively refining if every infinite nested chain of generated nodes \(R_1\supset R_2\supset\cdots\) that remains eligible for selection satisfies \[\operatorname{diam}(R_k)\longrightarrow0.\] Equivalently for rectangular nodes, no coordinate interval having positive limiting width may persist along such a chain. This is a refinement condition, not merely a requirement that infinitely many nodes be created: it requires localization along every infinite unresolved branch that the selection policy can retain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refinement is exhaustive when every infinite unresolved branch consists of nodes whose diameters tend to zero in all coordinates.
assumptions_latex: All generated nodes are compact subsets of a common compact search region.
Children cover the feasible portion of their parent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every infinite eligible nested node chain has diameter converging to zero.

notation.meaning: Node at depth k along a nested branch.
Node diameter in a fixed norm.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Balanced Near-Longest-Edge Splitting Implies Exhaustive Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient rectangular splitting rule for shrinkage of every infinite descendant chain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_k=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i^k,u_i^k]\) be an infinite nested chain of bounded boxes. Fix \(\gamma\in(0,1]\) and \(\eta\in(0,\tfrac12]\). At each split choose a coordinate \(i_k\) with \[u_{i_k}^k-\ell_{i_k}^k\geq\gamma\max_i(u_i^k-\ell_i^k),\] and split it so that both child widths in that coordinate are at most \((1-\eta)(u_{i_k}^k-\ell_{i_k}^k)\). Then every infinite descendant chain satisfies \(\operatorname{diam}(R_k)\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly balanced splitting of a coordinate within a fixed factor of the largest width makes every infinite box branch shrink to a point.
assumptions_latex: \(\gamma\in(0,1]\) and \(\eta\in(0,\tfrac12]\) are fixed independently of depth.
Every child is obtained by the stated balanced coordinate split.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{diam}(R_k)\to0\) along every infinite nested descendant chain.

notation.meaning: Required fraction of the current maximum coordinate width.
Box on an infinite descendant chain.

children.title: Coupled Convergence Architecture
children.top_down_role: Interaction between bound consistency and exhaustive refinement in global-gap closure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global lower- and upper-bound convergence under finite branching, monotone consistent bounds, fair processing, exhaustive localization, and consistent feasible recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be nonempty and compact and let \(f:F\to\mathbb R\) be continuous. Suppose a spatial branch-and-bound method maintains finitely many compact active nodes covering every unfathomed feasible point. Every retained node intersects \(F\), every split has finitely many covering children, node bounds are valid and satisfy \(L(C)\ge L(R)\) for each child \(C\) of \(R\), and every active node is eventually processed unless validly fathomed. Assume every infinite unresolved descendant chain has diameter tending to zero, the bounds are locally consistent, and feasible recovery on the nested nodes containing a global minimizer \(x^*\) returns objective values tending to \(f(x^*)\). Then, with \(L_k\) the least active-node bound and \(U_k\) the incumbent value, \[L_k\to f^*,\qquad U_k\to f^*,\qquad U_k-L_k\to0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite branching, hereditary valid bounds, fair exhaustive localization, local bound consistency, and consistent feasible recovery jointly close the global branch-and-bound gap.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is nonempty and compact, and \(f\) is continuous.
Retained active nodes intersect \(F\), splits are finite and covering, and fathoming is valid.
Child bounds dominate their parent bound, every active node is eventually processed unless fathomed, and every infinite unresolved branch shrinks to diameter zero.
Bounds are locally consistent and feasible recovery converges along nodes containing a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_k\to f^*\), \(U_k\to f^*\), and \(U_k-L_k\to0\).

notation.meaning: Least lower bound among active nodes at iteration k.
Incumbent feasible objective value at iteration k.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Bound-Refinement Convergence
Coupled Convergence Architecture
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global convergence obtained by coupling exhaustive refinement, consistent bounds, and incumbent discovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be nonempty and compact and let \(f:F\to\mathbb R\) be continuous. Consider a spatial branch-and-bound method with valid node lower bounds, exhaustive refinement, and localized bound consistency. Assume its fair selection rule eventually processes every node whose lower bound stays below the incumbent cutoff, and that feasible-point generation along nodes shrinking to any global minimizer \(x^*\) produces values converging to \(f(x^*)\). If \(L_k\) is the least active-node lower bound and \(U_k\) the incumbent value, then \[L_k\longrightarrow f(x^*),\qquad U_k\longrightarrow f(x^*).\] Consequently, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), the method eventually has \(U_k-L_k\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhaustive refinement, locally consistent bounds, fair node selection, and incumbent discovery jointly force lower and upper bounds to the global optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is nonempty and compact, and \(f\) is continuous.
Refinement is exhaustive and node lower bounds are valid and locally consistent.
Selection is fair and feasible-point generation approaches a minimizer along its shrinking nodes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_k\to f^*\), \(U_k\to f^*\), and every positive optimality tolerance is eventually attained.

notation.meaning: Least lower bound among active nodes at iteration k.
Incumbent objective value at iteration k.

children.title: Refinement Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Search configurations where insufficient localization prevents convergence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Selection Starvation Despite Exact Node Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent gap caused by permanently postponing the optimizer-containing node despite exact node bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Minimize \(f(x)=(x-1)^2\) on \([0,1]\), assigning every node the exact bound \(L(R)=\min_{x\in R}f(x)\). After splitting into \([0,\tfrac12]\) and \([\tfrac12,1]\), retain the right node but thereafter process only descendants of the left node. Sampling \(x=\tfrac12\) gives \(U_k=\tfrac14\); no point in the left subtree improves it, while the unprocessed right node has lower bound \(0\). Thus \(L_k=0\) and \(U_k-L_k=\tfrac14\) indefinitely, although the bound scheme is exact and locally consistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact locally consistent bounds do not ensure convergence when selection permanently starves the node containing the optimizer.
assumptions_latex: An active node may be retained indefinitely without selection.
Every node lower bound equals its exact restricted optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_k-L_k=\tfrac14\) for all subsequent iterations.

notation.meaning: Exact restricted minimum on node R.

knowledge_statements.title: Selection Starvation Despite Exact Node Bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent gap caused solely by a valid but nonconsistent lower-bound rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Minimize \(f(x)=1+(x-\tfrac12)^2\) on \([0,1]\). Refine the domain by exhaustive dyadic partitions, use \(L(R)=0\) for every nonempty node, and take the exact incumbent \(x=\tfrac12\), so \(U_k=1\). Although the bound is valid because \(f\geq1\), every active partition has global lower bound \(L_k=0\). Hence \(U_k-L_k=1\) for every \(k\), despite exhaustive refinement and exact incumbent discovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhaustive shrinking and an exact incumbent do not close the global gap when valid node bounds are not locally consistent.
assumptions_latex: The domain is exhaustively refined by dyadic partitions.
The lower-bound rule is valid but not required to be locally consistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_k-L_k=1\) for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.title: Exhaustive Refinement Without Bound Consistency
Refinement Failure Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure when an optimal region is retained but never selected or localized.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Minimize \(f(x)=(x-1)^2\) on \(F=[0,1]\). Start with incumbent \(x=0\), so \(U=1\), and use the valid but nonconsistent bound \(L(R)=0\) for every nonempty node. Partition \([0,1]\) into \([0,\tfrac12]\) and \([\tfrac12,1]\), but thereafter select and refine only descendants of \([0,\tfrac12]\); retain the right node without processing it. The global minimizer \(x^*=1\) is never sampled, \(U_k=1\), and the active lower bound remains \(0\). Thus neither infinite branching nor bound validity alone implies convergence when exhaustive refinement and fair selection fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid bound and infinitely many branches do not ensure convergence if the node containing the optimizer is permanently retained but never processed.
assumptions_latex: The selection policy may indefinitely postpone an active node.
The lower-bound rule is required to be valid but not locally consistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The search has \(U_k-L_k=1\) for every \(k\) although infinitely many refinements occur.

children.title: Branching Misalignment
children.top_down_role: Partitions that fail to target the sources of relaxation error.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Irrelevant-Coordinate Branching Leaves a Bilinear Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A concrete lifted-QP relaxation whose positive gap persists when branching targets only an unrelated variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min\{-xy:x+y=1,\ 0\leq x,y,z\leq1\}.\] Its optimum is \(-\tfrac14\). Introduce \(w=xy\), minimize \(-w\), and impose the McCormick relaxation for \(w=xy\) over \([0,1]^2\). The relaxed point \(x=y=\tfrac12,\ w=\tfrac12\) is feasible, so the relaxation value is \(-\tfrac12\), giving gap \(\tfrac14\). If every branch splits only the unrelated coordinate \(z\), the domains of \(x\) and \(y\), the relaxation value, and the gap remain unchanged at every descendant node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly splitting an unrelated variable leaves a quarter-unit bilinear relaxation gap unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The lifted product is relaxed only by the McCormick inequalities on the unchanged unit intervals for x and y.
Branching partitions only the unrelated coordinate z.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The node relaxation value remains \(-\tfrac12\) while the true value remains \(-\tfrac14\), so the gap is always \(\tfrac14\).

notation.meaning: Variable selected for branching but absent from the objective, equality, and lifted product.

knowledge_statements.title: Irrelevant-Coordinate Branching Leaves a Bilinear Gap

knowledge_statements.statement_title: McCormick Error Persists Under Irrelevant-Coordinate Splits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sharp envelope-error criterion showing why splitting coordinates absent from an error-driving product does not improve its relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(w=xy\) on \([\ell_x,u_x]\times[\ell_y,u_y]\), the greatest upward or downward deviation permitted by the McCormick relaxation from the product graph is \[\frac{(u_x-\ell_x)(u_y-\ell_y)}{4}.\] Consequently, partitioning only variables absent from this product leaves its McCormick error unchanged. The product relaxation becomes uniformly exact only if at least one factor width tends to zero, or another valid strengthening removes the error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Splitting variables unrelated to a bilinear product leaves its McCormick error unchanged; shrinking a factor width makes that product error vanish.
assumptions_latex: The product is relaxed by its four McCormick inequalities on the current factor box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Irrelevant-coordinate splits do not change the error \((u_x-\ell_x)(u_y-\ell_y)/4\).

notation.meaning: Lifted variable representing the product xy.
Current width of the x interval.
Current width of the y interval.

knowledge_statements.title: McCormick Error Persists Under Irrelevant-Coordinate Splits
Branching Misalignment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent relaxation error when branching leaves all error-driving variable widths bounded away from zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_k\) be a nested branch of rectangular nodes and let \(L(R_k)\) be relaxation lower bounds. Branching is misaligned with the relaxation error on this branch if there exist \(\eta>0\) and an infinite index set \(K\) such that \[\inf\{f(x):x\in F\cap R_k\}-L(R_k)\geq\eta\qquad(k\in K),\] while every variable or product responsible for this gap retains a positive-width domain. In particular, repeatedly splitting coordinates absent from the nonconvex terms need not reduce their convex-envelope error. The resulting branch violates localized bound consistency and cannot be closed by arbitrarily small tolerances using those bounds alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branching is misaligned when it refines irrelevant coordinates while the widths causing relaxation error persist, leaving a positive lower-bound gap.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation error has identifiable positive-width driving variables or terms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A persistent gap \(\eta>0\) prevents localized bound consistency along the branch.

notation.meaning: Relaxation lower bound on the kth node.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A branch whose error-driving widths stay positive need not have diameter tending to zero, so a persistent gap along that branch does not violate the shard's stated definition of localized bound consistency, which applies only to shrinking node sequences. The cited section must be inspected to determine a correct failure statement and the required branching assumptions.

children.title: Tailing-Explosion Failure Cascade
children.top_down_role: Slow global-gap closure across many weakly distinguished nodes.

children.title: Bound Tailing
children.top_down_role: Persistently slow improvement of node lower bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound Tailing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subgeometric late-stage decay of the active global optimality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_k=U_k-L_k>0\) denote the certified global optimality gap after iteration \(k\). A search exhibits asymptotic bound tailing when \[g_k\longrightarrow0\quad\text{and}\quad \frac{g_{k+1}}{g_k}\longrightarrow1.\] The second relation excludes any eventual uniform contraction \(g_{k+1}\leq\rho g_k\) with \(\rho<1\). Consequently, although the bounds converge, the iterations required for each additional fixed relative reduction can grow without bound, producing slow closure near the requested tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bound tailing occurs when the certified gap converges to zero but its successive contraction ratio tends to one, ruling out an eventual geometric rate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No \(\rho<1\) satisfies \(g_{k+1}\leq\rho g_k\) for every sufficiently large \(k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ratio condition is mathematically meaningful, but the record stipulates a nonstandard definition of bound tailing without evidence. Because the statement defines the phenomenon rather than asserting an established property of a specified algorithm, definition would be the more accurate content kind if a source supports this terminology.

children.title: Tree Explosion
children.top_down_role: Rapid growth of active nodes under weak pruning.

assumptions_latex: The rooted search tree has branching factor exactly \(b\geq2\) at every node of depth less than \(d\).
Every node of depth less than \(d\) is processed and expanded; in particular, no such node is fathomed or otherwise terminated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly \(b^d\) nodes at depth \(d\) and \((b^{d+1}-1)/(b-1)\) total nodes through depth \(d\) are generated.

notation.meaning: First depth at which fathoming or other termination may occur.
Total number of generated nodes through depth d.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial node growth forced by complete uniform expansion before fathoming becomes effective.

source_refs.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a rooted search tree in which every node of depth less than \(d\) is processed and produces exactly \(b\geq2\) children. Equivalently, the tree is fully expanded through depth \(d\), with no node fathomed or otherwise terminated at a smaller depth. The algorithm then generates \[N_d=1+b+\cdots+b^d=\frac{b^{d+1}-1}{b-1}\] nodes, including \(b^d\) nodes at depth \(d\). Thus a relaxation regime that forces complete \(b\)-way expansion through depth \(d(\varepsilon)\) before an \(\varepsilon\)-fathoming test can succeed requires at least \(b^{d(\varepsilon)}\) generated nodes. This bound counts node generation and is independent of the per-node relaxation cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete uniform b-way expansion through depth d generates exponentially many nodes in d.

children.title: Weak Node Differentiation
children.top_down_role: Near-indistinguishable node bounds that delay dominance decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Node Differentiation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sibling lower bounds provide too little separation for informative node ordering or early pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a parent node \(R\) have children \(R_1,\ldots,R_m\) with valid lower bounds \(L(R_i)\). For a scale \(\eta\geq0\), the children are weakly differentiated when \[\max_{1\leq i\leq m}L(R_i)-\min_{1\leq i\leq m}L(R_i)\leq\eta\quad\text{and}\quad \min_{1\leq i\leq m}L(R_i)-L(R)\leq\eta.\] The first inequality limits the information available for bound-based sibling ordering; the second shows that branching has produced little improvement in the best surviving lower bound. When \(\eta\) is small relative to the incumbent gap, bound-based selection and fathoming remain largely unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Children are weakly differentiated when their lower bounds are nearly equal and the best child scarcely improves the parent bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Sibling ordering has resolution at most \(\eta\), while the best child improves the parent bound by at most \(\eta\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two inequalities form a coherent proposed condition and the content kind fits, but the differentiation scale and its interpretation are nonstandard local terminology with no cited source or explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: Tailing-to-Explosion Escalation
children.top_down_role: Propagation of slow bound progress into excessive tree growth.

knowledge_statements.title: Tailing-to-Explosion Escalation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spatial branching with at least two children per surviving region and no pruning during a tailing episode.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_0\) be an active region in a minimization branch-and-bound tree, let \(U\) be the incumbent cutoff, and let \(d\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}\). Suppose every surviving region is divided into at least two children and, for \(d\) successive levels, every generated child \(R\) is feasible and has relaxation lower bound \(L(R)<U\). Then no child is eliminated by infeasibility or bound dominance during those levels, and the subtree rooted at \(R_0\) contains at least \(2^d\) active descendants at depth \(d\). Thus a tail in which branching fails to improve bounds enough for pruning produces exponential node growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If branching creates at least two children per surviving region for a nonnegative integer d levels without infeasibility or cutoff pruning, at least 2^d regions survive; persistent bound tailing therefore becomes tree explosion.
assumptions_latex: A spatial branch-and-bound method divides every surviving active region into at least two children.
The number of successive levels satisfies \(d\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}\).
At each of these \(d\) levels, relaxation bounds remain below the incumbent cutoff and no region is fathomed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At least \(2^d\) descendants survive at depth \(d\), so persistent bound tailing escalates into exponential tree growth.

notation.meaning: number of consecutive unproductive branching levels
