children.title: Feasibility-Based Bound Tightening
children.top_down_role: Interval and constraint-propagation families specialized to linear and quadratic relations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe coordinate contraction after interval bounding the nonisolated terms of a quadratic relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(a x_j^2+b x_j+h(x_{-j})\le0\) on the current box and interval evaluation certifies \(h(x_{-j})\ge\underline h\). Every feasible point then satisfies \(a x_j^2+b x_j+\underline h\le0\). Hence intersecting \([\ell_j,u_j]\) with \(\{t:a t^2+b t+\underline h\le0\}\) is a valid contractor. When \(a>0\), the scalar sublevel set is the interval between the real roots, or empty if the discriminant is negative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower-bound the nonisolated terms, solve the resulting scalar quadratic inequality, and intersect its solution set with the coordinate interval.
assumptions_latex: The original relation is \(a x_j^2+b x_j+h(x_{-j})\le0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible value of \(x_j\) lies in \([\ell_j,u_j]\cap\{t:a t^2+b t+\underline h\le0\}\).

notation.meaning: certified interval lower bound on the nonisolated terms

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Isolation Contractor

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-bound propagation from one affine inequality over a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\), \(x_i\in[\ell_i,u_i]\), and \(m_{-j}=\sum_{i\ne j}\min\{a_i\ell_i,a_i u_i\}\), every feasible point satisfies \(x_j\le(b-m_{-j})/a_j\) when \(a_j>0\), and \(x_j\ge(b-m_{-j})/a_j\) when \(a_j<0\). Intersecting the corresponding endpoint with \([\ell_j,u_j]\) gives the exact coordinate projection implied by that row and the other current intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear row contracts a coordinate by assigning all other terms their most favorable interval values and solving the remaining scalar inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The endpoint update retains every feasible box point and is exact for the coordinate projection of this single row.

notation.meaning: minimum possible contribution from all terms except coordinate j

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Single-Row Linear Contractor

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inability of interval-bound contraction to remove noninterval infeasible values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(x\in[0,1]\), the quadratic equation \(x(1-x)=0\) has feasible set \(\{0,1\}\), whose interval hull is \([0,1]\). Consequently, every contractor whose output must be one interval containing all feasible values returns the unchanged interval, although every \(x\in(0,1)\) is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A box contractor may make no progress when disconnected feasible values have the same interval hull as the original domain.
assumptions_latex: The contractor returns one interval containing every feasible value.
knowledge_statements.title: Box-Hull Propagation Blind Spot

assumptions_latex: The current domain is a finite box \(B=[\ell,u]\subset\mathbb R^n\).
Every propagation operation is a valid interval consequence of the linear and quadratic constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned box contains every feasible point of the original constraints lying in \(B\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: interval constraint propagation contracts domains by valid constraint-wise implications
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-wise interval propagation for linear and quadratic relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(B=[\ell,u]\) and constraints \(g_i(x)\le 0\), initialize \(B^0=B\). During pass \(k\), apply each valid contractor \(P_i\), obtained by interval evaluation and algebraic isolation of variables in \(g_i\), and set \(B^{k,i}=B^{k,i-1}\cap P_i(B^{k,i-1})\). Stop when a box is empty, no endpoint changes beyond a prescribed tolerance, or a pass limit is reached. Return the final box \(B'\). Validity requires \(\{x\in B:g_i(x)\le0\}\subseteq P_i(B)\), which implies that \(B'\) contains every point satisfying all original constraints in \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated interval propagation through linear and quadratic constraints removes impossible variable values while retaining every feasible point in the current box.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Based Bound Tightening

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The feasibility-preserving propagation algorithm fits the container and is mathematically coherent, but no inspectable source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Optimization-Based Bound Tightening
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary relaxation families used to infer sharper variable domains.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe node elimination detected by an OBBT auxiliary relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If F\subseteq R and R=\varnothing, then F=\varnothing. Thus certified infeasibility of an OBBT auxiliary problem having feasible region R certifies node infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified infeasibility of the valid OBBT relaxation safely eliminates the node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Infeasibility Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: What exact coordinate optimization over a relaxation does and does not recover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact minimization and maximization of every coordinate over nonempty R produce \operatorname{hull}_{\Box}(R)=\prod_j[\inf_{x\in R}x_j,\sup_{x\in R}x_j]. This box can contain points outside R and, when F\subsetneq R, can strictly contain \operatorname{hull}_{\Box}(F). Exact OBBT therefore removes every coordinate value excluded by R but does not preserve correlations or repair relaxation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact OBBT recovers the relaxation's coordinate hull, not its correlations or necessarily the feasible set's coordinate hull.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{hull}_{\Box}(F)\subseteq\operatorname{hull}_{\Box}(R),\quad \operatorname{hull}_{\Box}(R)\supsetneq R\ \text{is possible}.
knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate-Hull Exactness Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate bounds produced by nested valid relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If F\subseteq R_1\subseteq R_2, then for every coordinate j, \inf_{x\in R_2}x_j\le\inf_{x\in R_1}x_j and \sup_{x\in R_1}x_j\le\sup_{x\in R_2}x_j. Hence exact OBBT over the stronger relaxation R_1 cannot yield a weaker coordinate interval than exact OBBT over R_2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stronger nested relaxation produces coordinate bounds at least as tight as a weaker relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: [\inf_{R_1}x_j,\sup_{R_1}x_j]\subseteq[\inf_{R_2}x_j,\sup_{R_2}x_j]\quad\forall j.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Dominance Monotonicity

assumptions_latex: The current relaxation feasible set \(R\subseteq[\ell,u]\) contains the feasible set of the node.
Each auxiliary minimization or maximization is solved with a certified valid bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The updated bounds are valid for every point in \(R\), hence for every feasible node solution.

notation.meaning: tightened lower and upper bounds for variable j

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: optimization-based bound tightening uses auxiliary coordinate optimization over a valid relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-wise auxiliary optimization over a valid node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each selected coordinate \(j\), solve or validly bound the auxiliary problems \(m_j=\inf\{x_j:x\in R\}\) and \(M_j=\sup\{x_j:x\in R\}\). Update \(\ell'_j=\max\{\ell_j,\underline m_j\}\) and \(u'_j=\min\{u_j,\overline M_j\}\), where \(\underline m_j\le m_j\) and \(\overline M_j\ge M_j\) are certified bounds; exact auxiliary optima may be used directly. Retain unprocessed coordinates unchanged and declare the node infeasible if some \(\ell'_j>u'_j\). Because every \(x\in R\) satisfies \(m_j\le x_j\le M_j\), the resulting box preserves the entire relaxation feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize each selected variable over a valid node relaxation and intersect the resulting coordinate ranges with the current bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimization-Based Bound Tightening

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coordinate-wise auxiliary optimization algorithm and certified-bound directions are valid and fit optimization-based bound tightening, but the record has no cited source.

children.title: Dual-Cutoff Domain Reduction
children.top_down_role: Contraction derived from relaxation dual information and incumbent cutoffs.

children.title: Dual-Driven Domain Reduction
children.top_down_role: Variable-domain contraction derived from relaxation dual information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous variable contraction from a certified reduced-cost inequality and incumbent gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a relaxation on a domain with \(x_j\ge\ell_j\) has certified value \(L\) and a dual certificate establishes \(f(x)\ge L+r_j(x_j-\ell_j)\) for every original feasible \(x\), where \(r_j>0\). If \(U\) is a verified feasible incumbent value, every strictly improving point satisfies \(x_j<\ell_j+(U-L)/r_j\). Thus the upper bound may be contracted according to this threshold, using an endpoint convention consistent with whether ties must be retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive certified reduced cost converts the incumbent gap into a safe upper bound on movement from a variable's lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)\ge L+r_j(x_j-\ell_j)\) is valid for every original feasible point in the tested domain.
\(U\) is the value of a verified feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)<U\Rightarrow x_j<\ell_j+(U-L)/r_j\).
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Cost Variable Contraction

assumptions_latex: A relaxation provides a valid lower bound and a dual certificate for every imposed variable restriction.
The primal problem is a minimization problem with incumbent cutoff \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any tested subdomain whose certified lower bound is at least \(U\) can be removed without losing an improving feasible solution.

notation.meaning: certified relaxation lower bound on D

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: certified relaxation dual bounds justify cutoff-based domain exclusion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified exclusion of variable subdomains by relaxation dual bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be a candidate subdomain produced by restricting one or more variable bounds. Suppose a feasible dual solution of a valid relaxation on \(D\) certifies \(L(D)\le\inf\{f(x):x\in D\cap F\}\), where \(F\) is the original feasible set. If \(L(D)\ge U\), then every feasible \(x\in D\) satisfies \(f(x)\ge U\); consequently \(D\) contains no solution improving the incumbent and may be deleted. The dual solution together with its verified objective value is a checkable certificate for the deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subdomain is safely removed when a valid dual relaxation certificate proves that every feasible point there is no better than the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Driven Domain Reduction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dual lower-bound certificate gives a sound cutoff exclusion rule and fits the certificate container, but no supporting source and locator are provided.

children.title: Incumbent-Driven Domain Reduction
children.top_down_role: Domain contraction derived from incumbent objective cutoffs.

assumptions_latex: A feasible incumbent with objective value \(U\) is known.
Domain reduction uses only implications valid under the cutoff constraint \(f(x)<U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced domain retains every feasible point capable of strictly improving the incumbent.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: incumbent cutoffs restrict search to the strict objective level set containing improving solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain contraction conditional on a feasible incumbent cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem over \(F\cap B\), let \(\bar x\in F\cap B\) be an incumbent and set \(U=f(\bar x)\). Apply valid propagation or relaxation inference to the augmented system \(x\in F\cap B\) and \(f(x)<U\), obtaining a contracted box \(B'\). Validity means \(\{x\in F\cap B:f(x)<U\}\subseteq B'\subseteq B\). Therefore discarding \(B\setminus B'\) cannot remove a point that strictly improves the incumbent. If the augmented system is certified infeasible, the entire node may be fathomed by the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding the incumbent cutoff to propagation or relaxation safely removes values that cannot belong to any strictly improving feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent-Driven Domain Reduction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The strict incumbent-level-set preservation property fits the terminal container, but it lacks an inspectable supporting citation.

children.title: Dual-Cutoff Interaction
children.top_down_role: Complementary use of dual information and incumbent quality.

assumptions_latex: For each parameterized restriction \(D(t)\), a certified relaxation lower bound \(L(t)\) is available.
The incumbent value \(U\) is attained by a feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(L(t)\ge U\) is a sufficient exclusion test, and reductions can strengthen monotonically as \(L\) rises or \(U\) falls.

notation.meaning: certified relaxation lower bound on the restriction

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: domain exclusion compares a valid restricted dual bound with a feasible primal cutoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interaction between restricted relaxation bounds and the incumbent cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D(t)\) denote a candidate portion of the current domain and let \(L(t)\) satisfy \(L(t)\le\inf\{f(x):x\in F\cap D(t)\}\). With feasible incumbent value \(U\), the test \(L(t)\ge U\) certifies that \(D(t)\) contains no strictly improving solution. If a stronger dual certificate raises \(L(t)\), or a better incumbent lowers \(U\), every restriction previously excluded by this inequality remains excluded. Thus dual improvement and incumbent improvement interact monotonically through the comparison of a valid lower bound with a feasible upper cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted domain is excluded when its certified lower bound reaches the incumbent; stronger dual bounds or better incumbents can only enlarge this exclusion.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Cutoff Interaction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monotone interaction between a valid restricted lower bound and a feasible incumbent cutoff is correctly stated, but no source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Reduction Reliability Boundary
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of contractions to weak dual evidence or poor incumbents.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes weak valid evidence from invalid evidence that can corrupt domain reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L(D)\le v(D)\) be a valid restricted lower bound and let \(U\) be a verified feasible incumbent value. If \(L(D)<U\), the cutoff test yields no deletion even when \(U-L(D)\) is arbitrarily large; this is loss of strength, not soundness. By contrast, an alleged bound \(\widehat L(D)>v(D)\) may satisfy \(\widehat L(D)\ge U\) while \(v(D)<U\), causing an improving region to be deleted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak valid bounds merely fail to contract the domain; invalid bounds can make contraction unsound.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
\(U\) is a verified feasible incumbent value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Weakness affects efficacy, whereas violation of \(L(D)\le v(D)\) affects correctness.

notation.meaning: true optimum restricted to the tested subdomain

knowledge_statements.title: Strength–Soundness Separation

assumptions_latex: Domain deletion is based on a computed relaxation bound \(\widehat L(D)\) and cutoff \(\widehat U\).
The true restricted optimum is \(v(D)=\inf\{f(x):x\in F\cap D\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deletion is reliable only when certified inequalities establish \(\widehat L(D)\le v(D)\) and \(\widehat U\ge U\), with a comparison robust to numerical error.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: invalid lower bounds or numerically unsafe comparisons can delete improving solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness boundary for dual-and-cutoff domain deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The deletion test \(\widehat L(D)\ge\widehat U\) is sound only if \(\widehat L(D)\) is a certified lower bound on \(v(D)\), \(\widehat U\) is the value of a verified feasible incumbent, and rounding or solver tolerances cannot reverse the comparison. If \(\widehat L(D)>v(D)\) because of dual infeasibility, premature termination, or unsafe rounding, then one may have \(\widehat L(D)\ge\widehat U>v(D)\); deleting \(D\) then removes an improving feasible solution. Reliability therefore ends when either bound validity or numerically robust comparison is absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cutoff reduction is unsafe if the alleged lower bound is invalid, the incumbent is unverified, or numerical error can reverse their comparison.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduction Reliability Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The numerical-validity failure boundary is appropriate, but the conclusion introduces an undefined symbol U and the record provides no source for its reliability conditions.

children.title: Tightening Fixed-Point Calculus
children.top_down_role: Repeated domain-reduction passes and their stabilization behavior.

children.title: Repeated Tightening Passes
children.top_down_role: Successive application of compatible domain-reduction operators.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pass bound when endpoints range over finite representable sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose coordinate j's lower and upper endpoints range over finite sets of cardinalities p_j^- and p_j^+. If every nonterminal pass makes at least one strict endpoint change, stabilization occurs after at most \sum_j[(p_j^--1)+(p_j^+-1)] strict passes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With finitely many endpoint values, repeated contraction terminates after at most the total number of possible endpoint advances.
assumptions_latex: \ell_j^k\text{ and }u_j^k\text{ range over finite sets of sizes }p_j^-,p_j^+
B^{k+1}\subsetneq B^k\text{ in every nonterminal pass}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{strict}}\le\sum_j(p_j^-+p_j^+-2).

notation.meaning: numbers of representable lower and upper endpoints

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Lattice Termination Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic behavior of exact repeated tightening passes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \varnothing\neq B^{k+1}=T(B^k)\subseteq B^k be closed boxes contained in a bounded box B^0. Their lower endpoints are nondecreasing, their upper endpoints are nonincreasing, and B^\infty=\bigcap_{k\ge0}B^k is a nonempty closed box. If T is continuous from above on this chain, T(\bigcap_kB^k)=\bigcap_kT(B^k), then T(B^\infty)=B^\infty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested nonempty tightening boxes have a box limit; continuity from above makes that limit a fixed point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B^\infty=\bigcap_{k\ge0}B^k\neq\varnothing,\qquad T(B^\infty)=B^\infty.

notation.meaning: intersection limit of the nested boxes

knowledge_statements.title: Nested-Box Limit and Fixed-Point Condition

assumptions_latex: Each tightening operator is contracting and preserves the feasible set.
A finite family of operators is scheduled repeatedly until the stopping rule holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every iterate contains the feasible set, and the boxes form a nested sequence.

notation.meaning: composed tightening operator used in pass k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: repeated contracting feasible-set-preserving operators generate nested valid domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterated application of valid feasibility- and optimization-based contractors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(B^0=[\ell,u]\). For pass \(k=0,1,\ldots\), apply the scheduled valid contractors sequentially and set \(B^{k+1}=T_k(B^k)\). Each contractor must satisfy \(F\cap B^k\subseteq T_k(B^k)\subseteq B^k\), where \(F\) is the original feasible set. Stop if \(B^{k+1}=\varnothing\), if every endpoint changes by at most tolerance \(\varepsilon\), or if a prescribed resource limit is met; otherwise begin another pass. The output is the last box. Inductively, \(F\cap B^0\subseteq B^{k+1}\subseteq B^k\) for every completed pass.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly apply valid contractors to the current box; all iterates remain valid, shrink monotonically, and stop at emptiness, tolerance, or a resource limit.
knowledge_statements.title: Repeated Tightening Passes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The repeated-pass algorithm correctly yields nested feasible-set-preserving boxes and fits the container, but it has no cited evidence.

children.title: Tightening Fixed Points
children.top_down_role: Stable domains left unchanged by further tightening passes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasible Interval Hull as a Universal Fixed Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relationship between the exact feasible hull and valid box contractors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F\cap B^0\neq\varnothing and H=\operatorname{hull}_{\Box}(F\cap B^0). If T is contracting and preserves feasible points, F\cap B\subseteq T(B)\subseteq B for every B\subseteq B^0, then T(H)=H. Every box C\subseteq B^0 containing F\cap B^0 also contains H. Hence H is the smallest valid box and is fixed by every valid box contractor, although a particular contractor may have larger fixed points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The feasible interval hull is the smallest valid box and is fixed by every valid box contractor, but larger fixed points may exist.
assumptions_latex: F\cap B\subseteq T(B)\subseteq B\quad\text{for every box }B\subseteq B^0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T(H)=H,\qquad H\subseteq C\ \text{for every box }C\supseteq F\cap B^0.

notation.meaning: axis-aligned hull of feasible points in the initial box

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Interval Hull as a Universal Fixed Point

assumptions_latex: \(T\) maps boxes contained in an initial box \(B^0\) to boxes.
\(T\) is contracting and preserves all feasible points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A box \(B^*\) is a tightening fixed point exactly when another full application of \(T\) produces no contraction.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a propagation fixed point is a domain invariant under the aggregate contractor
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed points of an aggregate contracting box operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal B(B^0)\) be the set of axis-aligned boxes contained in \(B^0\), ordered by inclusion, and let \(T:\mathcal B(B^0)\to\mathcal B(B^0)\) satisfy \(T(B)\subseteq B\) and \(F\cap B\subseteq T(B)\) for every \(B\). A box \(B^*\in\mathcal B(B^0)\) is a tightening fixed point of \(T\) if \(T(B^*)=B^*\). Equivalently, a complete application of all contractors represented by \(T\) removes no additional interval value from \(B^*\), although \(B^*\) need not equal the interval hull of \(F\cap B^0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tightening fixed point is a valid box unchanged by another complete application of the aggregate contractor; it need not be the tightest feasible box.
knowledge_statements.title: Tightening Fixed Points

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The invariant-box definition is precise, appropriately distinguishes fixed-point consistency from hull tightness, and fits the definition container, but lacks a source.

children.title: Operator Scheduling Effects
children.top_down_role: Dependence of stabilization behavior on reduction order and pass composition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Order Independence for Commuting Idempotent Contractors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient algebraic conditions for schedule-independent finite stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let T_1,\ldots,T_m be pairwise commuting idempotent box contractors. Their complete-sweep composition T=T_m\circ\cdots\circ T_1 is independent of operator order, is idempotent, and satisfies T_i(T(B))=T(B) for every i. Consequently, every sweep applying each operator once produces the same common fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise commuting idempotent contractors reach the same common fixed point after one complete sweep, regardless of order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_i(T(B))=T(B)\quad\forall i,\qquad T\circ T=T.
knowledge_statements.title: Order Independence for Commuting Idempotent Contractors

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fair Iteration on a Finite Box Lattice
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schedule-independent termination under finite-domain monotonicity and fairness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal D be a finite lattice of boxes ordered by inclusion, and let every T_i:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D be monotone and contracting. From B^0, apply a fair schedule that continues activating every operator while changes remain possible. The iterates stabilize after finitely many strict contractions at the greatest common fixed point contained in B^0. All fair schedules therefore have the same terminal box.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite box lattice, fair iteration of monotone contracting operators terminates at a schedule-independent greatest common fixed point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B^k\text{ stabilizes finitely at }B^*,\quad T_i(B^*)=B^*\ \forall i.

notation.meaning: greatest common fixed point below the initial box

knowledge_statements.title: Fair Iteration on a Finite Box Lattice

assumptions_latex: Each operator in the finite family is contracting and feasible-set preserving.
Schedules may apply operators in different orders and may revisit them after domain changes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Intermediate boxes can depend on schedule; a common terminal box requires additional properties such as fairness and suitable monotonicity or confluence.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: noncommuting contractors yield schedule-dependent iterates; convergence equivalence needs fairness and operator regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schedule dependence for sequential noncommuting tightening operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a schedule \(\sigma=(i_0,i_1,\ldots)\), define \(B^{k+1}=T_{i_k}(B^k)\). If two contractors do not commute, so that \(T_i(T_j(B))\ne T_j(T_i(B))\) for some \(B\), then different schedules can produce different intermediate boxes and different finite-tolerance stopping points. Schedule-independent convergence to a common fixed point is not implied by contraction and feasibility preservation alone. It requires further hypotheses, for example fair repeated activation together with monotonicity and continuity on nested boxes, or a confluence property ensuring that all fair compositions have the same limiting fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noncommuting contractors make intermediate and tolerance-stopped domains order-dependent; schedule-independent limits require fairness plus monotonicity, continuity, or confluence assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Operator Scheduling Effects

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Schedule-dependent intermediate boxes are standard, but the stated sufficient conditions for a common terminal fixed point require authoritative support and more exact hypotheses than the uncited examples provide.

children.title: Stagnation Boundary
children.top_down_role: Premature stabilization with substantial residual domain width.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point stagnation caused by treating constraints separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On B=[0,1]^2, impose x=y and x=1-y. Each equation separately has projection [0,1] on both coordinates, so its exact coordinate-hull contractor leaves B unchanged. Their conjunction has the unique feasible point (1/2,1/2). Thus a full sweep fixes B although \operatorname{hull}_{\Box}(F)=\{(1/2,1/2)\}\subsetneq B.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate exact propagation of two constraints can leave the unit box unchanged even though their conjunction has one feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_2(T_1(B))=B,\qquad \operatorname{hull}_{\Box}(F)=\{(1/2,1/2)\}.

notation.meaning: exact coordinate-hull contractors for the individual equations

knowledge_statements.title: Individually Hull-Consistent Constraints Can Stagnate

assumptions_latex: The aggregate contractor \(T\) is valid and contracting.
The current box \(B\) strictly contains the interval hull of its feasible points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: It is possible that \(T(B)=B\); fixed-point stagnation therefore does not certify hull tightness or global optimality.

notation.meaning: interval hull of feasible points in B

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: local interval consistency can reach a fixed point weaker than the feasible interval hull
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point stagnation before attainment of the feasible interval hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Stagnation occurs at a nonempty box \(B\) when \(T(B)=B\), yet \(\operatorname{hull}(F\cap B)\subsetneq B\). At such a box, every contractor represented in \(T\) is locally unable to remove another endpoint value, although values in \(B\setminus\operatorname{hull}(F\cap B)\) cannot occur in any feasible point. Hence repeated passes produce the constant sequence \(B,B,\ldots\). This boundary shows that contractor fixed-point consistency alone neither computes the exact feasible interval hull nor certifies global optimality; stronger relaxations, reformulations, or branching may still be required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tightening can stagnate at a fixed box that strictly exceeds the feasible interval hull, so no-change does not certify exactness or global optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Stagnation Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stagnation phenomenon and its distinction from hull tightness fit the failure-boundary container, but no source with an inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Global Decomposition-Approximation Algorithm Family
children.top_down_role: Global methods separating nonconvex components or iteratively refining global approximations.

children.title: GOP Primal-Relaxed-Dual Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Decomposition architecture for biconvex, bilinear, and quadratic global models.

assumptions_latex: Variables are partitioned as \((x,y)\), with the primal subproblem convex in \(x\) for fixed \(y\).
The relaxed dual construction supplies valid lower-bounding regions over the admissible \(y\)-domain.
The feasible domain is compact and all subproblems and bounds are solved or certified to the required tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The maintained primal value is an upper bound, the relaxed-dual master value is a lower bound, and termination occurs when their gap meets tolerance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional GOP architecture for suitable biconvex, bilinear, or quadratic models.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 3. The GOP Primal-Relaxed Dual Decomposition Approach: Theory p. 67; 3.5 The Global Optimization (GOP) Algorithm p. 84

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a finite partition of the admissible \(y\)-domain, \(U_0=+\infty\), and \(L_0=-\infty\). At iteration \(k\), solve selected convex primal subproblems with \(y\) fixed to obtain feasible points and update \(U_k\). Use primal solutions and associated multipliers to construct valid relaxed-dual lower-bounding subproblems over partition regions; solve them to update \(L_k\), discard regions whose lower bounds are at least \(U_k\), and refine unresolved regions. Stop with the best feasible point when \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\); otherwise repeat. Under the stated validity and compactness assumptions, \(L_k\) and \(U_k\) bracket the global optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: GOP alternates convex primal solves with partitioned relaxed-dual lower bounds, pruning dominated regions until the certified upper-lower gap meets tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: GOP Primal-Relaxed-Dual Decomposition

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 3. The GOP Primal-Relaxed Dual Decomposition Approach: Theory p. 67; 3.5 The Global Optimization (GOP) Algorithm p. 84

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Valid GOP Bracketing Alone Does Not Force Gap Closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between valid primal/relaxed-dual bounds and convergence of the GOP iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Validity of bounds only gives \(L_k\le v^*\le U_k\); it does not imply \(U_k-L_k\to0\). For example, for \(\min\{y:0\le y\le1\}\), the feasible incumbent \(y=1\) gives \(U_k=1\), while the valid lower bound \(L_k=0\) may be retained at every iteration. Both bounds remain valid on the compact domain, yet \(U_k-L_k=1\) for all \(k\). Gap closure therefore additionally requires conditions such as exhaustive regional refinement, consistency of relaxed-dual bounds, and adequate primal recovery or sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid GOP upper-lower bracket may stagnate; convergence needs refinement consistency and primal recovery beyond compactness and bound validity.
assumptions_latex: The maintained values satisfy only \(L_k\le v^*\le U_k\).
No consistency or improving-primal condition is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_k\le v^*\le U_k\ \forall k\ \not\Rightarrow\ U_k-L_k\to0.

notation.meaning: valid relaxed-dual lower and primal upper bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Valid GOP Bracketing Alone Does Not Force Gap Closure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract convergence of a compact partition-and-bound scheme, not a GOP-specific primal-relaxed-dual theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\) be compact and let \(v^*\) be the global value. At iteration \(k\), let a finite active partition \(\mathcal P_k\) cover \(Y\), let each region \(R\in\mathcal P_k\) have a valid lower bound \(\ell(R)\), and set \(L_k=\min_{R\in\mathcal P_k}\ell(R)\). Suppose no region containing a global optimizer is pruned, \(\max_{R\in\mathcal P_k}\operatorname{diam}(R)\to0\), and there is a modulus \(\omega(t)\downarrow0\) such that \(\ell(R)\ge\inf_{y\in R}v(y)-\omega(\operatorname{diam}R)\). If feasible incumbents satisfy \(U_k\ge v^*\) and \(\limsup_kU_k\le v^*\), then \(L_k\to v^*\), \(U_k\to v^*\), and every positive gap tolerance is eventually met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consistent shrinking partitions and feasible recovery imply bound convergence in a generic partition-and-bound scheme.
assumptions_latex: Active-region diameters converge uniformly to zero.
Regional bounds satisfy the stated uniform consistency modulus.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_k\to v^*,\quad U_k\to v^*,\quad \forall\varepsilon>0\ \exists k:\ U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Consistent GOP Partition Convergence

intermediate_metadata.reason: The local inventory contains the accepted GOP primal–relaxed-dual architecture, its bound-gap certificate, and the stagnation boundary showing that valid bracketing alone does not imply convergence. The proposed abstract partition theorem is deferred because its canonical home is generic spatial bound convergence and it does not state GOP-specific relaxed-dual hypotheses. Negative-eigenspace search, generic outer approximation, and partition geometry were excluded as sibling scopes.

children.title: Negative-Eigenspace Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Global search concentrated on the subspace responsible for nonconvexity.

knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Eigenspace Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral difference-of-convex decomposition of an indefinite quadratic objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\) have orthogonal eigendecomposition \(Q=U\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)U^\top\). Define \(Q_+=U\operatorname{diag}((\lambda_i)_+)U^\top\) and \(Q_-=U\operatorname{diag}(({-\lambda_i})_+)U^\top\). Then \(Q=Q_+-Q_-\), with \(Q_+,Q_-\succeq0\), and
\[q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Q_+x+c^\top x-\tfrac12\lVert Q_-^{1/2}x\rVert^2.\]
Thus all negative curvature is confined to \(E_-:=\operatorname{range}(Q_-)\). On every affine slice fixing the projection of \(x\) onto \(E_-\), the remaining quadratic objective is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The spectral decomposition writes an indefinite quadratic as a convex quadratic minus a convex quadratic; only the span of negative eigenvectors requires nonconvex global search.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q=Q_+-Q_-\) and negative curvature is supported on \(E_-=\operatorname{range}(Q_-)\).

notation.meaning: real symmetric matrices of order n

source_refs.locator: 5. Approximation Algorithms in Quadratic Programming p. 38

source_witnesses.locator: 5. Approximation Algorithms in Quadratic Programming p. 38

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimal Dimension of a PSD-Minus-Gram Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Negative inertia is the smallest possible dimension of the concave quadratic core.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\) and let \(r=n_-(Q)\). If \(Q=A-BB^\top\) with \(A\succeq0\), then \(\operatorname{rank}(B)\ge r\). Equality is attained by the spectral construction \(A=Q_+\) and \(B=U_-\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{-\lambda_i}:\lambda_i<0)\). Thus the negative eigenspace supplies a PSD-minus-Gram representation with the smallest possible number of nonconvex projected coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The number of negative eigenvalues is exactly the minimum number of concave-square coordinates required in a positive-semidefinite-minus-Gram representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}(B)\ge n_-(Q),\text{ with equality attainable spectrally}.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Dimension of a PSD-Minus-Gram Decomposition

children.title: Successive Outer Approximation
children.top_down_role: Iterative refinement of convex or polyhedral global approximations.

knowledge_statements.title: Successive Outer Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-bounding refinement for a compact-domain nonconvex quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(v^*=\min\{q(x):x\in X\}\), let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be compact and let \(\ell_k\le q\) on \(X\). Initialize a finite relaxation model \(\ell_0\). At iteration \(k\), solve \(L_k=\min_{x\in X}\ell_k(x)\) and obtain \(x^k\); evaluate or locally improve \(x^k\) to update a feasible upper bound \(U_k\). If \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\), return the incumbent. Otherwise add valid supporting, secant, or partition-derived inequalities producing \(\ell_{k+1}\ge\ell_k\) while preserving \(\ell_{k+1}\le q\), and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve a valid lower approximation, improve a feasible incumbent, and refine the approximation until the certified upper–lower bound gap meets tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_k\le v^*\le U_k\), so \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\) certifies an \(\varepsilon\)-global incumbent.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.5 Relaxation (Successive Outer Approximation) Strategies p. 31

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.5 Relaxation (Successive Outer Approximation) Strategies p. 31

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validity and Nestedness Alone Do Not Ensure Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stagnation boundary for successive lower approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X=[-1,1]\), \(q(x)=x^2\), and \(\ell_k(x)=-1\) for all \(k\), every \(\ell_k\) is a valid nested lower approximation, yet \(L_k=-1\) while \(v^*=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid nested models can stagnate strictly below the optimum when their approximation error does not vanish.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_k\not\to v^*.
knowledge_statements.title: Validity and Nestedness Alone Do Not Ensure Convergence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordering of lower bounds from pointwise-strengthened underestimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\ell_k\le\ell_{k+1}\le q\) on nonempty \(X\), then \[L_k:=\inf_X\ell_k\le L_{k+1}:=\inf_X\ell_{k+1}\le v^*:=\inf_Xq.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise strengthening of valid lower approximations produces nondecreasing valid lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_k\le L_{k+1}\le v^*.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity of Nested Outer-Approximation Bounds

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform-Consistency Convergence of Successive Outer Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-independent sufficient condition for convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be nonempty and compact, let \(q\) be continuous, and suppose \(\ell_k\le\ell_{k+1}\le q\) on \(X\). If \[\delta_k:=\sup_{x\in X}(q(x)-\ell_k(x))\to0,\] then, for \(L_k=\min_X\ell_k\) and \(v^*=\min_Xq\), \[0\le v^*-L_k\le\delta_k,\] and therefore \(L_k\uparrow v^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly vanishing approximation error makes the monotone lower bounds converge to the global optimum.
assumptions_latex: The lower models are nested, valid, and uniformly consistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_k\uparrow v^*.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform-Consistency Convergence of Successive Outer Approximation

children.title: Partition Geometry Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Classical partition geometries supporting localized bounds.

children.title: Simplicial Partitioning
children.top_down_role: Simplex-based localization for constructing regional bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplicial Partitioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Successive partitioning of a compact polytope into simplices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty compact polytope, let \(q:X\to\mathbb R\) be a quadratic objective, define \(v^*=\min_{x\in X}q(x)\), and fix \(\varepsilon\ge0\). Triangulate \(X\) into finitely many simplices \(\mathcal T_0\). At iteration \(k\), compute for every active \(S\in\mathcal T_k\) a valid lower bound \(L(S)\le\min_{x\in S}q(x)\), and maintain a feasible incumbent \(\hat x_k\in X\) with \(U_k=q(\hat x_k)\). Discard every \(S\) satisfying \(L(S)\ge U_k-\varepsilon\). Select a remaining simplex and subdivide it, for example by longest-edge bisection. Continue until no active simplex remains; then return the incumbent. An exhaustive refinement rule requires the maximum diameter of repeatedly selected simplices to converge to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Triangulate the domain, bound the objective on each simplex, prune cells that cannot improve the incumbent beyond tolerance, and repeatedly subdivide active simplices. If no active simplex remains, the incumbent is epsilon-globally optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty compact polytope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination with no active simplex implies \(q(\hat x_k)-v^*\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: active simplicial partition at iteration k
valid lower bound on simplex S
objective value of the feasible incumbent

source_refs.locator: 11.3 Simplicial Successive Partitioning Algorithms p. 110

source_witnesses.locator: 11.3 Simplicial Successive Partitioning Algorithms p. 110

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validity Without Shrinking or Consistency Does Not Close the Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for simplicial lower-bound convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=[0,1]\), let \(q(x)=x^2\), retain \(S_k=X\), and use the valid bound \(L(S_k)=-1\) for every \(k\). Then \(v^*=0\) but \(L(S_k)=-1\) for all \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A permanently coarse simplex with a merely valid bound can retain a nonzero bound gap forever.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L(S_k)\not\to v^*.
knowledge_statements.title: Validity Without Shrinking or Consistency Does Not Close the Gap

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simplex-specific affine interpolation and diameter-dependent error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_n\}\), \(x=\sum_i\lambda_i v_i\), and \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^THx+c^Tx+d\), where \(H=H^T\). The affine vertex interpolant \(I_Sq(x)=\sum_i\lambda_iq(v_i)\) satisfies \[I_Sq(x)-q(x)=\tfrac12\sum_i\lambda_i(v_i-x)^TH(v_i-x).\] Hence \[|I_Sq(x)-q(x)|\le\tfrac12\|H\|_2\operatorname{diam}(S)^2,\] and \(I_Sq-\tfrac12\|H\|_2\operatorname{diam}(S)^2\) is a valid affine lower estimator on \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic's affine vertex interpolant has an exact curvature error identity and yields a simplex lower estimator with quadratic diameter error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: I_Sq(x)-\tfrac12\|H\|_2\operatorname{diam}(S)^2\le q(x)\quad\forall x\in S.

notation.meaning: affine interpolant matching q at the simplex vertices

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Barycentric Interpolation Error

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-bound convergence for an unpruned exhaustive simplicial partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be compact and let \(\mathcal T_k\) be nested finite simplicial partitions of \(X\). Suppose \(L(S)\le\min_{x\in S}q(x)\) and \[0\le\min_{x\in S}q(x)-L(S)\le\omega(\operatorname{diam}S),\qquad \omega(t)\to0\text{ as }t\downarrow0.\] If every simplex containing a global minimizer is refined along any infinite chain so that its diameter tends to zero, then \(B_k=\min_{S\in\mathcal T_k}L(S)\to v^*=\min_Xq\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shrinking refinement around every global minimizer, together with locally consistent bounds, makes the partition lower bound converge to the optimum.
assumptions_latex: The simplex bounds are valid and uniformly consistent in diameter.
Every infinite refinement chain containing a global minimizer shrinks to zero diameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B_k\to v^*.

notation.meaning: minimum lower bound over the simplicial partition

knowledge_statements.title: Convergence of Consistent Simplicial Refinement

children.title: Rectangular Partitioning
children.top_down_role: Box-based localization aligned with variable domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Rectangular Partitioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-and-bound refinement using axis-aligned boxes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty compact feasible region, let \(q:X\to\mathbb R\) be a quadratic objective, define \(v^*=\min_{x\in X}q(x)\), and fix \(\varepsilon\ge0\). Enclose \(X\) in a box \(B_0=[l,u]\) and maintain a collection \(\mathcal B_k\) of active boxes. For each \(B\in\mathcal B_k\), compute a valid lower bound \(L(B)\le\min\{q(x):x\in X\cap B\}\) when \(X\cap B\ne\varnothing\), and maintain a feasible incumbent \(\hat x_k\in X\) with \(U_k=q(\hat x_k)\). Prune \(B\) when \(X\cap B=\varnothing\) or \(L(B)\ge U_k-\varepsilon\). Otherwise bisect a selected box along a coordinate. Continue until all boxes are pruned. An exhaustive refinement rule requires box diameters along every infinite branch to tend to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cover the feasible set by axis-aligned boxes, compute valid cell lower bounds, prune empty or uncompetitive boxes, and bisect surviving boxes. If every box is pruned, the incumbent is epsilon-globally optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq B_0\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and compact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(\mathcal B_k=\varnothing\), the incumbent \(\hat x_k\) satisfies \(q(\hat x_k)-v^*\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: objective value of the feasible incumbent

source_refs.locator: 11.4 Rectangular Successive Partitioning Algorithms p. 117

source_witnesses.locator: 11.4 Rectangular Successive Partitioning Algorithms p. 117

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unfair Coordinate Bisection Is Not Exhaustive
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of rectangular shrinking when a positive-width coordinate is never refined.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_0=[0,1]^2\). Along an infinite branch, repeatedly bisect only the first coordinate and retain one child. The first-coordinate width tends to zero, but the second-coordinate width remains \(1\), so every retained box has Euclidean diameter at least \(1\). Coordinate bisection is therefore not exhaustive unless every relaxation-relevant positive-width coordinate shrinks along each infinite unresolved branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly splitting only one coordinate can leave boxes permanently wide in another coordinate, so coordinate fairness is required for exhaustive refinement.
assumptions_latex: Only the first coordinate is bisected along the infinite branch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_k\operatorname{diam}(B_k)\ge1,\quad\text{so }\operatorname{diam}(B_k)\not\to0.
knowledge_statements.title: Unfair Coordinate Bisection Is Not Exhaustive

children.title: Conical Partitioning
children.top_down_role: Cone-based localization organized by directional geometry.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Angular Refinement Alone Does Not Ensure Spatial Shrinking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric obstruction to inferring relaxation convergence solely from cone-angle refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a=0\), \(X=[0,1]^2\), and let \((K_k)\) be nested closed cones containing the ray \(\{te_1:t\ge0\}\), with angular diameters tending to zero. Every cell \(C_k=X\cap K_k\) contains both \(0\) and \(e_1\), so \(\operatorname{diam}(C_k)\ge1\) for all \(k\). Thus vanishing angular diameter alone does not imply spatial shrinking and cannot establish consistency for bounds whose errors depend on Euclidean diameter or radial extent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cones can become arbitrarily narrow while retaining a full radial segment, so angular refinement alone is insufficient for diameter-based bound convergence.
assumptions_latex: The angular diameters of \(K_k\) tend to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{diam}(X\cap K_k)\ge1\quad\forall k.
knowledge_statements.title: Angular Refinement Alone Does Not Ensure Spatial Shrinking
Conical Partitioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Successive angular subdivision of a compact region viewed from an apex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an apex \(a\in\mathbb R^n\) and cover the compact feasible set \(X\) by cells \(X\cap(a+K)\), where each \(K\) is a finitely generated convex cone. For every active cone \(K\), compute a valid lower bound \(L(K)\) over its cell and update a feasible incumbent \(U_k\). Prune cells with \(L(K)\ge U_k-\varepsilon\) or empty intersection. Subdivide a selected cone into cones whose union is the parent, without losing feasible points. Refine so that the angular diameters on every infinite branch tend to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition directions from an apex into cones, bound the feasible portion of each cone, prune dominated cells, and progressively refine angular regions.
assumptions_latex: Each subdivision covers its parent cone, and \(L(K)\) is valid on \(X\cap(a+K)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exhaustion of active cells yields an incumbent \(\hat x\) with \(q(\hat x)-v^*\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: lower bound on the conical cell

source_refs.locator: 11.5 Conical Successive Partitioning Algorithms p. 123

source_witnesses.locator: 11.5 Conical Successive Partitioning Algorithms p. 123

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited locator is relevant, but the generic claim that angular diameter alone suffices is unreliable without source-specific assumptions connecting angular refinement to relaxation consistency or radial control. Full-text inspection is needed before fixing the convergence conditions.

children.title: Partition-Geometry Selection
children.top_down_role: Structural considerations governing the choice among partition shapes.

knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Geometry Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry should align refinement with domain structure and nonconvex directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty compact feasible set, let \(q:X\to\mathbb R\) be the objective, and let \(\mathcal P\) be a family of partition cells used to construct lower bounds. Standard sufficient conditions for exhaustive global refinement are that child cells cover their parent, no feasible point is lost, every infinite branch shrinks in all directions on which the relaxation error depends, and the cell lower-bound error tends to zero under that refinement. Among families satisfying these conditions, simplices can align with polyhedral directional structure, boxes with coordinate bounds and separable relaxations, and cones with angular or radial structure. Computational preference does not replace validity and exhaustiveness of the chosen refinement scheme.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a partition geometry that matches the feasible region and relaxation structure. Complete coverage, preservation of feasible points, and asymptotically exact lower bounds provide sufficient conditions for exhaustive refinement.
assumptions_latex: \(q:X\to\mathbb R\) is the objective being lower-bounded.
The cell relaxation error vanishes under the geometry-relevant refinement measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coverage, preservation of feasible points, shrinking in relaxation-relevant directions, and consistent lower bounds are sufficient for an exhaustive partition-refinement scheme.

source_refs.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39
11.3–11.5 Simplicial, Rectangular, and Conical Successive Partitioning Algorithms pp. 110–123

children.title: Local-QP Multistart Interface
children.top_down_role: Local optimization families used to discover and diversify feasible incumbents.

children.title: Local-QP Incumbent Search
children.top_down_role: Use of local quadratic optimization to locate feasible incumbents.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-run local search supplies an incumbent only through a verified feasible output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a start \(x^0\), apply a local method to \(\min_{x\in X}q(x)\). If the returned point \(y\) is verified to satisfy \(y\in X\), compare it with the current feasible incumbent \(\hat x\) and set \(\hat x^+=y\) when \(q(y)<q(\hat x)\), otherwise set \(\hat x^+=\hat x\). Then \(v^*=\inf_{x\in X}q(x)\le q(\hat x^+)\le q(\hat x)\). A local termination or stationarity test, without an independent global lower bound, does not certify \(q(\hat x^+)=v^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept a local-search output only after checking feasibility; it can improve the incumbent upper bound but does not itself certify global optimality.
assumptions_latex: A returned local-search point is accepted only after verifying membership in \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v^*\le q(\hat x^+)\le q(\hat x),\text{ with no unconditional equality certificate.}

notation.meaning: global infimum over the feasible set

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Guarded Local-QP Incumbent Search

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Strict Local QP Minimum Need Not Be Global
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional box-QP boundary for interpreting local incumbent search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q(x)=-x^2+\tfrac12x\) on \([-1,1]\), \(x=1\) is a strict local minimizer relative to the feasible interval, but \(q(1)=-\tfrac12>-	frac32=q(-1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local solver may return the strict boundary minimum at one even though the opposite endpoint is globally better.
assumptions_latex: Local optimality is relative to the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x=1\text{ is a strict local minimizer but not a global minimizer.}
knowledge_statements.title: A Strict Local QP Minimum Need Not Be Global
Local-QP Incumbent Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local minimization supplies feasible upper bounds without asserting global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a feasible start \(x^0\in X\), apply a local quadratic-programming solver to \(\min_{x\in X}q(x)\), producing feasible iterates and a terminal point \(x^{\mathrm{loc}}\) satisfying the solver's local stationarity tolerance. Maintain an incumbent \(\hat x\): replace it by \(x^{\mathrm{loc}}\) exactly when \(q(x^{\mathrm{loc}})<q(\hat x)\). The value \(q(\hat x)\) is then a valid upper bound on the global minimum \(v^*\). Neither stationarity nor local minimality alone certifies \(q(\hat x)=v^*\) for an indefinite quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run a local QP solver from a feasible start and retain improvements as global-search incumbents; the result is an upper bound, not a global certificate.
assumptions_latex: Every accepted local-search output belongs to \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v^*\le q(\hat x)\), but local stationarity need not imply \(q(\hat x)=v^*\).

source_refs.locator: 5.1 Global vs. Local Optimum p. 127

source_witnesses.locator: 5.1 Global vs. Local Optimum p. 127

A locator for an appropriate local constrained-QP method is required.

children.title: Multistart Diversification
children.top_down_role: Diversification across initial points or search regions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection of distinct starts and aggregation of feasible local-search endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Select starts \(x^1,\ldots,x^N\in X\) by a declared design, such as independent sampling, stratified sampling, a space-filling design, or a feasible \(\delta\)-separated set. Apply the same local-search procedure to each start. Discard endpoints that fail the feasibility test and return a feasible endpoint \(\hat x\) of smallest objective value among those retained, together with any pre-existing feasible incumbent. Finite diversification alone gives no global-optimality or infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a declared diverse start design, retain only feasible local endpoints, and keep the best; finite diversification alone is not a global certificate.
assumptions_latex: Only endpoints verified to belong to \(X\) are retained.
A requested separated or stratified design is used only when the required feasible starts or nonempty strata exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q(\hat x)=\min\{q(y):y\text{ is a retained feasible endpoint or the prior incumbent}\},\text{ without an unconditional global guarantee.}

notation.meaning: optional minimum separation between retained starts

knowledge_statements.title: Diversified Local-QP Multistart
Multistart Diversification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diversified starting points expose a local solver to distinct attraction basins.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose starts \(x^1,\ldots,x^N\in X\) by a prescribed design, such as space-filling sampling, stratification, or deterministic separation. For each \(i\), run the same local-QP map \(T:X\to X\) and obtain \(y^i=T(x^i)\). Return \(\hat x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{1\le i\le N}q(y^i)\). To enforce diversification, require \(\lVert x^i-x^j\rVert\ge\delta\) for distinct retained starts, or sample from strata not previously represented. The procedure improves incumbent discovery but supplies no global certificate unless accompanied by a basin-coverage or global lower-bound argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generate well-separated or stratified starts, run identical local searches, and keep the best endpoint; diversification alone does not prove global optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(T(x)\in X\) for every selected start \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(\hat x)=\min_{1\le i\le N}q(T(x^i))\), without an unconditional global-optimality guarantee.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.3 Basic Ideas of Global Random Search p. 18

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.3 Basic Ideas of Global Random Search p. 18

children.title: Basin-Coverage Regimes
children.top_down_role: Coverage behavior across multiple local attraction regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Basin-Coverage Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample success depends on the probability mass of globally attracting basins.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) be independent random starts with common distribution \(\mu\) on \(X\). Let \(q:X\to\mathbb R\) and \(T:X\to X\) be measurable, define \(v^*=\inf_{x\in X}q(x)\), and fix \(\varepsilon\ge0\). Define \(B_\varepsilon=\{x\in X:q(T(x))\le v^*+\varepsilon\}\) and \(p_\varepsilon=\mu(B_\varepsilon)\). Then
\[\Pr\!\left(\min_{1\le i\le N}q(T(X_i))\le v^*+\varepsilon\right)=1-(1-p_\varepsilon)^N.\]
As \(N\to\infty\), this success probability converges to one if and only if \(p_\varepsilon>0\); when \(p_\varepsilon=0\), it is zero for every \(N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For independent starts, the probability of reaching an epsilon-global basin equals one minus the probability that every start misses it. The probability tends to one exactly when that basin has positive sampling mass.
assumptions_latex: \(X_1,ldots,X_N\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(\mu\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pr(\min_{1\le i\le N}q(T(X_i))\le v^*+\varepsilon)=1-(1-p_\varepsilon)^N\), which converges to \(1\) as \(N\to\infty\) exactly when \(p_\varepsilon>0\).

notation.meaning: set of starts whose local-search outputs are epsilon-global
sampling mass of the successful basin

source_refs.locator: 2.1 Introduction to Global Random Search p. 29; 2.1.2 Formal Scheme of Global Random Search Algorithms p. 33

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1 Introduction to Global Random Search p. 29; 2.1.2 Formal Scheme of Global Random Search Algorithms p. 33

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent-start budget required to hit a basin of known positive sampling mass with prescribed confidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<p_\varepsilon<1\) and \(0<\delta<1\), the least integer \(N\) satisfying \(1-(1-p_\varepsilon)^N\ge 1-\delta\) is \[N_\delta=\left\lceil\frac{\log\delta}{\log(1-p_\varepsilon)}\right\rceil.\] If \(p_\varepsilon=1\), then \(N_\delta=1\). Moreover, \(N\ge p_\varepsilon^{-1}\log(1/\delta)\) is sufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact confidence budget is ceiling(log delta divided by log(1-p)); the simpler order log(1/delta)/p budget suffices.
assumptions_latex: The starts are independent and have common success probability \(p_\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N\ge N_\delta\implies \Pr(\text{at least one success})\ge1-\delta.

notation.meaning: least start budget attaining failure probability at most delta
sampling mass of the epsilon-global basin

knowledge_statements.title: Independent-Start Basin Sample Complexity

children.title: Local-to-Global Handoff
children.top_down_role: Transfer of locally discovered candidates into deterministic global search.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-to-Global Handoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible local solutions update the incumbent and sharpen global pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a global method maintain a valid lower bound \(L_k\le v^*\) and incumbent \(\hat x_k\in X\) with \(U_k=q(\hat x_k)\). Pass a feasible trial point to the local-QP solver and obtain \(y_k\in X\). Set \(\hat x_{k+1}=y_k\) if \(q(y_k)<U_k\), and otherwise retain \(\hat x_k\); set \(U_{k+1}=q(\hat x_{k+1})\). Use \(U_{k+1}\) to prune every global-search region whose lower bound is at least \(U_{k+1}-\varepsilon\). Stop only when \(U_{k+1}-L_k\le\varepsilon\), not merely when the local solver terminates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transfer feasible local improvements to the global incumbent, use them for pruning, and declare global success only when a valid lower bound closes the gap.
assumptions_latex: \(L_k\le v^*\) is a valid global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_k\le v^*\le U_{k+1}\le U_k\), and \(U_{k+1}-L_k\le\varepsilon\) certifies ε-global optimality.
