children.title: Compact Feasible Domains
children.top_down_role: Bounded closed feasible regions supporting existence of global minimizers.

knowledge_statements.title: Compact Feasible Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weierstrass attainment regime for continuous quadratic objectives on compact feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and compact, and let \(f(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+q^{\mathsf T}x+c\) with \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\), \(q\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(c\in\mathbb R\). Since \(f\) is continuous, there exist \(x^{\min},x^{\max}\in F\) such that \[f(x^{\min})=\min_{x\in F}f(x),\qquad f(x^{\max})=\max_{x\in F}f(x).\] In particular, the global infimum is finite and attained, irrespective of whether \(Q\) is positive semidefinite, indefinite, or negative semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every continuous quadratic objective attains finite minimum and maximum values on a nonempty compact feasible domain, regardless of the Hessian's definiteness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\ne\varnothing\) and \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in F}f(x)\ne\varnothing\)

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structure of the full minimizer and maximizer sets on a compact feasible domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the compact-domain seed assumptions, let \(m=\min_{x\in F}f(x)\) and \(M=\max_{x\in F}f(x)\). Then \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)=F\cap f^{-1}(\{m\})\) and \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in F}f(x)=F\cap f^{-1}(\{M\})\) are nonempty compact subsets of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact feasible domain, the full minimizer and maximizer sets of a continuous quadratic are nonempty and compact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_F f\text{ and }\operatorname*{argmax}_F f\text{ are nonempty and compact}.
knowledge_statements.title: Compactness of the Extremizer Sets

children.title: Coercive Noncompact Regimes
children.top_down_role: Unbounded feasible regions where objective growth still supports finite attainment.

knowledge_statements.title: Coercive Noncompact Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment for continuous coercive objectives on closed, possibly unbounded feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and closed, and let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be continuous and coercive on \(C\), meaning that every sequence \((x_k)\subset C\) with \(\lVert x_k\rVert\to\infty\) satisfies \(f(x_k)\to+\infty\). Then \(f\) is bounded below on \(C\), and there exists \(x^\star\in C\) such that \[f(x^\star)=\min_{x\in C}f(x).\] In particular, this applies to an indefinite quadratic objective whenever its restriction to the specified noncompact feasible set is coercive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous objective attains its minimum on a closed noncompact feasible set if it diverges to positive infinity along every unbounded feasible sequence.
assumptions_latex: \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) is continuous and coercive on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\neq\varnothing\).

source_refs.locator: 5.1 Global vs. Local Optimum p. 127

source_witnesses.locator: 5.1 Global vs. Local Optimum p. 127

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative coercivity does not ensure attainment on a nonclosed feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=(0,\infty)\) and \(f(x)=x^2\). Then \(f\) is coercive on \(C\), but \(\inf_{x\in C}f(x)=0\) and \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coercive quadratic need not attain its infimum when the feasible set is not closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is coercive on }C,\quad \inf_C f=0,\quad \operatorname*{argmin}_C f=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Closedness Boundary for Coercive Attainment

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional characterization of coercivity relative to a closed feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and closed and let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be continuous. Then \(f\) is coercive on \(C\) if and only if every lower level set \(L_\alpha=\{x\in C:f(x)\le\alpha\}\), \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), is compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuous objective on a closed finite-dimensional feasible set, relative coercivity is equivalent to compactness of every lower level set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is coercive on }C\iff (\forall\alpha\in\mathbb R)\;\{x\in C:f(x)\le\alpha\}\text{ is compact}.

notation.meaning: lower level set at height alpha

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Coercivity via Compact Sublevels

children.title: Level-Set Compactness
children.top_down_role: Compact relevant sublevel regions supporting minimizer existence.

knowledge_statements.title: Level-Set Compactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment from one nonempty compact lower level set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and closed, let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be continuous, and let \(\bar x\in C\). Define \[L_{\bar x}=\{x\in C:f(x)\le f(\bar x)\}.\] If \(L_{\bar x}\) is compact, then there exists \(x^\star\in L_{\bar x}\) such that \[f(x^\star)=\min_{x\in C}f(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a continuous objective has a compact lower level set at some feasible reference point, then it attains its global minimum, even when the full feasible set is unbounded.
assumptions_latex: \(L_{\bar x}\) is compact for some \(\bar x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x^\star)=\min_{x\in C}f(x)\) for some \(x^\star\in L_{\bar x}\).

notation.meaning: lower level set at the feasible reference point

source_refs.locator: 5.1 Global vs. Local Optimum p. 127

source_witnesses.locator: 5.1 Global vs. Local Optimum p. 127

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A compact relevant sublevel replaces closedness of the full feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be continuous, and let \(\bar x\in C\). If \(L_{\bar x}=\{x\in C:f(x)\le f(\bar x)\}\) is compact as a subset of \(\mathbb R^n\), then there exists \(x^\star\in L_{\bar x}\) such that \(f(x^\star)=\min_{x\in C}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact relevant sublevel suffices for attainment even when the full feasible set is not closed.
assumptions_latex: \(L_{\bar x}\) is compact for some \(\bar x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\cap L_{\bar x}\ne\varnothing.

notation.meaning: lower level set at the feasible reference point

knowledge_statements.title: Compact-Sublevel Attainment Without Global Closedness

children.title: Nonattainment Boundary
children.top_down_role: Feasible finite-infimum regimes lacking a minimizing point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential and sublevel consequences of finite nonattainment on a closed finite-dimensional domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and closed, let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be continuous, and suppose \(m=\inf_C f\in\mathbb R\). Then \(\operatorname*{argmin}_C f=\varnothing\) if and only if every minimizing sequence \((x_k)\subset C\) satisfies \(\lVert x_k\rVert\to\infty\). In that case, for every \(\alpha>m\), the nonempty sublevel \(\{x\in C:f(x)\le\alpha\}\) is noncompact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a closed finite-dimensional domain, a finite infimum is unattained exactly when every minimizing sequence escapes to infinity; consequently no sublevel above the infimum is compact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_C f=\varnothing\iff (\forall (x_k)\text{ minimizing})\;\lVert x_k\rVert\to\infty.

notation.meaning: finite infimum of the objective on C

knowledge_statements.title: Escape Characterization of Finite Nonattainment

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A closed nonpolyhedral quadratic feasible set can have a finite unattained quadratic infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:xy=1\}\) and \(f(x,y)=x^2\). Then \(C\) is nonempty, closed, unbounded, and nonpolyhedral. Moreover, \(\inf_{(x,y)\in C}f(x,y)=0\), but no feasible point has \(x=0\), so \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y)\in C}f(x,y)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closedness alone does not prevent finite nonattainment on a nonpolyhedral quadratic feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_C f=0\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname*{argmin}_C f=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Closed Nonpolyhedral Finite Nonattainment

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Excludes finite nonattainment for quadratic minimization over a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron and let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+\gamma\), where \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\). If \(f\) is bounded below on \(P\), then there exists \(x^\star\in P\) such that \(f(x^\star)=\min_{x\in P}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Frank–Wolfe theorem rules out finite nonattainment for a quadratic objective over a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}f(x)\ne\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Frank–Wolfe Polyhedral Attainment Boundary
Nonattainment Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closedness and finite infimum do not ensure attainment without compactness or coercivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(C=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x\ge0,\ xy\ge1\}\) and \(f(x,y)=x^2\). The set \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and unbounded, and \(f\) is a continuous quadratic function bounded below by zero on \(C\). For every \(t>0\), the point \((t,t^{-1})\) belongs to \(C\) and has value \(t^2\), so \(\inf_C f=0\). No feasible point has \(x=0\); hence no point in \(C\) attains this infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous quadratic can have a finite but unattained infimum on a closed unbounded set when compact level sets and coercivity both fail.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{(x,y)\in C}f(x,y)=0\) and \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y)\in C}f(x,y)=\varnothing\).

children.title: Improving Recession Directions
children.top_down_role: Feasible asymptotic directions supporting objective decrease without a finite lower limit.

knowledge_statements.title: Improving Recession Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ray-based descent directions for a quadratic over a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron, let \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) satisfy \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\), let \(c\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\), and define \(f:P\to\mathbb R\) by \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+\gamma\). For \(x\in P\), a nonzero vector \(d\in\operatorname{rec}(P)\) is an improving recession direction at \(x\) if either \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd<0\), or \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd=0\) and \(d^{\mathsf T}(Qx+c)<0\). Equivalently, \[f(x+td)=f(x)+t d^{\mathsf T}(Qx+c)+\tfrac12t^2d^{\mathsf T}Qd\] tends to \(-\infty\) as \(t\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An improving recession direction is a feasible ray whose negative quadratic coefficient, or whose negative linear coefficient in the zero-curvature case, forces the objective to negative infinity.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric, \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d\) is improving at \(x\) exactly when \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd<0\), or when \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd=0\) and \(d^{\mathsf T}(Qx+c)<0\).

source_refs.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

children.title: Unbounded Recession Faces
children.top_down_role: Faces of the recession structure supporting unbounded objective behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Recession Faces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric characterization of unbounded faces of a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron and let \(F\) be a nonempty face of \(P\). Then \(F\) is unbounded if and only if its recession cone contains a nonzero vector: \[F\text{ is unbounded}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{rec}(F)\setminus\{0\}\ne\varnothing.\] Moreover, every \(x\in F\) and \(d\in\operatorname{rec}(F)\) satisfy \(x+td\in F\) for all \(t\ge0\). Thus an improving direction lying in \(\operatorname{rec}(F)\) supplies an unbounded feasible ray entirely contained in that face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral face is unbounded exactly when its recession cone has a nonzero direction; any improving such direction remains inside the face.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is unbounded if and only if \(\operatorname{rec}(F)\setminus\{0\}\ne\varnothing\).

source_refs.locator: 2.13.3 Conic Programming p. 80

source_witnesses.locator: 2.13.3 Conic Programming p. 80

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Active-Constraint Representation of a Face Recession Cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic description of recession directions remaining in a specified polyhedral face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\), and let the nonempty face \(F\) be represented by \(F=\{x\in P:A_Ix=b_I\}\). Then \[\operatorname{rec}(F)=\{d\in\mathbb R^n:Ad\le0,\ A_Id=0\}.\] Consequently, \(F\) is unbounded if and only if this homogeneous system has a nonzero solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The recession cone of a polyhedral face consists of feasible recession directions preserving every equality defining the face.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rec}(F)=\{d:Ad\le0,\ A_Id=0\}.

notation.meaning: indices fixed at equality on the face

children.title: Unboundedness Certificates
children.top_down_role: Verifiable evidence that no finite global optimum exists.

knowledge_statements.title: Unboundedness Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactly checkable ray certificate for quadratic unboundedness over a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(P=\{z\in\mathbb R^n:Az\le b\}\). Let \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) satisfy \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\), let \(c\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\), and define \(f(z)=\tfrac12z^{\mathsf T}Qz+c^{\mathsf T}z+\gamma\). A pair \((x,d)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^n\) certifies \(\inf_{z\in P}f(z)=-\infty\) if \(Ax\le b\), \(Ad\le0\), \(d\ne0\), and either \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd<0\), or \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd=0\) and \(d^{\mathsf T}(Qx+c)<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point and a nonzero recession direction certify unboundedness when the exact quadratic ray coefficients force the objective to negative infinity.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(P=\{z\in\mathbb R^n:Az\le b\}\neq\varnothing\).
\(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric, \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Verification Cost of a Rational Ray Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic and bit complexity of checking the seed certificate for explicitly encoded rational data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(A,b,Q,c,x,d\) in the seed certificate are rational and encoded explicitly. The conditions \(Ax\le b\), \(Ad\le0\), \(d\ne0\), and the required signs of \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd\) and \(d^{\mathsf T}(Qx+c)\) can be checked using \(O(mn+n^2)\) rational arithmetic operations. Exact rational arithmetic verifies the certificate in time polynomial in the total encoded size of the input and witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For rational data, a proposed feasible-origin and recession-direction certificate is exactly verifiable in polynomial time.
assumptions_latex: \(A,b,Q,c,x,d\) have rational entries with explicit binary encodings.

children.title: Recession Evidence Boundary
children.top_down_role: Cases where unbounded behavior is difficult to expose through simple directional evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Recession Evidence Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A nonimproving tested ray cannot establish global boundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, let \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) satisfy \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\), let \(c\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\), and define \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+\gamma\). For \(x\in P\) and \(d\in\operatorname{rec}(P)\setminus\{0\}\), set \(a=d^{\mathsf T}Qd\) and \(s=d^{\mathsf T}(Qx+c)\). If \(a>0\), or if \(a=0\) and \(s\ge0\), then \(f(x+td)\) does not tend to \(-\infty\) as \(t\to\infty\). This excludes only the selected pair \((x,d)\) as an unboundedness certificate; it does not exclude another improving recession direction and does not imply \(\inf_{z\in P}f(z)>-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tested ray that does not decrease indefinitely is excluded as an unboundedness certificate, but this alone cannot prove that the quadratic program is bounded below.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric, \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a>0\) or \((a=0\land s\ge0)\) invalidates the selected ray as an unboundedness certificate but does not imply \(\inf_{z\in P}f(z)>-\infty\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Nonimproving Ray Does Not Imply Boundedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rejecting one tested recession ray provides no global boundedness conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\mathbb R^2\), \(f(x_1,x_2)=x_1^2-x_2^2\), and \(x=(0,0)\). For \(d_1=(1,0)\), \(f(x+td_1)=t^2\to+\infty\). For \(d_2=(0,1)\), \(f(x+td_2)=-t^2\to-\infty\). Thus \(\inf_P f=-\infty\) despite the nonimproving tested ray \(d_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An indefinite quadratic may increase along one recession ray while tending to minus infinity along another.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_1\text{ is nonimproving, while }f(x+td_2)\to-\infty\text{ and }\inf_P f=-\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: A Nonimproving Ray Does Not Imply Boundedness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validated Spectral Box Bound for a Quadratic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outward-rounded lower bound for a quadratic objective on one coordinate box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\), where \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\), and let \(B=\{m+s:|s_i|\le r_i\}\). Put \(g=Qm+c\). If validated arithmetic certifies \(\underline\lambda\le\lambda_{\min}(Q)\), then \[q(x)\ge q(m)-\sum_{i=1}^n|g_i|r_i+\tfrac12\min\{\underline\lambda,0\}\|r\|_2^2=:L_B\quad(x\in B).\] If every operation producing \(\widehat L_B\) is rounded outward toward \(-\infty\), then \(\widehat L_B\le L_B\le\inf_{x\in B}q(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified lower eigenvalue bound and directed rounding give a rigorous quadratic lower bound on a box.
assumptions_latex: Evaluation of \(\widehat L_B\) encloses all arithmetic errors downward.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat L_B\le\inf_{x\in B}q(x)\).

notation.meaning: Validated lower bound on the smallest eigenvalue of Q.

knowledge_statements.title: Validated Spectral Box Bound for a Quadratic

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rigorous global QCQP lower bound from a verified convex quadratic Lagrangian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\inf\{q_0(x):q_j(x)\le0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), choose \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\), and write \(L_\lambda(x)=q_0(x)+\sum_j\lambda_jq_j(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}H_\lambda x+h_\lambda^{\mathsf T}x+k_\lambda\). If validated linear algebra certifies \(H_\lambda\succ0\) and outward-rounded computation certifies \(\underline d\le k_\lambda-\tfrac12h_\lambda^{\mathsf T}H_\lambda^{-1}h_\lambda\), then \(\underline d\le\inf\{q_0(x):q_j(x)\le0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A verified positive-definite quadratic Lagrangian and a downward-rounded enclosure of its minimum give a rigorous global lower bound.
assumptions_latex: Validated computation certifies \(H_\lambda\succ0\) and encloses the minimum value downward.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline d\le\inf\{q_0(x):q_j(x)\le0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\).

notation.meaning: Quadratic Lagrangian associated with nonnegative multipliers.
Validated downward enclosure of the Lagrangian minimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Validated Quadratic-Lagrangian Lower Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nearest-Rounded Curvature Can Invalidate a Box Lower Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact scalar example showing why a purported curvature lower bound and its evaluation must be outward validated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=-1-2^{-54}\), \(q(x)=\tfrac12Qx^2\), and \(B=[-1,1]\). Then \(\inf_{x\in B}q(x)=\tfrac12Q=-\tfrac12-2^{-55}\). If the exactly specified coefficient \(Q\) is converted to binary64 by ordinary round-to-nearest, it is stored as \(\widetilde Q=-1\). Treating \(\widetilde\lambda=-1\) as though it were a certified lower bound on \(\lambda_{\min}(Q)\) yields the claimed box lower bound \(\widetilde L=-\tfrac12\), but \(\widetilde L>\inf_{x\in B}q(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nearest rounding can move negative curvature upward and produce a purported quadratic lower bound that lies above the true minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=-1-2^{-54}\) is the exact rational input coefficient.
Coefficient conversion uses binary64 round-to-nearest rather than directed downward rounding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widetilde L=-\tfrac12>-	frac12-2^{-55}=\inf_{x\in[-1,1]}q(x)\).

notation.meaning: Purported lower bound computed from the nonvalidated coefficient.

knowledge_statements.title: Nearest-Rounded Curvature Can Invalidate a Box Lower Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp finite-minimum extension of validated Lagrangian bounding to singular positive-semidefinite curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+h^{\mathsf T}x+k\), with \(H\succeq0\). If validated linear algebra certifies \(h\in\operatorname{Range}(H)\) and certifies a downward-rounded number \(\underline d\le k-\tfrac12h^{\mathsf T}H^{\dagger}h\), then \(L(x)\ge\underline d\) for all \(x\). Consequently, when \(L=q_0+\sum_j\lambda_jq_j\) with \(\lambda\ge0\), \(\underline d\) is a rigorous lower bound for \(\inf\{q_0(x):q_j(x)\le0\}\). If the range condition fails, \(\inf_xL(x)=-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular positive-semidefinite quadratic Lagrangian has a finite validated minimum exactly when its linear term lies in the Hessian range; otherwise it is unbounded below.
assumptions_latex: Validated computation certifies either \(h\in\operatorname{Range}(H)\) or its failure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h\in\operatorname{Range}(H)\Rightarrow \underline d\le\inf_xL(x)\); otherwise \(\inf_xL(x)=-\infty\).

notation.meaning: Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of the Lagrangian Hessian
Downward-rounded enclosure of the finite quadratic minimum

knowledge_statements.title: Validated Singular-PSD Quadratic-Lagrangian Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Entrywise validated lower eigenvalue bound for use in rigorous quadratic box bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\). Suppose validated arithmetic gives \(\underline q_{ii}\le Q_{ii}\) and \(\overline a_{ij}\ge |Q_{ij}|\) for \(i\ne j\). With all sums and subtractions rigorously enclosed downward, define \[\underline\lambda_G=\min_i\left(\underline q_{ii}-\sum_{j\ne i}\overline a_{ij}\right).\] Then \(\underline\lambda_G\le\lambda_{\min}(Q)\). The certificate requires \(O(\operatorname{nnz}(Q)+n)\) arithmetic operations when the stored sparsity pattern is scanned once, and \(\underline\lambda_G\) may replace the validated curvature lower bound in a rigorous spectral box bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outward-rounded Gershgorin row bounds give an inexpensive rigorous lower enclosure of a symmetric quadratic matrix's smallest eigenvalue.
assumptions_latex: Diagonal entries are enclosed downward and off-diagonal magnitudes upward.
Row sums and the final minimum use rigorous directed enclosures.
The complexity count assumes standard sparse storage and explicit diagonal access.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline\lambda_G\le\lambda_{\min}(Q)\), computable in \(O(\operatorname{nnz}(Q)+n)\) arithmetic operations.

notation.meaning: Validated Gershgorin lower bound on the smallest eigenvalue

review_flags: The certificate may be conservative; it establishes validity, not tightness.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Outward-Rounded Natural Interval Bound for a Quadratic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct validated evaluation of a sparse quadratic over one coordinate box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12\sum_iQ_{ii}x_i^2+\sum_{i<j}Q_{ij}x_ix_j+\sum_i c_ix_i+d\), where \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\), and let \(B=\prod_i[\ell_i,u_i]\). Using outward-rounded interval arithmetic and enclosing intervals for all coefficients, evaluate every displayed term and their sum to obtain \([\underline q_B,\overline q_B]\). Then \(q(B)\subseteq[\underline q_B,\overline q_B]\), so \(\underline q_B\le\inf_{x\in B}q(x)\). Scanning a sparse symmetric representation once uses \(O(\operatorname{nnz}(Q)+n)\) interval operations and constant auxiliary storage beyond the input and interval accumulator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outward-rounded termwise interval evaluation gives a rigorous, potentially conservative lower bound for a quadratic on a box in work linear in its stored nonzeros.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\), and every coefficient is exact or represented by an enclosing interval.
Every interval product and sum is evaluated with outward rounding.
Each symmetric off-diagonal coefficient is included exactly once in the displayed representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline q_B\le\inf_{x\in B}q(x)\), using \(O(\operatorname{nnz}(Q)+n)\) interval operations.

notation.meaning: Coordinate box on which the quadratic is bounded.

knowledge_statements.title: Outward-Rounded Natural Interval Bound for a Quadratic
Validated QP Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outward-rounded regional bounds combine into a rigorous global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^m B_i\), where the \(B_i\) are search regions. Suppose validated arithmetic produces numbers \(L_i\) satisfying \(L_i\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in C\cap B_i\), including all rounding and relaxation errors. Then \[L=\min_{1\le i\le m}L_i\le\inf_{x\in C}f(x).\] If a rigorously feasible point \(\hat x\in C\) is also available, then \([L,f(\hat x)]\) encloses the global optimal value. The certificate is auditable through the cover, regional bounds, and directed-rounding records.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validated regional lower bounds over a finite cover yield a rigorous global bound; a verified feasible point supplies the matching upper bound.
assumptions_latex: \(L_i\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in C\cap B_i\), with numerical errors enclosed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\le\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\), and a verified \(\hat x\in C\) gives \(\inf_C f\in[L,f(\hat x)]\).

children.title: Tolerance-Aware Pruning
children.top_down_role: Reliable node elimination near feasibility or dominance thresholds.

knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Aware Pruning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe branch-and-bound pruning relative to a requested absolute optimality tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the feasible set for minimizing \(f:C\to\mathbb R\), let \(B\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a search region, and let \(U=f(\hat x)\) for a verified feasible incumbent \(\hat x\in C\). Suppose \(L_B\in\mathbb R\) satisfies \(L_B\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in C\cap B\). For an absolute tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), the region \(B\) may be pruned when \[L_B\ge U-\varepsilon.\] If certified interval enclosures \(\boldsymbol L_B=[\underline L_B,\overline L_B]\) and \(\boldsymbol U=[\underline U,\overline U]\) contain \(L_B\) and \(U\), respectively, then the directed-rounding test \(\underline L_B\ge\overline U-\varepsilon\) is sufficient for pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A search region may be pruned when its certified lower bound proves that no feasible point in the region can improve the verified incumbent by more than the allowed absolute tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(U=f(\hat x)\) for a verified \(\hat x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_B\ge U-\varepsilon\) permits safe pruning of \(B\) for absolute \(\varepsilon\)-optimality.

notation.meaning: certified lower bound for the search region

children.title: Tolerance-Aware Termination
children.top_down_role: Reliable stopping near absolute or relative global-gap thresholds.

knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Aware Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global stopping test using certified lower and feasible upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the feasible set for minimizing \(f:C\to\mathbb R\), and define \(f^\star=\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\). Let \(U=f(\hat x)\) for a verified feasible incumbent \(\hat x\in C\), and let \(L\) be a certified global lower bound satisfying \(L\le f^\star\). For an absolute tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), termination is certified when \[U-L\le\varepsilon.\] Under this condition, \(f(\hat x)-f^\star\le\varepsilon\). If certified intervals \(\boldsymbol U=[\underline U,\overline U]\) and \(\boldsymbol L=[\underline L,\overline L]\) contain \(U\) and \(L\), respectively, then \(\overline U-\underline L\le\varepsilon\) is a sufficient outward-rounded termination test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Termination is certified when the verified incumbent and a certified global lower bound differ by no more than the requested absolute tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(U=f(\hat x)\) for a verified \(\hat x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U-L\le\varepsilon\) implies \(f(\hat x)-f^\star\le\varepsilon\).

children.title: Feasibility-Tolerance Interaction
children.top_down_role: Influence of feasibility tolerances on pruning and incumbent validity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual-Feasible Values Need Not Be Upper Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample family showing why an infeasible approximate point cannot be used directly as an incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R:x\ge0\}\) and \(f(x)=x\), the optimum is \(f^*=0\). For every \(\delta>0\), the point \(\tilde x=-\delta\) has constraint residual \(\delta\) but objective value \(f(\tilde x)=-\delta<f^*\). Hence residual feasibility alone does not make \(f(\tilde x)\) a valid upper bound; feasibility repair, exact verification, or a certified error allowance is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An arbitrarily small feasibility violation can produce an objective value below the true optimum, so the value of a merely tolerance-feasible point is not automatically an incumbent upper bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\tilde x)=-\delta<f^*=0\) despite feasibility residual \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Feasible Values Need Not Be Upper Bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-compatible conversion of polyhedral residual error into distance and objective-value error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\ne\varnothing\), and fix norms \(\|\cdot\|_p\) on points and \(\|\cdot\|_r\) on residuals. There exists a Hoffman constant \(H<\infty\), depending on \(A\) and the chosen norms, such that \[\operatorname{dist}_p(x,P)\le H\|(Ax-b)_+\|_r\quad\text{for every }x.\] If \(\|(A\tilde x-b)_+\|_r\le\varepsilon_f\), \(x^P\in P\) realizes the distance, and \(f\) is \(K\)-Lipschitz on a set containing the segment between \(\tilde x\) and \(x^P\), then \[|f(\tilde x)-f(x^P)|\le KH\varepsilon_f.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty polyhedron, a norm-compatible Hoffman constant converts constraint residual into distance to feasibility; local Lipschitz continuity then converts that distance into objective error.
assumptions_latex: The point and residual norms are fixed and \(H\) is their corresponding Hoffman constant.
\(f\) is \(K\)-Lipschitz on the segment joining \(\tilde x\) to a nearest feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}_p(\tilde x,P)\le H\varepsilon_f\) and \(|f(\tilde x)-f(x^P)|\le KH\varepsilon_f\).

notation.meaning: Hoffman constant for the declared pair of norms
Lipschitz constant of the objective on the relevant segment
Nearest feasible point in the declared point norm

knowledge_statements.title: Hoffman–Lipschitz Feasibility Error Propagation
Feasibility-Tolerance Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of constraint residual tolerance into distance and objective error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\), and suppose a computed point \(\tilde x\) satisfies \(\lVert(A\tilde x-b)_+\rVert_\infty\le\varepsilon_f\). If a Hoffman constant \(H\) is valid, then \(\operatorname{dist}(\tilde x,P)\le H\varepsilon_f\). If \(f\) is \(K\)-Lipschitz on a neighborhood containing \(\tilde x\) and a nearest feasible point \(x^P\), then \[|f(\tilde x)-f(x^P)|\le KH\varepsilon_f.\] Thus an objective certificate using \(\tilde x\) must include this feasibility-induced error unless feasibility is verified exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual feasibility tolerance affects objective certification through an error bound and the objective's local Lipschitz constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(\tilde x,P)\le H\varepsilon_f\) and \(|f(\tilde x)-f(x^P)|\le KH\varepsilon_f\).

notation.meaning: local Lipschitz constant of the objective

children.title: Numerical Ambiguity Boundary
children.top_down_role: Near-threshold cases where finite precision obscures a reliable search decision.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit enclosure family for which midpoint arithmetic falsely certifies a zero-tolerance decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varepsilon=0\), \(\boldsymbol L=[0,2]\), and \(\boldsymbol U=[1,1]\). Comparing midpoints gives \(\operatorname{mid}(\boldsymbol L)=\operatorname{mid}(\boldsymbol U)=1\), which would suggest both \(L\ge U\) for pruning and \(U-L=0\) for termination. Yet the enclosed values may be \(L=0\) and \(U=1\), for which neither conclusion holds. The certified endpoint tests correctly fail because \(\underline L=0<1=\overline U\) and \(\overline U-\underline L=1>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal interval midpoints can suggest pruning or termination even though admissible enclosed values violate both decisions.
assumptions_latex: The intervals are treated as certified enclosures rather than point values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Midpoint equality does not certify \(L\ge U\) or \(U-L\le0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Midpoint Decision Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unknown outcome when certified enclosures do not establish either side of a pruning or termination threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\boldsymbol L=[\underline L,\overline L]\) and \(\boldsymbol U=[\underline U,\overline U]\) be outward-rounded enclosures of a valid lower bound \(L\) and a verified feasible value \(U\). At tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), pruning is certified if \(\underline L\ge\overline U-\varepsilon\), and termination is certified if \(\overline U-\underline L\le\varepsilon\). If the relevant sufficient endpoint inequality fails, the requested action is not certified; failure does not establish its negation. The correct outcome is unknown until tighter enclosures, increased precision, or additional search information resolves the comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validated threshold comparisons have three outcomes: certified action, certified contrary inequality when available, or unknown; overlapping enclosures must not be forced into a decision.
assumptions_latex: \(L\in\boldsymbol L\) and \(U\in\boldsymbol U\) with outward-rounded certified endpoints.
\(L\) is a valid lower bound and \(U\) is a verified feasible value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of the sufficient endpoint test leaves pruning or termination uncertified.

notation.meaning: Certified enclosure of the lower bound
Certified enclosure of the feasible upper bound

knowledge_statements.title: Three-Way Validated Threshold Decision
Numerical Ambiguity Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Overlapping enclosures cannot support pruning or termination decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let certified intervals \(\boldsymbol L=[\underline L,\overline L]\) and \(\boldsymbol U=[\underline U,\overline U]\) contain a true lower bound and a feasible upper bound, respectively. Pruning at tolerance \(\varepsilon\) is certified by \(\underline L\ge\overline U-\varepsilon\), and termination is certified by \(\overline U-\underline L\le\varepsilon\). If the relevant endpoint inequality fails because the enclosures overlap its decision threshold, the numerical data are ambiguous: neither action is certified. More precision, tighter bounds, or further subdivision is required; midpoint comparisons are invalid certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When rigorous bound intervals overlap a pruning or stopping threshold, the algorithm must refine rather than decide from midpoint values.
assumptions_latex: \(\boldsymbol L\) and \(\boldsymbol U\) are outward-rounded certified enclosures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of the appropriate endpoint test leaves pruning or termination uncertified.

interval enclosure of the feasible upper bound

children.title: Certificate Auditing
children.top_down_role: Retained evidence needed for independent checking of a global-QP result.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic retained evidence and verification conditions, with lower-bound witness checks delegated to the method that produced the bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q^*=\inf_{x\in P}q(x)\), an independently auditable \(\tau\)-global certificate consists of a reproducible description of \(q\) and \(P\), retained evidence verifying \(\hat x\in P\), a method-specific witness whose independently checked conditions imply \(L\le q^*\), and validated evaluations enclosing \(U=q(\hat x)\) and \(L\). Acceptance requires verified inequalities \[L\le q^*\le U,\qquad U-L\le\tau.\] A solver status, log, or unvalidated floating-point residual that does not establish these predicates is not by itself a mathematical certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An audit must reproduce the instance, verify incumbent feasibility, check the bound method's witness, validate the reported values, and confirm the requested gap; logs and unchecked residuals alone are insufficient.
assumptions_latex: The audited instance and its numerical representation are identified reproducibly.
The retained lower-bound witness has a specified verification rule implying \(L\le q^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\le q^*\le U\) and \(U-L\le\tau\) certify \(q(\hat x)-q^*\le\tau\).

notation.meaning: Verified lower and feasible upper objective bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Method-Independent Global-QP Audit Predicate
Certificate Auditing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic audit predicate for retained global-QP primal and lower-bound evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An auditable global-optimality certificate retains \(Q,c,d\), the complete description of \(P\), a feasible point \(\hat x\), and independently checkable bound data proving \(L\le q^*:=\min_{x\in P}q(x)\). An auditor recomputes feasibility, verifies every algebraic or conic constraint supporting \(L\), and evaluates \(U=q(\hat x)\) with directed rounding or validated error bounds. Acceptance requires \(\hat x\in P\), \(L\le q^*\le U\), and \(U-L\le\tau\); thus \(\hat x\) is certified \(\tau\)-globally optimal. Solver logs or unverified floating-point residuals alone do not establish these inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Audit acceptance requires reproducible feasibility, a validated lower bound, a feasible upper bound, and a certified gap within tolerance; unverified solver logs are insufficient.
assumptions_latex: The instance is \(\min\{q(x):x\in P\}\), where \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2c^{\mathsf T}x+d\) and \(P\) is compact.
Reported primal and lower-bound values use a declared absolute tolerance \(\tau\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance requires \(\hat x\in P\), \(L\le q^*\le U\), and \(U-L\le\tau\), certifying \(\hat x\) as \(\tau\)-globally optimal.

notation.meaning: Certified lower and feasible upper objective bounds.

children.title: Box-QP Hardness
children.top_down_role: Hardness retained under simple bounded continuous domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Box-QP Hardness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact NP-hardness through a weighted Max-Cut reduction to continuous box minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a weighted graph \(G=(V,E)\), define \(q(x)=-\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}(x_i+x_j-2x_ix_j)\). The polynomial \(q\) is affine in each coordinate separately, so it has a box minimizer in \(\{0,1\}^n\). For every binary \(x\), \(-q(x)\) equals the weight of the cut encoded by \(x\). Consequently, \(\min_{x\in[0,1]^n}q(x)=-\operatorname{MaxCut}(G)\). Hence exact continuous quadratic minimization over a box, and its rational threshold-decision version, are NP-hard despite bounded continuous variables and no general linear constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted Max-Cut is exactly the negative minimum of a multi-affine quadratic over a continuous unit box, proving NP-hardness of box-constrained quadratic minimization.
assumptions_latex: The edge weights \(w_{ij}\) are nonnegative rational numbers.
Optimization is over the continuous box \([0,1]^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in[0,1]^n}q(x)=-\operatorname{MaxCut}(G)\), so exact box-constrained quadratic minimization and its rational threshold-decision version are NP-hard.

notation.meaning: Multi-affine quadratic encoding the negative cut weight.

children.title: Concave-Minimization Hardness
children.top_down_role: Combinatorial difficulty induced by concave minimization over polyhedra.

knowledge_statements.title: Concave-Minimization Hardness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak NP-hardness reduction from subset sum using a strictly concave integrality detector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n x_i(1-x_i)\). Its Hessian is \(-2I\), so \(f\) is concave, and \(f(x)\ge0\) on \([0,1]^n\). Moreover, \(f(x)=0\) exactly when \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\). Therefore \(\min_{x\in P}f(x)=0\) if and only if the subset-sum equation \(a^{\mathsf T}x=b\) has a binary solution. Deciding whether a concave quadratic has minimum zero over a nonempty rational polytope is consequently NP-hard. Concavity places some minimizer at an extreme point but does not make the combinatorial selection tractable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a nonempty subset-sum polytope, a concave quadratic vanishes precisely at binary box points, so testing whether its minimum is zero decides subset sum.
assumptions_latex: The input consists of positive integers \(a_1,\ldots,a_n,b\) encoded in binary, with \(b\le\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\).
The feasible polytope is \(P=\{x\in[0,1]^n:a^{\mathsf T}x=b\}\), which is nonempty under the stated restriction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in P}f(x)=0\) if and only if \(a^{\mathsf T}x=b\) has a binary solution; hence the zero-minimum decision problem for concave quadratic minimization over a rational polytope is NP-hard.

notation.meaning: Subset-sum equality polytope inside the unit box.

children.title: Binary-Quadratic Embedding Hardness
children.top_down_role: Continuous models inheriting discrete quadratic hardness through embeddings.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-preserving embedding of an unconstrained rational binary quadratic into continuous unit-box quadratic minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let p(z)=z^{\mathsf T}Qz+2c^{\mathsf T}z+d with Q=Q^{\mathsf T}, and choose rational M>\max_i Q_{ii}. Define F_M(x)=p(x)+M\sum_{i=1}^n x_i(1-x_i) on [0,1]^n. Then F_M is strictly concave in each coordinate separately, every feasible point can be replaced coordinatewise by a vertex with no larger objective value, and the penalty vanishes on {0,1}^n. Consequently, \min_{x\in[0,1]^n}F_M(x)=\min_{z\in\{0,1\}^n}p(z). The construction has polynomial encoding size and transfers NP-hardness of unconstrained binary quadratic minimization to continuous box-QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial-size separable quadratic penalty makes every coordinate concave, forces an equally good box vertex, and embeds binary quadratic minimization exactly into continuous box-QP.
assumptions_latex: p(z)=z^{\mathsf T}Qz+2c^{\mathsf T}z+d has rational data and Q=Q^{\mathsf T}.
M is rational and satisfies M>\max_i Q_{ii}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{x\in[0,1]^n}F_M(x)=\min_{z\in\{0,1\}^n}p(z), yielding a polynomial reduction from binary quadratic minimization to continuous box-QP.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Separable-Penalty Embedding
Binary-Quadratic Embedding Hardness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact box embedding by a separable quadratic penalty that forces an optimal vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the continuous quadratic \(F_M(x)=p(x)+M\sum_{i=1}^n x_i(1-x_i)\) on \([0,1]^n\). Holding all other coordinates fixed, the coefficient of \(x_i^2\) is \(Q_{ii}-M<0\); hence a coordinatewise minimum is attained at \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\). Replacing fractional coordinates successively by minimizing endpoints produces a vertex \(z\) with \(F_M(z)\le F_M(x)\). Since the penalty vanishes at every vertex, \(\min_{x\in[0,1]^n}F_M(x)=\min_{z\in\{0,1\}^n}p(z)\). Thus every NP-hard binary quadratic optimization family embeds exactly into continuous box-QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sufficiently strong separable quadratic penalty makes each coordinate concave, forcing a box optimum to a vertex while preserving every binary objective value and transferring binary-QP hardness.
assumptions_latex: The binary objective is \(p(z)=z^{\mathsf T}Qz+2c^{\mathsf T}z+d\), with rational symmetric \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in[0,1]^n}F_M(x)=\min_{z\in\{0,1\}^n}p(z)\), so NP-hard binary quadratic families embed exactly into continuous box-QP.

children.title: Single-Quadratic-Constraint Tractability
children.top_down_role: Efficient regimes supported by hidden convexity and exact quadratic alternatives.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global Optimality Certificate for One Quadratic Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar-multiplier certificate obtained from the S-lemma under strict feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q_i(x)=x^{\mathsf T}A_i x+2b_i^{\mathsf T}x+c_i\), and suppose some \(\bar x\) satisfies \(q_1(\bar x)<0\). A feasible point \(x^*\) is globally optimal for \(\min\{q_0(x):q_1(x)\le0\}\) if there exists \(\lambda^*\ge0\) such that \(A_0+\lambda^*A_1\succeq0\), \((A_0+\lambda^*A_1)x^*+b_0+\lambda^*b_1=0\), and \(\lambda^*q_1(x^*)=0\). If the finite optimum is attained, the S-lemma guarantees such a multiplier at a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under strict feasibility, feasibility, complementary slackness, stationarity, and a positive-semidefinite Lagrangian Hessian give a global optimality certificate; under attainment such a certificate exists.
assumptions_latex: For the existence assertion, the finite optimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q_1(x^*)\le0,\ \lambda^*\ge0,\ \lambda^*q_1(x^*)=0,\ \nabla(q_0+\lambda^*q_1)(x^*)=0,\ A_0+\lambda^*A_1\succeq0\ \Longrightarrow\ x^*\text{ is globally optimal}.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative multiplier for the sole quadratic inequality.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Optimality Certificate for One Quadratic Inequality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary failure of the classical scalar-multiplier S-lemma when strict feasibility is absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q_1(x)=x^2\) and \(q_0(x)=2x\). The feasible set \(\{x:q_1(x)\le0\}\) is \(\{0\}\), so \(q_0(x)\ge0\) on it. Nevertheless, for every \(\lambda\ge0\), the polynomial \(q_0(x)+\lambda q_1(x)=2x+\lambda x^2\) is negative at some real \(x\). Thus the usual scalar-multiplier conclusion can fail without strict feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The degenerate constraint x squared at most zero satisfies the desired implication only at zero, but no nonnegative multiplier makes the augmented quadratic globally nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q_1(x)\le0\Rightarrow q_0(x)\ge0\quad\text{but}\quad\nexists\lambda\ge0:\ q_0(x)+\lambda q_1(x)\ge0\ \forall x.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure Without Strict Feasibility
Single-Quadratic-Constraint Tractability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Slater-qualified S-lemma formulation for one quadratic inequality and finite optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p^*=\inf\{q_0(x):q_1(x)\le0\}\), the S-lemma gives the exact semidefinite dual representation \(p^*=\sup\{\gamma:\exists\lambda\ge0,\ M(\lambda,\gamma)\succeq0\}\), where \(M(\lambda,\gamma)=\begin{pmatrix}A_0+\lambda A_1&b_0+\lambda b_1\\(b_0+\lambda b_1)^{\mathsf T}&c_0+\lambda c_1-\gamma\end{pmatrix}\). The matrix inequality is equivalent to \(q_0(x)+\lambda q_1(x)-\gamma\ge0\) for every \(x\). Thus the optimal value with one quadratic inequality has an exact convex SDP representation; polynomial-time weak optimization additionally requires a specified rational SDP model and the usual quantitative boundedness or conditioning assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under strict feasibility and finite value, a quadratic program with one quadratic inequality has an exact S-lemma semidefinite value formulation; weak polynomial-time optimization requires a precise rational SDP model and quantitative bounds.
assumptions_latex: Let \(q_i(x)=x^{\mathsf T}A_i x+2b_i^{\mathsf T}x+c_i\) for \(i\in\{0,1\}\), with symmetric rational matrices.
There exists \(\bar x\) satisfying \(q_1(\bar x)<0\), and the primal infimum is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^*=\sup\{\gamma:\exists\lambda\ge0,\ M(\lambda,\gamma)\succeq0\}\); weak polynomial-time optimization requires an explicitly specified rational SDP complexity model and quantitative bounds.

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the one-constraint quadratic problem.
Nonnegative multiplier for the quadratic inequality.

children.title: Fixed-Dimension Tractability
children.top_down_role: Global solvability when continuous dimension is treated as fixed.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit-complexity of rational quadratic threshold feasibility over a rational polytope when the continuous dimension is fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed n, the sentence \exists x\in\mathbb R^n\,[Ax\le b\ \wedge\ x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2c^{\mathsf T}x+d\le\alpha] contains a fixed number of real variables and polynomials of degree at most two. Fixed-variable existential real-algebraic decision algorithms decide it in time polynomial in the number of inequalities and the binary coefficient length, with the polynomial exponent allowed to depend on n. Thus rational quadratic threshold optimization over a bounded rational polytope is polynomial-time decidable for fixed n. This statement does not give a uniform polynomial bound when n is input, and exact values or optimizers require an algebraic output representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic threshold feasibility over a rational polytope is polynomial-time decidable when the number of continuous variables is fixed; variable dimension and exact algebraic output are separate boundaries.
assumptions_latex: A,b,Q,c,d,\alpha are rational and encoded in binary, with Q=Q^{\mathsf T}.
P=\{x:Ax\le b\} is bounded for the optimization interpretation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For fixed n, deciding whether \min_{x\in P}(x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2c^{\mathsf T}x+d)\le\alpha is polynomial in the input length; no such claim is made for variable n or an unspecified exact-output encoding.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Dimension Quadratic Threshold Tractability
Fixed-Dimension Tractability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit-complexity claim for rational polyhedral QP with fixed continuous dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The threshold question \(\exists x\in\mathbb R^n\,[Ax\le b\ \wedge\ x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2c^{\mathsf T}x+d\le\alpha]\) is an existential semialgebraic decision problem with fixed variable dimension and degree two. Fixed-dimensional real-algebraic decision algorithms determine it in time polynomial in the number of inequalities and coefficient bit length, with the polynomial degree allowed to depend on \(n\). Consequently, rational threshold decisions for global quadratic optimization over a bounded rational polytope are polynomial-time solvable when \(n\) is fixed. Exact optimal values or optimizers require an explicitly specified algebraic output representation; no polynomial claim is made when \(n\) is part of the input.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With dimension fixed, quadratic threshold feasibility over a bounded rational polytope is a fixed-variable semialgebraic problem decidable in polynomial input time; exact outputs require an algebraic encoding.
assumptions_latex: The dimension \(n\) is a fixed constant.
The quadratic objective, rational polytope \(P=\{x:Ax\le b\}\), and rational threshold \(\alpha\) are encoded in binary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For fixed \(n\), rational quadratic threshold feasibility over \(P\) is decidable in polynomial input time; exact optimizer claims require a specified algebraic output model.

children.title: Restricted-Inertia Tractability
children.top_down_role: Efficient or parameterized behavior governed by few nonconvex curvature directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Inertia Tractability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional tractability with fixed negative inertia and polynomially manageable projected feasible geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2c^{\mathsf T}x+d\), introducing \(y=U^{\mathsf T}x\) yields \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Hx+2c^{\mathsf T}x+d-\|y\|_2^2\). Conditional on the stated polynomial-size exact decomposition of \(U^{\mathsf T}P\), enumerate its regions, construct on each the stipulated valid affine lower representation of \(-\|y\|_2^2\) that is exact at all candidate data required by the decomposition theorem, and solve the resulting convex quadratic subproblems. If that theorem guarantees that these candidates contain a global minimizer, fixed \(r\) and a polynomial decomposition yield a polynomial number of convex solves. Restricted inertia alone does not guarantee such a projection description.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed negative inertia supports the stated polynomial reduction only when an exact theorem supplies a polynomially manageable projected decomposition whose convex subproblems contain a global minimizer.
assumptions_latex: The objective Hessian admits \(Q=H-UU^{\mathsf T}\), where \(H\succeq0\) and \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\).
An exact polynomial-size decomposition theorem for \(U^{\mathsf T}P\) supplies convex subproblems whose candidates include a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under the stated exact decomposition theorem, the problem reduces to polynomially many convex quadratic solves; fixed negative inertia alone is not sufficient.

notation.meaning: Basis factor for the nonconvex subspace.

children.title: Low-Rank Tractability
children.top_down_role: Efficient or parameterized behavior governed by low-rank quadratic structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rational threshold decision for box-QP with fixed total Hessian rank through a fixed-dimensional zonotope projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let B=[\ell,u]\subset\mathbb R^n be a rational box and let the rational symmetric matrix Q have rank at most the fixed constant r. A rational factorization Q=USU^{\mathsf T} gives y=U^{\mathsf T}x and x^{\mathsf T}Qx=y^{\mathsf T}Sy. Appending z=c^{\mathsf T}x projects B to the zonotope Z=\{(U^{\mathsf T}x,c^{\mathsf T}x):x\in B\}\subset\mathbb R^{r+1}, while the objective becomes y^{\mathsf T}Sy+2z+d. For fixed r, Z has polynomial combinatorial complexity and a rational polyhedral description can be enumerated in polynomial time. Fixed-dimensional quadratic threshold feasibility over Z is then decidable in polynomial input time. Hence rational box-QP with fixed total Hessian rank has a polynomial-time threshold-decision algorithm; the exponent may depend on r, and the conclusion does not extend by this argument when r is variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-total-rank box quadratic projects, together with its linear term, to a fixed-dimensional zonotope; enumerating that zonotope and solving the resulting fixed-dimensional threshold problem yields polynomial-time exact decision.
assumptions_latex: B=[\ell,u] is a nonempty rational box.
Q is rational symmetric with rank at most a fixed constant r.
The objective data and rational threshold are encoded in binary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For fixed r, deciding whether \min_{x\in B}(x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2c^{\mathsf T}x+d)\le\alpha is polynomial in the input length; the bound is not uniform in variable r.

notation.meaning: Fixed-dimensional zonotope image of the box.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Rank Box-QP Projection Algorithm
Low-Rank Tractability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional fixed-rank rational box-QP via fixed-dimensional zonotope enumeration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(y=U^{\mathsf T}x\). Then \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx=y^{\mathsf T}Sy\), and \(U^{\mathsf T}B\) is an \(r\)-dimensional zonotope generated by the columns of \(U^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{diag}(u-\ell)\). For fixed \(r\), its faces and vertices have polynomial combinatorial complexity in \(n\). Including the linear term as an additional projected coordinate keeps the projected dimension fixed. An exact polynomial-time algorithm additionally requires a theorem reducing minimization of the resulting projected quadratic-linear objective to a polynomially enumerable family of exactly solvable auxiliary problems. Subject to that theorem and exact rational arithmetic, fixed-rank box-QP is tractable; variable rank removes the fixed-dimensional enumeration bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-rank box quadratic projects to a fixed-dimensional zonotope of polynomial combinatorial complexity, but exact tractability also requires a justified reduction from the projected objective to polynomially many solvable auxiliary problems.
assumptions_latex: The feasible region is the rational box \(B=[\ell,u]\subset\mathbb R^n\).
The symmetric objective matrix factors as \(Q=USU^{\mathsf T}\), with fixed rank \(r\).
An exact reduction theorem supplies polynomially many solvable auxiliary problems for the projected quadratic-linear objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under the stated exact reduction theorem, fixed-rank rational box-QP is solvable through polynomially bounded fixed-dimensional zonotope enumeration; this bound does not extend to variable rank.

notation.meaning: Fixed-rank factor of the quadratic matrix.

children.title: Nonconvex-Subspace Parameterization
children.top_down_role: Complexity organized by the dimension of the effective nonconvex subspace.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex-Subspace Parameterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral parameterization isolating every negative-curvature direction of an indefinite quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exist \(H\succeq0\), \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), and diagonal \(D\succ0\) such that \(Q=H-UDU^{\mathsf T}\). With \(y=D^{1/2}U^{\mathsf T}x\), the objective has the exact representation \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Hx+2c^{\mathsf T}x+d-\|y\|_2^2\), subject to the linking equation \(y=D^{1/2}U^{\mathsf T}x\). Hence all negative curvature is confined to the \(r\)-dimensional coordinate \(y\); for fixed \(y\), minimizing over \(x\) subject to convex feasible constraints is a convex quadratic problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spectral decomposition isolates all nonconvexity in as many projected coordinates as the Hessian has negative eigenvalues; fixing them leaves a convex quadratic problem.
assumptions_latex: The objective is \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2c^{\mathsf T}x+d\), with symmetric \(Q\).
The matrix \(Q\) has exactly \(r\) negative eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All negative curvature is confined to \(y\in\mathbb R^r\); fixing \(y\) leaves a convex quadratic problem in \(x\) under convex feasible constraints.

notation.meaning: Basis and scaling for negative eigendirections.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimal Dimension of a Convex-Minus-Projected-Quadratic Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic dimension required to contain every negative-curvature direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\) satisfy \(\nu_-(Q)=r\). If \(Q=H-UDU^{\mathsf T}\), where \(H\succeq0\), \(D\succ0\), and \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\), then \(k\ge r\). Conversely, the negative spectral decomposition supplies such a representation with \(k=r\). Hence the minimum projected dimension leaving a positive-semidefinite remainder is \(\nu_-(Q)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative inertia is exactly the minimum number of projected coordinates needed to isolate all nonconvex curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min\{k:Q=H-UDU^{\mathsf T},\ H\succeq0,\ D\succ0,\ U\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\}=\nu_-(Q)\).

notation.meaning: Number of strictly negative eigenvalues of Q, counted with multiplicity.
Dimension of the projected nonconvex coordinate.

children.title: Rank-Inertia Tractability Boundary
children.top_down_role: Transition from restricted structural regimes to general hard instances.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary showing that bounded negative inertia alone does not ensure tractability over general polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Rational quadratic programming \(\min\{x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b\}\) is NP-hard even when the symmetric matrix \(Q\) has exactly one negative eigenvalue. Therefore fixing \(\nu_-(Q)=1\) does not by itself yield polynomial-time solvability over arbitrary explicitly represented rational polyhedra; a tractability theorem must impose additional structure unless \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One negative eigenvalue already permits NP-hard polyhedrally constrained quadratic programs, so restricted inertia requires additional structure for tractability.
assumptions_latex: The feasible region is an explicitly represented rational polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A polynomial-time algorithm for the entire class would imply \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\).

notation.meaning: Negative inertia of the symmetric quadratic matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Hardness with One Negative Eigenvalue
Rank-Inertia Tractability Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between fixed-parameter spectral structure and unrestricted indefinite-QP hardness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the permitted rank or number of negative eigenvalues grows with \(n\), the class contains unrestricted indefinite box-QP, including the Max-Cut instances \(\min_{x\in[0,1]^n}-\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}(x_i+x_j-2x_ix_j)\), and is NP-hard. Accordingly, a polynomial guarantee parameterized by rank or negative inertia cannot be extended unchanged to unbounded parameter values unless \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}\). Separately, any fixed-parameter algorithm based specifically on enumerating a projected feasible set also requires a polynomial bound on the representation or enumeration used by that algorithm. Spectral restriction is therefore a parameterized regime, not an unconditional convexity surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allowing nonconvex rank or negative inertia to grow recovers NP-hard box-QP; projection-enumeration algorithms additionally need a polynomial representation bound for the projection they enumerate.
assumptions_latex: Quadratic programs have rational data and bounded polyhedral feasible regions.
The permitted rank or negative-inertia parameter may grow with the input.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unbounded rank or negative inertia contains NP-hard box-QP; fixed-parameter projection-enumeration guarantees additionally depend on a polynomial projection representation bound.

notation.meaning: Edge weight in the embedded Max-Cut instance.

children.title: Semidefinite Approximation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem classes supporting quantitative guarantees from semidefinite bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Approximation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical semidefinite approximation regime: nonnegative weighted Max-Cut on a sign domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The weighted-cut sign quadratic \(\operatorname{CUT}(s)=\frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}(1-s_is_j)\) has the semidefinite relaxation \(\max\{\frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}(1-X_{ij}):X\succeq0,\ X_{ii}=1\}\). Factor an optimal \(X\) as Gram vectors and round them by a uniformly random hyperplane. The expected cut value is at least \(\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\operatorname{OPT}\), where \(\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}=\min_{0\le\theta\le\pi}\frac{2\theta}{\pi(1-\cos\theta)}>0.878\). The SDP is polynomially weakly solvable, and the rounding can be derandomized, yielding a polynomial-time \(\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\)-approximation for nonnegative weighted Max-Cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonnegative weighted Max-Cut, semidefinite relaxation plus hyperplane rounding achieves the polynomial-time Goemans-Williamson approximation ratio exceeding 0.878.
assumptions_latex: The objective is the maximum weighted cut over signs \(s_i\in\{-1,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A polynomial-time algorithm returns a cut of value at least \(\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\operatorname{OPT}\), where \(\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}>0.878\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semidefinite relaxation and Gaussian-hyperplane rounding for positive-semidefinite quadratic maximization over signs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and \[v_\star=\max_{s\in\{-1,1\}^n}s^\top Qs,\qquad v_{\mathrm{SDP}}=\max\{\langle Q,X\rangle:X\succeq0,\ X_{ii}=1\}.\] Factor an SDP solution as \(X_{ij}=u_i^\top u_j\), draw a standard Gaussian vector \(g\), and set \(s_i=\operatorname{sign}(g^\top u_i)\). Then \[\mathbb E[s^\top Qs]\ge \frac{2}{\pi}v_{\mathrm{SDP}}\ge\frac{2}{\pi}v_\star.\] Consequently this rounding gives a randomized polynomial-time \(2/\pi\)-approximation for PSD sign-quadratic maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive-semidefinite quadratic maximized over signs, SDP relaxation followed by Gaussian hyperplane rounding achieves the factor two over pi.
assumptions_latex: The SDP is solved to the precision required by the approximation guarantee.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[s^\top Qs]\ge(2/\pi)v_{\mathrm{SDP}}\ge(2/\pi)v_\star\).

notation.meaning: Value of the standard elliptope relaxation
Gram vectors representing the SDP matrix

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Real Grothendieck Semidefinite Approximation for Bilinear Signs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant-factor semidefinite approximation for real bilinear sign optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A=(a_{ij})\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), define \[\operatorname{OPT}(A)=\max_{\varepsilon_i,\delta_j\in\{-1,1\}}\left|\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}\varepsilon_i\delta_j\right|\] and \[\operatorname{SDP}(A)=\max_{\|u_i\|=\|v_j\|=1}\left|\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}u_i^{\mathsf T}v_j\right|.\] The real Grothendieck inequality gives \(\operatorname{SDP}(A)\le K_G^{\mathbb R}\operatorname{OPT}(A)\) for a universal constant \(K_G^{\mathbb R}<\infty\). Classical Krivine rounding can produce signs in randomized polynomial time whose expected absolute objective is at least \[\frac{2\log(1+\sqrt2)}{\pi}\operatorname{SDP}(A).\] Hence real bilinear sign optimization admits a universal constant-factor semidefinite approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The real Grothendieck inequality bounds the vector SDP by a universal constant times the bilinear sign optimum, and classical Krivine rounding converts SDP vectors into a polynomial-time constant-factor sign solution.
assumptions_latex: The vector SDP is solved to the precision required by the rounding guarantee.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{SDP}(A)\le K_G^{\mathbb R}\operatorname{OPT}(A)\), and classical randomized rounding achieves expected absolute value at least \(2\log(1+\sqrt2)\operatorname{SDP}(A)/\pi\).

notation.meaning: Unit vectors in the bilinear semidefinite relaxation

knowledge_statements.title: Real Grothendieck Semidefinite Approximation for Bilinear Signs

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed generic relaxation-bound certificate rather than a theorem specific to semidefinite approximation regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v_\star\) be the optimum of a maximization problem with nonnegative objective values, let \(U\ge v_\star\) be any relaxation upper bound, and let \(z\) be feasible with \(L=f(z)\ge0\). If \(U>0\), then \(L/v_\star\ge L/U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible value divided by any valid relaxation upper bound gives an instance-specific approximation certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L/U\le L/v_\star\).
knowledge_statements.title: A Posteriori SDP Approximation Certificate

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Sign Approximation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative pairwise coefficients on a sign domain reduce to weighted Max-Cut approximability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The coefficient condition \(w_{ij}\ge0\) makes every pairwise term a nonnegative disagreement reward and identifies \(F(s)=\frac12\sum_{i<j}w_{ij}(1-s_is_j)\) with a weighted cut objective. Replacing products \(s_is_j\) by Gram entries \(X_{ij}\), imposing \(X\succeq0\) and \(X_{ii}=1\), and applying random-hyperplane rounding yields \(\mathbb E[F(\hat s)]\ge\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\max_s F(s)\), with \(\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}>0.878\). The guarantee depends jointly on the coefficient signs and sign domain; arbitrary signed weights need not define a nonnegative objective and do not inherit this multiplicative guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative disagreement coefficients turn a sign quadratic into weighted Max-Cut, enabling the 0.878 semidefinite guarantee; arbitrary signed coefficients fall outside this ratio statement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[F(\hat s)]\ge\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\max_sF(s)\), where \(\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}>0.878\); this guarantee does not extend as stated to arbitrary signed weights.

children.title: Domain-Sensitive Approximation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Approximation behavior induced by box, simplex, sphere, or polyhedral domains.

assumptions_latex: \(\widehat x\in D\) is a feasible output.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The range-normalized error \(\rho(D,f,\widehat x)\) depends on the feasible domain, so a guarantee for one domain does not automatically transfer to another.

notation.meaning: range-normalized additive error of a specified feasible point
minimum and maximum of the objective over the domain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, range-normalized approximation over compact continuous domains.

source_refs.locator: 5. Approximation Algorithms in Quadratic Programming p. 38

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(f_D^{\min}=\min_{x\in D}f(x)\) and \(f_D^{\max}=\max_{x\in D}f(x)\). For \(\widehat x\in D\), define \[\rho(D,f,\widehat x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{f(\widehat x)-f_D^{\min}}{f_D^{\max}-f_D^{\min}},&f_D^{\max}>f_D^{\min},\\0,&f_D^{\max}=f_D^{\min}.\end{cases}\] If \(D_1\subseteq D_2\) and \(\widehat x\in D_1\), the extrema and therefore the normalized error can differ between \(D_1\) and \(D_2\). Consequently, a normalized bound established on \(D_2\), such as a box or ball, does not automatically give the same bound on \(D_1\), such as a simplex or constrained polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective-range normalization depends on both the feasible domain and the specified feasible output, so changing the domain can change the measured approximation quality.
knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Sensitive Approximation Regimes

children.title: Sign-Domain Interaction
children.top_down_role: Combined influence of coefficient patterns and feasible-domain geometry.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The effect of coefficient signs depends jointly on the attainable signs and magnitudes of coordinate products over \(D\).

notation.meaning: set of upper-triangular coordinate-product vectors generated by the domain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interaction of coefficient signs with feasible coordinate-product signs.

source_refs.locator: 5. Approximation Algorithms in Quadratic Programming p. 38

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Pi(D)=\{(x_ix_j)_{1\leq i\leq j\leq n}:x\in D\}\). The values contributed by the quadratic terms depend jointly on the coefficients and on the signs and magnitudes attained by the products \(x_ix_j\) over \(D\). For example, if \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}_+^n\), then every attainable product is nonnegative, whereas a sign-symmetric domain may permit both signs for an off-diagonal product. Consequently, a coefficient-sign approximation regime established on a nonnegative domain cannot be transferred to a sign-symmetric domain without additional analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic coefficient's effect depends on the signs and magnitudes of coordinate products permitted by the feasible domain, so coefficient-sign regimes need not transfer between nonnegative and sign-symmetric domains.
knowledge_statements.title: Sign-Domain Interaction

children.title: Approximation-Guarantee Breakdown
children.top_down_role: Structural transitions where favorable approximation guarantees cease to apply.

assumptions_latex: \(D\) is nonempty and \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) has finite minimum.
\(A\) is an algorithm whose feasible output depends only on the optimization instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without a fixed nonnegative normalization, a multiplicative approximation ratio is not invariant under equivalent objective shifts.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of raw multiplicative ratios under objective translation.

source_refs.locator: 5. Approximation Algorithms in Quadratic Programming p. 38

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(\beta\in\mathbb{R}\), set \(f_\beta(x)=f(x)+\beta\). The minimizers of \(f\) and \(f_\beta\) coincide, and an algorithm returning \(\widehat x\) has shifted ratio \[\frac{f_\beta(\widehat x)}{f_\beta^*}=\frac{f(\widehat x)+\beta}{f^*+\beta},\] whenever \(f^*+\beta\neq0\). By choosing \(\beta\) near \(-f^*\), this ratio becomes arbitrarily large in magnitude unless \(f(\widehat x)=f^*\). Therefore a raw multiplicative guarantee is meaningless for unrestricted indefinite quadratic objectives unless sign and normalization assumptions exclude such shifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant objective shift preserves all minimizers but can destroy any raw multiplicative approximation ratio, so such guarantees require a fixed normalization.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximation-Guarantee Breakdown

source_witnesses.locator: 5. Approximation Algorithms in Quadratic Programming p. 38

children.title: Inapproximability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where broad additive or multiplicative guarantees are unavailable.

assumptions_latex: The instance class is closed under positive rational scaling \(f\mapsto Mf\) and rational translation \(f\mapsto f+\beta\).
The algorithm \(A\) is representation-invariant under these transformations: it returns the same feasible point for \(f\), \(Mf\), and \(f+\beta\).
The claimed guarantee is uniform over the transformed instance class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(A\) is nonexact on some instance, no finite uniform absolute-error bound can hold under unrestricted positive scaling, and no uniform raw multiplicative ratio can hold under unrestricted translation when objective values may cross zero.

notation.meaning: feasible output returned by the transformation-invariant algorithm

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transformation-based boundary under explicit algorithmic representation invariance, not an NP-hardness threshold.

source_refs.locator: 5. Approximation Algorithms in Quadratic Programming p. 38

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(A\) returns \(\widehat x\) on an instance with gap \(\delta=f(\widehat x)-f^*>0\). For every positive rational \(M\), representation invariance makes \(A\) return \(\widehat x\) for \(Mf\), whose gap is \(M\delta\). Hence no fixed finite absolute-error bound can hold over the scaling-closed class. Likewise, for \(f_\beta=f+\beta\), the raw ratio of that output is \[\frac{f_\beta(\widehat x)}{f_\beta^*}=\frac{f(\widehat x)+\beta}{f^*+\beta},\] whenever \(f^*+\beta\neq0\); its magnitude is unbounded as \(\beta\) approaches \(-f^*\). Thus broad guarantees require normalization, restricted transformations, or a transformation-stable error convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an algorithm whose output is invariant under objective rescaling and translation, scaling defeats uniform absolute-error bounds and translation defeats raw multiplicative ratios unless the algorithm is exact or the instance class is normalized.
knowledge_statements.title: Inapproximability Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: 5. Approximation Algorithms in Quadratic Programming p. 38

children.title: Binary Domain-Relaxation Family
