children.title: Binary-to-Box Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Replacement of binary restrictions by coordinate-wise continuous bounds.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{\mathrm{box}}\leq v_F\), with equality only when the box relaxation has a binary optimal solution or the two minima otherwise coincide.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct continuous relaxation of a binary minimization problem.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.5 Relaxation (Successive Outer Approximation) Strategies p. 31

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The binary-to-box relaxation of \(v_F=\min\{f(x):x\in F\}\) replaces binary membership by coordinate bounds while retaining all explicitly selected continuous side constraints. In the unconstrained QUBO case it is \[v_{\mathrm{box}}=\min\{f(x):0\leq x_i\leq1,\ i=1,\ldots,n\}.\] Since \(F\subseteq[0,1]^n\), this is a relaxation for minimization and satisfies \(v_{\mathrm{box}}\leq v_F\). Indefiniteness of \(Q\) permits a strictly better fractional minimizer, so the relaxation need not be exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing binary variables by unit-interval variables gives a continuous minimization relaxation and a lower bound, but an indefinite objective may favor fractional points.
knowledge_statements.title: Binary-to-Box Relaxations

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.5 Relaxation (Successive Outer Approximation) Strategies p. 31

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Raw Quadratic Box Relaxation Can Have a Strict Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-variable boundary example for direct evaluation of a quadratic extension on the unit box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F=\{0,1\}\) and \(f(x)=(x-\tfrac12)^2\), \[\min_{x\in F}f(x)=\tfrac14,\qquad \min_{0\le x\le1}f(x)=0,\] and the relaxed minimum is uniquely attained at \(x=\tfrac12\). Thus a raw quadratic box relaxation can have a strict gap even for a convex quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic centered at one half has binary value one quarter but box value zero, so direct box relaxation can be inexact even under convex curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{\mathrm{box}}=0<\tfrac14=v_F\).
knowledge_statements.title: Raw Quadratic Box Relaxation Can Have a Strict Gap

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact unconstrained unit-box extension obtained by applying binary diagonal identities before relaxing the domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\) on \(\{0,1\}^n\), where \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\), and define \[\widehat f(x)=\sum_{i\ne j}Q_{ij}x_ix_j+\sum_i(Q_{ii}+c_i)x_i+d.\] Then \(\widehat f=f\) on \(\{0,1\}^n\), and \[\min_{x\in[0,1]^n}\widehat f(x)=\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}f(x).\] A minimizer of \(\widehat f\) can be moved coordinatewise to box endpoints without increasing its value, yielding a binary minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearizing binary square terms produces a multiaffine extension whose unconstrained unit-box minimum has a binary optimizer and equals the QUBO optimum.
assumptions_latex: There are no side constraints beyond \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\).
The identities \(x_i^2=x_i\) are applied before domain relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{[0,1]^n}\widehat f=\min_{\{0,1\}^n}f\), and a binary box minimizer exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiaffine QUBO Extension Is Box-Exact

children.title: Binary-to-Polytope Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Replacement of binary restrictions by structured polyhedral domains.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty compact polytope satisfying \(F\subseteq P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The value \(v_P\) is a valid lower bound on \(v_F\), and nested smaller valid polytopes give no weaker minimization bounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact polyhedral domain relaxation for binary quadratic minimization.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.5 Relaxation (Successive Outer Approximation) Strategies p. 31

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(v_F=\min\{f(x):x\in F\}\). A binary-to-polytope relaxation is \[v_P=\min\{f(x):x\in P\},\] where the compact polytope \(P\) contains every binary feasible point and may be formed from \([0,1]^n\) together with valid linear inequalities. Inclusion gives \(v_P\leq v_F\). If \(F\subseteq P_1\subseteq P_2\) for compact polytopes \(P_1\) and \(P_2\), then \(v_{P_2}\leq v_{P_1}\leq v_F\). Taking \(P=\operatorname{conv}(F)\) removes domain enlargement, although minimizing an indefinite quadratic over that convex hull can still attain a value below the discrete minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact polytope containing all binary feasible points yields a valid lower bound; smaller valid polytopes are stronger, though the binary convex hull need not preserve an indefinite quadratic minimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Binary-to-Polytope Relaxations

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.5 Relaxation (Successive Outer Approximation) Strategies p. 31

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Concave Vertex Exactness for Binary Polytopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient exactness condition for minimization over a polytope whose extreme points are binary feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), let \(P\) be a nonempty compact polytope satisfying \(F\subseteq P\) and \(\operatorname{ext}(P)\subseteq F\), and let \(f\) be concave on \(P\). Then some minimizer of \(f\) over \(P\) is an extreme point, so \[\min_{x\in P}f(x)=\min_{x\in F}f(x).\] In particular, this applies to \(P=\operatorname{conv}(F)\) whenever \(f\) is concave on that polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A concave objective is exact on a valid polytope whose extreme points are binary feasible points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in P}f(x)=\min_{x\in F}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Set of extreme points of P.

knowledge_statements.title: Concave Vertex Exactness for Binary Polytopes

children.title: Side-Constraint Retention
children.top_down_role: Preservation of discrete-model side structure within continuous relaxations.

assumptions_latex: The relaxation replaces only the integrality constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every discrete feasible point remains feasible, so the retained-side-constraint model is a valid minimization relaxation.

notation.meaning: continuous domain with retained side constraints

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Retention of linear side constraints during integrality relaxation.

source_refs.locator: 3.8 The GOP for Quadratic Problems with Linear Constraints p. 95

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Side-constraint retention forms \[P_{\mathrm{ret}}=\{x\in[0,1]^n:Ax\leq b,\ Ex=h\}.\] Validity requires \(F\subseteq P_{\mathrm{ret}}\), which follows because every binary feasible point satisfies the same linear inequalities and equalities. Hence \[\min_{x\in P_{\mathrm{ret}}}f(x)\leq\min_{x\in F}f(x).\] Dropping any retained constraint produces a superset and cannot improve the minimization lower bound; adding a valid inequality may strengthen it without excluding a discrete feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keeping the original linear side constraints while relaxing integrality preserves every binary feasible point and is at least as strong as dropping those constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Side-Constraint Retention

source_witnesses.locator: 3.8 The GOP for Quadratic Problems with Linear Constraints p. 95

children.title: Domain-Relaxation Strength
children.top_down_role: Relative bound quality across box and structured-polytope domains.

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq P_1\subseteq P_2\) are nonempty compact sets.
The same objective \(f\) is minimized over all three sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{P_2}\leq v_{P_1}\leq v_F\); strength is monotone under reverse feasible-set inclusion.

notation.meaning: minimum of the objective over a set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-inclusion ordering of minimization relaxations.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.5 Relaxation (Successive Outer Approximation) Strategies p. 31

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each nonempty compact set \(S\), let \(v_S=\min_{x\in S}f(x)\). If \(F\subseteq P_1\subseteq P_2\), then \[v_{P_2}\leq v_{P_1}\leq v_F.\] Thus \(P_1\) is at least as strong as \(P_2\) for minimization. Its absolute relaxation gap \(v_F-v_{P_1}\) is no larger than \(v_F-v_{P_2}\). This ordering compares bounds for the same objective and does not by itself compare computational cost or approximation ratios using different normalizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, a smaller valid relaxation gives a no-weaker lower bound and a no-larger absolute relaxation gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Relaxation Strength

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.5 Relaxation (Successive Outer Approximation) Strategies p. 31

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Containment Need Not Strictly Strengthen a Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of inclusion-based comparison: strict domain containment guarantees only weak bound dominance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Even if \(F\subseteq P_1\subsetneq P_2\), \(v_{P_2}\leq v_{P_1}\) need not be strict. For \(F=\{0\}\), \(P_1=[0,1]\), \(P_2=[0,2]\), and \(f(x)=x^2\), \[v_F=v_{P_1}=v_{P_2}=0.\] Strict improvement occurs exactly when \(\min_{P_2}f<\min_{P_1}f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly smaller valid domain can yield the same lower bound; removed points strengthen the bound only when they affect the relaxed optimum.
assumptions_latex: The same objective is minimized over nested nonempty compact domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_1\subsetneq P_2\) does not imply \(v_{P_1}>v_{P_2}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Containment Need Not Strictly Strengthen a Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Incomparable Domains Have No Inclusion-Based Strength Order
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limitation of the domain-inclusion criterion to nested relaxation domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If valid domains \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) are not nested, validity alone gives no ordering of their bounds. For \(F=\{0\}\), \(P_1=[0,1]\), and \(P_2=[-1,0]\), minimizing \(f(x)=x\) gives \(v_{P_2}<v_{P_1}\), whereas minimizing \(g(x)=-x\) gives \(v_{P_1}<v_{P_2}\). Thus nonnested domains require objective-specific comparison or another dominance relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnested valid domains have no objective-independent strength order; either may give the stronger bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No universal ordering of \(v_{P_1}\) and \(v_{P_2}\) follows from validity alone.
knowledge_statements.title: Incomparable Domains Have No Inclusion-Based Strength Order

children.title: Lifted BQP Relaxation Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Product-variable, semidefinite, and exact-conic bounds for binary quadratic models.

children.title: Product-Variable Linear Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Linear lifted bounds based on variables representing binary products.

assumptions_latex: The underlying variables are binary, \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), and are relaxed to \(x\in[0,1]^n\).
\(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\), and \(Y=Y^{\mathsf T}\) is a lifted matrix intended to represent \(xx^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pairwise McCormick inequalities give the convex hull of each off-diagonal bilinear graph over the unit square, while their joint use with \(Y_{ii}=x_i\) is a linear outer relaxation of the lifted binary-product set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise McCormick lifting for a binary quadratic problem after unit-box relaxation.

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Approximation by Affine Functions p. 56

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replace \(xx^{\mathsf T}\) by a symmetric matrix \(Y\) and the quadratic objective by \(\langle Q,Y\rangle+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\). Relax \(x\) to \([0,1]^n\). For each \(i<j\), impose \[Y_{ij}\geq0,\qquad Y_{ij}\geq x_i+x_j-1,\qquad Y_{ij}\leq x_i,\qquad Y_{ij}\leq x_j.\] Retain the binary square identity \(Y_{ii}=x_i\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\). For each pair, the four inequalities describe the convex hull of \(Y_{ij}=x_ix_j\) over \([0,1]^2\). Imposing them jointly gives a linear outer relaxation of the lifted binary-product set because pairwise consistency need not imply a common binary realization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a binary quadratic problem, lift products to a symmetric matrix, relax the variables to the unit box, impose pairwise McCormick inequalities, and retain the binary diagonal identities; each pair is modeled exactly but the joint binary-product set may not be.
knowledge_statements.title: Product-Variable Linear Relaxations

source_witnesses.locator: 2.6 Approximation by Affine Functions p. 56

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pairwise Product Consistency Need Not Be Jointly Realizable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three-variable point satisfying every pairwise unit-box McCormick system but not belonging to the convex hull of binary product lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n=3\), set \(x_i=\tfrac12\) for all \(i\), set \(Y_{ii}=x_i\), and set \(Y_{ij}=0\) for \(i\ne j\). Every pair \((x_i,x_j,Y_{ij})\) satisfies \[Y_{ij}\ge0,\quad Y_{ij}\ge x_i+x_j-1,\quad Y_{ij}\le x_i,\quad Y_{ij}\le x_j.\] However, no probability distribution on \(\{0,1\}^3\) has these first and second moments: \(Y_{ij}=0\) for all pairs would permit at most one coordinate to equal one almost surely, whereas \(\mathbb E[\sum_i x_i]=3/2\). Thus the point is outside the convex hull of jointly realizable binary product lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Three half-valued variables with all off-diagonal products zero satisfy every pairwise McCormick envelope but have no common binary realization.
assumptions_latex: Three binary variables are relaxed to the unit box.
Only the diagonal identities and pairwise McCormick inequalities are imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x,Y)\text{ satisfies every pairwise envelope but }(x,Y)\notin\operatorname{conv}\{(z,zz^{\mathsf T}):z\in\{0,1\}^3\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise Product Consistency Need Not Be Jointly Realizable

children.title: BQP Semidefinite Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Matrix-lifted bounds using positive-semidefinite structure.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a symmetric lifted matrix representing \(xx^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The positive-semidefinite lifted system contains every binary rank-one point and therefore yields a convex lower-bounding relaxation for minimization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order moment semidefinite relaxation of QUBO.

source_refs.locator: 2.14 Semidefinite Programming p. 81

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The basic semidefinite relaxation replaces \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) by \[Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,\qquad X_{ii}=x_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,n),\] and minimizes \(\langle Q,X\rangle+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\), together with lifted valid side constraints when present. Every binary vector gives the feasible rank-one matrix \(Z=(1,x)(1,x)^{\mathsf T}\). Dropping the rank-one condition enlarges the lifted feasible set, so the semidefinite optimum is a lower bound for binary minimization. Entrywise or linear valid inequalities may be added to strengthen it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The SDP lift keeps positive semidefiniteness and binary diagonal identities but drops rank one, producing a convex lower bound that can be strengthened by valid inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: BQP Semidefinite Relaxations

source_witnesses.locator: 2.14 Semidefinite Programming p. 81

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Higher-Rank Feasibility Does Not Represent One Binary Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit feasible first-order BQP moment matrix that is not the lift of a single binary vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(n\ge 1\), let \(x=\tfrac12\mathbf 1\), \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}+\tfrac14 I\), and \[Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}.\] Then \(Z\succeq0\) because its Schur complement is \(X-xx^{\mathsf T}=\tfrac14I\succeq0\), and \(X_{ii}=\tfrac12=x_i\) for every \(i\). Nevertheless \(x\notin\{0,1\}^n\) and \(Z\) has rank greater than one, so this feasible SDP point is not the moment matrix of one binary vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PSD feasibility and binary diagonal identities alone can admit a higher-rank matrix whose first moments are fractional, so the matrix need not represent one binary point.
assumptions_latex: The basic BQP SDP imposes \(Z\succeq0\) and \(X_{ii}=x_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Z\succeq0,\quad X_{ii}=x_i\ \forall i,\quad x\notin\{0,1\}^n,\quad \operatorname{rank}(Z)>1.
knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Rank Feasibility Does Not Represent One Binary Point

children.title: BQP Exact-Conic Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Exact conic representations or bounds for binary quadratic structure.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Optimization over the binary moment cone slice is exactly equivalent in value to optimization over \(F\).

notation.meaning: cone generated by lifted binary feasible points

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conic hull formulation using the binary feasible moment cone.

source_refs.locator: 2.13.3 Conic Programming p. 80

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the binary moment cone \[\mathcal K_F=\operatorname{cone}\{(1,z)(1,z)^{\mathsf T}:z\in F\}.\] Then the binary quadratic problem has the exact conic representation \[\min\{\langle Q,Z_{1:n,1:n}\rangle+c^{\mathsf T}Z_{0,1:n}+d:Z\in\mathcal K_F,\ Z_{00}=1\}.\] Indeed, the slice \(Z_{00}=1\) is precisely the convex hull of lifted feasible binary matrices, and a linear objective has the same minimum over a finite set and its convex hull. Tractable SDP or polyhedral cones arise by replacing \(\mathcal K_F\) with computable outer approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conic hull of lifted feasible binary rank-one matrices gives an exact linear conic formulation; practical relaxations replace that cone by tractable supersets.
knowledge_statements.title: BQP Exact-Conic Relaxations

source_witnesses.locator: 2.13.3 Conic Programming p. 80

children.title: Lifted-Relaxation Strength Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Bound-strength relationships among linear, semidefinite, and exact-conic liftings.

assumptions_latex: All lifted formulations minimize the same linearized objective.
Their feasible regions satisfy \(\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{exact}}\subseteq\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{strong}}\subseteq\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{weak}}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{\mathrm{weak}}\leq v_{\mathrm{strong}}\leq v_{\mathrm{exact}}=v_F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-set inclusion hierarchy for lifted minimization bounds.

source_refs.locator: 2.13.3 Conic Programming p. 80
2.14 Semidefinite Programming p. 81

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L(Z)\) denote the common linearized objective. If \(\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{exact}}\subseteq\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{strong}}\subseteq\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{weak}}\), then \[\min_{Z\in\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{weak}}}L(Z)\leq\min_{Z\in\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{strong}}}L(Z)\leq\min_{Z\in\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{exact}}}L(Z).\] Thus adding valid lifted inequalities or conic constraints strengthens a minimization lower bound. Pairwise product linearizations and basic SDP constraints are not universally ordered unless one formulation explicitly contains the other's constraints; their intersection is at least as strong as either. The exact binary moment-cone slice attains the discrete optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested lifted feasible sets order minimization bounds in reverse; combining incomparable valid constraint families strengthens both, while the exact moment cone recovers the binary optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Relaxation Strength Hierarchy

source_witnesses.locator: 2.13.3 Conic Programming p. 80
2.14 Semidefinite Programming p. 81

children.title: BQP Integrality-Gap Interface
children.top_down_role: Comparison of continuous lower bounds with discrete optima.

knowledge_statements.title: BQP Integrality-Gap Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive and relative gaps between a binary quadratic optimum and a valid continuous lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n\in\mathbb N\), let \(q:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be a quadratic function, let \(B\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) be a nonempty binary feasible set, and let \(R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) satisfy \(B\subseteq R\). Suppose the finite optimal values are
\[p_{\mathrm R}:=\inf_{x\in R}q(x)\le p_{\mathrm B}:=\min_{x\in B}q(x).\]
The additive integrality gap is
\[g_{\mathrm{add}}:=p_{\mathrm B}-p_{\mathrm R}\ge0.\]
When \(0<p_{\mathrm R}\le p_{\mathrm B}\), the relative gap is
\[g_{\mathrm{rel}}:=\frac{p_{\mathrm B}-p_{\mathrm R}}{p_{\mathrm R}}.\]
A zero additive gap means that the relaxation and binary problem have the same optimal value; it does not imply that every relaxed optimizer is binary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The additive integrality gap is the binary optimum minus the continuous-relaxation lower bound. A zero gap means that the optimal values coincide, not that every relaxed optimizer is binary.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb N\), \(q:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is quadratic, \(\varnothing\ne B\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), and \(B\subseteq R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
Both displayed optimal values are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_{\mathrm{add}}=p_{\mathrm B}-p_{\mathrm R}\ge0\), and \(g_{\mathrm{add}}=0\) exactly when \(p_{\mathrm B}=p_{\mathrm R}\).

notation.meaning: Relative integrality gap under a positive relaxation value.

source_refs.locator: 5. Approximation Algorithms in Quadratic Programming p. 38

source_witnesses.locator: 5. Approximation Algorithms in Quadratic Programming p. 38

children.title: Max-Cut Relaxation Bridge
children.top_down_role: Canonical links between sign-constrained quadratics, spectral bounds, and semidefinite relaxation.

children.title: Max-Cut Spectral Bounds
children.top_down_role: Eigenvalue-based continuous bounds for cut quadratics.

knowledge_statements.title: Max-Cut Spectral Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Laplacian largest-eigenvalue upper bound for nonnegatively weighted undirected Max-Cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G\) be an undirected graph on \(n\) vertices with nonnegative edge weights and weighted Laplacian \(L\). Encoding a cut by \(x\in\{-1,1\}^n\), its weight is
\[w(\delta(x))=\frac14x^{\mathsf T}Lx.\]
Because \(\lVert x\rVert_2^2=n\), the Rayleigh-quotient bound gives
\[\operatorname{MaxCut}(G)=\max_{x\in\{-1,1\}^n}\frac14x^{\mathsf T}Lx\le \frac n4\lambda_{\max}(L).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum cut weight is at most one quarter of the vertex count times the largest eigenvalue of the weighted Laplacian.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is undirected with nonnegative edge weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{MaxCut}(G)\le n\lambda_{\max}(L)/4\).

source_refs.locator: 5. Approximation Algorithms in Quadratic Programming p. 38

source_witnesses.locator: 5. Approximation Algorithms in Quadratic Programming p. 38

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equality Condition for a Fixed Spectral Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rayleigh-bound equality characterized by a sign vector in the top eigenspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(u\) with \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}u=0\) and let \(M=L+\operatorname{Diag}(u)\). For \(x\in\{-1,1\}^n\), \[x^{\mathsf T}Lx=n\lambda_{\max}(M)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad Mx=\lambda_{\max}(M)x.\] Consequently, the fixed spectral upper bound is exact when an optimal cut vector lies in the top eigenspace; conversely, any sign vector attaining the bound is an optimal cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed perturbed spectral bound is attained exactly by sign vectors in the matrix's largest-eigenvalue eigenspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{\mathsf T}Lx=n\lambda_{\max}(M)\iff Mx=\lambda_{\max}(M)x\).
knowledge_statements.title: Equality Condition for a Fixed Spectral Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best constant-norm spectral bound obtained from zero-sum diagonal perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(u\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}u=0\) and every \(x\in\{-1,1\}^n\), \[x^{\mathsf T}(L+\operatorname{Diag}(u))x=x^{\mathsf T}Lx.\] Hence \[\operatorname{MaxCut}(G)\le\frac n4\inf_{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}u=0}\lambda_{\max}(L+\operatorname{Diag}(u))\le\frac n4\lambda_{\max}(L).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizing a zero-sum diagonal perturbation can improve the basic Laplacian largest-eigenvalue bound.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is the weighted Laplacian of a finite undirected graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{MaxCut}(G)\le\frac n4\inf_{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}u=0}\lambda_{\max}(L+\operatorname{Diag}(u))\).
review_flags: The optimized value is equivalent to the basic Max-Cut SDP dual and is cross-indexed there.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimized Diagonal-Perturbation Eigenvalue Bound

children.title: Max-Cut Semidefinite Relaxations
children.top_down_role: The canonical matrix-lifted relaxation family for Max-Cut.

knowledge_statements.title: Max-Cut Semidefinite Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical correlation-matrix relaxation of the sign-vector Max-Cut formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a weighted undirected graph with Laplacian \(L\), introduce \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) for \(x\in\{-1,1\}^n\). Dropping only the rank-one requirement yields
\[\operatorname{SDP}(G):=\max\left\{\frac14\langle L,X\rangle:X\succeq0,\ \operatorname{diag}(X)=\mathbf1\right\}.\]
Every cut matrix \(xx^{\mathsf T}\) is feasible, so
\[\operatorname{MaxCut}(G)\le \operatorname{SDP}(G).\]
Equivalently, feasible matrices are Gram matrices \(X_{ij}=u_i^{\mathsf T}u_j\) of unit vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing a cut’s rank-one sign matrix by any positive-semidefinite correlation matrix gives the canonical SDP upper bound for Max-Cut.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is the Laplacian of a weighted undirected graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{MaxCut}(G)\le\max\{\langle L,X\rangle/4:X\succeq0,\operatorname{diag}(X)=\mathbf1\}\).

source_refs.locator: 2.14.3 SDP Programming p. 84
5. Approximation Algorithms in Quadratic Programming p. 38

source_witnesses.locator: 2.14.3 SDP Programming p. 84
5. Approximation Algorithms in Quadratic Programming p. 38

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual of the Basic Max-Cut SDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual representation and strong duality for the correlation-matrix relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(C=L/4\), the primal relaxation \[\max\{\langle C,X\rangle:X\succeq0,\ \operatorname{diag}(X)=\mathbf1\}\] has dual \[\min\{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}y:\operatorname{Diag}(y)-C\succeq0\}.\] Since \(X=I\succ0\) satisfies the diagonal equations, primal Slater feasibility holds. The optimal values therefore agree, and every dual-feasible \(y\) certifies \(\operatorname{MaxCut}(G)\le\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The basic Max-Cut SDP has a diagonal-shift dual; strong duality holds, and every dual-feasible shift certifies an upper bound.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is the Laplacian of a finite weighted undirected graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{SDP}(G)=\min\{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}y:\operatorname{Diag}(y)-L/4\succeq0\}\).

notation.meaning: Dual multipliers for the unit-diagonal equations.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual of the Basic Max-Cut SDP

children.title: Strengthened Max-Cut Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Valid-inequality and hierarchy enhancements of the basic semidefinite bound.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric inequalities added to the basic Max-Cut correlation SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\) with \(X_{ii}=1\), define \(d_{ij}=(1-X_{ij})/2\). Every cut metric satisfies, for distinct \(i,j,k\), \[d_{ij}\le d_{ik}+d_{kj},\qquad d_{ij}+d_{ik}+d_{jk}\le2.\] Adding all such inequalities to the basic correlation SDP preserves every cut matrix and can only decrease its Max-Cut upper bound. All violated triangle inequalities can be detected by enumerating vertex triples in \(O(n^3)\) arithmetic comparisons.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Triangle and triangle-perimeter inequalities valid for every cut metric strengthen the basic SDP and admit cubic-time exhaustive separation.
assumptions_latex: The base formulation is the Max-Cut correlation SDP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{MaxCut}(G)\le U_{\triangle}\le\operatorname{SDP}(G)\).

notation.meaning: Upper bound after all triangle inequalities are imposed.

knowledge_statements.title: Triangle-Inequality Strengthening

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone moment strengthening of the sign formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the polynomial formulation with \(x_i^2=1\), let \(U_r\) be the order-\(r\) moment-relaxation value under the convention that moments of square-free monomials through degree \(2r\) are represented consistently. Then \[\operatorname{MaxCut}(G)\le U_{r+1}\le U_r.\] The first nontrivial level contains the correlation SDP, and the full level representing all square-free monomials—certainly by order \(n\) under this convention—is exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Max-Cut moment relaxations form decreasing SDP upper bounds and become exact at a finite level no later than the full square-free-monomial level.
assumptions_latex: The hierarchy consistently enforces the equations \(x_i^2=1\).
The stated order convention represents moments through degree \(2r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{MaxCut}(G)\le U_{r+1}\le U_r\), with finite exactness by the full level.
review_flags: Hierarchy indexing differs across conventions; finite exactness is stated relative to the full square-free-monomial level.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Max-Cut Moment-Hierarchy Convergence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact endpoint of valid-inequality strengthening for Max-Cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\delta(x)\in\{0,1\}^{E}\) denote the cut induced by \(x\in\{\pm1\}^n\), where \(\delta_{ij}(x)=(1-x_ix_j)/2\), and let \[\operatorname{CUT}(G)=\operatorname{conv}\{\delta(x):x\in\{\pm1\}^n\}.\] For edge weights \(w\), \[\operatorname{MaxCut}(G)=\max\{w^{\mathsf T}d:d\in\operatorname{CUT}(G)\}.\] Hence imposing every valid inequality of the cut polytope closes the relaxation gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cut polytope is the exact endpoint obtained when all valid cut inequalities are imposed.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite undirected weighted graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{MaxCut}(G)=\max_{d\in\operatorname{CUT}(G)}w^{\mathsf T}d.

notation.meaning: Cut-incidence vector induced by a sign vector.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Polytope Exact Endpoint

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hypermetric valid inequalities added to the Max-Cut correlation SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal B\subseteq\{b\in\mathbb Z^n:\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}b\text{ is odd}\}\) and define \[U_{\mathcal B}=\max\left\{\tfrac14\langle L,X\rangle:X\succeq0,\ \operatorname{diag}(X)=\mathbf1,\ b^{\mathsf T}Xb\ge1\ \forall b\in\mathcal B\right\}.\] Every cut matrix \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\), \(x\in\{\pm1\}^n\), satisfies these inequalities. Hence \[\operatorname{MaxCut}(G)\le U_{\mathcal B}\le\operatorname{SDP}(G),\] and \(\mathcal B_1\subseteq\mathcal B_2\) implies \(U_{\mathcal B_2}\le U_{\mathcal B_1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Odd-sum hypermetric inequalities preserve every cut matrix and form a monotone family of strengthened Max-Cut SDP upper bounds.
assumptions_latex: Every \(b\in\mathcal B\) is integral and has odd coordinate sum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{MaxCut}(G)\le U_{\mathcal B}\le\operatorname{SDP}(G)\), monotonically under enlargement of \(\mathcal B\).
knowledge_statements.title: Odd-Sum Hypermetric Strengthening
Strengthened Max-Cut Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hypermetric valid inequalities added to the basic Max-Cut correlation SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal B\) be any collection of integer vectors \(b\in\mathbb Z^n\) whose coordinate sum is odd. The strengthened relaxation is
\[U_{\mathcal B}:=\max\left\{\frac14\langle L,X\rangle:X\succeq0,\ \operatorname{diag}(X)=\mathbf1,\ b^{\mathsf T}Xb\ge1\ \forall b\in\mathcal B\right\}.\]
For every cut matrix \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\), each added constraint is valid. Consequently,
\[\operatorname{MaxCut}(G)\le U_{\mathcal B}\le\operatorname{SDP}(G),\]
and enlarging \(\mathcal B\) can only decrease the upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding hypermetric inequalities to the correlation SDP preserves every cut matrix and produces a monotone family of tighter Max-Cut upper bounds.
assumptions_latex: Every \(b\in\mathcal B\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) has odd coordinate sum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{MaxCut}(G)\le U_{\mathcal B}\le\operatorname{SDP}(G)\), monotonically in \(\mathcal B\).

notation.meaning: Selected family of odd-sum integer vectors.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: hypermetric inequalities are standard valid inequalities for cut correlation matrices

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The odd-sum hypermetric constraints and resulting monotone bound ordering are mathematically coherent and fit the container, but no inspectable citation supports this exact strengthened Max-Cut formulation.

children.title: QAP Relaxation Bound Bridge
children.top_down_role: Continuous lower-bound families linking assignment geometry, spectral structure, product liftings, and semidefinite cones.

children.title: Assignment-Polytope QAP Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Doubly stochastic and related continuous assignment relaxations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Nonexactness on the Birkhoff Polytope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fractional optimum showing that convex-hull exactness for linear objectives does not extend to quadratic QAP objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\ge2\), take \(A=B=I_n\) and \(C=0\). Every permutation matrix \(P\) has \(\operatorname{tr}(APBP^{\mathsf T})=\|P\|_F^2=n\). Over \(\mathcal D_n\), the uniform matrix \(X=\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}/n\) minimizes \(\|X\|_F^2\) with value \(1\). Thus the quadratic relaxation has value \(1<n\), although \(\mathcal D_n=\operatorname{conv}(\Pi_n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identity flow and distance matrices give a strict fractional gap: permutations cost n while the uniform doubly stochastic matrix costs 1.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{X\in\mathcal D_n}\|X\|_F^2=1<n=\min_{P\in\Pi_n}\|P\|_F^2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Nonexactness on the Birkhoff Polytope

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-hull structure underlying continuous assignment domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The doubly stochastic polytope \[\mathcal D_n=\{X\ge0:X\mathbf1=\mathbf1,\ X^{\mathsf T}\mathbf1=\mathbf1\}\] equals \(\operatorname{conv}(\Pi_n)\), and its extreme points are precisely the permutation matrices. Consequently, every linear objective has a permutation-matrix optimizer over \(\mathcal D_n\); the conclusion does not extend to arbitrary quadratic objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Doubly stochastic matrices are convex combinations of permutation matrices, giving linear-objective exactness but not general quadratic exactness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal D_n=\operatorname{conv}(\Pi_n)\) and \(\operatorname{ext}(\mathcal D_n)=\Pi_n\).
knowledge_statements.title: Birkhoff–von Neumann Structure

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Kronecker Curvature of the Doubly Stochastic QAP Objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature test for the quadratic retained by the assignment-polytope relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For symmetric \(A,B\), \[\operatorname{tr}(AXBX^{\mathsf T})=\operatorname{vec}(X)^{\mathsf T}(B\otimes A)\operatorname{vec}(X),\] so the ambient Hessian is \(2(B\otimes A)\). The objective is therefore convex on the Birkhoff polytope whenever \(B\otimes A\succeq0\), including when both \(A,B\succeq0\) or both \(A,B\preceq0\). A negative eigenvalue of \(B\otimes A\) proves ambient nonconvexity, although convexity may still hold after restriction to the affine hull of the Birkhoff polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vectorization exposes the relaxation Hessian as a Kronecker product, giving an ambient convexity test and an affine-hull qualification.
assumptions_latex: The linear term does not affect curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla^2\!\left[\operatorname{tr}(AXBX^{\mathsf T})+\langle C,X\rangle\right]=2(B\otimes A).
knowledge_statements.title: Kronecker Curvature of the Doubly Stochastic QAP Objective

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Concave-Objective Exactness on the Assignment Polytope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature regime in which the Birkhoff relaxation has a permutation optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(X)=\operatorname{tr}(AXBX^{\mathsf T})+\langle C,X\rangle\), with \(A,B\in\mathbb S^n\), and let \(\mathcal T=\{H:H\mathbf1=0,\ H^{\mathsf T}\mathbf1=0\}\). If \(\operatorname{vec}(H)^{\mathsf T}(B\otimes A)\operatorname{vec}(H)\le0\) for every \(H\in\mathcal T\), then \(q\) is concave on \(\mathcal D_n\). Consequently, some minimizer over \(\mathcal D_n\) is an extreme point and hence a permutation matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the QAP quadratic is concave on the affine hull of the Birkhoff polytope, the relaxation has a permutation minimizer and is exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{X\in\mathcal D_n}q(X)=\min_{P\in\Pi_n}q(P)\).

notation.meaning: Direction space of the affine hull of the Birkhoff polytope.

knowledge_statements.title: Concave-Objective Exactness on the Assignment Polytope

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct continuous assignment-domain relaxation of a permutation-matrix QAP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A,B\in\mathbb S^n\), \(C\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(\Pi_n\) the permutation matrices, and \(\mathcal D_n=\{X\ge0:X\mathbf1=\mathbf1,\ X^{\mathsf T}\mathbf1=\mathbf1\}\), define \[p_{\mathrm{QAP}}=\min_{P\in\Pi_n}\{\operatorname{tr}(APBP^{\mathsf T})+\langle C,P\rangle\}\] and \[p_{\mathcal D}=\min_{X\in\mathcal D_n}\{\operatorname{tr}(AXBX^{\mathsf T})+\langle C,X\rangle\}.\] Since \(\Pi_n\subseteq\mathcal D_n\), \(p_{\mathcal D}\le p_{\mathrm{QAP}}\). The retained quadratic may be nonconvex, so validity of the bound requires global solution of the relaxed problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing permutation matrices by doubly stochastic matrices gives a valid QAP lower bound, but the resulting continuous quadratic problem need not be convex.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation over \(\mathcal D_n\) is solved globally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_{\mathcal D}\le p_{\mathrm{QAP}}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Birkhoff-Polytope QAP Lower Bound
Assignment-Polytope QAP Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Birkhoff-polytope relaxation of the permutation-matrix QAP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For symmetric \(A,B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(C\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), write
\[p_{\mathrm{QAP}}:=\min_{P\in\Pi_n}\left\{\operatorname{tr}(APBP^{\mathsf T})+\langle C,P\rangle\right\}.\]
Replacing the permutation set by the Birkhoff polytope
\[\mathcal D_n:=\{X\in\mathbb R_+^{n\times n}:X\mathbf1=\mathbf1,\ X^{\mathsf T}\mathbf1=\mathbf1\}\]
gives the continuous relaxation
\[p_{\mathcal D}:=\inf_{X\in\mathcal D_n}\left\{\operatorname{tr}(AXBX^{\mathsf T})+\langle C,X\rangle\right\}\le p_{\mathrm{QAP}}.\]
The relaxed objective may remain nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing permutation matrices by doubly stochastic matrices yields a continuous, possibly nonconvex QAP relaxation whose global optimum is a valid lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The relaxed problem is solved to global optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_{\mathcal D}\le p_{\mathrm{QAP}}\).

notation.meaning: Birkhoff polytope of doubly stochastic matrices.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the Birkhoff polytope contains every permutation matrix

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Birkhoff-polytope relaxation and lower-bound direction are correct, including the warning that the relaxed quadratic objective may remain nonconvex, but the record lacks a QAP-specific citation.
