children.title: QAP Eigenvalue Bounds
children.top_down_role: Spectral lower bounds derived directly from QAP matrix eigenstructure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct evaluation of the homogeneous symmetric QAP eigenvalue lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute and sort the eigenvalues of A and B nondecreasingly, reverse one list, and return \[L_{\mathrm{eig}}=\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i(A)\lambda_{n+1-i}(B).\] Dense symmetric eigendecompositions require O(n^3) arithmetic and O(n^2) storage; sorting is lower order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute the bound using two symmetric eigendecompositions, opposite ordering, and one dot product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_{\mathrm{eig}}\text{ is computable in }O(n^3)\text{ arithmetic and }O(n^2)\text{ storage}.
knowledge_statements.title: Eigenvalue-Bound Computation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition under which a permutation attains the unrestricted orthogonal eigenvalue bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A=U\operatorname{Diag}(a_1,\ldots,a_n)U^{\mathsf T} and B=W\operatorname{Diag}(b_1,\ldots,b_n)W^{\mathsf T}, with both spectra ordered nondecreasingly. The eigenvalue bound is exact iff some permutation matrix belongs to \operatorname*{argmin}_{Q\in\mathcal O(n)}\operatorname{tr}(AQBQ^{\mathsf T}). With simple spectra, this is equivalent to the existence of a permutation P and signs s_i\in\{-1,1\} satisfying \[P w_{n+1-i}=s_i u_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,n).\] With repeated eigenvalues, orthogonal basis changes inside equal-eigenvalue eigenspaces are allowed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The eigenvalue bound is exact precisely when a feasible permutation realizes an opposite eigenspace pairing that solves the orthogonal relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The vector criterion assumes simple spectra; repeated spectra use subspace alignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_{\mathrm{QAP}}=L_{\mathrm{eig}}\iff \Pi_n\cap\operatorname*{argmin}_{Q\in\mathcal O(n)}\operatorname{tr}(AQBQ^{\mathsf T})\ne\varnothing.

notation.meaning: Ordered orthonormal eigenvectors of A and B

review_flags: The simple-spectrum vector form must not be used unchanged for repeated eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.title: Exactness by Opposite Eigenspace Alignment
QAP Eigenvalue Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal-relaxation eigenvalue lower bound for the homogeneous symmetric QAP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A,B\in\mathbb S^n\), with eigenvalues ordered as \(\lambda_1(A)\le\cdots\le\lambda_n(A)\) and \(\lambda_1(B)\le\cdots\le\lambda_n(B)\). Since every permutation matrix is orthogonal,
\[\min_{P\in\Pi_n}\operatorname{tr}(APBP^{\mathsf T})\ge\min_{Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I}\operatorname{tr}(AQBQ^{\mathsf T})=\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i(A)\lambda_{n+1-i}(B).\]
Thus oppositely ordered eigenvalue pairing supplies a computable QAP lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxing permutation matrices to all orthogonal matrices gives a lower bound equal to the oppositely ordered eigenvalue pairing of the two QAP matrices.
assumptions_latex: The QAP objective has no additional linear term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_{\mathrm{QAP}}\ge\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i(A)\lambda_{n+1-i}(B)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: orthogonal relaxation combined with the symmetric trace rearrangement theorem

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The orthogonal relaxation and oppositely ordered eigenvalue formula are standard for the homogeneous symmetric QAP, but an authoritative source for the exact formula and hypotheses is required.

children.title: QAP Projected Spectral Bounds
children.top_down_role: Spectral bounds formed after eliminating assignment subspaces.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Computation of the Invariant-Direction Projected Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense evaluation procedure for the reduced closed-form projected bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an orthonormal basis V of e^\perp, form A_\perp=V^{\mathsf T}AV and B_\perp=V^{\mathsf T}BV, compute and oppositely sort their eigenvalues, and add a_0b_0. Dense basis formation, projection, and eigendecomposition require O(n^3) arithmetic and O(n^2) storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project both matrices onto the assignment-orthogonal subspace, apply opposite eigenvalue pairing there, and add the fixed-direction term.
assumptions_latex: The invariant-direction assumptions of the reduced formula hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_{\mathrm{proj}}\text{ is computable in }O(n^3)\text{ arithmetic and }O(n^2)\text{ storage}.

notation.meaning: Orthonormal basis for the all-ones orthogonal complement

knowledge_statements.title: Computation of the Invariant-Direction Projected Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reduced Eigenvalue Formula in the Invariant-Direction Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed form for the assignment-preserving orthogonal relaxation when both QAP matrices preserve the all-ones direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let v_0=e/\sqrt n, let V have orthonormal columns spanning e^\perp, and suppose Av_0=a_0v_0 and Bv_0=b_0v_0. Define A_\perp=V^{\mathsf T}AV and B_\perp=V^{\mathsf T}BV. Every Q\in\mathcal O_e has the form \[Q=v_0v_0^{\mathsf T}+VRV^{\mathsf T},\qquad R\in\mathcal O(n-1),\] and therefore \[L_{\mathrm{proj}}=a_0b_0+\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\lambda_i(A_\perp)\lambda_{n-i}(B_\perp),\] where the reduced eigenvalues are ordered nondecreasingly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When both matrices preserve the all-ones direction, the projected bound is the fixed all-ones contribution plus opposite eigenvalue pairing on its orthogonal complement.
assumptions_latex: The all-ones direction is an eigenvector of both matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_{\mathrm{proj}}=a_0b_0+\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\lambda_i(A_\perp)\lambda_{n-i}(B_\perp).

notation.meaning: Restrictions of A and B to the all-ones orthogonal complement

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced Eigenvalue Formula in the Invariant-Direction Regime
QAP Projected Spectral Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral relaxation retaining the assignment-invariant all-ones direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(e=\mathbf1\) and
\[\mathcal O_e:=\{Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}:Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I,\ Qe=e\}.\]
For symmetric \(A,B\), define
\[L_{\mathrm{proj}}:=\min_{Q\in\mathcal O_e}\operatorname{tr}(AQBQ^{\mathsf T}).\]
Every permutation matrix belongs to \(\mathcal O_e\), whereas \(\mathcal O_e\) is contained in the full orthogonal group. Hence
\[p_{\mathrm{QAP}}\ge L_{\mathrm{proj}}\ge L_{\mathrm{eig}},\qquad L_{\mathrm{eig}}:=\min_{Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I}\operatorname{tr}(AQBQ^{\mathsf T}).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Requiring the orthogonal relaxation to fix the all-ones vector preserves assignments and cannot weaken the unrestricted QAP eigenvalue lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_{\mathrm{QAP}}\ge L_{\mathrm{proj}}\ge L_{\mathrm{eig}}\).

notation.meaning: Orthogonal matrices fixing the all-ones vector.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nested feasible-set relaxation gives the bound ordering

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nested-set bound ordering is correct, but the exact assignment-preserving spectral relaxation has no citation, and \(p_{\mathrm{QAP}}\) should be defined within this record when it is revised after sourcing.

children.title: Assignment-Subspace Projection
children.top_down_role: Role of assignment identities in defining the projected spectral space.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dimension and Isometry of Assignment-Subspace Coordinates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry of reduced coordinates after eliminating row and column sums.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let e=\mathbf1, J=ee^{\mathsf T}/n, and let V have orthonormal columns spanning e^\perp. The affine space \[\mathcal A=\{X:Xe=e,\ X^{\mathsf T}e=e\}\] has dimension (n-1)^2. Under X=J+VYV^{\mathsf T}, \[\|X_1-X_2\|_F=\|Y_1-Y_2\|_F,\qquad \langle X_1-J,X_2-J\rangle=\langle Y_1,Y_2\rangle.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating assignment sums leaves (n−1)-squared degrees of freedom, and orthonormal reduced coordinates preserve Frobenius geometry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \dim(\mathcal A)=(n-1)^2\text{ and }Y\mapsto VYV^{\mathsf T}\text{ is a Frobenius isometry}.

notation.meaning: Affine space satisfying both assignment-sum systems

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension and Isometry of Assignment-Subspace Coordinates
Assignment-Subspace Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine decomposition of doubly stochastic matrices along the all-ones direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(e=\mathbf1\), \(J=ee^{\mathsf T}/n\), and choose \(V\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-1)}\) satisfying
\[V^{\mathsf T}V=I,\qquad V^{\mathsf T}e=0.\]
Every matrix \(X\) satisfying \(Xe=e\) and \(X^{\mathsf T}e=e\) has the unique representation
\[X=J+VYV^{\mathsf T},\qquad Y=V^{\mathsf T}XV.\]
If \(X=P\) is a permutation matrix, then \(Y\) is orthogonal. Thus the assignment equalities isolate a fixed component \(J\) and an \((n-1)\)-dimensional variable component on \(e^\perp\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every matrix satisfying both assignment equalities splits uniquely into a fixed all-ones component and a reduced matrix acting on the orthogonal assignment subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X=ee^{\mathsf T}/n+V(V^{\mathsf T}XV)V^{\mathsf T}\), uniquely; permutation \(X\) gives orthogonal \(V^{\mathsf T}XV\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: orthogonal decomposition induced by the assignment equalities

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine decomposition and orthogonality of the reduced permutation action are correct and appropriately represented, but the record has no inspectable source for this QAP projection construction.

children.title: Projection-Gain Regimes
children.top_down_role: Instance structures where projection materially strengthens spectral bounds.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proper Projection Can Have Zero Gain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective regimes in which assignment-preserving projection does not strengthen the eigenvalue bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Although \mathcal O_e=\{Q:Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I,\ Qe=e\} is a proper subset of \mathcal O(n) for n\ge2, the two minima can coincide. If A=\alpha I or B=\beta I, then \[\operatorname{tr}(AQBQ^{\mathsf T})=\alpha\operatorname{tr}(B)\quad\text{or}\quad\beta\operatorname{tr}(A)\] for every orthogonal Q. Hence the projection gain is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection need not improve the bound: if either QAP matrix is scalar, the orthogonal objective is constant.
assumptions_latex: At least one of A,B is a scalar multiple of the identity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Delta=0.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal matrices fixing the all-ones vector
Projected minimum minus unrestricted orthogonal minimum

knowledge_statements.title: Proper Projection Can Have Zero Gain
Projection-Gain Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact condition for strict improvement over the unrestricted orthogonal eigenvalue bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f(Q):=\operatorname{tr}(AQBQ^{\mathsf T})\), let
\[\mathcal M:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I}f(Q),\qquad \mathcal O_e:=\{Q:Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I,\ Qe=e\}.\]
The projection gain
\[\Delta:=\min_{Q\in\mathcal O_e}f(Q)-\min_{Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I}f(Q)\]
is nonnegative. Moreover,
\[\Delta>0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\mathcal M\cap\mathcal O_e=\varnothing.\]
Thus projection improves the spectral bound precisely when no unrestricted orthogonal minimizer preserves the assignment direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projected bound is strictly stronger exactly when none of the unrestricted orthogonal minimizers fixes the all-ones assignment direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta>0\) if and only if \(\mathcal M\cap\mathcal O_e=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Increase in the lower bound caused by projection.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: compact feasible sets and nested minimization domains yield the strictness criterion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The strict-improvement equivalence follows from continuous minimization over compact nested orthogonal sets and fits a condition container, but the exact criterion is unsupported by a citation.

children.title: QAP Linearization-RLT Bound Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Product-variable bounds strengthened by assignment identities.

children.title: QAP Product-Variable Linearization
children.top_down_role: Lifted linear representations of quadratic assignment products.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size of the unreduced ordered-pair QAP product lift and its symmetric indexing variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A QAP with n^2 assignment variables has n^4 ordered-pair variables y_{ij,k\ell}. Applying the four unit-box product inequalities to every ordered pair uses O(n^4) variables and inequalities. Using y_{ij,k\ell}=y_{k\ell,ij} after symmetrizing the objective reduces the variable count to n^2(n^2+1)/2, without changing the quartic order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct QAP product lift has quartic size; symmetric indexing nearly halves its variables but remains quartic.
assumptions_latex: Every ordered pair of the n^2 assignment variables is lifted.
Objective coefficients are symmetrized when unordered indexing is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_y=n^4\text{ in ordered indexing and }N_y=n^2(n^2+1)/2\text{ in symmetric indexing}.
knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Product-Lift Size

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the basic product inequalities after assignment integrality is relaxed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For n=2, let x_{ij}=1/2 for all i,j and set y_{ij,k\ell}=0 for every pair. The matrix x satisfies all row and column assignment equations, and each triple satisfies \[0\le y_{ij,k\ell}\le x_{ij},\quad y_{ij,k\ell}\le x_{k\ell},\quad y_{ij,k\ell}\ge x_{ij}+x_{k\ell}-1.\] Nevertheless, y_{ij,k\ell}=0\ne x_{ij}x_{k\ell}=1/4.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The product inequalities are exact at binary assignments but admit incorrect products at fractional doubly stochastic points.
assumptions_latex: Only the basic pairwise product inequalities and assignment equations are imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x,y)\text{ is feasible for the basic lift while }y\ne xx^{\mathsf T}.
knowledge_statements.title: Fractional Failure of Binary-Product Linearization
QAP Product-Variable Linearization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted product variables converting the quadratic assignment objective into a linear objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For assignment variables \(x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\), introduce
\[y_{ij,k\ell}:=x_{ij}x_{k\ell}.\]
Then the quadratic term
\[\sum_{i,j,k,\ell}a_{ik}b_{j\ell}x_{ij}x_{k\ell}\]
becomes the linear expression
\[\sum_{i,j,k,\ell}a_{ik}b_{j\ell}y_{ij,k\ell}.\]
On binary points the product identity is represented by
\[0\le y_{ij,k\ell}\le x_{ij},\quad y_{ij,k\ell}\le x_{k\ell},\quad y_{ij,k\ell}\ge x_{ij}+x_{k\ell}-1.\]
Together with binary assignment constraints, these inequalities give an exact lifted formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable for every pairwise assignment product makes the QAP objective linear; standard binary product inequalities recover the exact products at integer assignments.
assumptions_latex: \(x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) satisfy the row and column assignment equations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted objective is linear in \(y\), and the displayed inequalities enforce \(y_{ij,k\ell}=x_{ij}x_{k\ell}\) at binary points.

notation.meaning: Lifted product of two assignment variables.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: binary-product linearization is exact on binary assignments

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary-product inequalities give an exact lifted formulation at binary assignments and the representation fits the leaf, but a QAP-specific linearization source is required.

children.title: QAP RLT Bounds
children.top_down_role: Reformulation-linearization bounds for lifted QAP models.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: RLT Elimination of Incompatible Assignment Products
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-product consequences of first-level lifted assignment equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the QAP RLT system imposes \[\sum_j y_{ij,k\ell}=x_{k\ell},\qquad \sum_i y_{ij,k\ell}=x_{k\ell},\qquad y_{k\ell,k\ell}=x_{k\ell},\qquad y\ge0,\] together with y_{ij,k\ell}=y_{k\ell,ij}. Then \[y_{kj,k\ell}=0\ (j\ne\ell),\qquad y_{i\ell,k\ell}=0\ (i\ne k).\] Hence products of mutually incompatible assignments vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: First-level QAP RLT forces lifted products of mutually incompatible assignments to zero.
assumptions_latex: The displayed lifted row and column equations, diagonal identities, nonnegativity, and product symmetry are imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y_{ij,k\ell}=0\text{ if }(i=k,\ j\ne\ell)\text{ or }(i\ne k,\ j=\ell).
knowledge_statements.title: RLT Elimination of Incompatible Assignment Products
QAP RLT Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-level reformulation-linearization constraints derived from assignment equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Multiply each assignment equation by every \(x_{k\ell}\) and replace products by \(y_{ij,k\ell}\). The first-level RLT system includes
\[\sum_j y_{ij,k\ell}=x_{k\ell}\quad(\forall i,k,\ell),\qquad \sum_i y_{ij,k\ell}=x_{k\ell}\quad(\forall j,k,\ell),\]
together with
\[y_{ij,k\ell}=y_{k\ell,ij},\qquad y_{ij,ij}=x_{ij},\qquad y_{ij,k\ell}\ge0.\]
Minimizing the linearized QAP objective over these constraints and the continuous assignment equations gives an LP lower bound on the minimization QAP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: First-level RLT multiplies assignment equations by assignment variables, linearizes every product, and yields an LP lower bound for a minimization QAP.
assumptions_latex: The QAP is posed as a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimum of the displayed RLT linear program is no larger than the QAP optimum.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: multiplying valid assignment equalities and linearizing preserves all integer assignments

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed first-level RLT identities preserve every integer assignment and yield a valid LP lower bound, but no source supports this exact QAP RLT system and indexing convention.

children.title: Assignment-Identity Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Use of assignment equalities to tighten lifted product-variable bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted identities inherited from binary idempotence and product commutativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) be permutation-assignment variables and let \(y_{ij,k\ell}\) represent \(x_{ij}x_{k\ell}\). Every integral assignment lift satisfies \[y_{ij,ij}=x_{ij},\qquad y_{ij,k\ell}=y_{k\ell,ij}.\] Imposing these equalities preserves every permutation lift and cannot decrease a minimization relaxation's lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary idempotence identifies diagonal product variables with assignments, and commutativity makes the lifted product array symmetric.
assumptions_latex: \(x_{ij}\) is binary at every original feasible assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_{ij,ij}=x_{ij}\) and \(y_{ij,k\ell}=y_{k\ell,ij}\) are valid for every permutation lift.

notation.meaning: Lifted product of two assignment variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Idempotence and Product-Symmetry Identities

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Permutation Assignment Zero-Product and Marginal Identities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted equalities induced by row and column assignment equations and mutual exclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\) be a permutation assignment and let \(y_{ij,k\ell}=x_{ij}x_{k\ell}\) on integral lifts. Then \[y_{ij,ik}=0\quad(j\ne k),\qquad y_{ji,ki}=0\quad(j\ne k),\] and, for every fixed \((k,\ell)\), \[\sum_j y_{ij,k\ell}=x_{k\ell},\qquad \sum_i y_{ij,k\ell}=x_{k\ell}.\] Adding these equalities to a product-variable relaxation preserves every permutation lift and cannot decrease its lower bound for a minimization QAP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Row and column mutual exclusion force zero products, while lifted assignment equations produce row and column product marginals.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is a permutation assignment at every original feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed zero-product and marginal equalities are valid for every permutation lift and monotonically strengthen a minimization relaxation.

notation.meaning: Assignment of row object i to column j.
Lifted product of two assignment variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Permutation Assignment Zero-Product and Marginal Identities
Assignment-Identity Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted zero-product identities implied by mutual exclusion in permutation assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every permutation assignment, two distinct assignments in the same row or the same column are mutually exclusive. Hence the lifted variables satisfy
\[y_{ij,ik}=0\quad(j\ne k),\qquad y_{ji,ki}=0\quad(j\ne k).\]
They also satisfy the marginal identities
\[\sum_jy_{ij,k\ell}=x_{k\ell},\qquad \sum_i y_{ij,k\ell}=x_{k\ell}.\]
Adding these equalities to any product-variable relaxation preserves every feasible permutation assignment and, for a minimization QAP, can only increase its relaxation lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mutual exclusion and assignment marginals create valid lifted equalities that preserve all permutations and can only strengthen a minimization-QAP lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is a permutation assignment at every integer feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adding the displayed assignment identities preserves integer feasibility and cannot decrease the relaxation lower bound.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: row and column exclusivity are defining properties of permutation assignments

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The zero-product and marginal identities are valid for permutation assignments and can only strengthen a minimization relaxation, but the exact lifted identities require an inspectable source.

children.title: Linearization-Strength Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Relative bound quality across basic linearizations and strengthened RLT systems.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Improvement Between Nested Linearization Levels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-specific criterion for strict improvement between adjacent nested QAP relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let P_{r+1}\subseteq P_r be nonempty compact relaxation sets with common linear objective g, and let F_r:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in P_r}g(u). Then \[\min_{u\in P_{r+1}}g(u)>\min_{u\in P_r}g(u)\iff F_r\cap P_{r+1}=\varnothing.\] Thus proper containment alone need not improve the bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nested strengthening improves the bound strictly exactly when it removes every optimum of the weaker relaxation.
assumptions_latex: P_{r+1}\subseteq P_r are nonempty and compact.
The same linear objective g is minimized over both sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_{r+1}>z_r\iff \operatorname*{argmin}_{P_r}g\cap P_{r+1}=\varnothing.

notation.meaning: Optimal face of the level-r relaxation

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Improvement Between Nested Linearization Levels
Linearization-Strength Hierarchy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hierarchy induced by successively adding valid assignment identities to a product-variable QAP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_0\) be the lifted assignment relaxation containing variables \(x\) and \(y\), the assignment constraints on \(x\), and valid envelope constraints for \(y_{ij,k\ell}=x_{ij}x_{k\ell}\). Let \(P_1\) add first-level reformulation-linearization constraints obtained by multiplying assignment equalities by individual variables, and let \(P_2\) add further valid assignment-product identities. Then \(P_2\subseteq P_1\subseteq P_0\). Consequently, for every linearized minimization objective \(g(x,y)\), the relaxation values satisfy \[\min_{(x,y)\in P_0}g(x,y)\leq \min_{(x,y)\in P_1}g(x,y)\leq \min_{(x,y)\in P_2}g(x,y)\leq z^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding valid assignment-product identities shrinks the QAP linearization feasible region and monotonically improves its minimization lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(P_0,P_1,P_2\) retain every lifted point generated by a feasible permutation.
\(z^*\) is the minimum of the original QAP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_2\subseteq P_1\subseteq P_0\) and the corresponding lower bounds are nondecreasing.
review_flags: Exact QAP RLT hierarchy locator is absent from the supplied inventory.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nesting and lower-bound monotonicity are mathematically coherent and fit the hierarchy leaf, but the QAP-specific RLT levels and assignment-product identities have no cited source or inspectable locator.

children.title: QAP Semidefinite Bounds
children.top_down_role: Matrix relaxations coupling assignment structure and quadratic consistency.

knowledge_statements.title: QAP Semidefinite Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic lifted semidefinite relaxation for a vectorized permutation formulation of QAP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write the QAP as \(z^*=\min\{\langle Q,xx^{\mathsf T}\rangle+c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in\mathcal P_n\}\), where \(\mathcal P_n\) is the set of vectorized permutation matrices. A semidefinite lower bound is obtained by replacing \(xx^{\mathsf T}\) with \(X\) and solving \[z_{\mathrm{SDP}}=\min\{\langle Q,X\rangle+c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal P_n),\ \operatorname{diag}(X)=x,\ \begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,\ \mathcal A(X,x)=0\}.\] Here \(\mathcal A(X,x)=0\) denotes any retained valid lifted assignment identities. Every feasible permutation induces \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\), hence \(z_{\mathrm{SDP}}\leq z^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite moment matrix and lifted assignment identities yield a convex lower bound for the minimization QAP.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is symmetric, after replacing it by its symmetric part if necessary.
Every equation in \(\mathcal A(X,x)=0\) is valid for \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) and \(x\in\mathcal P_n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{\mathrm{SDP}}\leq z^*\).

source_refs.locator: 2.14.3 SDP Programming p. 84

review_flags: QAP-specific lifted identities require dedicated source confirmation.

source_witnesses.locator: 2.14.3 SDP Programming p. 84

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank-One Exactness Certificate for the QAP SDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal certificate that the semidefinite lower bound equals the QAP optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[M=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,\qquad \operatorname{diag}(X)=x,\qquad x\in\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal P_n).\] If an optimal SDP solution satisfies \operatorname{rank}(M)=1, then X=xx^{\mathsf T}; consequently x_i^2=x_i for every i. The assignment equations then imply x\in\mathcal P_n, so the recovered permutation is QAP-optimal and z_{\mathrm{SDP}}=z^*.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal rank-one QAP moment matrix certifies SDP exactness and recovers a globally optimal permutation.
assumptions_latex: The SDP contains the assignment equations and \operatorname{diag}(X)=x.
The leading moment entry is one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}(M)=1\Longrightarrow X=xx^{\mathsf T},\ x\in\mathcal P_n,\ z_{\mathrm{SDP}}=z^*.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-One Exactness Certificate for the QAP SDP

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension growth of the dense vectorized-permutation SDP lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an n\times n QAP, x=\operatorname{vec}(P) has n^2 entries and the augmented moment matrix has order n^2+1. Dense symmetric storage therefore has \[\frac{(n^2+1)(n^2+2)}2=\Theta(n^4)\] scalar entries before valid zeros, symmetry reduction, or facial reduction are exploited.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dense QAP SDP has a moment matrix of order n-squared plus one and quartically many stored scalar entries.
assumptions_latex: The full vectorized-permutation moment matrix is stored densely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{ord}(M)=n^2+1\text{ and dense storage is }\Theta(n^4).
knowledge_statements.title: Dense QAP Moment-Matrix Size

knowledge_statements.scope_note: QAP-specific zero pattern inherited from mutually exclusive assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For x=\operatorname{vec}(P) with P a permutation matrix and X=xx^{\mathsf T}, \[X_{(i,j),(i,\ell)}=0\quad(j\ne\ell),\qquad X_{(i,j),(k,j)}=0\quad(i\ne k).\] These valid linear equations remain available after rank one is relaxed and may be imposed in the QAP SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lifted matrix has forced zeros for mutually exclusive assignments; imposing them strengthens the SDP without removing permutations.
assumptions_latex: x=\operatorname{vec}(P) and X=xx^{\mathsf T} before relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X_{(i,j),(k,\ell)}=0\text{ for every mutually incompatible assignment pair}.
review_flags: Often called gangster constraints; terminology is intentionally omitted from the title because no dedicated source was supplied.
knowledge_statements.title: Assignment-Incompatibility Zero Constraints

children.title: QAP Symmetry-Reduced Bounds
children.top_down_role: Invariant and association-scheme reductions lowering the cost of conic bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate reduction of an invariant lifted QAP relaxation by entry orbits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a finite group \(G\) permutes the scalar entries of a lifted variable \(Z\). A fixed point is constant on each entry orbit \(\mathcal O_1,\ldots,\mathcal O_q\), so it has the unique representation \[Z=\sum_{r=1}^q z_rE_r,\] where \(E_r\) is the indicator matrix of \(\mathcal O_r\). Substitution into invariant objectives and affine constraints produces an equivalent fixed-point formulation with one scalar variable per orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invariant lifted matrices use one scalar per entry orbit, reducing the fixed-point formulation exactly.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and acts by permutations of lifted-variable entries.
The objective and affine constraint system are invariant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Z\in\operatorname{Fix}(G)\iff Z=\sum_{r=1}^qz_rE_r,\qquad \dim\operatorname{Fix}(G)=q.

notation.meaning: Indicator matrix of the r-th orbit.

knowledge_statements.title: Orbit-Variable Aggregation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure Without Objective or Feasible-Set Invariance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failures of fixed-point averaging when either invariance hypothesis is absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=\{I,\tau\}\) swap two coordinates. The simplex \(K=\{z\ge0:z_1+z_2=1\}\) is invariant, but \(f(z)=z_1\) is not, and \[\min_{z\in K}f(z)=0<\tfrac12=\min_{z\in K\cap\operatorname{Fix}(G)}f(z).\] Conversely, \(K'=\{(1,0)\}\) is not invariant, and averaging its only point gives \((1/2,1/2)\notin K'\). Thus objective invariance is needed to preserve value and feasible-set invariance to preserve feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A noninvariant objective can change the fixed-point optimum, while a noninvariant feasible set can reject the averaged point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Dropping either principal invariance hypothesis invalidates the general averaging conclusion.}
knowledge_statements.title: Failure Without Objective or Feasible-Set Invariance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatible symmetry restriction of an invariant conic primal-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a conic primal-dual pair whose cones, affine maps, right-hand sides, and objective data are invariant under compatible orthogonal actions of a finite group \(G\). Averaging any primal-feasible or dual-feasible point preserves feasibility and objective value. Consequently, restriction to the corresponding fixed-point spaces preserves each side's optimal value and weak-duality pairing; any attained optimum has an invariant representative. Equality of primal and dual values still requires whatever regularity applies to the unreduced pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible averaging preserves primal and dual feasible values, so both sides of an invariant conic relaxation admit exact symmetry restriction.
assumptions_latex: The group actions preserve the primal and dual cones.
All affine maps and objective data intertwine the actions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p^*_{\operatorname{Fix}(G)}=p^*,\qquad d^*_{\operatorname{Fix}(G)}=d^*.

notation.meaning: Original primal and dual optimal values.

review_flags: Strong duality is not asserted without regularity for the underlying conic pair.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Symmetry Compatibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Association-scheme specialization reducing PSD blocks to scalar inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathbb S^m\) be a finite-dimensional unital commutative matrix algebra. Its elements are simultaneously orthogonally diagonalizable. For its mutually orthogonal primitive idempotents \(F_1,\ldots,F_s\), every \(Z\in\mathcal A\) has a unique expansion \[Z=\sum_{r=1}^s\theta_rF_r,\qquad Z\succeq0\iff\theta_r\ge0\ \text{for all }r.\] Hence an invariant SDP whose matrix variable lies in such an algebra reduces its PSD condition to scalar nonnegativity. A noncommutative invariant algebra generally yields matrix blocks instead.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a commutative symmetric invariant algebra, simultaneous diagonalization reduces positive semidefiniteness to nonnegative primitive-idempotent coefficients.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathbb S^m\) is finite-dimensional, unital, and commutative.
The invariant SDP matrix variable lies in \(\mathcal A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Z=\sum_r\theta_rF_r\succeq0\iff\theta_r\ge0\quad\forall r.

notation.meaning: Coefficient on the r-th invariant subspace.

knowledge_statements.title: Commutative Invariant-Algebra Scalarization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact block reduction of the PSD constraint in a group-invariant QAP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\rho:G\to O(m)\) be an orthogonal representation of a finite or compact group, and let \(\mathcal C=\{T\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}:T\rho(g)=\rho(g)T\ \forall g\in G\}\) be its real commutant. The finite-dimensional real \(*\)-algebra \(\mathcal C\) admits an isotypic decomposition under which every symmetric \(Z\in\mathcal C\) is represented by repeated Hermitian blocks over \(\mathbb R\), \(\mathbb C\), or \(\mathbb H\). Under this representation, \[Z\succeq0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad Z_r\succeq0\ \text{for every reduced Hermitian block }Z_r.\] Therefore substituting these blocks in an invariant SDP is an exact reformulation of its fixed-point PSD constraint and does not change its optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The symmetric commutant of an orthogonal group action decomposes into smaller real, complex, or quaternionic Hermitian blocks, preserving positive semidefiniteness and the invariant SDP value.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite or compact and \(\rho(G)\subseteq O(m)\).
The SDP matrix variable has already been restricted to the symmetric commutant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z\succeq0\iff Z_r\succeq0\) for every reduced invariant block.

notation.meaning: Real commutant algebra of the group representation.
Reduced Hermitian block in the isotypic decomposition.

review_flags: Block fields and multiplicities depend on the real, complex, or quaternionic type of each irreducible representation.
knowledge_statements.title: Invariant-Algebra Block Diagonalization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Fixed-Point Reduction by Reynolds Averaging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact symmetry restriction of a finite-group-invariant convex conic QAP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite group \(G\) act linearly on a vector space, let \(K\) be a convex \(G\)-invariant feasible set, and let the linear objective \(f\) satisfy \(f(g\cdot Z)=f(Z)\). For every \(Z\in K\), the Reynolds average \[\mathcal R(Z)=|G|^{-1}\sum_{g\in G}g\cdot Z\] lies in \(K\cap\operatorname{Fix}(G)\) and satisfies \(f(\mathcal R(Z))=f(Z)\). Consequently, \[\inf_{Z\in K}f(Z)=\inf_{Z\in K\cap\operatorname{Fix}(G)}f(Z).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex invariant relaxation and invariant linear objective can be restricted exactly to the group-fixed subspace by averaging.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is convex and invariant under the group action.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{Z\in K}f(Z)=\inf_{Z\in K\cap\operatorname{Fix}(G)}f(Z)\).

notation.meaning: Subspace fixed by every group element.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Fixed-Point Reduction by Reynolds Averaging
QAP Symmetry-Reduced Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact symmetry reduction of a group-invariant conic QAP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite group \(G\) act orthogonally on the variables of a convex conic QAP relaxation, and suppose its feasible set \(K\) and linear objective \(f\) are invariant under this action. For every \(Z\in K\), the Reynolds average \(\bar Z=|G|^{-1}\sum_{g\in G}g\cdot Z\) belongs to \(K\), is fixed by \(G\), and satisfies \(f(\bar Z)=f(Z)\). Therefore restricting the relaxation to the fixed-point subspace does not change its optimal bound. Simultaneous block diagonalization of the invariant matrix algebra converts its semidefinite constraint into smaller positive-semidefinite blocks without weakening the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A group-invariant conic QAP relaxation has an invariant optimum and can be block-diagonalized without changing its bound.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and acts linearly and orthogonally.
\(f(g\cdot Z)=f(Z)\) for every \(g\in G\) and \(Z\in K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{Z\in K}f(Z)=\inf_{Z\in K\cap\operatorname{Fix}(G)}f(Z)\).

notation.meaning: subspace fixed by every group element

review_flags: No supplied locator covers Reynolds averaging or association-scheme reduction.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The invariant averaging and block-diagonalization claims fit the symmetry-reduced-bound container and are mathematically plausible, but no source supports the exact fixed-point and invariant-algebra assertions.

children.title: Continuous-Bound to Discrete-Solution Interface
children.top_down_role: The boundary between continuous relaxation output and discrete optimization workflows.

children.title: Relaxation-Bound Transport
children.top_down_role: Use of continuous lower bounds within discrete exact-search frameworks.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Bound Transport
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transport of node-specific continuous lower bounds into exact minimization search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_v\) be the discrete feasible set remaining at a node \(v\) of an exact-search tree, and let \(R_v\supseteq S_v\) be a continuous relaxation using all restrictions imposed along the path to \(v\). If \(L_v=\inf_{x\in R_v}f(x)\), then \(L_v\leq\inf_{x\in S_v}f(x)\). Given the value \(U\) of a known feasible discrete solution, the node may be pruned whenever \(L_v\geq U\). Reusing a parent bound at a child is valid, but resolving the child relaxation can only improve the lower bound when its feasible region is nested in the parent relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid continuous node lower bound can prune discrete search whenever it reaches the incumbent feasible value.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
\(R_v\) contains every discrete completion feasible at node \(v\).
\(U\) is attained by a globally feasible discrete solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_v\geq U\) certifies that node \(v\) contains no improving solution.

notation.meaning: discrete feasible completions at search node v
node lower bound and incumbent upper bound

source_refs.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

source_witnesses.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transport of continuous-relaxation infeasibility to a discrete search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(v\), let \(S_v\subseteq R_v\), where \(S_v\) is the set of discrete completions and \(R_v\) its continuous relaxation. If \(R_v=\varnothing\), then \(S_v=\varnothing\), so the node may be fathomed without reference to an incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified infeasibility of a containing continuous relaxation certifies that the discrete node has no feasible completion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_v=\varnothing\Rightarrow S_v=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Discrete completion set and containing continuous relaxation at node v.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Infeasibility Fathoming

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global lower-bound construction from node bounds on a frontier covering the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be the original feasible set and suppose \(S\subseteq\bigcup_{v\in\mathcal F}S_v\). If \(L_v\le\inf_{x\in S_v}f(x)\) for every \(v\in\mathcal F\), then \[L_{\mathcal F}:=\min_{v\in\mathcal F}L_v\le z^*:=\inf_{x\in S}f(x).\] Hence a feasible incumbent of value \(U\) satisfies \(0\le U-z^*\le U-L_{\mathcal F}\). Closed nodes may be omitted only when their exclusion certificate preserves the stated coverage or supplies a lower bound no smaller than the retained aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimum valid bound over a frontier covering every feasible solution is a global lower bound and yields an incumbent-gap certificate.
assumptions_latex: The frontier node sets cover the original feasible set.
Every node bound is valid on its node.
\(U\) is attained by an original feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\mathcal F}\le z^*\le U\).

notation.meaning: Minimum valid bound over that frontier.

review_flags: The covering condition corrects the builder's overly weak condition that only unexcluded solutions be covered.

children.title: Discrete Rounding-Recovery Interface
children.top_down_role: Conversion of fractional or matrix solutions into discrete feasible candidates.

children.title: Fractional-Solution Rounding
children.top_down_role: Conversion of fractional relaxation points into discrete candidates.

knowledge_statements.title: Fractional-Solution Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nearest-permutation rounding of a fractional assignment matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a fractional assignment matrix \(\bar X\in[0,1]^{n\times n}\), preferably doubly stochastic. Initialize weights \(w_{ij}=\bar X_{ij}\). Solve the linear assignment problem \[P^\star\in\arg\max_{P\in\Pi_n}\langle \bar X,P\rangle.\] Output \(P^\star\). Because every \(P\in\Pi_n\) satisfies \(\|P\|_F^2=n\), this rule is equivalent to minimizing \(\|P-\bar X\|_F^2\) over \(P\in\Pi_n\). The algorithm stops after one exact assignment solve and always returns a permutation matrix, although it need not minimize the original quadratic objective among possible roundings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project a fractional assignment matrix onto the nearest permutation matrix by solving one linear assignment problem.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar X\) is a finite real matrix of order \(n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P^\star\in\Pi_n\) and \(P^\star\) minimizes \(\|P-\bar X\|_F\) over \(\Pi_n\).

source_refs.locator: 5. Approximation Algorithms in Quadratic Programming p. 38

review_flags: Exact nearest-permutation rounding locator should be confirmed.

source_witnesses.locator: 5. Approximation Algorithms in Quadratic Programming p. 38

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Componentwise Threshold Rounding for the Binary Cube
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic nearest-vertex rounding when no coupled discrete constraints must be preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\bar x\in[0,1]^n\), choose \(\hat x_i=0\) when \(\bar x_i<\tfrac12\), choose \(\hat x_i=1\) when \(\bar x_i>\tfrac12\), and choose either value at a tie. Then \[\hat x\in\arg\min_{y\in\{0,1\}^n}\|y-\bar x\|_2^2.\] The coordinates can be rounded in \(O(n)\) time. This proximity statement gives neither preservation of coupled side constraints nor optimality for the original quadratic objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Thresholding at one half produces a nearest binary-cube vertex in linear time, but need not preserve coupled constraints or optimize the quadratic objective.
assumptions_latex: The target set for the proximity claim is the full cube \(\{0,1\}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \hat x\in\arg\min_{y\in\{0,1\}^n}\|y-\bar x\|_2^2.
knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Threshold Rounding for the Binary Cube

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A fractional point satisfying a cardinality equality whose coordinatewise rounding is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[D=\{x\in\{0,1\}^3:x_1+x_2+x_3=1\},\qquad \bar x=(0.4,0.3,0.3).\] The point \(\bar x\) satisfies the continuous relaxation \(0\le x\le1\) and \(x_1+x_2+x_3=1\), but threshold rounding at one half gives \(\hat x=(0,0,0)\notin D\). Thus coordinatewise rounding has no general feasibility guarantee for coupled discrete constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fractional point can satisfy a cardinality equality while independent threshold rounding violates it.
assumptions_latex: Rounding is performed independently at threshold one half.
The target discrete set contains a coupled cardinality equality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x\in\{x\in[0,1]^3:\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x=1\},\qquad \hat x=(0,0,0)\notin D.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupled-Constraint Failure of Componentwise Rounding

children.title: Matrix-Solution Recovery
children.top_down_role: Extraction of discrete candidates from lifted or semidefinite solutions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact deterministic recovery from a normalized rank-one positive-semidefinite moment matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,\qquad \operatorname{rank}(Z)=1.\] The normalization \(Z_{00}=1\) forces \[Z=(1,x)(1,x)^{\mathsf T},\qquad X=xx^{\mathsf T}.\] If \(X_{ii}=x_i\) for every \(i\), then \(x_i^2=x_i\) and hence \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\). If every other required lifted constraint is an exact lifting of an original constraint, the extracted vector is feasible for the original discrete problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized rank-one moment matrix yields one exact vector; binary diagonal identities make it binary, and exact lifted side constraints transfer feasibility.
assumptions_latex: For complete feasibility, all required side constraints are represented by exact lifted constraints satisfied by \(Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Z=(1,x)(1,x)^{\mathsf T},\quad X=xx^{\mathsf T},\quad X_{ii}=x_i\ \forall i\Longrightarrow x\in\{0,1\}^n.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-One Moment Recovery
Matrix-Solution Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-one spectral extraction followed by assignment projection from an SDP moment matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a positive-semidefinite relaxation matrix \(Y\in\mathbb S_+^{n^2}\). Compute a unit leading eigenvector \(u\) of \(Y\), reshape \(u\) and \(-u\) into matrices \(U^+\) and \(U^-\), and project each onto the permutation set: \[P^s\in\arg\max_{P\in\Pi_n}\langle U^s,P\rangle,\qquad s\in\{+,-\}.\] Evaluate the original QAP objective at both candidates and output the better one. The method stops after the eigenvector computation, two linear assignment solves, and two objective evaluations. Its output is feasible, but rank-one extraction alone provides no universal approximation guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extract a leading SDP direction, reshape both signs, project them to permutations, and retain the better QAP solution.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is symmetric positive semidefinite and indexed consistently with vectorized assignments.
The original QAP objective can be evaluated on permutation matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output belongs to \(\Pi_n\).

children.title: Discrete Feasibility Repair
children.top_down_role: Restoration of combinatorial feasibility after candidate extraction.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Feasibility Repair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal assignment-feasibility repair by projection onto permutation matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an arbitrary tentative matrix \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), possibly violating integrality or row and column assignment constraints. Solve \[P^\star\in\arg\min_{P\in\Pi_n}\|P-Z\|_F^2=\arg\max_{P\in\Pi_n}\langle Z,P\rangle.\] Output \(P^\star\) and stop after the linear assignment solve. This projection repairs integrality, row sums, and column sums simultaneously. Side constraints beyond permutation feasibility require a correspondingly constrained discrete repair problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repair a tentative assignment by projecting it onto the permutation matrices with one linear assignment solve.
assumptions_latex: Required feasibility consists solely of membership in \(\Pi_n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P^\star\in\Pi_n\) minimizes \(\|P-Z\|_F\) over \(P\in\Pi_n\).

source_refs.locator: 5. Approximation Algorithms in Quadratic Programming p. 38

review_flags: Exact repair discussion requires locator confirmation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projection onto the Complete Discrete Feasible Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact minimum-distance repair when combinatorial side constraints accompany integrality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\{0,1\}^m\) be nonempty, let \(z\in\mathbb R^m\), and let \(W\in\mathbb S_{++}^m\). Any solution \[x^{\mathrm{rep}}\in\arg\min_{x\in D}(x-z)^{\mathsf T}W(x-z)\] satisfies every constraint encoded by \(D\) and is a minimum-weighted-distance feasible repair. Projection onto a strict superset of \(D\), or independent repair of only selected constraints, does not by itself guarantee membership in \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimum-distance projection onto the complete discrete feasible set restores all encoded constraints; projection onto only a relaxation may not.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^{\mathrm{rep}}\in D,\qquad \|x^{\mathrm{rep}}-z\|_W=\min_{x\in D}\|x-z\|_W.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection onto the Complete Discrete Feasible Set

children.title: Recovery-Quality Assessment
children.top_down_role: Comparison of recovered candidate quality against relaxation bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Recovery-Quality Assessment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori global quality certificate for a recovered feasible minimization solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^R\) be a recovered discrete feasible solution with value \(U=f(x^R)\), and let \(L\) be a certified lower bound on the global optimum \(z^*\). Then \[L\leq z^*\leq U,\qquad 0\leq U-z^*\leq U-L.\] Thus \(U-L\) is an absolute suboptimality certificate. For any positive scaling denominator \(d\), the reported normalized gap \((U-L)/d\) certifies \((U-z^*)/d\leq(U-L)/d\). In particular, \(U=L\) certifies global optimality of the recovered solution. Empirical recovery quality may additionally compare multiple recovered candidates, but such comparisons do not replace the bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible recovered value and a valid lower bound certify its absolute and normalized global optimality gaps.
assumptions_latex: \(x^R\) is feasible for the original discrete minimization problem.
\(d>0\) when a normalized gap is reported.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq f(x^R)-z^*\leq f(x^R)-L\).

notation.meaning: certified lower bound and recovered feasible value

source_refs.locator: 5.1 Global vs. Local Optimum p. 127

source_witnesses.locator: 5.1 Global vs. Local Optimum p. 127

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicative assessment for minimization when the certified lower bound is positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^R\) be feasible, \(U=f(x^R)\), and \(0<L\le z^*\le U\). Then \[1\le \frac{U}{z^*}\le \frac{U}{L}.\] Therefore, for \(\rho\ge1\), \(U/L\le\rho\) certifies \(U\le\rho z^*\). If \(L\le0\), this quotient supplies no finite multiplicative certificate, although the additive certificate remains valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive certified lower bound yields a multiplicative recovery guarantee; nonpositive lower bounds support only additive-gap assessment.
assumptions_latex: \(x^R\) is feasible for the original minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U/z^*\le U/L\), so \(U/L\le\rho\Rightarrow U\le\rho z^*\).

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound, recovered value, and global optimum value.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplicative Recovery Certificate

children.title: Relaxation Strength–Cost Comparison
children.top_down_role: Comparison among box, spectral, linearized, semidefinite, and exact-conic bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Strength–Cost Comparison
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-inclusion criterion for comparing lower-bound strength, separated from computational cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem with feasible set \(S\), objective \(f\), and optimal value \(z^*=\inf_{x\in S}f(x)\), let \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) be valid relaxations satisfying \(S\subseteq R_2\subseteq R_1\). Their lower bounds satisfy \[L_1:=\inf_{x\in R_1}f(x)\leq L_2:=\inf_{x\in R_2}f(x)\leq z^*.\] Thus genuine nesting makes the smaller relaxation's bound at least as strong, but it implies no ordering of solution time or memory consumption. Relaxation families that are not nested cannot be ordered by this inclusion principle and must be compared using both bound quality and computational resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nested smaller relaxation gives a lower bound at least as strong as that of a larger relaxation, but bound strength does not determine computational cost; nonnested families require separate comparison.
assumptions_latex: All infima use the same minimization objective \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_1\leq L_2\leq z^*\), with no implied ordering of computational cost.

notation.meaning: optimal value of the original minimization problem

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Bound Dominance and Bound–Cost Pareto Order
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instance-class comparison of relaxation strength and measured computational cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization-instance class \(\mathcal I\), family \(A\) bound-dominates family \(B\) when \(L_A(I)\ge L_B(I)\) for every \(I\in\mathcal I\), with strict inequality for some instance under strict dominance. For a fixed resource convention \(C\), \(A\) Pareto-dominates \(B\) on an instance when \(L_A\ge L_B\) and \(C_A\le C_B\), with at least one strict inequality. Nonnesting alone implies neither order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxations admit a uniform bound-dominance order and a separate bound–cost Pareto order; nonnested families need not be comparable.
assumptions_latex: All bounds use the same minimization objective and instance convention.
The instance class and resource measurement convention are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\succeq_{\mathcal I}B\iff L_A(I)\ge L_B(I)\ \forall I\in\mathcal I\).

notation.meaning: Bounds produced by families A and B on instance I.
Costs under a fixed resource convention.

review_flags: Measured cost can depend on implementation, platform, and accuracy convention.
